Process Details:
# 7.6.3 Manage Retirement

## Overview
Manage Retirement covers the end-to-end process of transitioning an employee from active employment to retired status. The process ensures retirees receive accurate and timely pension/retirement benefits, final pay, and post-employment support while the organization securely offboards the individual, captures knowledge, and maintains compliance with legal, regulatory, and plan requirements.

Purpose and role in the organization:
- Protect the retiree experience: provide clear guidance, accurate calculations, and on-time payments and benefits transitions.
- Safeguard the organization: ensure compliance, mitigate operational and security risks, and reduce financial leakage (overpayments, benefits errors).
- Support workforce planning: align retirements with succession planning, role backfill, and knowledge transfer to maintain business continuity.
- Maintain brand and alumni relations: treat retirees as brand ambassadors and leverage alumni networks for referrals, contracting, or mentoring.

Scope includes normal, early, and deferred retirements; executive and union retirements; and special cases such as disability retirement where applicable. It interfaces closely with benefits, payroll, IT/security deprovisioning, facilities, and workforce planning.

## Key Activities
- Retirement readiness and counseling (education on options, timelines, and impacts)
- Eligibility validation and service/age verification
- Pension/retirement benefit estimation and elections (DB, DC, hybrid, SERP, union plans)
- Final pay calculation (accrued leave, bonuses, commissions, deductions, equity)
- Benefits transition (healthcare, retiree medical, COBRA or equivalents, life insurance conversion)
- Regulatory and plan compliance (notices, disclosures, consents, tax reporting)
- Knowledge transfer and transition planning
- Approvals and documentation (retirement notice, manager acknowledgment, HR approval)
- Offboarding coordination (IT access, assets, facilities, vendors)
- Exit interview and alumni onboarding
- Records retention and case closure
- Post-retirement support (issue resolution, corrections, statements)

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Employee intent to retire (target retirement date, form or ticket)
- Employee master data (DOB, start date, service breaks, employment agreements)
- Plan documents and rules (pension/retirement plan, retiree medical, life insurance)
- Service and compensation history (for benefit calculations)
- Accrued leave balances and time-off records
- Union/CBA provisions (if applicable)
- Outstanding loans or obligations (401(k)/DC loans, relocation paybacks, garnishments)
- Asset and access inventory (laptops, phones, cards, licenses)
- Current benefits elections and dependent data
- Role criticality assessment and succession plan status

Prerequisites:
- Confirm retirement eligibility per plan and policy (age/service/hours)
- No unresolved compliance blocks (e.g., active investigations requiring retention of access or equipment hold)
- Tax and identity information up to date (addresses, banking)
- Manager acknowledgement of retirement date and coverage plan
- Availability of required internal approvers (HR, payroll, benefits, IT)

Dependencies on other processes:
- Administer Compensation and Benefits (benefits enrollment, plan administration)
- Payroll processing (final wages, deductions, tax handling)
- Identity and access management (account deprovisioning)
- Asset management and facilities (equipment return, badge, parking)
- Workforce and succession planning (backfill decisions, internal mobility)
- Records management and compliance (data retention, regulatory filings)
- Vendor management (third-party plan administrators)

## Process Steps
1) Initiation and Counseling (T-12 to T-6 months preferred; minimum T-90 days)
- Employee notifies manager and HR via formal retirement notice.
- HR creates a retirement case in the HRIS/case tool and sends acknowledgment with timeline and checklist.
- Schedule retirement counseling session(s): explain options, plan rules, benefit start timing, tax considerations, healthcare/COBRA/Medicare equivalents, and key deadlines.
- Provide pension/benefit estimate(s) and decision guide; invite spouse/partner if allowed.

2) Eligibility and Data Verification
- HR/Benefits verifies age and service; resolves discrepancies in employment history or service breaks.
- Confirm union/CBA provisions, executive contracts, or SERP rules where relevant.
- Validate personal data (address, banking, beneficiaries, dependents).

3) Retirement Option Modeling and Elections
- Generate official benefit estimates (DB annuity vs. lump sum, DC withdrawal strategies per plan rules).
- Provide tools or vendor sessions for scenario modeling (start dates, survivor options, cost-of-living adjustments).
- Employee selects preliminary options; document elections with required consents and notarizations if required.

4) Transition Planning and Knowledge Transfer
- Manager creates a transition plan: role coverage, handoff timeline, critical process mapping.
- Identify and assign successors or interim coverage; schedule shadowing, SOP updates, and artifact capture.
- Define final working arrangements (last day on-site/remote, final meetings, knowledge sessions).

5) Approvals and Case Controls
- Manager approves retirement date; HR validates compliance; Legal/Compliance engaged if special conditions.
- Two-person review on benefit calculations and final pay elements for high-risk cases (executives, complex accruals).
- Confirm any incentives (early retirement packages) and secure signed agreements.

6) Final Pay and Benefits Administration
- Calculate final pay: base pay to last day, overtime, shift differentials, accrued leave payout or forfeiture, commissions, discretionary bonuses (per policy), outstanding deductions.
- Coordinate with equity administration: vesting, exercise windows, post-termination rules.
- Trigger retiree medical or COBRA-equivalent notices; process life insurance conversion/portability.
- Initiate pension/benefit elections to vendors; collect spousal consents and identity verification.
- Schedule first benefit payment date and method; align with last paycheck and coverage end/start dates.

7) Offboarding Logistics
- IT: schedule deprovisioning of logical access effective EOD last day; set up email forwarding/auto-reply per policy.
- Facilities: collect badges, parking, keys; handle workspace clearance.
- Asset management: return laptops, phones, cards, tokens; reconcile software licenses.
- Vendor/Client notifications if the retiree is a designated contact.

8) Exit Interview and Alumni Engagement
- Conduct exit interview; capture feedback and improvement ideas.
- Invite to alumni network, mentorship, or retiree engagement programs; collect preferred contact channel.

9) Day 0 to Day +5 Execution
- Process final payroll; issue required pay statements and tax withholdings.
- Confirm benefit coverage end/start and distribute certificates or ID cards where applicable.
- Disable access and confirm deprovisioning completion; close or reassign tickets and workflow items.

10) Post-Retirement Support and Case Closure (Day +5 to +90)
- Resolve any discrepancies (payroll, benefit amounts, address corrections).
- Issue required tax forms related to distributions per jurisdiction.
- Finalize records retention tagging and archive case.
- Update metrics and report outcomes; feed insights to workforce planning and process improvement.

Decision points and variations:
- Early vs. normal retirement: validate eligibility and impact on benefit factors.
- Disability retirement: coordinate with disability plans and additional medical documentation.
- Phased retirement/re-hire as contractor or part-time: ensure policy compliance, avoid benefit conflicts, and set new engagement terms.
- International transfers: handle cross-border tax, social security totalization, and plan portability.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Approved retirement case with documented elections and consents
- Accurate final paycheck with reconciled adjustments and deductions
- Initiated pension/retirement benefits and/or DC distribution setup
- Benefits transition executed (retiree medical, COBRA equivalents, life insurance actions)
- Completed offboarding: deprovisioning, asset return, facilities clearance
- Knowledge transfer artifacts (SOPs, process maps, credentials handover, project notes)
- Exit interview summary and alumni enrollment (if applicable)
- Compliance filings and notices delivered within statutory timelines
- Archived records per retention schedule

Success criteria:
- Retiree receives first benefit payment and final pay accurately and on time
- Zero critical compliance breaches; all notices on or before due date
- All accesses revoked within SLA; 100% asset return accounted
- Knowledge transfer completed as per plan; successor confirmed
- Retiree satisfaction meets or exceeds target threshold

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Employee (Retiree): Provide notice; attend counseling; make timely elections; return assets; participate in knowledge transfer and exit interview.
- People Manager: Acknowledge notice; approve retirement date; execute transition plan; ensure knowledge transfer; confirm coverage/backfill.
- HR Business Partner: Advise manager on workforce impact and succession; support employee with policy guidance.
- HR Operations/Shared Services: Own retirement case; coordinate tasks and communications; ensure documentation completeness; quality checks.
- Benefits Administrator/Provider: Verify eligibility; produce estimates; process elections; manage retiree medical/COBRA; provide confirmations.
- Payroll: Calculate and process final pay; handle deductions, tax withholdings, and reporting.
- Pension/DC Plan Vendor(s): Calculate and disburse benefits; manage participant communications; maintain records.
- Legal/Compliance: Review complex cases; ensure adherence to laws, plan documents, and CBAs; advise on international and executive scenarios.
- IT Security/Identity Management: Deprovision access; ensure data security; confirm completion.
- Facilities/Asset Management: Recover assets; deactivate badges/parking; update inventories.
- Finance: Reconcile costs, accruals, and any severance/retirement incentives; support audits.
- Talent Management/Workforce Planning: Coordinate backfill/succession; capture retirement trends.
- Records Management: Apply retention schedules; ensure secure archiving.
- Alumni/Communications: Manage retiree engagement and ongoing communication.

## Best Practices
- Start early: offer retirement readiness programs and counseling 12–18 months before anticipated retirement.
- Standardize with checklists and RACI: reduce omissions; clarify handoffs; automate reminders.
- Two-person review on high-risk calculations: pension factors, final pay, equity handling.
- Integrate systems: HRIS, payroll, benefits, identity management with event-driven workflows and APIs to prevent delays.
- Provide clear, plain-language communications: timelines, what to expect, and who to contact.
- Optimize knowledge transfer: structured plan with artifacts, job shadowing, and validation of successor readiness.
- Respect privacy and dignity: minimize access to sensitive data; apply need-to-know principles.
- Define retiree rehire policy: criteria, cooling-off periods, impact on benefits; prevent misclassification.
- Track and act on feedback: retiree experience surveys and trend analysis.
- Align with jurisdictional requirements: ensure notices, tax reporting, and benefits rules are current; involve local experts for cross-border cases.
- Conduct post-implementation reviews: audit a sample of cases quarterly to identify control gaps or training needs.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Data discrepancies in service history
  - Solution: Run pre-retirement audits annually; reconcile with vendors; maintain a master service record.
- Late notice compressing timelines
  - Solution: Communicate minimum notice periods; offer incentives for early notification; fast-track workflow with priority SLAs when needed.
- Complex benefit rules and errors
  - Solution: Use certified calculators; vendor SLAs; independent quality checks; maintain current plan documentation.
- Missed or delayed access deprovisioning
  - Solution: Automate identity workflows triggered by retirement date; real-time deprovisioning confirmations to HR.
- Knowledge loss and operational disruption
  - Solution: Mandatory knowledge transfer plans; measure completion; engage retirees as short-term advisors where policy allows.
- Benefits transition confusion (e.g., retiree medical, COBRA equivalents)
  - Solution: Provide step-by-step guides and hotlines; proactive outreach before and after retirement date.
- Equity and commission handling
  - Solution: Clear policies, centralized equity admin coordination, and communication timed to vesting/exercise windows.
- International tax and compliance complexity
  - Solution: Engage tax advisors; use country-specific playbooks; ensure correct local notices and filings.
- Overpayments and recoupment issues
  - Solution: Pre-issue validation checks; post-pay reconciliation within defined windows; clear recoupment procedures.

## Performance Metrics
- Processing timeliness
  - Percentage of retirements completed on or before target date
  - Median cycle time from notice to case closure
- Accuracy and quality
  - First-pass yield for final pay and benefit calculations
  - Number of payroll/benefit corrections per 100 retirements
- Compliance and risk
  - On-time delivery of required notices and filings

Deliver employee communications is the execution layer of the internal communications function. It also facilitates dialogue between employees and leadership and across teams, reinforcing culture, enabling change, and mitigating risk.

This process sits within the Manage employee communication capability and interfaces closely with HR, IT, Legal/Compliance, Security, and Business Units. It covers message production, channel distribution, facilitation of engagement, monitoring, and continuous improvement.

[9.10.2] Manage transactions

Process Details:
## Overview
Manage transactions is the end-to-end process by which an organization executes, controls, and records cross-border fund transfers and currency conversions arising from trade, investments, intercompany activities, and treasury operations. The purpose is to move money to the right place, in the right currency, at the right time, at minimal total cost and risk—while complying with tax rules, sanctions/AML regimes, exchange controls, and internal policies. This process underpins enterprise liquidity, supports international growth, and protects capital by optimizing payment methods, FX execution, routing, and regulatory posture.

## Key Activities
- Intake and classification of transaction requests (e.g., vendor payment, intercompany funding, dividend, capex, investment, debt service).
- Sanctions/AML and regulatory screening of counterparties, countries, and payment purpose.
- Payment method and routing selection (local vs. cross-border rails, SWIFT, SEPA, ACH, RTP).
- Currency strategy and FX execution (spot/forward/NDF/options; internal netting vs. external hedge).
- Determination of settlement instructions (beneficiary, intermediaries, charges option OUR/SHA/BEN, value date).
- Tax and regulatory assessment (withholding tax, treaty forms, capital controls, documentary requirements).
- Approvals and segregation of duties enforcement (payment, FX deal, high-risk jurisdictions).
- Payment file creation, bank connectivity, and submission (ISO 20022 pain.001; MT101; host-to-host/API/EBICS/SWIFT).
- Monitoring, tracking, and exception handling (SWIFT gpi, bank returns, RFIs/holds).
- Posting, reconciliation, and accounting for FX gains/losses, fees, and intercompany positions.
- Regulatory and management reporting (balance-of-payments, derivative reporting, cash visibility).
- Continuous optimization (fee analysis, STP rate improvement, route optimization, policy updates).

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs
- Approved payment request or funding need with business justification and due date.
- Beneficiary master data: legal name, address, bank details (IBAN/BBAN, BIC/SWIFT, routing), tax IDs.
- Currency, amount, and required value date; supporting invoices/contracts.
- Intercompany agreements and transfer pricing terms (for internal flows).
- Current FX exposures/limits; benchmark rates; hedging policy.
- Bank account availability, signatory mandates, and fee schedules.
- Country/jurisdiction requirements (withholding tax certificates, documentary evidence).
- Compliance data: sanctioned entity/country lists, internal watchlists, KYC status.

Prerequisites
- Treasury policy and procedures approved (payment authority matrix, FX and liquidity policies).
- Bank connectivity established and tested (formats, channels, cut-off times, holiday calendars).
- Sanctions/AML screening tools and workflows operational.
- Master data governance in place (vendor/beneficiary onboarding, validation, periodic review).
- Authorized approvers and dual-control configured in TMS/ERP/bank.
- Accounting configuration (GL accounts, tax codes, FX revaluation rules).

Dependencies on other processes
- 9.10.1 Manage cash positioning and forecasting (to ensure liquidity).
- Bank account management/mandates.
- Accounts Payable/Receivable processing and approvals.
- 9.3 Manage foreign exchange risk.
- Intercompany accounting and netting.
- Compliance management (KYC, sanctions, AML).
- General accounting and financial reporting.

## Process Steps
1) Trigger and intake
- Receive transaction request from business unit/AP/treasury (portal or TMS workflow).
- Classify transaction type and priority (critical, standard, low value).
- Check due date vs. cut-off times/time zones.

2) Validate data and documentation
- Validate beneficiary data (IBAN check, Confirmation of Payee/beneficiary pre-validation where available).
- Confirm purpose of payment and supporting documents (invoice, loan agreement, dividend resolution).
- For intercompany: confirm legal entities, agreements, interest terms, and currency.

3) Compliance screening
- Screen counterparties, banks, countries, and narrative against sanctions/AML lists.
- Apply export controls/trade compliance if trade-related.
- Determine if enhanced due diligence or Legal/Compliance review is required (e.g., high-risk country, PEP exposure).
- Decision: proceed, escalate, or reject. Record outcomes.

4) Tax and regulatory assessment
- Determine withholding tax applicability and treaty relief; ensure forms/Certificates of Residence in place.
- Identify regulatory filings/approvals (e.g., central bank reporting, capital control approvals, balance-of-payments).
- For dividends/interest/royalties: ensure substance and transfer pricing documentation.
- Estimate taxes/fees and configure charges option (OUR/SHA/BEN) per policy.

5) Payment method and route design
- Select optimal payment rail and route (local clearing, SWIFT MT103, SEPA Credit Transfer, RTP).
- Decide use of in-house bank, payment-on-behalf-of (POBO), or collection-on-behalf-of (COBO) structures.
- Evaluate correspondent/intermediary banks to reduce lifting fees and repairs.
- Confirm value date feasibility and cut-off compliance.

6) Currency strategy and FX execution
- Determine if natural offset/netting can reduce external FX.
- Choose instrument (spot/forward/NDF/options) per FX policy and exposure.
- Execute FX via approved platform (e.g., 360T/FXall) within dealer limits; target benchmark (e.g., WMR 4pm or RFQ best-of-three).
- Consider CLS settlement to reduce Herstatt risk for eligible currencies.
- Link FX deal to payment in TMS; lock rates and settlement instructions.

7) Approvals
- Route for approvals according to authority matrix (amount, currency, counterparty risk).
- Obtain tax/legal sign-off if required.
- Enforce dual approval and SoD (initiator ≠ approver ≠ releaser).
- Log all approvals in system audit trail.

8) Payment preparation
- Create payment file(s) in required format (ISO 20022 pain.001, local formats).
- Validate against bank format rules (schema and bank-specific).
- Apply charge code, remittance info, and regulatory purpose codes (e.g., CN reg. codes, IN purpose codes).

9) Submission and execution
- Transmit via secure channel (SWIFT, H2H, API, EBICS); confirm receipt/ACK.
- Monitor STP status and SWIFT gpi tracker for cross-border wires.
- Respond to bank RFIs promptly (source of funds, invoice copy, KYC info).

10) Settlement and monitoring
- Verify debit and credit value dates; check for deductions (lifting fees).
- Handle returns or repairs: identify root cause (details mismatch, sanction hit, regulatory block), correct, and resubmit.
- Communicate status to stakeholders (supplier portal update, internal notifications).

11) Accounting and reconciliation
- Post accounting entries (AP/AR, intercompany, bank, fees).
- Recognize realized FX gain/loss; update hedging documentation and effectiveness as applicable.
- Reconcile bank statements (camt.053/MT940) and clear open items.

12) Regulatory and management reporting
- File required reports (balance-of-payments, derivatives reporting, FATCA/CRS where applicable).
- Update cash visibility dashboards and liquidity reports.
- Maintain transaction dossier for audit (supporting docs, approvals, screenings, FX deal tickets).

13) Review and continuous improvement
- Analyze exceptions, fees, FX slippage vs. benchmark.
- Update routing tables, standing settlement instructions, and approved bank list.
- Conduct quarterly fee audits and annual policy reviews.

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs
- Executed cross-border payment or collection in target currency and value date.
- FX deals executed and linked to underlying flows.
- Accurate accounting entries and reconciled bank statements.

Deliverables
- Payment confirmations (SWIFT MT103/gpi UETR), bank statements (camt.053/MT940).
- Compliance records (sanctions screening logs, RFIs, approvals).
- Tax documentation (withholding tax forms, treaty relief evidence).
- Regulatory filings and acknowledgments.
- Exception and incident logs with resolutions.
- Performance reports (KPIs, fee analysis, STP rate).

Success criteria
- Right amount/currency credited on-time with no unanticipated deductions.
- 98%+ STP rate; low exception/repair rate.
- Compliance with sanctions/AML and regulatory obligations; zero violations.
- FX execution within policy and slippage tolerance.
- Complete, timely accounting and reconciliations.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Group Treasurer: Owns policy, risk appetite, banking strategy, and oversight.
- Treasury Front Office (Dealers): Execute FX; propose routing; manage market risk within limits.
- Treasury Operations/Back Office: Prepare/submit payments; confirmations; settlement; documentation; reconciliation.
- Shared Service Center AP/AR: Initiate requests; validate invoices; provide remittance info; vendor master maintenance.
- Tax: Assess WHT/treaty positions; approve tax-sensitive flows; maintain documentation.
- Legal/Compliance: Sanctions/AML/KYC oversight; respond to bank RFIs; approve high-risk jurisdictions.
- Local Finance Controllers: Ensure local compliance (exchange controls, reporting); maintain local bank relationships.
- Intercompany/Accounting: Record intercompany flows; transfer pricing compliance; period-end FX revaluation.
- IT/Integration: Maintain TMS/ERP/payment hub connectivity, formats, and security.
- Bank Partners/Providers: Execute payments; provide confirmations; support investigations; fee transparency.
- Internal Audit/Risk: Periodic reviews; control testing; policy adherence.

## Best Practices
- Centralize cross-border payments in a payment factory with POBO/COBO and an in-house bank.
- Use intercompany netting to reduce external flows and FX transactions.
- Maintain standard settlement instructions (SSIs) with dual control and periodic revalidation.
- Pre-validate beneficiaries (IBAN checkers, Confirmation of Payee) and whitelist trusted partners.
- Enforce strict SoD and multi-factor approvals; use hardware tokens/PKI for bank portals.
- Adopt ISO 20022 end-to-end with strong schema and bank-rule validation to maximize STP.
- Apply routing optimization (preferred correspondents, gpi insights) to minimize lifting fees and delays.
- Execute FX via competitive electronic platforms; measure slippage vs. benchmarks; use CLS where possible.
- Maintain up-to-date holiday/cut-off calendars and time-zone-aware scheduling.
- Implement sanctions/AML screening with fuzzy logic and risk-based escalation; keep watchlists current.
- Periodically benchmark and renegotiate bank fees; analyze OUR/SHA cost trade-offs by corridor.
- Use virtual accounts to streamline reconciliation for high-volume cross-border collections.
- Maintain a country-by-country regulatory and tax playbook (capital controls, docs, purpose codes).
- Conduct quarterly exception root-cause analysis and correct master data/process defects.
- Test disaster recovery and payment failover channels; define emergency cash procedures.

## Common Challenges
- Sanctions/AML holds or RFIs: Mitigate with robust screening, clear payment purpose narratives, pre-cleared documents, and rapid RFI response SLAs.
- Payment returns/repairs due to data errors: Use validation tools, structured remittance info, and beneficiary verification; enforce four-eye checks on SSIs.
- High and unpredictable correspondent fees (lifting): Optimize routes, negotiate all-in fees, use local rails where possible, and set charges option per corridor.
- FX volatility and slippage: Hedge per policy, time execution to liquidity windows, and measure dealers against benchmarks.
- Cut-off time misses/time-zone gaps: Schedule earlier; use global processing centers; maintain calendars and reminders; leverage RTP where available.
- Exchange controls/capital restrictions: Maintain local expertise, pre-approve channels, stage payments, or use approved onshore funding mechanisms.
- Inconsistent tax treatment/WHT: Centralize tax review, maintain treaty documents, and standardize payment purpose coding and documentation.
- Bank connectivity outages: Maintain redundant channels (SWIFT + H2H + portal) and a tested manual fallback.
- Data quality in vendor master: Govern onboarding with validations and periodic recertification.
- Audit trail gaps: Use workflow systems with immutable logs; standardize transaction dossiers.

## Performance Metrics
- STP rate (% payments processed without manual repair).
- On-time settlement rate (% credited by required value date).
- Exception/repair rate and mean time to resolve (MTTR).
- Total cost per transaction (FX spread + bank fees + lifting fees), by corridor.
- FX execution slippage vs. benchmark (bps), by instrument.
- Sanctions/AML hit rate and false positive rate; average RFI resolution time.
- Payment return rate (% value returned) and top root causes.
- Percentage of flows through preferred rails (SEPA/local ACH vs. SWIFT).
- gpi coverage and tracking utilization rate; average end-to-end settlement time.
- Bank fee variance vs. contract (%).
- Hedging effectiveness (per IFRS 9/ASC 815 if hedge accounting is used).
- Regulatory reporting timeliness and accuracy (% on-time with zero defects).

## Technology and Tools
- Treasury Management Systems (TMS): SAP TRM, Kyriba, GTreasury, FIS Integrity—for workflows, FX, settlements, and exposure management.
- ERP/AP platforms: SAP S/4HANA, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics—for payment runs and accounting.
- Payment hubs/connectivity: SWIFT (Alliance Lite2/MASE), host-to-host, APIs, EBICS; ISO 20022 engines and validators.
- FX trading/execution: 360T, FXall, Bloomberg, Refinitiv; CLS for settlement risk mitigation.
- Sanctions/AML screening: Fircosoft, LexisNexis/Accuity, Dow Jones; internal watchlist management.
- Bank portals and gpi trackers: For submission, approvals, and real-time tracking.
- Validation utilities: IBAN/BBAN checkers, Confirmation of Payee, LEI/BIC validation, address verification.
- Reconciliation and close: BlackLine, Trintech Cadency, Redwood.
- Document and workflow management: ServiceNow/Jira, e-signature (DocuSign), DMS for tax and TP docs.
- Reporting/analytics: Power BI/Tableau; bank fee analysis tools; holiday/cut-off calendar services.
- Security: MFA, PKI certificates, HSMs; role-based access control and audit logging.

This documentation provides a structured, actionable foundation to operate, control, and continuously improve cross-border transaction management within an international treasury framework.

[12.3.2] Report audit findings
Level: 3

Process Details:
## Overview
Report audit findings is the formal process of communicating the results of an internal audit engagement to management and the board (typically via the Audit Committee). Its purpose is to provide clear, evidence-based insight into control design and operating effectiveness, compliance with policies and regulations, and risks that require attention. The process synthesizes audit observations into actionable findings that include criteria, condition, cause, effect, and recommendations, along with management’s agreed action plans and timelines.

Within Manage relations with board of directors, this process is a critical mechanism for transparency and governance. It equips directors with independent assurance, trend analysis across audits, and confidence that management is remediating issues in a timely, risk-aligned manner. It also fulfills professional standards for internal auditing communications and monitoring.

## Key Activities
- Consolidate and validate audit evidence and observations from fieldwork.
- Analyze root causes and risk implications; assign risk ratings to findings.
- Draft clear, balanced audit reports using a standard findings framework.
- Review drafts through internal quality assurance and legal/compliance checks as needed.
- Conduct exit/debrief meetings with management; obtain formal responses and action plans.
- Finalize reports; disseminate to management and the Audit Committee.
- Prepare board-level materials (executive summaries, dashboards, themes, trends).
- Log findings and action plans in the issue tracking system; monitor remediation.
- Escalate accepted risks beyond appetite to the board when required.
- Maintain records and ensure alignment with audit methodology and professional standards.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs to begin this process:
  - Approved audit plan and completed fieldwork for the engagement.
  - Documented observations, test results, evidence, and workpapers.
  - Defined audit criteria (policies, procedures, laws/regulations, contracts, standards).
  - Risk assessment and rating methodology (impact/likelihood scales).
  - Stakeholder list and distribution matrix (management, Audit Committee, external auditor if applicable).

- Prerequisites that must be met:
  - Audit scope/objectives finalized; significant scoping changes documented.
  - Evidence sufficiency and appropriateness confirmed; workpapers reviewed.
  - Preliminary themes communicated to management to avoid surprises.
  - Independence and objectivity affirmed; conflicts addressed.
  - Legal/compliance review determined for sensitive issues (e.g., fraud, litigation).

- Dependencies on other processes:
  - Plan and execute internal audits (risk-based planning, fieldwork).
  - Manage issue tracking and remediation monitoring.
  - Manage board governance and reporting cadence (Audit Committee calendar).
  - Coordinate with external auditors/compliance (as relevant to SOX, regulatory exams).

## Process Steps
1. Prepare for reporting
   - Confirm fieldwork completion and internal review of workpapers.
   - Consolidate observations; group by theme/process/control to avoid duplication.
   - Map each observation to criteria (policy/standard/law), condition, cause, effect.

2. Analyze and rate findings
   - Perform root cause analysis (e.g., 5 Whys, fishbone, control design vs. execution).
   - Assess risk impact and likelihood; consider financial, operational, compliance, reputational impacts.
   - Classify deficiencies per applicable frameworks (e.g., SOX: control deficiency, significant deficiency, material weakness).
   - Prioritize findings (High/Medium/Low) and determine overall conclusion/opinion.

3. Draft the audit report
   - Include: executive summary; scope/objectives; methodology; summary of testing; detailed findings with 5 Cs (Criteria, Condition, Cause, Consequence/Effect, Corrective Action/Recommendation); ratings; management response templates; conclusion; appendices (process maps, data analytics results).
   - Use clear, non-accusatory language; quantify impacts and sample sizes where possible.
   - Align terminology to enterprise risk taxonomy and control library.

4. Internal quality review
   - Engagement Manager reviews for accuracy, sufficiency of evidence, and consistency with methodology.
   - Independent quality reviewer/CAE review for high-risk engagements.
   - Legal/compliance review for sensitive matters; apply privilege if directed by counsel.
   - Red-team for clarity and readability if needed.

5. Management validation and exit meeting
   - Share draft with responsible management; hold exit/debrief to validate facts, context, and feasibility of recommendations.
   - Negotiate management action plans that are SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound) with named owners and due dates.
   - Resolve disputes on ratings; document rationale for any disagreements.

6. Finalize report
   - Incorporate agreed changes; capture management responses verbatim or in standardized format.
   - Document any unresolved disagreements and auditor’s rationale.
   - Obtain CAE sign-off and confirm distribution list per protocol.

7. Disseminate results
   - Issue final report to management, relevant executives, and archived recipients.
   - Update the GRC/issue tracking system with findings, owners, and due dates.
   - Prepare Audit Committee materials: executive summary, issue heatmap, trend analyses, status of prior findings, and any accepted risks beyond appetite.

8. Board/Audit Committee reporting
   - Provide pre-read materials via the board portal; brief the Committee Chair.
   - Present key findings, themes, and overall control environment view; respond to questions.
   - Document board feedback, directives, and required follow-ups.

9. Monitor and escalate
   - Track remediation progress and validate closures (test of design/operating effectiveness).
   - Report aging of open issues and overdue action plans; escalate per governance thresholds.
   - If management accepts high risk beyond appetite, communicate to the board per policy.

10. Records management and continuous improvement
    - Retain reports and workpapers per retention schedule.
    - Capture lessons learned; update templates, rating criteria, and training based on feedback.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Expected outputs:
  - Final audit report per engagement.
  - Issue register entries with risk ratings, owners, and due dates.
  - Audit Committee/board reporting pack (executive summaries, dashboards, trends).
  - Management action plans and remediation timelines.
  - Follow-up reports on remediation status and closures.

- Deliverables produced:
  - Draft and final audit reports.
  - Exit meeting minutes and action plan tracker.
  - Board presentation deck and pre-read materials.
  - Risk acceptance memos (if applicable).
  - Updated enterprise risk/control insights for the annual audit plan.

- Success criteria:
  - Reports are timely, accurate, balanced, and actionable.
  - High agreement rate on facts and ratings with management; minimal post-issuance corrections.
  - Remediation of high/medium issues by due dates; reduction in repeat findings.
  - Positive Audit Committee feedback; no material surprises at board level.
  - Compliance with IIA Standards for communications and monitoring.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Chief Audit Executive (CAE)
  - Approves reports; ensures quality and alignment with standards.
  - Interfaces with the Audit Committee; escalates accepted risks beyond appetite.
- Audit Manager/Lead Auditor
  - Leads drafting, reviews evidence, facilitates exit meetings, and validates management responses.
- Internal Auditors/Team
  - Analyze data, document findings, perform root cause analysis, and draft sections.
- Process Owners/Management
  - Validate facts, provide responses and action plans, implement remediation.
- Legal/Compliance (as needed)
  - Review sensitive findings; advise on privilege, regulatory disclosures, and wording.
- External Auditor (informational/coordination)
  - Informed of SOX-significant deficiencies/material weaknesses; coordinate to reduce duplication.
- Audit Committee/Board of Directors
  - Receive and challenge results; oversee remediation and risk acceptance decisions.
- PMO/Issue Management Office (if established)
  - Track and report remediation progress; coordinate cross-functional fixes.

## Best Practices
- No surprises: communicate emerging issues to management during fieldwork.
- Use a standard findings framework (criteria/condition/cause/effect/recommendation) and rating scale.
- Quantify impacts and include data visualizations for clarity; avoid overly technical jargon.
- Focus on root causes and systemic themes; recommend pragmatic, risk-proportionate actions.
- Ensure independence and objectivity; avoid prescriptive solutions that design controls for management.
- Align findings to enterprise risk appetite, policies, and control frameworks (e.g., COSO).
- Calibrate ratings consistently through periodic norming sessions across audit teams.
- Obtain SMART management action plans with accountable owners and testable outcomes.
- Integrate with GRC tooling to streamline tracking and board reporting.
- Apply legal review for potential litigation, regulatory matters, or whistleblower cases.
- Conduct post-engagement lessons learned; continuously improve templates and guidance.
- Follow IIA Standards (notably 2400, 2410, 2420, 2440, 2500, 2600) and ISO 19011 guidance for audits.

## Common Challenges
- Management pushback on ratings or wording
  - Mitigation: early communication, transparent criteria, evidence-backed rationale, escalation paths.
- Insufficient or ambiguous evidence
  - Mitigation: enhance sampling/testing, seek corroboration, extend fieldwork, clarify criteria.
- Overly prescriptive recommendations
  - Mitigation: propose risk-aligned options; leave design decisions to management; focus on outcomes.
- Delayed management responses and action plans
  - Mitigation: set SLAs, send reminders, involve executives, tie to performance objectives.
- Inconsistent rating across audits
  - Mitigation: calibration sessions, central QA, reference exemplars, maintain a rating playbook.
- Sensitive findings (fraud, legal exposure)
  - Mitigation: involve Legal early, restrict distribution, consider privilege, coordinate with investigations.
- Repeat findings and remediation fatigue
  - Mitigation: analyze systemic causes, escalate to board, prioritize root-cause initiatives.

## Performance Metrics
- Timeliness
  - Cycle time from fieldwork end to draft report; draft to final issuance.
  - On-time delivery of Audit Committee materials vs. board calendar.
- Quality and effectiveness
  - Management agreement rate on findings and ratings.
  - Post-report corrections or retractions (target: zero).
  - Board/Audit Committee satisfaction scores.
- Impact
  - Percentage of high/medium issues remediated by due date.
  - Reduction in repeat findings and control exceptions over time.
  - Thematic risk reduction indicators (e.g., fewer incidents, loss events, or policy breaches).
- Efficiency
  - Auditor hours spent on reporting as a percent of total engagement hours.
  - Automation utilization (e.g., GRC workflows, analytics embedded in reports).
- Compliance
  - Adherence to IIA Standards checkpoints (communication, dissemination, monitoring).
  - Percentage of reports that include SMART action plans.

## Technology and Tools
- GRC/Audit management platforms: AuditBoard, TeamMate+, Galvanize/HighBond, RSA Archer, ServiceNow GRC, Workiva.
- Issue tracking and workflow: integrated GRC modules or enterprise tools (e.g., ServiceNow, JIRA) for action plans.
- Document and evidence management: SharePoint, Box, Confluence, secure repositories with version control.
- Data analytics and visualization: ACL/HighBond Analytics, IDEA, SQL/Python, Power BI, Tableau for impact quantification and dashboards.
- Board portals: Diligent, Boardvantage, Nasdaq Boardvantage for secure dissemination of materials.
- Communication and collaboration: MS Teams, Outlook, Zoom for exit meetings and reviews.
- eDiscovery/legal hold tools (as needed): for sensitive matters under counsel direction.
- Electronic signatures/approvals: DocuSign, Adobe Sign for management responses and sign-offs.

This process, executed consistently and transparently, strengthens governance, enables timely corrective action, and provides the board with reliable assurance on the state of the control environment.

Process Details:
## Overview
Create ethics policies is the structured process of defining, drafting, approving, publishing, and maintaining the organization’s Code of Ethics and related ethical conduct policies. Its purpose is to articulate the organization’s values, set clear behavioral expectations, reduce legal and reputational risk, and guide decision-making for employees, contractors, directors, suppliers, and other external partners. It is a cornerstone of the organization’s legal and ethical compliance framework and a key enabler of trust with stakeholders (investors, regulators, industry bodies, community, and the public).

This process delivers a coherent, accessible, and enforceable Code of Ethics aligned to applicable laws, industry standards, and the organization’s strategy and culture, and integrates with training, reporting channels, supplier requirements, and governance.

## Key Activities
- Establish governance and sponsorship for ethics policy development and maintenance.
- Conduct stakeholder and materiality analysis to identify topics that matter most to the organization and its stakeholders.
- Identify applicable legal/regulatory obligations and industry standards.
- Define policy scope, structure, and hierarchy (Code, topic-specific policies, procedures, guidelines).
- Draft the Code of Ethics and companion policies using clear, inclusive, plain language and real-life scenarios.
- Perform legal, risk, and operational reviews; incorporate feedback.
- Secure executive and Board (or designated committee) approval.
- Localize and translate as needed; address jurisdictional variances.
- Design, format, and publish the Code and policies across channels (intranet, external website, supplier portal).
- Implement training and acknowledgment/certification programs for employees and third parties.
- Communicate rollout and maintain a speak-up/reporting framework (hotline, non-retaliation commitments).
- Monitor effectiveness, collect metrics, manage exceptions, and update on a defined review cadence.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs to begin this process
  - Organizational values, mission, and culture statements.
  - Applicable laws and regulations (e.g., anti-bribery/anti-corruption, antitrust, conflicts of interest, data privacy, trade compliance, labor and human rights, environmental rules).
  - Industry standards and frameworks (e.g., OECD Guidelines, UN Global Compact, ISO 37301 Compliance Management, ISO 37001 Anti-Bribery, ILO Core Conventions).
  - Existing policies and procedures to harmonize or replace.
  - Risk assessments, audit findings, hotline/case trends, employee survey results.
  - Stakeholder inputs (employees, managers, Board, suppliers, investors, community).
  - Brand and communications guidelines.
  - Language and accessibility requirements.

- Prerequisites that must be met
  - Executive sponsor identified (e.g., CEO or Chief Ethics & Compliance Officer).
  - Policy governance model established (ownership, review, approval, maintenance).
  - Budget and resources allocated (legal, compliance, HR, communications, design, translation).
  - Approved policy template and style guide.
  - Case management and hotline/reporting mechanisms available or planned.

- Dependencies on other processes
  - [12.4] Manage legal and ethical issues (overall compliance framework).
  - Enterprise risk management and compliance obligation management.
  - Board governance/secretariat for approvals.
  - HR learning and development for training and acknowledgments.
  - Corporate communications and PR for internal and external communication.
  - Supplier/vendor management for third-party distribution and attestations.
  - Records and document management for version control and retention.
  - Investigations and discipline processes for enforcement (referenced, not created here).

## Process Steps
1. Initiate and Charter
   - Appoint executive sponsor and policy owner (e.g., Chief Compliance Officer).
   - Define objectives, scope, timeline, budget, and success criteria.
   - Form a cross-functional working group (Legal, HR, Procurement, Finance, Operations, IT/InfoSec, Internal Audit, ESG/CSR, Corporate Communications, regional reps).

2. Gather Requirements and Context
   - Compile applicable legal and regulatory obligations by jurisdiction.
   - Review existing policies, audits, investigation trends, and risk registers.
   - Conduct stakeholder interviews, focus groups, and surveys.
   - Perform a materiality assessment to prioritize topics (e.g., anti-bribery, conflicts, gifts/hospitality, privacy, cybersecurity, fair competition, human rights, workplace conduct, social media, political activities, financial integrity, environment and sustainability, sanctions/trade compliance).
   - Define audience segments (employees, contractors, directors, suppliers, agents) and channel requirements.

3. Define Policy Framework and Scope
   - Establish hierarchy: Code of Ethics (principles and expectations) + topic-specific policies + procedures + job aids/FAQs.
   - Determine global minimum standards and identify where local addenda are needed.
   - Define exceptions governance and approval thresholds.

4. Drafting
   - Draft Code content with clear principles, expected behaviors, do/don’t examples, decision frameworks, and scenario-based guidance.
   - Include commitments: compliance with law, non-retaliation, respect and inclusion, data protection, safe workplace, responsible sourcing, environmental stewardship, accurate records, fair dealing, avoiding conflicts, anti-bribery, competition law, use of company assets, communications and social media.
   - Define “speak-up” mechanisms and confidentiality protections.
   - Draft a Supplier Code of Conduct aligned to the Code and contractual clauses.
   - Ensure alignment with brand voice and accessibility guidelines.

5. Review and Risk/Legal Validation
   - Legal review for statutory alignment and legal risk.
   - Compliance review for control alignment and ISO/industry standards.
   - Operational review by functional owners for practicality.
   - Regional/local counsel review for jurisdictional adaptation.
   - Incorporate feedback, resolve conflicts, and record rationale.

6. Design, Usability, and Accessibility
   - Apply visual design for readability (headings, icons, summaries, hyperlinks).
   - Ensure accessibility (screen reader compatibility, color contrast, alt text).
   - Prepare translations/localizations and verify culturally appropriate examples.

7. Approval
   - Route final draft through executive leadership and Board or Audit/Compliance Committee as required by governance.
   - Record approvals and version details; update policy register.

8. Deployment and Communication
   - Publish on intranet, external website, and supplier portal.
   - Embed into onboarding and annual training curricula.
   - Launch communication plan (emails, town halls, manager toolkits, posters, videos, FAQs).
   - Configure acknowledgment/certification workflows for employees and targeted third parties.
   - Update contracts and purchase terms to reference the Supplier Code.

9. Training and Acknowledgment
   - Deliver role-based training (e.g., sales, procurement, execs, high-risk third parties).
   - Track completion and understanding (knowledge checks).
   - Capture acknowledgments and store records per retention policy.

10. Integration with Speak-Up and Case Management
    - Promote hotline and reporting channels; reiterate non-retaliation.
    - Ensure reports route to case management system with triage and investigation protocols defined elsewhere.

11. Monitoring and Continuous Improvement
    - Monitor adoption metrics, hotline awareness, and incident trends.
    - Collect user feedback; run pulse surveys.
    - Perform periodic audits for accessibility, relevance, and enforcement consistency.
    - Manage exceptions and maintain an exceptions log.

12. Maintenance and Review
    - Establish review cadence (at least annually or upon significant regulatory or organizational change).
    - Trigger out-of-cycle updates for new laws, acquisitions, or material incidents.
    - Version control, archive superseded versions, and communicate changes.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Code of Ethics document (global).
- Topic-specific policies and procedures.
- Supplier Code of Conduct and standard contractual clauses.
- Translations/localizations and accessibility-compliant formats.
- Communication materials (launch plan, FAQs, videos, slide decks).
- Training content and completion records.
- Acknowledgment/certification records for employees and relevant third parties.
- Policy map and cross-reference index to related documents.
- Policy register entry with version history and approvals.
- Exceptions log and rationale.
- Public-facing web page hosting the Code and reporting channels.

- Success criteria
  - Board/executive approval obtained; policy published and accessible.
  - ≥95% employee acknowledgment within defined timeframe.
  - ≥95% completion of required training within SLA.
  - Supplier acknowledgment for high-risk third parties meets target (e.g., ≥90%).
  - Positive comprehension scores on knowledge checks (e.g., ≥85% average).
  - Increased awareness of speak-up channels; adherence to non-retaliation.
  - Reduction or stabilization of relevant incidents relative to exposure.
  - Favorable audit outcomes; no major findings on policy accessibility or gaps.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Executive Sponsor (CEO or CECO)
  - Sets tone at the top; approves strategy; ensures resources; endorses communications.
- Policy Owner (Chief Ethics & Compliance Officer or General Counsel)
  - Owns content, governance, and maintenance; ensures legal alignment; reports to Board.
- Cross-Functional Working Group (Legal, HR, Procurement, Finance, Operations, IT/InfoSec, Internal Audit, ESG, Communications, regional leads)
  - Contributes content, reviews for practicality, ensures integration with operations.
- Board or Audit/Compliance Committee
  - Reviews and approves Code; oversees effectiveness.
- Corporate Communications/Brand
  - Ensures clarity, tone, and multi-channel communication; designs materials.
- HR and L&D
  - Integrates into onboarding and annual training; tracks completion; handles employee acknowledgments.
- Supplier/Vendor Management and Procurement
  - Communicates Supplier Code; embeds requirements into contracts; tracks attestations.
- Local/Regional Compliance Leads
  - Localize content; ensure regional deployment and training; monitor local compliance.
- IT/Systems Owners
  - Support policy management system, intranet, LMS, case management, and analytics.
- Records Management
  - Manages version control and retention.
- External Counsel/Advisors (as needed)
  - Provide specialized legal guidance, benchmarking, and cultural/translation review.
- People Managers
  - Cascade messages; reinforce expectations; address questions; model behavior.

## Best Practices
- Tone at the top: visible leadership endorsement and accountability.
- Plain language and inclusivity: avoid legal jargon; use examples and decision trees.
- Scenario-based guidance relevant to job roles and risk areas.
- One policy framework: clear hierarchy, naming conventions, and cross-references to avoid duplication.
- Global minimum standards with local addenda where stricter laws apply; never “opt down.”
- Strong speak-up culture: multiple reporting channels, non-retaliation reinforced and enforced.
- Accessibility and usability: mobile-friendly, searchable, translated, and accessible formats.
- Embed into lifecycle: onboarding, performance reviews, supplier onboarding, and contract clauses.
- Data-driven updates: use case trends, audits, and survey insights to refine content.
- Governance discipline: defined owners, review cadence, change control, and exception management.
- External transparency: publish the Code, supplier standards, and hotline information publicly.
- Training that is periodic, role-based, and risk-adjusted; micro-learning refreshers.
- Align with recognized standards (e.g., ISO 37301, ISO 37001) for maturity and auditability.

## Common Challenges
- Cultural misalignment or low engagement
  - Solution: co-create content with staff; use regional champions; include real examples and leadership stories.
- Overly legalistic or complex content
  - Solution: plain-language editing; UX design; layered content with summaries and links.
- Global vs. local conflicts
  - Solution: define global minima; maintain local addenda; obtain local legal review.
- Limited adoption and acknowledgment gaps
  - Solution: manager cascades, nudges, multi-channel reminders, integrate with HRIS and LMS.
- Translation and localization quality
  - Solution: professional translation, back-translation, local SME review, cultural QA.
- Supplier compliance and tracking
  - Solution: risk-based onboarding, contractual clauses, portal attestations, escalation for non-compliance.
- Stale content and drift from practice
  - Solution: annual reviews, change triggers, governance dashboards, and assigned owners.
- Measuring effectiveness beyond completion rates
  - Solution: add comprehension checks, hotline awareness surveys, behavioral KPIs, and audit testing.
- Fear of retaliation suppressing speak-up
  - Solution: reinforce non-retaliation, anonymous channels, swift and fair responses, publish aggregated outcomes.

## Performance Metrics
- Policy coverage and access
  - Percentage of workforce and targeted third parties with access to the Code.
  - Time to publish from initiation; page views and unique visitors; search analytics.
- Adoption and understanding
  - Acknowledgment rate and cycle time.
  - Training completion rates and average assessment scores.
  - Hotline awareness score from surveys.
- Behavioral and control indicators
  - Speak-up rate per 100 employees; case substantiation rates; time to close cases.
  - Incident trends in high-risk areas (e.g., gifts, conflicts, data protection).
  - Number and severity of exceptions granted.
- Quality and governance
  - Audit findings related to policy framework.
  - On-time completion of annual review/updates.
  - Translation/localization defect rate; accessibility compliance score.
- Third-party compliance
  - Supplier attestation rate in high-risk categories.
  - Number of contracts referencing Supplier Code and clauses.

## Technology and Tools
- Policy management/GRC platforms for authoring, approval workflows, version control, and distribution.
- Intranet/portal CMS for publishing and search.
- Learning Management System (LMS) for training delivery, tracking, and assessments.
- E-signature/acknowledgment systems integrated with HRIS and vendor management.
- Whistleblower hotline and case management systems with analytics and reporting.
- Translation management systems and localization QA tools.
- Document and records management for retention and audit trails.
- Accessibility checkers and readability tools.
- Survey and pulse-feedback tools to capture comprehension and culture indicators.
- Analytics/BI tools to monitor KPIs and drive continuous improvement.

Process Details:
# [12.4.2] Manage Corporate Governance Policies

## Overview
Manage Corporate Governance Policies defines, maintains, communicates, and enforces the system of rules, practices, and processes that direct and control the organization. It ensures the organization’s structure, decision-making, accountability, and disclosure are aligned with stakeholder interests (shareholders, management, employees, customers, suppliers, financiers, regulators, and the community), legal requirements, and strategic objectives. This process establishes the governance framework, board and committee charters, codes and policies, delegation of authority, internal control standards, performance and disclosure practices, and oversight mechanisms.

Purpose:
- Safeguard integrity, transparency, and ethical conduct.
- Ensure legal and regulatory compliance.
- Enable effective oversight of strategy, risk, performance, and culture.
- Promote stakeholder trust and sustainable value creation.

Role in the organization:
- Provides the foundation and “rules of the game” by which all other processes operate.
- Connects board oversight with management execution via clear policies, controls, and reporting.
- Integrates with risk management, internal control, compliance, legal, and disclosure processes.

## Key Activities
- Establish governance framework, principles, and “policy on policy” (policy lifecycle, ownership, approval).
- Develop and maintain board governance documents (board charter, committee charters).
- Define and maintain core corporate governance policies:
  - Code of conduct/ethics and conflict of interest management.
  - Anti-bribery and corruption; gifts, hospitality, and third-party due diligence.
  - Insider trading and securities dealing.
  - Whistleblowing and non-retaliation.
  - Related-party transactions and approvals.
  - Delegation of authority (DOA) and decision rights.
  - Information disclosure, investor communications, and continuous disclosure.
  - Risk management and internal control framework (e.g., COSO).
  - Data privacy, information security governance, and record retention.
  - ESG/sustainability governance and reporting oversight.
- Regulatory horizon scanning and benchmarking to applicable codes/standards (e.g., OECD Principles, SOX, UK/ASX/NYSE/Nasdaq codes).
- Policy drafting, legal review, and board/committee approval.
- Policy dissemination, training, certifications/attestations, and accessibility.
- Embedding policies into processes and systems (workflows, controls, segregation of duties).
- Monitoring, assurance, and reporting (KPIs, incidents, audit findings).
- Exception/waiver management and remediation.
- Governance disclosures (annual report, website) and stakeholder engagement.
- Periodic evaluation and refresh (annual cycle and ad hoc updates).

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Corporate strategy, values, and risk appetite.
- Applicable laws, regulations, listing rules, and governance codes.
- Current policies, charters, DOA, and internal control documentation.
- Audit findings, risk assessments, incident/whistleblower reports, and past exceptions.
- Stakeholder feedback (investors, regulators, employees).
- Board directives and committee recommendations.
- Benchmarking and industry best practices.

Prerequisites:
- Established governance structure (board, committees, corporate secretary function).
- Named policy owners and custodians; approved “policy on policy.”
- Defined risk and control framework; authority matrix; policy repository.
- Budgeted resources for legal, compliance, training, and GRC tools.

Dependencies on other processes:
- Risk Management and Internal Controls (define/control environment).
- Legal and Regulatory Compliance (interpretation, monitoring).
- Ethics and Integrity Management (code of conduct, speak-up).
- Enterprise Strategy and Performance Management (alignment, KPIs).
- HR and Talent (training, disciplinary processes, executive compensation).
- Investor Relations and External Reporting (disclosures).
- IT and Information Security Governance (access controls, data protection).
- Internal Audit and Assurance (independent testing).
- Records and Information Management (retention, e-discovery).
- Third-Party Risk Management (ABAC, due diligence).

## Process Steps
1. Initiate annual governance cycle and plan
   - Corporate Secretary/Compliance create a governance calendar (policy reviews, committee meetings, disclosure deadlines).
   - Confirm policy inventory, owners, and review cadences.

2. Regulatory horizon scanning and benchmarking
   - Legal/Compliance analyze new/changed laws, listing rules, and governance codes.
   - Benchmark governance practices against peers and standards; identify gaps.

3. Define scope and priorities
   - Risk, Legal, and Compliance map regulatory/gap findings to impacted policies and processes.
   - Board/Nomination & Governance Committee (NGC) endorses priorities and timelines.

4. Draft or revise governance documents
   - Policy owners draft updates (policies, charters, DOA, governance manual) using templates.
   - Incorporate risk appetite, control requirements (e.g., COSO principles), and operational feasibility.

5. Cross-functional review and validation
   - Circulate drafts to Legal, Compliance, Risk, HR, Finance, IT, Internal Audit for comment.
   - Conduct impact assessments (process, system, training, change management).
   - Resolve comments and document rationale for key decisions.

6. Committee review
   - NGC reviews governance policies and board charters.
   - Audit & Risk Committee reviews risk, internal control, whistleblowing; Finance-related governance.
   - Remuneration/Compensation Committee reviews executive pay and related governance.
   - Record minutes and recommendations.

7. Board approval
   - Corporate Secretary schedules board agenda, provides materials.
   - Board deliberates and approves; document decisions and effective dates.

8. Implementation planning
   - Define implementation tasks: system changes, control updates, form changes, training content.
   - Assign owners, timelines; update DOA in ERP and workflow systems.
   - Prepare communications plan and FAQs.

9. Communication and rollout
   - Publish policies in the repository/portal; ensure version control and accessibility.
   - Announce via email, town halls; highlight key changes and effective dates.
   - Notify external stakeholders where relevant (website disclosures, investor FAQ).

10. Training and attestation
    - HR/Compliance deploy mandatory training by role and risk.
    - Capture attestations for Code of Conduct, insider trading, conflicts, etc.
    - Track completion; escalate non-compliance.

11. Embed controls and procedures
    - Update process documentation and control matrices.
    - Configure systems for DOA, segregation of duties, pre-clearance for trading, gift registers.
    - Establish related-party and conflict-of-interest registers and workflows.

12. Monitor and enforce
    - Ongoing surveillance (insider trading, gifts, related-party transactions).
    - Operate speak-up channels; investigate allegations; enforce consequences.
    - Internal Audit/Second line perform testing; track and remediate findings.

13. Report and disclose
    - Management reports KPIs, incidents, policy exceptions, training status to committees/board.
    - Prepare governance statement in annual report; website updates; listing disclosures.

14. Manage exceptions and waivers
    - Formal process to request, approve (usually board or committee for senior roles), and log waivers.
    - Time-bound, with compensating controls and post-implementation review.

15. Evaluate effectiveness and improve
    - Conduct annual board and committee self-assessments (and periodic external evaluations).
    - Review policy performance vs. metrics; refresh content.
    - Incorporate lessons learned from incidents, audits, and stakeholder feedback.

16. Documentation and retention
    - Archive versions, approvals, minutes, training records, attestations, and registers per retention schedule.

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs:
- Approved board and committee charters; governance manual.
- Corporate governance policies and procedures (current, version-controlled).
- Delegation of authority matrix implemented in systems.
- Training modules and completion/attestation records.
- Registers: conflicts of interest, related-party transactions, gifts/hospitality, waivers.
- Monitoring and assurance reports; audit reports and remediation logs.
- Governance disclosures (annual report section, website).
- Board/committee agendas, papers, and minutes.

Deliverables produced:
- Governance calendar and policy review plan.
- Policy impact assessments and implementation plans.
- Communication artifacts (FAQs, summaries).
- Investigation reports and disciplinary outcomes when applicable.

Success criteria:
- Zero material governance non-compliance or late disclosures.
- Board/committee approvals on time; positive board evaluation outcomes.
- Training completion rate meets targets (e.g., >98%) with satisfactory assessment scores.
- Timely remediation of audit issues (e.g., 90% within agreed due dates).
- Reduced/controlled number and severity of governance incidents.
- Positive stakeholder indicators (say-on-pay support, proxy advisor ratings, regulator feedback).

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Board of Directors
  - Approves governance framework, charters, and major policies; oversees effectiveness.
- Board Chair
  - Ensures effective board functioning and agenda-setting; drives tone at the top.
- Nomination & Governance Committee (NGC)
  - Oversees governance policies, board composition, succession, evaluations.
- Audit & Risk Committee
  - Oversees risk, internal control, whistleblowing, financial reporting governance.
- Remuneration/Compensation Committee
  - Oversees executive pay, incentives alignment, related governance policies.
- CEO and Executive Management
  - Ensure implementation and adherence; allocate resources; reinforce culture.
- General Counsel/Chief Compliance Officer
  - Owns legal interpretation, policy drafting standards, investigations, compliance monitoring.
- Corporate Secretary
  - Manages governance calendar, board/committee processes, documentation, disclosures.
- Chief Risk Officer
  - Aligns policies with risk appetite and ERM; advises on control implications.
- Internal Audit
  - Independently assesses adherence and control effectiveness; reports to Audit Committee.
- HR
  - Integrates governance into performance management, disciplinary procedures, and training.
- Finance/Controller
  - Implements financial governance controls, related-party monitoring, disclosures.
- IT/Information Security
  - Enforces technical controls, access management, data governance.
- Investor Relations
  - Coordinates governance disclosures and investor engagement.
- External Counsel/Auditors (as needed)
  - Provide independent advice, assurance, and benchmarking.

## Best Practices
- Establish a clear governance framework aligned to recognized codes (e.g., OECD, local corporate governance codes) and the COSO internal control framework.
- Maintain independence and competence on the board; separate Chair and CEO roles or implement robust lead independent director arrangements.
- Use a “policy on policy” with lifecycle controls: ownership, drafting standards, versioning, approval thresholds, review cadence, archival.
- Keep policies principle-based with practical procedures and role-based checklists; avoid excessive complexity.
- Link DOA to system-enforced controls; periodically test and certify DOA accuracy.
- Implement strong whistleblower protections with multiple anonymous channels and independent oversight.
- Require annual conflicts of interest declarations and event-driven updates; maintain searchable registers.
- Conduct annual board and committee evaluations; periodic external board effectiveness reviews.
- Integrate ESG governance (materiality assessment, data controls, assurance) into the governance framework.
- Use technology (GRC and board portals) as a single source of truth for policies, issues, audits, and disclosures.
- Align executive compensation with long-term value creation; disclose pay practices transparently.
- Perform regular regulatory horizon scanning; document rationale for policy positions.
- Provide targeted, role-based training with assessments; reinforce via leadership messaging.
- Implement a robust subsidiary governance model (entity management, local compliance mapping).
- Ensure crisis management and disclosure controls integrate with governance policies.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Regulatory complexity and change
  - Solution: Dedicated horizon scanning, external counsel alerts, mapped obligations register; agile update procedures.
- Global consistency vs. local requirements
  - Solution: Global minimum standards with local addenda; localization governance and translation management.
- Policy proliferation and ambiguity
  - Solution: Rationalize policy library; adopt a taxonomy; consolidate overlapping documents; enforce templates.
- Cultural resistance and low adoption
  - Solution: Tone at the top, change champions, practical guidance, scenario-based training.
- Weak enforcement and accountability
  - Solution: Clear consequences matrix, escalation paths, performance metrics tied to compliance.
- Data quality and fragmented tooling
  - Solution: Central GRC platform integration; single policy repository; data governance and ownership.
- Board capacity and information overload
  - Solution: Concise board papers, dashboards, early committee deep-dives, annual calendar discipline.
- Third-party risk and ABAC compliance
  - Solution: Risk-based due diligence, contract clauses, gift/hospitality pre-approvals, monitoring.
- Insider trading and disclosure breaches
  - Solution: Pre-clearance, blackout periods, surveillance tooling, real-time disclosure controls.
- Inadequate documentation and retention
  - Solution: Records policy, automated retention schedules, board portal archives.

## Performance Metrics (KPIs)
- Policy governance
  - Percentage of policies reviewed/approved on schedule.
  - Average policy age vs. target review cadence.
  - Number of policy waivers; percentage with compensating controls and timely expiry.
- Training and awareness
  - Completion rate and assessment scores for mandatory governance trainings.
  - Time to complete training post-release; overdue rate.
- Compliance and incidents
  - Number and severity of governance-related incidents (ABAC, insider trading, conflicts).
  - Time to investigate and close cases; substantiation and recurrence rates.
  - Whistleblower intake volume and time to triage; retaliation incidents (target: zero).
- Controls and assurance
  - Control effectiveness rate (testing results); % of critical audit findings remediated on time.
  - DOA exceptions or overrides; SOD violation rate.
- Board effectiveness and disclosures
  - Board and committee attendance; timeliness of materials; completion of annual evaluations.
  - On-time regulatory and listing disclosures; restatements due to governance failures (target: zero).
  - Say-on-pay support percentage; proxy advisor governance scores; ESG governance rating.
- Stakeholder trust
  - Shareholder engagement metrics; number of engagement meetings; key concerns resolved.
  - Employee ethics survey scores; speak-up culture index.

## Technology and Tools
- Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platforms: Diligent One, ServiceNow GRC, RSA Archer, MetricStream, OneTrust.
- Board portals and entity management: Diligent Boards/Entities, Nasdaq Boardvantage, BoardEffect.
- Policy management: NAVEX PolicyTech, ConvergePoint, PowerDMS, SharePoint with governance add-ons.
- Disclosure and reporting: Workiva, Certent, Broadridge; website CMS for governance pages.
- Learning Management Systems (LMS): SAP SuccessFactors, Cornerstone OnDemand, SAI360.
- Whistleblowing and investigations: NAVEX EthicsPoint, Whispli, Convercent, case management tools.
- Audit and controls: AuditBoard, TeamMate+, Galvanize/HighBond.
- Insider trading surveillance and equity plan management: NASDAQ BWise, Global Shares, Carta.
- Contract and third-party governance: Icertis CLM, Coupa, ProcessUnity, Aravo.
- Identity and access management/SOD control: SailPoint, SAP GRC, Oracle Risk Management Cloud.
- Regulatory intelligence: Thomson Reuters Regulatory Intelligence, LexisNexis, Diligent Compliance.
