## Outputs and Deliverables
- Program charter, governance model, and policies (selection, participation, incentives).
- Competency model and success profiles by level.
- Selection criteria, tools, and calibrated cohort lists.
- Assessment reports, 360 summaries, and IDPs.
- Learning journey artifacts: curriculum, schedules, project briefs, rotation agreements.
- Contracts with vendors/coaches; configured systems and dashboards.
- Communications, manager/mentor toolkits, resource libraries.
- Recognition records and compensation actions (spot awards, retention grants, differentiated increases).
- Reports: progress dashboards, diversity and equity analyses, impact/ROI reports.
Success criteria:
- Bench strength and time-to-ready improvements for critical roles.
- Higher internal fill rate and promotion velocity for participants vs. controls.
- Increased retention of high performers/high potentials.
- Positive participant/manager NPS and completion rates.
- Diverse representation in cohorts and successor slates.
- Measurable business impact from action learning projects.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- CHRO/Head of Talent: Sponsor; approve strategy, budget, and policies; chair steering committee.
- Talent Management CoE: Design program; own selection methodology, curriculum, and governance; manage evaluation and continuous improvement.
- Learning & Development: Build and deliver learning content; curate LXP pathways; manage vendors/coaches.
- Compensation/Rewards: Align incentives; ensure pay equity, market competitiveness, and compliance; execute compensation actions.
- HR Business Partners: Facilitate nominations and calibrations; coach managers; monitor participant progress; ensure local adoption.
- Business Leaders/Sponsors: Provide strategic projects; sponsor cohorts; champion participation and recognition.
- People Managers: Nominate participants; support IDPs; provide stretch assignments and feedback; protect time for development.
- DEI Officer: Embed equity safeguards; monitor representation; advise on accessibility and inclusivity.
- Finance: Validate budgets; track program spend and ROI assumptions.
- Legal/Compliance: Review policies, data privacy, labor law, and incentive compliance.
- Participants: Engage fully; complete IDPs; deliver on development experiences and project outcomes.
- External Partners (assessment, coaching, content): Deliver services to defined SLAs; provide consolidated reporting.

## Best Practices
- Align to strategy: Tie programs to critical roles, future skills, and transformation objectives.
- Distinguish performance vs. potential: Use clear definitions; not all high performers are high potentials.
- Use multi-method assessment: Combine manager input, calibrated 9-box, 360 feedback, and validated tools to reduce bias.
- Transparent eligibility and process: Publish criteria and timelines; train managers on equitable nominations.
- 70-20-10 learning design: Prioritize real business experiences and sponsorship over classroom-only training.
- Integrate incentives thoughtfully: Balance monetary and non-monetary recognition; avoid perverse incentives tied solely to program completion.
- Ensure DEI and fairness: Set representation goals; run adverse impact analyses; provide access and accommodations.
- Manager enablement: Equip managers with toolkits and expectations; hold them accountable for development support.
- Governance and data discipline: Standardize calibration; protect data privacy; audit incentives and outcomes.
- Pilot and iterate: Start with a pilot; collect feedback; scale with evidence.
- Mobility and visibility: Use internal talent marketplaces; formalize rotations; create alumni networks.
- Measure what matters: Focus on pipeline health and business impact, not just activity metrics.
- Global/local balance: Establish global standards and allow local adaptation to context and law.

## Common Challenges
- Bias in selection leading to inequitable cohorts
  - Solutions: Structured criteria, blind nomination review where possible, calibration sessions, adverse impact analysis.
- Manager “talent hoarding” or weak support
  - Solutions: Senior leadership expectations, manager KPIs tied to talent development, backfill planning for rotations.
- Program perceived as elitist
  - Solutions: Clear, transparent criteria; broader development pathways for all employees; communicate benefits across the organization.
- Limited capacity for stretch assignments and rotations
  - Solutions: Executive-sponsored portfolio of projects; capacity planning; project marketplace tools.
- Inconsistent application across regions/functions
  - Solutions: Global standards, local champions, playbooks, and governance checkpoints.
- Insufficient integration with rewards
  - Solutions: Predefined incentive matrix; sync with compensation cycle; communicate recognition moments.
- Participant burnout or disengagement
  - Solutions: Workload balancing agreements; manager training; opt-in with clear expectations; well-being support.
- Attrition after program completion (unmet expectations)
  - Solutions: Career path transparency; proactive placement into roles; retention incentives aligned with milestones.
- Budget cuts/ROI scrutiny
  - Solutions: Tie projects to strategic value; track impact; create scalable options (e.g., internal coaches, blended learning).

## Performance Metrics
Pipeline and progression:
- Internal fill rate for leadership/critical roles
- Time-to-ready for successors; bench strength coverage (1+ ready now/ready soon per critical role)
- Promotion velocity and role progression rates of participants vs. non-participants

Retention and engagement:
- Retention of high performers/high potentials vs. baseline
- Participant and manager NPS; engagement score changes pre/post

Diversity and equity:
- Representation of underrepresented groups in cohorts and successor slates
- Adverse impact ratio on selection and advancement
- Pay equity outcomes for incentives granted

Program execution and learning:
- Cohort completion rate; IDP completion rate
- Participation in experiential learning (rotations, projects, mentoring)
- Skill/competency gains measured via assessments or 360 deltas

Business impact and efficiency:
- Value delivered by action learning projects (e.g., cost savings, revenue uplift)
- Time-to-fill reductions for leadership roles
- Program cost per participant; ROI vs. baseline

Governance and compliance:
- Calibration adherence; audit findings; data privacy incidents (target: zero)
- Incentive policy adherence rate

## Technology and Tools
- HRIS and Talent Suites: Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM for profiles, performance data, succession, calibration.
- LMS/LXP: Cornerstone, Degreed, EdCast for learning delivery and curation.
- Assessment and 360 Platforms: SHL, Hogan, Korn Ferry, PSI, CultureAmp/Qualtrics for 360s and surveys.
- Coaching and Mentoring: BetterUp, Torch, CoachHub; mentoring platforms like Chronus or MentorcliQ.
- Internal Talent Marketplace/Project Platforms: Gloat, Fuel50, Eightfold to source stretch assignments and rotations.
- Recognition and Rewards: Workhuman, Bonusly, Achievers integrated with HRIS/Payroll for incentives.
- Analytics and Dashboards: Power BI, Tableau, Visier for pipeline and impact metrics.
- Collaboration and Communication: Teams, Slack, SharePoint for communities, resources, and updates.
- Compliance and Pay Equity: Syndio, PayAnalytics; documentation in Confluence/SharePoint.
- Workflow/Automation: ServiceNow, Jira, HR case management for approvals and tracking.

Process Details:
## Overview
Developing a Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) plan is a structured process to assess, define, and execute an organization’s strategy to build a diverse workforce, equitable systems, and an inclusive culture. It aligns people practices with business objectives, strengthens the employer brand, mitigates legal and reputational risk, and drives performance through broader perspectives and engagement.

This process creates a multi-year DEI strategy and annual plan that:
- Sets a clear DEI vision, principles, and goals aligned to business strategy.
- Integrates DEI across the employee lifecycle (attraction, hiring, development, rewards, retention, and exit).
- Establishes governance, policies, measurement, and accountability.
- Ensures compliance with applicable anti-discrimination, equal opportunity, accessibility, and data privacy laws.
- Embeds continuous improvement through data-driven insights and employee voice.

It sits within workforce strategy and policy development and informs related processes such as talent acquisition, learning and development, compensation and benefits, performance management, employee relations, and workplace experience.

## Key Activities
- Establish governance, sponsorship, and a DEI council.
- Conduct a baseline assessment (representation, pay equity, hiring and promotion flows, sentiment, accessibility, policy gap analysis).
- Define DEI vision, guiding principles, and strategic pillars.
- Set SMART goals and select KPIs; define measurement and reporting cadence.
- Identify, prioritize, and resource DEI initiatives across the employee lifecycle.
- Update or create policies (e.g., non-discrimination, accommodations, flexible work, inclusive benefits).
- Design inclusive hiring and advancement practices (structured interviews, debiased job descriptions, calibrated promotion processes).
- Develop enablement (training, toolkits, interview guides, communication assets).
- Implement change management and communications plan.
- Monitor, report, and refine through continuous improvement and annual refresh.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs
- Workforce data: headcount, hires, promotions, exits, performance, compensation, employee location and job levels.
- Voluntary self-identification data where legally permissible; clear consent and privacy notices.
- Employee listening insights: engagement/inclusion surveys, focus groups, exit interviews.
- Current HR policies, processes, and tools inventory.
- External benchmarks (industry representation, pay, recruiting metrics).
- Legal and compliance requirements by jurisdiction (EEO, anti-discrimination, accessibility, data privacy).

Prerequisites
- Executive sponsorship (CEO/CHRO) and governance structure (DEI council/steering committee).
- People analytics capabilities and data governance (privacy-by-design, de-identification).
- Budget and resource plan (DEI program lead, project management, analytics support).
- Agreement on scope, timelines, and success criteria.

Dependencies on other processes
- Workforce analytics and planning (to understand supply/demand and representation targets).
- Talent acquisition process design (to implement inclusive sourcing and assessment).
- Compensation and benefits design (for pay equity and inclusive benefits).
- Learning and development (for inclusive leadership and bias mitigation training).
- Performance and succession management (equitable calibration and promotion processes).
- Employee relations and ethics (incident reporting, investigations, anti-harassment).
- IT/workplace services (accessibility and assistive technologies).
- Risk, compliance, and legal review.

## Process Steps
1. Initiate and charter
   - Identify executive sponsor and appoint a DEI leader.
   - Draft a charter with vision, scope, guardrails, and decision rights.
   - Form the DEI council with cross-functional, diverse representation.
   - Establish a project plan, timeline, and budget.

2. Legal, risk, and privacy alignment
   - Map relevant laws by jurisdiction (e.g., Title VII, ADA/ADAAA, ADEA, EEOC/OFCCP, Equal Pay, UK Equality Act, EU Equality directives, Accessibility laws, GDPR/CCPA/PIPEDA, local data sovereignty).
   - Perform a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) for DEI data.
   - Define lawful bases for collecting and processing sensitive data; implement consent and access controls.

3. Baseline and diagnose
   - Data audit: inventory datasets, assess quality, completeness, and accessibility.
   - Representation analysis: by level, function, location, job family vs internal availability/external labor market.
   - Talent flow analysis: sourcing, screening, interview, offer, promotion, performance ratings, retention by demographic (where lawful).
   - Pay equity analysis: controlled (like-for-like) and uncontrolled gaps; root-cause analysis.
   - Inclusion and culture: survey inclusion index, psychological safety, fairness, belonging; qualitative input via focus groups.
   - Policy/practice gap analysis: recruitment, onboarding, development, performance, flexible work, accommodations, grievance handling.
   - Accessibility audit: digital tools, facilities, events, documents, and meetings.

4. Stakeholder engagement and voice
   - Identify stakeholders (employees, managers, ERG leaders, unions/works councils, legal, HR COEs, IT, facilities, procurement).
   - Conduct listening sessions with confidentiality safeguards; include intersectional perspectives and remote/hybrid workers.
   - Establish feedback channels and escalation paths.

5. Define DEI vision, principles, and strategic pillars
   - Draft a concise vision statement and 4–6 guiding principles (e.g., evidence-based, inclusive by design, privacy-first, global + local).
   - Select strategic pillars (e.g., inclusive hiring, equitable growth, pay and benefits equity, inclusive leadership, accessibility, culture and community).

6. Set goals, OKRs, and KPIs
   - Create SMART goals per pillar; use baselines and realistic trajectories.
   - Define metrics, data sources, owners, and review cadence.
   - Establish compliance reporting requirements and internal dashboards.
   - Avoid unlawful quotas; instead use lawful goals and process measures.

7. Design initiative portfolio
   - Ideate and prioritize initiatives with impact-effort analysis.
   - Examples: debiased job descriptions, structured interviews, diverse slates/panels where legal; outreach partnerships; apprenticeship/returnships; mentorship/sponsorship programs; equitable promotion calibration; manager enablement; inclusive benefits (e.g., caregiving, mental health); accommodations program enhancements; ERG framework; accessibility remediation plan; pay equity remediation policy.
   - Create initiative charters: objectives, scope, owner, budget, success measures, timelines, dependencies, risks.

8. Policy and process updates
   - Update or create: non-discrimination/anti-harassment, equal opportunity, accommodations and leave, flexible/hybrid work, caregiver support, transition at work, religious accommodations, vendor/supplier diversity standards, inclusive events.
   - Embed inclusive practices into core processes (job posting templates, structured scorecards, calibration rubrics, succession criteria).

9. Resource, enable, and procure
   - Secure budget and staff; define DEI program management roles.
   - Procure tools (survey, analytics, pay equity, JD debiasing, accessibility) following privacy and security reviews.
   - Build training curricula (inclusive leadership, interviewer certification, bystander intervention, microaggressions, accessibility awareness).

10. Change management and communications
    - Develop a narrative linking DEI to strategy and values.
    - Plan communications by audience (executives, managers, employees, candidates, external).
    - Identify change champions; schedule training; integrate into onboarding.
    - Provide toolkits and office hours for managers.

11. Implement and pilot
    - Launch quick wins and pilots; monitor adoption and outcomes.
    - Capture lessons learned; iterate and prepare for scale.

12. Scale, embed, and govern
    - Roll out initiatives enterprise-wide; incorporate into manager goals and performance reviews.
    - Stand up governance routines: quarterly DEI council reviews, risk/issue logs, policy attestation cycles.
    - Align with business planning and budget cycles.

13. Measure, report, and improve
    - Maintain dashboards; publish internal updates; meet regulatory reporting obligations.
    - Conduct annual re-baseline and plan refresh; adjust goals and investments.
    - Commission external audits or third-party reviews as appropriate.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- DEI strategy document (vision, principles, pillars) and multi-year roadmap.
- Annual DEI operating plan with goals, KPIs, initiatives, owners, and budget.
- DEI governance charter and council cadence.
- Policy updates and new policies (anti-discrimination, accommodations, flexible work, inclusive benefits, supplier diversity standards).
- Inclusive hiring toolkit (JD guidelines, structured interview guides, scorecards, panel guidance).
- Training curricula and learning paths; manager toolkits.
- Pay equity analysis report and remediation plan.
- Accessibility audit report and remediation plan.
- ERG framework and playbook (charters, funding, governance).
- Communication plan and assets (internal/external).
- Data management and privacy documentation (DPIA, consent notices, access controls).
- Dashboards and reporting packs (internal leadership, regulatory reporting, optional external transparency reports).

Success criteria
- Leadership and managerial adoption of inclusive practices.
- Measurable progress against KPIs within lawful boundaries.
- Positive movement in inclusion index and employee experience.
- Closed or narrowed pay equity gaps per remediation plans.
- Compliance with relevant laws and timely reporting.
- Sustained governance and continuous improvement cadence.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Executive Sponsor (CEO/CHRO): Sets tone, approves strategy and budget, holds executives accountable.
- Head of DEI/DEI Program Lead: Owns strategy, roadmap, governance, and outcomes; orchestrates cross-functional execution.
- DEI Council/Steering Committee: Provides guidance, removes blockers, prioritizes initiatives, monitors progress.
- HR Business Partners: Embed DEI in business unit people plans; coach managers; track adoption.
- Talent Acquisition Leader: Implements inclusive sourcing/assessment; monitors funnel metrics.
- Compensation and Benefits Lead: Conducts pay equity analyses; designs equitable rewards and benefits.
- Learning and Development Lead: Curates and delivers DEI capability-building; certifies interviewers.
- People Analytics Lead: Ensures data quality; builds DEI dashboards; conducts advanced analyses.
- Legal/Compliance: Reviews policies and practices; ensures legal compliance; oversees privacy, DPIAs, and reporting.
- Employee Relations/HR Operations: Manages incidents and grievances; ensures fair investigations; tracks case metrics.
- Accessibility/Workplace/IT: Delivers accessible tools, spaces, and accommodations.
- Communications/Brand: Crafts internal/external messaging; supports employer brand.
- Procurement/Supplier Diversity: Integrates DEI standards into vendor management.
- Finance: Oversees budgeting and ROI tracking for DEI initiatives.
- ERG Leaders: Provide community insights; partner on programs and events.
- People Managers: Model inclusive behaviors; apply equitable processes; support team development.
- All Employees: Engage respectfully, complete required training, offer feedback.

## Best Practices
- Secure visible, sustained leadership commitment; integrate DEI into business and talent strategies, not as a standalone program.
- Use evidence-based interventions and test for impact; avoid one-off training without systems and process changes.
- Build privacy-first analytics with explicit consent, minimal necessary data, and robust governance.
- Apply an intersectional lens to address overlapping identities and experiences.
- Localize plan for regional legal and cultural contexts while maintaining global principles.
- Focus on behavior and system design (structured interviews, transparent criteria) to reduce bias.
- Set clear, lawful goals with transparent measurement and reporting; avoid quotas or unlawful preferences.
- Tie manager objectives and rewards to inclusive leadership and team outcomes.
- Co-design with employees and ERGs; maintain continuous listening loops.
- Invest in accessibility from the start (digital, physical, communications).
- Pilot, learn, and iterate before scaling; publish lessons learned.
- Ensure sustainability: assign owners, fund initiatives, and embed in annual planning.

## Common Challenges
- Data limitations and privacy constraints: Mitigate via opt-in self-ID, de-identification, aggregation thresholds, and legal guidance.
- Perception of quotas or unfairness: Communicate lawful goals focused on equitable processes and opportunity; educate on the business case and legal framework.
- Managerial inconsistency or resistance: Provide practical toolkits, coaching, and incentives; use change champions and leadership modeling.
- Tokenism or program fatigue: Shift from events to systemic changes; measure impact; sunset low-impact activities.
- Global variability in laws and norms: Maintain a global framework with local adaptations; partner with regional HR and legal.
- Measuring inclusion: Use multi-method approaches (surveys, listening sessions, behavioral data) and triangulate findings.
- Limited resources: Prioritize high-impact, low-effort wins; leverage technology; partner with external organizations.
- Accessibility gaps: Conduct formal audits; prioritize remediation; embed accessibility checks in development and procurement lifecycles.

## Performance Metrics
Representation and flow
- Representation by level, function, and geography relative to internal availability and external labor market data.
- Hiring funnel diversity at each stage; offer acceptance rates.
- Promotion and lateral movement rates; time-in-level by demographic where lawful.
- Retention/turnover, regretted loss, and new-hire 12-month retention.

Equity and reward
- Pay equity gaps (controlled/uncontrolled), remediation status, and governance adherence.
- Performance rating distribution and bonus/equity outcomes by comparable roles.

Inclusion and experience
- Inclusion index (belonging, fairness, voice, psychological safety).
- ERG participation and satisfaction; mentorship/sponsorship participation.
- Accommodation request volume, cycle time, and satisfaction; accessibility issue closure times.

Process adoption
- Percentage of roles using structured interviews and calibrated scorecards.
- JD debiasing coverage; compliance with diverse slate/panel policies where legal.
- Manager completion rates for inclusive leadership/interviewer training and demonstrated behavior change.

Risk and compliance
- Timely completion of regulatory reports; audit findings and remediation closure.
- Employee relations case volume by type and time to resolution.

Program health
- Initiative completion rate vs plan; budget utilization; cadence adherence to governance reviews.

## Technology and Tools
- HRIS/HCM (e.g., Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM) for core people data and workflows.
- ATS (e.g., Greenhouse, Lever, SmartRecruiters) with structured interviews, candidate anonymization options, and pipeline reporting.
- People analytics and BI (e.g., Visier, Tableau, Power BI, Looker) for dashboards and advanced analysis.
- Pay equity analytics (e.g., Syndio, PayAnalytics) for rigorous compensation analyses and remediation tracking.
- Survey and listening platforms (e.g., Qualtrics, Culture Amp, Glint) for inclusion indices, pulse checks, and lifecycle feedback.
- JD optimization/debiasing (e.g., Textio, Gender Decoder) to improve job postings.
- Learning platforms (e.g., LMS, LXP) for scalable DEI curricula and certifications.
- ERG and community management (e.g., Teleskope, Workrowd) for governance and engagement analytics.
- Case management/HR service delivery (e.g., ServiceNow HRSD) for accommodations and ER case tracking.
- Accessibility tools and services (e.g., WAVE, Axe, Microsoft Accessibility Checker; captioning and ASL services).
- Policy management and attestation systems for distribution and tracking.
- Data privacy and security tools (DLP, consent management, data masking/anonymization).
- Regulatory reporting and compliance tools (e.g., EEO/OFCCP reporting in the US), tailored per jurisdiction.
- Communications and collaboration tools (e.g., intranet, email automation, webinars) for change management.

## Overview
Implement diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) plan is the end-to-end execution of an organization’s DEI strategy and roadmap. It operationalizes commitments into concrete practices, programs, and governance that foster fair access to opportunities, equitable outcomes, a sense of belonging, and a respectful, safe workplace. The process integrates DEI into the employee lifecycle (attraction, hiring, development, performance, promotion, compensation, retention, and exit), workplace policies and culture, leadership behaviors, and supporting infrastructure (systems, facilities, communications, procurement).

Purpose:
- Translate DEI strategy into measurable actions and results.
- Mitigate legal, ethical, and reputational risk related to discrimination, harassment, pay inequity, and inequitable access/opportunity.
- Improve business outcomes through broader talent pipelines, better decision quality, stronger engagement, and innovation.

Role in the organization:
- Cross-functional operational program that aligns HR, Legal/Compliance, Communications, IT, Facilities/Real Estate, and business units under a common DEI governance and accountability model.
- Provides data, targets, and continuous improvement to ensure DEI is embedded in everyday processes rather than standalone initiatives.

## Key Activities
- Establish DEI governance and accountability (charter, roles, decision rights, operating cadence).
- Baseline and analyze workforce and workplace data (representation, hiring/promotion/retention, pay equity, engagement).
- Prioritize and plan initiatives (roadmap, budgets, resourcing, milestones).
- Update policies and procedures (anti-discrimination, anti-harassment, reasonable accommodation, flexible work, caregiver/parental leave).
- Inclusive talent practices:
  - Job design and posting standards; remove non-essential requirements.
  - Sourcing and employer branding to reach underrepresented groups.
  - Structured, bias-mitigated selection (interview guides, criteria, panel composition).
  - Equitable onboarding and sponsorship/mentorship programs.
  - Performance, promotion, and succession processes with bias controls.
  - Pay equity analysis and remediation; equitable total rewards.
- Learning and leadership enablement (inclusive leadership, bystander intervention, respectful workplace, accommodations training).
- Employee Resource Group (ERG) framework (charters, budgets, objectives, governance).
- Accessibility and inclusive design (digital, physical, communications; accommodations process).
- Safe reporting and case management for concerns, with anti-retaliation controls.
- External partnerships and community engagement (pipelines, suppliers as applicable).
- Measurement and reporting (KPIs, dashboards, regulatory filings, ESG reporting).
- Change management and communications (narrative, stakeholder plans, feedback loops).
- Risk management and compliance (jurisdictional DEI data rules, AI in HR risk controls).
- Continuous improvement (inspect/adapt cycles based on outcomes and feedback).

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Approved DEI strategy/plan, business case, and high-level goals.
- Baseline HR data and analyses (workforce demographics where lawful, talent flows, pay, engagement/sentiment).
- Current HR policies, handbooks, recruiting processes, performance frameworks, and compensation structures.
- Legal and compliance requirements per jurisdiction (EEO/affirmative action, gender pay gap reporting, accessibility requirements).
- Budget, resource plan, and technology inventory (HRIS, ATS, LMS, survey tools).
- Leadership commitments and sponsorship model.

Prerequisites:
- Data governance and privacy framework for sensitive DEI data; legal review of data collection in each jurisdiction.
- Clear DEI governance and decision rights (e.g., DEI Council, executive sponsors).
- Change management plan and communications framework.

- Learning and development.
- Performance management, succession planning, and total rewards/pay processes.
- Employee relations and investigations.
- IT identity/data management and analytics.
- Facilities/real estate and HSE for accessibility and safety.

## Process Steps
1) Mobilize governance and kickoff
- Responsible: Chief Diversity Officer (CDO)/DEI Lead, CHRO, executive sponsors.
- Actions: Confirm charter, roles (RACI), operating cadence, escalation paths. Approve scope, milestones, and budget. Set enterprise and BU-level targets.

2) Legal, data, and risk readiness
- Responsible: Legal/Compliance, Data Privacy, HRIS/Analytics.
- Actions: Map applicable regulations by location; define lawful demographic attributes; update consent and privacy notices; implement data minimization, role-based access; validate baseline datasets and quality; document risks and controls (including for AI-enabled tools).

3) Baseline and diagnostics
- Responsible: People Analytics.
- Actions: Analyze representation by level/function/location; hiring funnel conversion and adverse impact; promotion and performance outcomes; pay equity (regression-based analysis controlling for legitimate factors); engagement and inclusion index; accommodation request volumes and SLAs; exit data. Identify root causes and opportunity areas.

4) Prioritize initiatives and finalize roadmap
- Responsible: DEI PMO with HR COEs.
- Actions: Rank initiatives by impact, feasibility, risk, cost; define scope, owners, timelines, success metrics; select pilot areas; align with business strategy and local nuances.

5) Policy and procedure updates
- Responsible: HR Policy, Legal, Employee Relations.
- Actions: Update anti-discrimination/harassment policies; anti-retaliation; accommodations; flexible work; caregiver/parental leave; complaint intake; ERG governance; supplier/partner standards where relevant. Publish and socialize updates.

6) Embed DEI in talent acquisition
- Responsible: Talent Acquisition (TA), Hiring Managers.
- Actions:
  - Standardize inclusive job templates; remove unnecessary credentials; inclusive language scanners.
  - Expand sourcing channels; partnerships with schools/associations.
  - Ensure diverse interview slates where lawful and appropriate; structured interviews with anchored rubrics; panel training; accommodations in interviews.
  - Monitor funnel metrics and adverse impact; remediate process steps causing disparity.

7) Embed DEI in performance, development, and advancement
- Responsible: HRBPs, L&D, Talent Management.
- Actions:
  - Calibrate performance ratings; review for pattern disparities.
  - Transparent promotion criteria and sponsorship/mentorship programs.
  - Succession plans with diverse slates; development access tracking.
  - Inclusive leadership and manager capability programs; bystander intervention and respectful workplace training.

8) Pay equity and rewards
- Responsible: Total Rewards, People Analytics, Legal.
- Actions: Conduct pay equity analyses; prioritize remediation actions; adjust compensation practices (offer guidelines, negotiation policies, pay transparency practices per law); monitor starting pay differences; publish statutory reports.

9) ERGs and community engagement
- Responsible: DEI Office, ERG Leaders, Communications.
- Actions: Establish ERG charters, objectives, budgets; leadership sponsors; programming tied to business and community impact; ERG leader support and recognition.

10) Accessibility and accommodations
- Responsible: Facilities/IT/HR, HSE.
- Actions: Audit physical and digital accessibility; align to WCAG and ADA/ADAAA/equivalents; implement reasonable accommodations intake, review, and fulfillment process with SLAs; inclusive event standards.

11) Safe reporting and case management
- Responsible: Employee Relations, Ethics & Compliance.
- Actions: Maintain confidential, multiple-channel reporting; train investigators; track case cycle times, themes; prevent retaliation; communicate outcomes and learnings where appropriate.

12) Communications and change management
- Responsible: Change Management, Corporate Communications, HRBPs.
- Actions: Stakeholder mapping; targeted messaging; leadership narratives; manager toolkits; office hours; FAQ; celebrate wins; address concerns transparently.

13) Measurement, reporting, and transparency
- Responsible: People Analytics, DEI PMO.
- Actions: Build dashboards; track KPIs vs. targets; statutory filings (e.g., EEO-1, gender pay reports); ESG disclosures; quarterly reviews with executives and BU leaders.

14) Continuous improvement and scaling
- Responsible: DEI PMO, COEs, BU Leaders.
- Actions: Run pilots, A/B test interventions; gather feedback; adjust policies and programs; sunset low-impact activities; scale effective practices enterprise-wide; update roadmap annually.

15) Assurance and audit
- Responsible: Internal Audit, Compliance.
- Actions: Periodic audits of DEI processes (e.g., structured interviews adherence, pay equity controls, accommodation process). Implement corrective actions.

Stage gates: 1) Governance/Readiness sign-off, 2) Roadmap approval, 3) Pilot go/no-go, 4) Scale-up readiness, 5) Annual review/reset.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Implemented DEI initiatives and embedded practices across talent lifecycle.
- Updated, published policies and procedures.
- Training programs and completion records; manager toolkits.
- DEI dashboards and reports; statutory filings; ESG disclosures.
- Pay equity analysis and remediation logs.
- ERG governance documents and activity plans.
- Accessibility audit findings and remediation plans.
- Case management reports and corrective actions.
- Risk register and control inventory.

Success criteria:
- Target progress on representation, equity, and inclusion indices.
- Statutory compliance with no material findings.
- Measurable reduction in pay gaps unexplained by legitimate factors.
- Reduced adverse impact across hiring/promotion.
- Improved engagement and belonging scores for underrepresented groups.
- On-time delivery of roadmap milestones and closure of audit findings.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Executive Sponsor/CEO: Set tone, allocate resources, hold leaders accountable; periodic reviews.
- CHRO: Integrate DEI into all HR COEs; ensure policy and process alignment.
- Chief Diversity Officer/DEI Lead: Own DEI roadmap execution; governance; metrics; cross-functional coordination.
- DEI Program Manager/PMO: Plan, track, and report program; manage risks, dependencies, and communications.
- HR Business Partners: Localize initiatives; coach leaders/managers; monitor outcomes.
- Talent Acquisition Lead: Implement inclusive hiring practices; monitor funnel metrics and corrective actions.
- Total Rewards Lead: Conduct pay equity analyses; drive remediation and compensation policy adjustments.
- Learning & Development Lead: Design and deliver inclusive leadership and required trainings.
- People Analytics Lead: Data strategy, dashboards, insights, and adverse impact monitoring.
- Legal/Compliance: Ensure regulatory alignment; advise on lawful data collection; review policies; oversee investigations standards.
- Employee Relations: Manage complaints, investigations, anti-retaliation, and corrective actions.
- IT/HRIS: Enable tooling, access controls, integrations, and data privacy/security.
- Facilities/Real Estate/HSE: Physical accessibility and inclusive workplace standards.
- Corporate Communications/Change Management: Messaging strategy, storytelling, and stakeholder engagement.
- ERG Leaders and Sponsors: Program design and delivery; feedback channel to leadership.
- People Managers: Apply inclusive people practices; complete training; support team accommodations; contribute to targets.
- Internal Audit: Provide independent assurance and recommendations.

## Best Practices
- Leadership accountability: Tie a portion of leader incentives to DEI outcomes and inclusive leadership behaviors.
- Data-driven goals: Set realistic, local-law-compliant targets and measure both outcomes and process health.
- Intersectional analysis: Examine outcomes across multiple attributes where lawful to avoid masking disparities.
- Evidence-based training: Use practice-based, manager-focused learning with follow-up coaching; avoid one-and-done sessions.
- Structured decisions: Use standardized criteria and documented rationales for hiring, performance, promotions, and compensation.
- Pay equity discipline: Repeat analyses at least annually; fix root causes (ranges, negotiation policies, leveling).
- Inclusive design: Apply accessibility and inclusive language standards in systems, facilities, content, and events.
- Localize global strategy: Adapt for jurisdictional laws, labor markets, and cultural context while maintaining core principles.
- Safe reporting culture: Multiple channels, confidentiality, anti-retaliation enforcement, and visible consequences.
- AI governance: Validate HR tech for bias, document intended use, monitor outcomes, and maintain human oversight.
- Transparent progress: Share metrics and actions regularly; explain what’s working and what’s not.
- Pilot and scale: Test interventions, evaluate impact, and scale the ones that work; sunset low-yield activities.

## Common Challenges
- Data and privacy constraints: Some jurisdictions restrict demographic data collection.
  - Solutions: Use voluntary, consent-based self-ID; focus on process metrics; aggregate or proxy data where necessary under legal guidance.
- Resistance or backlash: Misunderstandings about DEI intent; fear of change.
  - Solutions: Clear business rationale, leadership modeling, two-way dialogue, manager enablement, and myth-busting communications.
- Tokenism and initiative fatigue: Activities without impact or overreliance on ERGs.
  - Solutions: Prioritize high-impact, structural interventions; protect ERG leaders from role overload; measure outcomes.
- Inconsistent manager capability: Frontline managers are critical but underprepared.
  - Solutions: Practical toolkits, coaching, just-in-time learning, and reinforcing consequences/rewards.
- Siloed ownership and fragmented tools: Disconnected efforts across HR and business units.
  - Solutions: Strong PMO, common metrics, integrated systems, and a clear RACI.
- Legal risks in pay and selection practices: Unintended adverse impact or pay disparities.
  - Solutions: Regular audits, validated selection tools, documented decision criteria, and swift remediation with Legal partnership.

## Performance Metrics
Representation and flow:
- Representation by level/function/location vs. labor market benchmarks.
- Hiring funnel conversion by stage and demographic; adverse impact ratio (4/5ths rule where applicable).
- Promotion, performance rating distribution, and succession slate diversity.

Equity and rewards:
- Adjusted pay gap (regression-based) by level/role; percentage of gap remediated per cycle.
- Starting pay variance vs. midpoint by demographic.

Inclusion and experience:
- Inclusion index from engagement survey (belonging, fairness, voice, respect).
- Retention/voluntary turnover rates and regret loss for underrepresented groups.
- Accommodation cycle time and satisfaction.

Process health:
- Training completion and behavior adoption (e.g., structured interview usage rate).
- Policy compliance audit pass rate; investigation cycle time; retaliation rate.

Program delivery:
- Milestone adherence (% on-time), budget variance, number of pilots scaled.
- External obligations: On-time statutory filings; audit findings closed within SLA.

Qualitative:
- ERG participation and impact stories tied to business outcomes.

Targets should be specific, lawful, time-bound, and contextualized by location/market.

## Technology and Tools
- HRIS/People platform: Core data, org structures, role-based access.
- ATS and recruiting enablement:
  - Structured interview and scoring tools.
  - Job description optimization (inclusive language) tools.
  - Sourcing platforms and CRM for targeted talent communities.
- People analytics and DEI dashboards: Data warehouse/BI; DEI analytics suites for representation, flow, and adverse impact.
- Pay equity analysis tools: Statistical modeling and remediation planning; compensation management systems with guardrails.
- LMS and learning experience platforms: Assignments, tracking, practice simulations, nudges.
- Survey and listening platforms: Engagement, pulse, lifecycle surveys; sentiment analysis.
- Case management and hotline systems: Intake, triage, investigation workflow; anonymous reporting.
- Accommodations management: Requests intake, tracking, documentation.
- Accessibility tools: Digital accessibility scanners; captioning/ASR; assistive tech compatibility; inclusive event tools.
- Internal communications and collaboration: Intranet, knowledge base, messaging platforms.
- Policy management systems: Version control, attestation tracking.
- AI governance utilities: Model documentation, bias testing, monitoring for HR tech.

This process framework provides a practical, auditable approach to implementing DEI plans with clear ownership, safeguards, and measurable outcomes.

Process Details:
## Overview
Administer HR policies is the end-to-end process of operationalizing, communicating, enforcing, and continuously improving the organization’s HR policies. It ensures policies are accessible, understood, and followed; that compliance with laws and regulations is achieved; and that necessary, controlled deviations (exceptions/waivers) are granted when justified. This process translates workforce strategy and policy design into day-to-day practice, reduces compliance risk, fosters a fair and consistent employee experience, and supports organizational culture and performance.

Scope includes: policy governance and lifecycle management, publication and communication, training and acknowledgment, interpretation and advisory support, exception and waiver management, monitoring and audits, incident/violation handling, records management, and continuous improvement.

## Key Activities
- Establish policy governance: roles, RACI, approval matrix, review cadence, and controls.
- Maintain a central policy inventory/repository with version control and metadata.
- Publish, communicate, and localize policies; ensure accessibility and inclusivity.
- Provide training and collect employee acknowledgments/attestations.
- Offer advisory and interpretation support to managers and employees.
- Manage policy exceptions/waivers via defined criteria, workflow, and approvals.
- Monitor compliance through audits, sampling, and system controls.
- Investigate policy violations and coordinate corrective actions.
- Update policies based on legal changes, organizational changes, and lessons learned.
- Report on compliance metrics and drive continuous improvement.
- Ensure records retention and defensible documentation of evidence.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs:
  - Approved HR policies and procedures (global and local), including Code of Conduct.
  - Regulatory and legal requirements (labor, employment, benefits, DEI, privacy, health & safety).
  - Collective bargaining agreements and works council requirements where applicable.
  - Policy governance framework (RACI, approval thresholds, review schedule).
  - Training curricula and content; acknowledgment language.
  - Disciplinary matrix and employee relations guidelines.
  - Standard forms: exception request, incident report, investigation templates.
  - Policy taxonomy and metadata standards (owner, region, audience, risk level).
- Prerequisites:
  - Operational HRIS/LMS/Intranet/Policy Management and Case Management tools.
  - Identified Policy Owners and a Policy Governance Board or senior HR sponsor.
  - Legal/Compliance counsel available for interpretation and updates.
  - Communication channels and content standards (plain language, accessibility).
  - Data privacy controls for policy and case data.
- Dependencies on other processes:
  - 7.1.2.x Policy development and updates (design/approval input).
  - Compliance management and regulatory monitoring.
  - Learning & Development (training delivery).
  - Onboarding, transfers, and offboarding (policy acknowledgment life-cycle).
  - Employee Relations (investigations, corrective actions).
  - Internal Communications (campaigns, change management).
  - IT/Security (access controls, system-enforced policy controls).
  - Internal Audit and Risk Management.

## Process Steps
1. Plan and Set Governance
   - Define policy administration charter, scope, and RACI (Policy Owner, HR Policy Admin, Legal, ER, L&D, IT, Audit).
   - Establish approval matrix by policy risk tier (e.g., High: HR VP + Legal; Medium: Policy Owner + Legal; Low: Policy Owner).
   - Configure tools: policy repository, workflows, acknowledgment tracking, dashboards.

2. Maintain Policy Inventory and Lifecycle
   - Create/maintain a centralized inventory with metadata (title, owner, effective/expiry dates, jurisdictions, audience, dependencies).
   - Assign review cadence (e.g., annually for high-risk; biennially for low-risk) and automated reminders.
   - Control versions and retain superseded versions per retention schedule.
   - Map policies to regulatory obligations and internal controls (obligations register).

3. Publish and Communicate
   - Validate final content: legal review, brand and accessibility checks, localization needs.
   - Publish to a single source of truth (intranet/policy portal) with clear “effective date” and “what changed.”
   - Push targeted communications by audience and region; include FAQs and manager talking points.
   - Provide accessible, inclusive formats (plain language, translations, mobile-friendly, ADA/WCAG-compliant).

4. Train and Acknowledge
   - Assign mandatory training per role/risk level; set due dates and recurrence.
   - Deliver learning via LMS; embed microlearning, scenario-based modules.
   - Collect electronic acknowledgments; capture timestamp, version, user ID, jurisdiction.
   - Escalate overdue items to managers; enforce consequences for persistent non-compliance.

5. Provide Advisory and Interpretation Support
   - Operate an HR policy helpdesk (ticketing/knowledge base) for inquiries.
   - Document interpretations and add to FAQs; escalate complex scenarios to Legal/ER.
   - Ensure consistent responses; update policy where repeated ambiguities occur.

6. Manage Exceptions and Waivers
   - Define exception criteria, evidence requirements, risk assessment, and time-bounded approvals.
   - Route requests via workflow to Policy Owner, Legal/Privacy, ER, and business approvers as needed.
   - Record decisions, rationale, effective period, and conditions; link to impacted employees/locations.
   - Monitor exception aging and renewals; sunset expired exceptions.

7. Monitor and Audit Compliance
   - Perform periodic sampling (e.g., 5–10% of population) for high-risk policies.
   - Use system controls (e.g., access contingent on training/acknowledgment completion).
   - Track third-party/contingent worker compliance where in scope.
   - Document evidence and remediation actions; integrate with internal audit plan.

8. Handle Incidents and Violations
   - Provide confidential reporting channels; protect against retaliation.
   - Triage cases by severity; initiate investigations per ER protocol.
   - Determine findings and corrective actions (coaching, retraining, disciplinary measures).
   - Capture case files, timelines, outcomes; analyze trends to prevent recurrence.

9. Update and Improve
   - Trigger reviews on regulatory changes, M&A/organizational changes, or incident trends.
   - Run change control: stakeholder review, impact assessment, translations, communications, training updates.
   - Retire/merge redundant policies; maintain deprecation notices and redirects.
   - Conduct post-implementation reviews and incorporate feedback.

10. Report and Govern
   - Produce monthly/quarterly dashboards for leadership and the Policy Governance Board.
   - Review KPIs, exceptions, incidents, and audit outcomes; approve improvement actions.
   - Maintain readiness for regulator or external auditor inquiries.

11. Records Retention and Closure
   - Store acknowledgments, training completions, exceptions, and investigation records per legal retention schedules.
   - Secure and restrict access; enable eDiscovery when needed.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Centralized, current policy repository with version history and metadata.
- Communication artifacts: announcements, FAQs, manager toolkits, change logs.
- Training completion and acknowledgment records, auditor-ready evidence.
- Exception/waiver register with status, durations, conditions, and approvals.
- Monitoring and audit reports; remediation plans and closure evidence.
- Investigation case files and corrective action documentation.
- KPI dashboards and governance meeting minutes.
- Updated policies or decommissioning records.

Success criteria:
- High and timely acknowledgment/training completion rates.
- Minimal/zero high-severity audit findings and regulatory breaches.
- Policies reviewed/updated within defined cadences and within SLA after legal changes.
- Reduction in repeat violations; positive employee understanding scores.
- Timely exception processing with controlled risk and low overdue exceptions.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Policy Governance Board / HR Leadership: Approve high-risk policies, review KPIs, resolve escalations.
- Policy Owner (HR COE lead, e.g., Benefits, Compensation, ER): Own content, risk tiering, approvals, and decisions on exceptions.
- HR Policy Administrator: Maintain repository, manage workflows, publish content, track acknowledgments, compile reports.
- Legal/Compliance Counsel: Ensure legal conformity, interpret regulatory requirements, approve high-risk changes, advise on exceptions.
- Employee Relations (ER): Lead investigations, advise on discipline, trend analysis.
- Learning & Development: Build/deliver training, manage curricula, track completions.
- Internal Communications: Craft messages, campaigns, and change communications.
- HRIS/IT Security: Configure systems for access controls, integrate LMS/HRIS/policy portal, ensure data security and analytics.
- Data Privacy Officer: Review policies impacting personal data; approve exceptions that affect privacy.
- Internal Audit/Risk: Perform independent audits, validate controls, advise on improvements.
- Line Managers: Reinforce policies, ensure team compliance, approve/monitor exceptions, support investigations.
- Employees/Contingent Workers: Read, acknowledge, comply with policies, complete training, report concerns.
- Union/Works Council Liaison (where applicable): Coordinate notices/consultations, integrate CBAs with policies.

## Best Practices
- Single source of truth: Central policy portal with search, filters, and mobile access.
- Plain language and inclusive design; provide localized versions with legal review.
- Risk-based governance: Higher rigor for high-risk policies; tighter review cadences and controls.
- Strong version control and visible “what changed” summaries.
- Integrate with lifecycle events (onboarding, role changes, location transfers).
- Just-in-time learning and reminders embedded in daily tools (e.g., Teams/Slack nudges).
- Formal exception governance with time limits, conditions, and documented risk assessments.
- Use metrics to drive improvements; close the loop on audit and incident findings.
- Prevent policy sprawl; maintain taxonomy; retire redundant/overlapping content.
- Proactive regulatory horizon scanning; maintain an obligations register mapped to policies.
- Privacy and security by design for policy and case data; least-privilege access.
- Regular stakeholder forums and employee feedback channels to gauge clarity and usability.

## Common Challenges
- Policy sprawl and outdated content: Solve via inventory, taxonomy, scheduled reviews, and deprecation workflows.
- Low awareness/engagement: Use plain language, manager toolkits, targeted communications, microlearning.
- Inconsistent interpretation: Centralize Q&A, publish interpretations, train HRBPs/managers.
- Weak acknowledgment tracking: Automate via LMS/HRIS, enforce escalations and system gates.
- Exception misuse or creep: Enforce criteria, expirations, periodic review, and executive visibility.
- Cross-border conflicts: Maintain global baseline with local addenda; legal review for each jurisdiction.
- Union/works council requirements: Integrate consultation timelines; track commitments.
- Manual processes: Implement policy management, case management, and workflow tools; integrate systems.
- Data privacy risks: Minimize personal data in cases, apply retention, access controls, and DPO oversight.
- Audit fatigue: Risk-based audit plan, sampling, and coordinated schedules across assurance functions.

## Performance Metrics
- Policy coverage ratio: percent of workforce with access to applicable policies.
- Timely review rate: percent of policies reviewed/updated per cadence.
- Time-to-publish: average days from approval to portal publication.
- Acknowledgment rate and cycle time by policy/risk tier.
- Training completion rate and on-time completion.
- Incident rate per 1,000 employees by policy; repeat violation rate.
- Investigation cycle time and closure rate within SLA.
- Audit findings: count and severity; remediation closure time.
- Exception metrics: volume, approval rate, average aging, percent overdue/expired.
- Employee understanding: quiz pass rates, pulse survey clarity scores, search success rate.
- Access and engagement: portal visits, unique viewers, time on page, bounce rate.
- Localization lag: average days between global update and local publication.
- Cost and efficiency: admin hours per policy, automation rate, cost per employee to administer.

## Technology and Tools
- Policy Management System: PolicyTech, ConvergePoint, NAVEX, PowerDMS, ServiceNow Policy & Compliance.
- HRIS/LMS: Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM; Cornerstone, Docebo, Workday Learning.
- Intranet/Portal/Knowledge Base: SharePoint, ServiceNow HRSD, LumApps.
- Case and Investigation Management: ServiceNow HRSD, NAVEX, Resolver; secure evidence storage.
- E-signature/Acknowledgment: DocuSign, Adobe Sign, LMS-native attestations.
- Communication and Engagement: Email platforms, Teams/Slack, digital signage, newsletters.
- Analytics/BI: Power BI, Tableau; LMS/HRIS dashboards and data warehouse integrations.
- Workflow and Automation: ServiceNow, Power Automate, Jira, low-code tools.
- Translation/Localization: Smartling, Memsource; in-country legal partners.
- Audit and Records: GRC tools, eDiscovery, retention management solutions.
- Identity and Access: SSO/IDP integrations to enforce access gates based on compliance status.
- Chatbot/Virtual Assistant: Knowledge retrieval and guided Q&A for policy topics.

# [7.2.1.6] Notify Hiring Manager

## Overview
This process ensures the hiring manager is promptly and accurately informed of new requisitions, changes to existing requisitions, or status updates that require action or awareness. It bridges the requisition creation/approval workflow and downstream recruiting activities by triggering the hiring manager to engage (e.g., confirm requisition details, schedule intake, prioritize hiring timeline).

Purpose:
- Ensure hiring managers receive timely, actionable notifications with the right level of detail.
- Capture acknowledgement and any required decisions from the hiring manager.
- Maintain an auditable communication trail and meet SLA, compliance, and data privacy requirements.

Role in the organization:
- Enables smooth handoffs between HR/Talent Acquisition (TA) and the business.
- Reduces delays in recruiting by preventing missed or ambiguous communication.
- Supports governance by standardizing content, timing, and recipients of communications.

## Key Activities
- Monitor triggers (new requisition approved/opened, changes, re-openings, cancellations).
- Validate notification readiness (complete data, correct recipients, required approvals).
- Select appropriate notification type and channel(s) based on event severity and preferences.
- Generate notification content via templates; include context and call-to-action (CTA).
- Dispatch notification, confirm delivery, and capture acknowledgement.
- Follow up with reminders and escalation per SLA.
- Log communications and outcomes in ATS/HRIS for audit and reporting.
- Coordinate next steps (e.g., intake meeting scheduling, requisition adjustments).

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Requisition data: requisition ID, title, job family, level/grade, location, employment type, hiring reason (backfill/new), budgeted comp range, target start date, headcount, cost center, job description, hiring approvals status.
- Hiring manager data: name, title, email, chat handle, location/time zone, delegate/backup.
- Change details (if applicable): what changed, who changed it, effective date, reason.
- Notification templates and SLAs.
- Communication preferences and distribution list rules (e.g., include HRBP, TA Lead).

Prerequisites:
- Requisition created and routed in ATS; approval stage completed if required for notification.
- Hiring manager assigned and active in ATS/HRIS with correct contact details.
- Data privacy classification applied (e.g., comp data visibility limited to authorized roles).
- Communication channels configured and tested (email, MS Teams/Slack, in-app notifications).

Dependencies on other processes:
- [7.2.1.2–5] Create, review, and approve job requisitions.
- Identity and access management for ATS/HRIS roles and permissions.
- HR policy for notification content, confidentiality, and records retention.
- Enterprise communications standards (branding, accessibility, language).

## Process Steps
1. Detect trigger
   - Automatic: ATS event fires when a requisition is approved/opened, re-opened, materially changed (grade/comp/location/headcount), or paused/cancelled.
   - Manual: TA Coordinator flags a change requiring notification (e.g., hiring timeline shift).

2. Validate readiness
   - Confirm required fields are complete.
   - Confirm hiring manager assignment and contact details; identify delegate if manager is out-of-office.
   - Confirm approvals are at the correct stage for notification.
   - Classify the event: new open, minor update, material change, urgent issue, pause/cancel.

3. Determine recipients
   - Mandatory: Hiring Manager (HM).
   - Optional/cc per policy: Recruiter, HRBP, TA Lead, Finance partner (for comp-impacting changes), Security/Facilities (for start-readiness), Diversity/EEO partner (where applicable).
   - Confidential requisitions: restrict recipients to HM and designated TA staff.

4. Select channel(s) and SLA
   - Primary: ATS in-app + email.
   - Secondary: Teams/Slack direct message for urgent or time-sensitive updates.
   - SLA targets (suggested): send notification within 30 minutes of trigger; HM acknowledgement within 1 business day.

5. Build message
   - Use approved template based on event type and country/region.
   - Include required elements:
     - Subject: clear event and requisition ID (e.g., “Action Required: Requisition 12345 – Product Manager (NYC)”).
     - Summary details: title, location, level, headcount, target start date, hiring reason, req owner, recruiter.
     - What changed (if applicable) with before/after highlights.
     - CTA: acknowledge, review, approve adjustments, schedule intake, or provide missing info.
     - Links: deep link to requisition in ATS; intake form/calendar link.
     - SLA and due date.
     - Confidentiality notice and support contact.

6. Quality checks
   - Validate placeholders resolved; no PII beyond policy.
   - Ensure audience aligns with confidentiality.
   - Verify deep links and calendar invites function.

7. Dispatch notification
   - Send via ATS notification service; post to selected secondary channel if configured.
   - For urgent changes, include priority flag and SMS if approved.

8. Confirm delivery and log
   - Capture delivery status (sent, delivered, bounced).
   - Log event in ATS audit trail with timestamp, recipients, channel, template version.

9. Capture acknowledgement and actions
   - HM acknowledges via ATS button or reply; system updates acknowledgement status.
   - If action needed (e.g., approve change, provide details), capture response and update requisition fields.

10. Reminders and escalation
   - Automated reminder at 24 hours if no acknowledgement.
   - Escalate at 48 hours to HM’s manager and TA Lead; notify HRBP for prolonged delays.

11. Close notification
   - Mark notification closed once acknowledged and required actions are complete.
   - Update requisition status to “Ready for Intake” or appropriate next step.
   - Archive communication in case record per retention policy.

12. Exceptions
   - HM out-of-office: automatically route to delegate; extend SLA by policy.
   - Multiple HMs: send to primary HM; cc secondary; require primary acknowledgement.
   - System outage: use manual email template; attach PDF snapshot; log retroactively when systems restore.

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs:
- Delivered notification with clear CTA.
- Acknowledgement record and any captured decisions/inputs.
- Updated requisition status and audit log.

Deliverables:
- Communication artifact (email/in-app message/Teams post).
- Intake meeting invite (if applicable).
- Updated requisition data (e.g., confirmed target start date, job description edits).

Success criteria:
- 100% notifications sent within SLA after trigger.
- ≥98% delivered successfully (no bounces).
- ≥95% HM acknowledgements within SLA.
- Zero confidential data leaks; correct recipients only.
- Downstream milestone met (intake scheduled within 2 business days of approval).

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Recruiter
  - Confirms requisition readiness, validates content, and ensures CTA aligns with next steps.
  - Monitors acknowledgement and follows up with HM.
- TA Coordinator/Operations
  - Oversees dispatch, reminders, escalations, and audit logging.
  - Manages templates, channel configurations, and SLAs.
- Hiring Manager (HM)
  - Reviews notification, acknowledges receipt, provides required inputs, and schedules intake.
  - Delegates if unavailable and ensures continuity.
- HR Business Partner (HRBP)
  - Supports alignment on role definition and approvals; assists with escalations.
- TA Lead/Manager
  - Ensures SLA adherence; intervenes on escalations; addresses systemic issues.
- Finance/Compensation Partner (as needed)
  - Reviews and approves compensation-impacting changes.
- ATS/HRIS Administrator
  - Maintains notification rules, roles, integrations, and audit/reporting capabilities.
- IT/Enterprise Communications
  - Ensures channel reliability, deliverability, and security policies.

## Best Practices
- Use event-driven notifications integrated with ATS workflow to minimize manual steps.
- Standardize templates by event type and region; keep messages concise with explicit CTAs and due dates.
- Include deep links and one-click acknowledgement to reduce friction.
- Tier notifications by severity; reserve high-priority channels for urgent items to reduce noise.
- Maintain accurate recipient mappings, including delegates and time zone-aware scheduling.
- Implement read receipts/ack tracking and dashboard visibility for recruiters/TA ops.
- Apply least-necessary data principle; avoid distributing sensitive comp details outside authorized roles.
- Localize templates for language and legal notices; ensure accessibility (plain language, readable formatting).
- Run periodic tests (drills) and A/B improvements on subject lines and CTAs to improve response times.
- Maintain a knowledge base with FAQs and quick guides for HMs on how to respond.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Missed notifications due to email filtering
  - Solution: Authenticate domains (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), whitelist ATS domain, provide alternate channel fallback.
- Notification fatigue
  - Solution: Digest minor updates; prioritize only material changes for immediate notices; consolidate messages.
- Incorrect or stale recipient data
  - Solution: Sync HM assignments from HRIS nightly; enforce validation in requisition creation; maintain delegate lists.
- Delayed HM acknowledgement
  - Solution: Automated reminders and time-bound escalations; provide mobile-friendly CTA; highlight business impact.
- Confidentiality breaches
  - Solution: Role-based content filtering; require explicit selection of confidential template; approval gate for sensitive changes.
- System outages
  - Solution: Manual templates and BCP playbook; retroactive logging; monitor with status page subscriptions.
- Multi-HM or matrix structures
  - Solution: Define “primary HM” ownership; require single point acknowledgement; clarify cc-only recipients.
- Global time zones
  - Solution: Send during local business hours; display times in local time zone; set equitable SLAs.

## Performance Metrics
- Time-to-notify: median minutes from trigger to sent.
- Delivery rate: percentage delivered vs attempted.
- Acknowledgement time: median and 90th percentile time from sent to HM acknowledgement.
- SLA adherence: percentage of notifications sent and acknowledged within defined SLAs.
- Escalation rate: percentage requiring escalation; resolution time post-escalation.
- Action completion rate: percentage of notifications resulting in required action within timeframe (e.g., intake scheduled).
- Error rate: misaddressed recipients, template errors, broken links.
- Notification volume by type: to monitor noise and optimize templates.
- Stakeholder satisfaction: periodic HM survey scores on clarity and usefulness.
- Compliance and audit completeness: percentage with complete logs and retained artifacts.

## Technology and Tools
- Applicant Tracking System (ATS): Workday Recruiting, Greenhouse, Lever, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle Recruiting.
  - Event triggers, templates, in-app notifications, audit logs.
- HRIS: Workday HCM, SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central, Oracle HCM.
  - Source of truth for manager assignments and org structure.
- Communication platforms: Microsoft 365/Exchange, Google Workspace, Slack, Microsoft Teams.
  - Email and chat channels; message delivery and read receipts where supported.
- Workflow/orchestration: ServiceNow, Jira, Power Automate, Zapier.
  - Routing, reminders, escalations, exception handling.
- Calendar and scheduling: Outlook, Google Calendar, Calendly.
  - Intake meeting scheduling integrated into CTA.
- Analytics and dashboards: Power BI, Tableau, ATS-native reporting.
  - SLA tracking, throughput, and trend analysis.
- Identity and access management: Okta, Azure AD.
  - Role-based access and SSO for secure links.
- Archiving and compliance: Proofpoint, Mimecast, enterprise archiving.
  - Retention and eDiscovery of communications.

Implementation notes:
- Define and publish SLAs (e.g., send within 30 minutes; acknowledge within 1 business day; intake scheduled within 2 business days).
- Configure ATS event rules to differentiate minor vs material changes and select appropriate template/channel.
- Build a notification runbook including exception scenarios, escalation contacts, and manual fallback steps.
- Review metrics monthly with TA leadership; run root cause analysis for SLA misses and implement improvements.
