Process Details:
## Overview
Select and reject candidates is the decision point of the recruiting lifecycle where final evaluations from interviews and tests are synthesized to determine who will receive an offer recommendation and who will be declined. Its purpose is to make timely, fair, evidence-based hiring decisions that optimize quality of hire, uphold legal and policy compliance, and maintain a positive candidate experience.

This process consumes structured evidence from:
- Interview candidates [10457]: behavioral, technical, and values-based interview scorecards and notes.
- Test candidates [10458]: job-relevant assessments (e.g., work samples, coding exercises, case studies, simulations).

It outputs an approved recommendation to extend an offer (with alternates/backup candidates) and communicates rejections to non-selected candidates. It safeguards the employer brand, mitigates bias, and protects the organization through rigorous documentation and compliance.

## Key Activities
- Consolidate and validate evaluation data from interviews and tests.
- Facilitate a structured debrief and calibration among interviewers.
- Apply a predefined selection rubric and decision matrix to compare candidates.
- Run fairness and compliance checks (e.g., adverse impact screening where permissible).
- Confirm headcount and compensation fit; gather required approvals.
- Conduct pre-offer reference checks if required by policy/local law.
- Document decision rationale and audit trail in the ATS.
- Communicate decisions to candidates (offer recommendation or rejection).
- Maintain alternates/backup shortlist and talent pool tagging.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs
- Approved job requisition with role profile, competencies, and compensation band.
- Complete interview scorecards and notes from all interviewers.
- Test/assessment results mapped to competencies.
- Candidate resumes, applications, and eligibility information (e.g., work authorization).
- Hiring plan and headcount/budget confirmation.
- Selection rubric and pass/fail thresholds for must-have competencies.
- DEI and legal hiring guidelines (EEO/OFCCP, ADA, GDPR/CCPA, local “ban-the-box” rules).
- Internal mobility or rehire policies, union or CBA provisions if applicable.

Prerequisites
- All planned interviews/tests completed and scorecards submitted independently.
- Interviewers trained on structured evaluation, anti-bias, and documentation requirements.
- Compensation pre-brief on expected level/band and pay equity constraints.
- Decision meeting scheduled with the hiring manager and selection panel.

Dependencies on other processes
- Upstream: Job analysis and requisition approval; source and screen; conduct interviews [10457]; administer tests [10458].
- Downstream: Prepare and extend offers; background checks (if post-offer per jurisdiction); onboarding.
- Parallel/consulted: Legal/Compliance, Compensation, HRBP, Mobility/Immigration.

## Process Steps
1. Verify gating conditions
   - Confirm open headcount, level, and budget availability.
   - Ensure job description, competencies, and selection rubric are current and approved.

2. Consolidate evaluation data
   - Pull all interview scorecards and test results into the ATS.
   - Lock scorecards after submission to prevent retrospective edits.
   - Chase missing or incomplete scorecards; reschedule follow-ups only if essential.

3. Pre-debrief calibration prep
   - Recruiter/Talent Advisor compiles an evaluation summary per candidate: strengths, concerns, evidence against each competency, and test outcomes.
   - Compute initial aggregate scores per competency; flag pass/fail on must-haves.

4. Fairness and quality checks (preliminary)
   - Review consistency of ratings across interviewers; identify anomalies.
   - Where permissible, run preliminary pass-through comparisons for potential adverse impact indicators; if signals emerge, re-examine criteria and evidence before final decisions.

5. Structured debrief meeting
   - Facilitate a time-boxed panel debrief; each interviewer presents evidence first, then opinions.
   - Discuss gaps, conflicting signals, and job-related concerns; avoid groupthink (the recruiter moderates).
   - Ensure “culture add” is assessed via defined behaviors, not subjective similarity.

6. Apply decision matrix
   - Use the selection rubric to classify each competency as: exceeds, meets, marginal, or does not meet.
   - Weigh tests/work samples more heavily for technical competencies when policy dictates.
   - Consider role requirements (e.g., clearance, shift availability, travel).
   - Identify top candidate(s) and rank alternates.

7. Risk and feasibility check
   - Validate compensation fit (band/level/pay equity); consult Compensation if exceptions are requested.
   - Confirm work authorization or visa feasibility and timelines with Mobility/Legal (no unlawful pre-offer inquiries).
   - Note any role-specific prerequisites (licenses, language proficiency).

8. Reference checks (if required pre-offer)
   - Conduct job-related, structured reference checks per policy and local law.
   - Document outcomes; if negative, escalate per adverse information handling guidelines.

9. Finalize selection recommendation
   - Hiring Manager selects the finalist and backup candidates.
   - Recruiter drafts an offer recommendation outline: level, target start date, compensation range compliant with internal equity, contingencies.

10. Approvals workflow
   - Route the decision packet for approvals: Hiring Manager, HR/Talent Acquisition, Compensation, HRBP, Finance/Headcount owner, and executive approver (if required).
   - Capture approvals electronically in the ATS or HRIS.

11. Decision documentation
   - Record decision rationale tied to job-related criteria; retain all supporting evidence.
   - Tag non-selected candidates with standardized, policy-compliant reasons (avoid sensitive or subjective labels).

12. Candidate communication
   - Call selected candidate to confirm continued interest and key expectations; proceed to offer preparation process.
   - Notify non-selected candidates:
     - Late-stage finalists: personalized communication (call or tailored email); offer brief feedback where policy allows.
     - Earlier-stage candidates: respectful templated communication via ATS; invite to talent community if appropriate.
   - Ensure communications meet local legal requirements and accessibility standards.

13. ATS updates and pipeline management
   - Move selected candidate to Offer stage; associate approvals and decision docs.
   - Move declined candidates to appropriate disposition statuses; set GDPR/CCPA retention timers.
   - Flag strong alternates for silver-medalist pools and future requisitions.

14. Closeout and continuous improvement
   - Log debrief outcomes, hiring insights, and process issues.
   - If SLA or fairness thresholds were missed, open an action item (e.g., interviewer coaching, rubric refinement).

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs
- Selected candidate approved for offer, with documented rationale and approvals.
- Ranked list of alternates/backups with notes.
- Dispositioned and notified non-selected candidates.

Deliverables
- Decision summary in ATS (evaluation synthesis, decision matrix, rubric results).
- Offer recommendation packet (level, compensation guidance, start date, contingencies).
- Reference check summaries (if conducted pre-offer).
- Candidate communications (offer intent confirmation, rejections).
- Audit trail: scorecards, test results, debrief notes, approval records.

Success criteria
- Decisions made within SLA from final interview (e.g., 3 business days).
- 100% scorecard completion and documented rationale.
- Compliance with DEI/legal requirements; no substantiated bias complaints.
- Positive candidate experience (e.g., candidate NPS above target).
- High offer acceptance and low early attrition for selected hires.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Hiring Manager (Accountable): Makes final selection recommendation; participates in debrief; ensures role fit and team needs; secures approvals.
- Recruiter/Talent Advisor (Responsible): Orchestrates process, ensures data completeness, facilitates debrief, runs approvals, communicates decisions, maintains ATS compliance.
- Interview Panelists (Responsible): Submit timely, evidence-based scorecards; participate in debrief; avoid bias and undue influence.
- HR Business Partner (Consulted): Advises on policy, equity, and organizational fit; supports escalation and dispute resolution.
- Compensation/Total Rewards (Consulted/Approver): Validates level and pay; ensures pay equity and budget alignment.
- Finance/Headcount Owner (Approver): Confirms funding and headcount availability.
- Legal/Compliance or DEI (Consulted): Advises on legal risks, adverse impact reviews, and documentation standards.
- Mobility/Immigration (Consulted): Assesses visa/work authorization feasibility and timelines.
- Recruiting Operations/ATS Admin (Consulted): Ensures workflow integrity, reporting, and retention controls.

## Best Practices
- Use structured scorecards with behaviorally anchored rating scales tied to competencies.
- Require independent submission of scorecards before debrief to reduce conformity bias.
- Time-box debriefs and follow a consistent agenda to drive timely decisions.
- Apply a predefined decision matrix with must-have thresholds; avoid post-hoc criteria changes.
- Conduct light-weight adverse impact checks where lawful; recalibrate criteria if unintended disparity is detected.
- Focus on “culture add” via defined values/behaviors; avoid subjective “fit” proxies.
- Train interviewers regularly on bias mitigation and lawful hiring practices.
- Provide personalized feedback to finalists when policy and law allow; never ghost candidates.
- Maintain a strong audit trail; lock evaluations after submission.
- Prepare alternates and communicate timelines to reduce offer back-and-forth and time-to-fill.
- Partner early with Compensation to prevent later offer-blockers; uphold pay equity.
- Respect privacy laws (GDPR/CCPA); set data retention and candidate consent in the ATS.

## Common Challenges
- Incomplete or late scorecards delaying decisions
  - Solution: Enforce SLAs, automated reminders, and manager escalation; measure compliance.
- Conflicting interviewer opinions
  - Solution: Use evidence-based debrief facilitation; weight assessments by relevance; bring in a tie-break interviewer if needed.
- Bias and subjective “fit” influencing outcomes
  - Solution: Structured rubrics, interviewer training, independent scoring, and fairness checks.
- Compensation misalignment or pay equity constraints
  - Solution: Early comp calibration; clear non-negotiables; alternative levers (sign-on, start date).
- Work authorization or relocation constraints
  - Solution: Early feasibility screening by Mobility/Legal; realistic timelines; consider remote options where feasible.
- Candidate timing pressures or competing offers
  - Solution: Accelerate debriefs; maintain warm engagement; identify alternates.
- Legal compliance missteps (e.g., ban-the-box, reference practices)
  - Solution: Jurisdiction-specific guardrails in ATS; recruiter training; consult Legal as needed.
- High-volume requisitions overwhelming panels
  - Solution: Tiered decision gates, batch debriefs, and standardized decision matrices; leverage assessments to prioritize.

## Performance Metrics
- Time to decision: median days from final interview to decision.
- Scorecard completeness rate: % of interviews with on-time, locked evaluations.
- Debrief SLA adherence: % of debriefs held within target timeframe.
- Selection ratio: selected to total assessed candidates; monitor by stage and requisition.
- Interview-to-offer yield: % of finalists resulting in offer recommendation.
- Offer acceptance rate (downstream proxy for selection quality).
- Candidate experience (NPS/CSAT) for finalists.
- Hiring manager satisfaction with finalist slate and decision process.
- Adverse impact indicators: pass-through ratios by demographic where lawful and with appropriate safeguards.
- Documentation completeness: % decisions with full rationale and approvals captured.
- Early attrition/first-90-day success rate for selected candidates (leading indicator of selection quality).

## Technology and Tools
- Applicant Tracking System (ATS) (e.g., Workday, Greenhouse, Lever): scorecards, workflows, approvals, communications, reporting, retention controls.
- Assessment platforms: coding tests, case/simulation tools, work sample scoring.
- Video interview and collaboration tools: conferencing and debrief facilitation.
- Reference checking tools (if used pre-offer): structured and compliant surveys.
- Compensation tools: market data and pay equity analysis.
- Analytics/BI dashboards: pipeline metrics, SLA tracking, fairness indicators.
- Communication tools: email/SMS templates, calendar scheduling, e-sign for approvals.
- Privacy/compliance tooling: consent tracking, data retention policies, audit logs.
- Accessibility tools: ensure candidate communications and platforms meet accessibility standards.

## Overview
The Negotiate Offer process ensures the organization and a selected candidate reach a clear, equitable, and compliant agreement on employment terms. It translates an approved offer into an accepted offer by aligning compensation, benefits, work arrangements, and start date with both business constraints and candidate expectations. This process protects internal equity and budget, supports compliance with pay and employment laws, and preserves a positive candidate experience that influences acceptance, time-to-start, and employer brand.

This process sits within Manage new hire/re-hire and follows creation and approval of a draft offer. It interfaces tightly with compensation, legal, hiring managers, and talent acquisition (TA) operations, and culminates in a signed offer and handoff to pre-boarding.

## Key Activities
- Prepare negotiation strategy and guardrails based on job architecture, internal parity, and approved budget.
- Communicate total rewards (base pay, variable comp, equity, benefits, PTO, work flexibility) and role value proposition.
- Elicit and document candidate priorities and constraints.
- Evaluate candidate counterproposals against compensation ranges and policy.
- Secure approvals for deviations/exceptions; adjust offer components as needed.
- Manage timing, expectations, and decision deadlines; coordinate with multiple stakeholders.
- Update formal offer letter and contingencies; facilitate e-signature.
- Record decisions, rationale, and exception data in ATS/HRIS.
- Close the loop: acceptance/decline captured; requisition and pre-boarding actions triggered.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs:
  - Approved requisition with job level, FLSA status, geo/work location, and compensation range.
  - Draft offer terms (base, bonus/commission/OTE where applicable, equity or long-term incentives, benefits summary, start date, contingencies).
  - Internal equity data for comparable roles/levels.
  - Candidate profile and contact details in ATS; interview feedback and final selection decision.
  - Market compensation benchmarks (e.g., survey data for the role and location).
  - Policy documents: pay transparency guidance, relocation/immigration policies, sign-on bonus policy, equity guidelines, remote/hybrid policy, background check/drug screen policy.

- Prerequisites:
  - Compensation and hiring manager alignment on the initial offer and “walk-away” limits.
  - Offer approval obtained per approval matrix for initial terms.
  - Compliance readiness:
    - Adherence to pay transparency laws where applicable.

    - Data privacy controls for candidate information (e.g., GDPR/CCPA).
  - Availability of an updated offer letter template and e-signature tool.

- Dependencies on other processes:
  - [7.2.4.1] Create offer (prior step producing the draft and approvals).
  - Background screening and pre-boarding initiation (triggered upon acceptance).
  - Immigration evaluation (if sponsorship is needed).
  - Relocation benefits administration (if applicable).

## Process Steps
1. Prepare and plan
   - Review approved offer terms, budget, and compensation guardrails.
   - Identify tradable components (e.g., start date flexibility, sign-on bonus, relocation assistance, equity mix, title within band, remote work days) and non-negotiables.
   - Align with hiring manager and compensation partner on negotiation strategy and escalation paths. Define turnaround SLAs (e.g., 24–48 hours).

2. Schedule and set expectations
   - Arrange a negotiation call/video with the candidate within 24–48 hours of offer creation.
   - Share a high-level total rewards summary and confirm that detailed offer letter will follow pending alignment.
   - Communicate a tentative decision timeline and any statutory disclosures (pay range where required).

3. Present the offer and value proposition
   - Clearly explain role scope, impact, team, growth path, and total compensation components:
     - Base pay and pay frequency; geo-differentials.
     - Variable comp: bonus/commission/OTE structure, accelerators, and guarantee (if any).
     - Equity: type (RSU/Options), grant value, vesting schedule, refresh policies.
     - Benefits highlights: healthcare, retirement, PTO, wellness, parental leave, education assistance.
     - Work model: onsite/hybrid/remote expectations, travel, equipment.
     - Contingencies: background check, drug screen, export controls, employment-at-will (as applicable).
   - Avoid discussing or relying on candidate salary history where prohibited; focus on role-based ranges and market data.

4. Elicit candidate priorities and concerns
   - Ask open-ended questions to surface must-haves (e.g., flexibility, start date, sign-on to offset bonus clawback, visa support).
   - Confirm any competing offers and decision timelines (without pressuring).
   - Document in ATS notes, maintaining professional and non-discriminatory language.

5. Capture and analyze counterproposal
   - Request specifics in writing for clarity: amounts, components, rationale.
   - Compare to:
     - Internal equity for peers at the same level/location.
     - Approved compensation range and budget.
     - Policy limits for sign-on, equity, relocation, and remote arrangements.
   - Consider non-cash alternatives if base salary limit is reached (sign-on with clawback, earlier comp review, additional PTO where policy allows, training budget).

6. Evaluate and secure approvals
   - If within guardrails: recruiter and hiring manager can proceed.
   - If outside guardrails: prepare an exception request including:
     - Justification (business impact, scarcity, competing offers).
     - Equity analysis (parity implications and mitigation).
     - Cost analysis and ongoing budget impact.
   - Route through compensation, HRBP, finance, and possibly executive approvers per approval matrix. Target approval turnaround (e.g., <24 hours for standard exceptions).

7. Revise and formalize terms
   - Update the offer letter template with approved changes; ensure all legal clauses and disclosures are current for the candidate’s jurisdiction.
   - Include any repayment/clawback terms for sign-on, commission guarantees, relocation, or tuition.
   - Verify accuracy of job title, level, reporting line, work location, and contingencies.

8. Communicate revised offer
   - Walk the candidate through changes and trade-offs; reiterate the total rewards narrative and career growth.
   - Set a clear response deadline (commonly 3–5 business days; adjust to market norms and seniority).
   - Provide written FAQs or one-pagers explaining variable pay and equity valuation.

9. Manage decision and close
   - If accepted:
     - Obtain e-signature via approved tool.
     - Update ATS to “Offer Accepted”; attach signed documents.
     - Trigger background check, IT provisioning, and pre-boarding workflows.
   - If countered again:
     - Assess feasibility; limit to reasonable rounds (e.g., max 2–3) to reduce cycle time.
     - Repeat Steps 6–8 as needed.
   - If declined:
     - Capture decline reason categorically and verbatim.
     - Inform hiring manager; decide on next candidate or reopening the search.
     - Log learning for market calibration.

10. Post-negotiation hygiene
    - Record final compensation data in HRIS/comp planning tools.
    - Document exception rationale and approvals for audit and pay equity analysis.
    - Send candidate experience survey.
    - Debrief with hiring manager on what worked/what didn’t; update playbooks.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Outputs:
  - Signed offer letter and any addenda (e.g., sign-on agreement, relocation, confidentiality/IP assignment).
  - Updated ATS status and complete negotiation log.
  - Exception approval records (if any).
  - Triggered pre-boarding and background check tasks.

- Deliverables:
  - Final compensation package details recorded in HRIS.
  - Candidate communication artifacts (emails, FAQs, equity/variable pay explainer).
  - Post-offer notes including decline reasons or competitive intel.

- Success criteria:
  - Offer accepted within target timeframe and within compensation policy.
  - Internal equity preserved; exceptions documented and approved.
  - Positive candidate experience (satisfaction/NPS).
  - Compliance with applicable laws and policies (no violations or rework).

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Recruiter/TA Partner (process owner)
  - Lead negotiation and candidate communications.
  - Ensure policy compliance and documentation in ATS.
  - Coordinate approvals and update offer materials.
- Hiring Manager
  - Define role value proposition and priorities.
  - Partner on negotiation strategy; approve trade-offs within guardrails.
  - Provide timely input on counteroffers.
- Compensation Partner/Total Rewards
  - Provide ranges, market data, and internal equity analysis.
  - Review and approve exceptions; advise on tradables.
- HR Business Partner (HRBP)
  - Advise on organizational impact, equity, and precedent.
  - Support exception rationale and stakeholder alignment.
- Finance
  - Validate budget impact; approve material deviations.
- Legal/Employment Counsel
  - Review offer templates and non-standard terms; ensure compliance with local laws.
- TA Operations/Coordinator
  - Generate offer letters, manage e-signature, trigger background checks.
- Mobility/Immigration (as needed)
  - Scope relocation packages; assess visa feasibility and timelines.
- Candidate
  - Communicate priorities and timelines; review and sign documents; provide necessary information for contingencies.

## Best Practices
- Start early: Pre-close on compensation expectations and key levers before formal offer to reduce negotiation cycles.
- Total rewards storytelling: Emphasize overall value, development, and culture—don’t fixate solely on base salary.
- Set clear guardrails: Define walk-away limits and tradables; avoid ad-hoc concessions that erode equity.
- Pay equity first: Anchor proposals to job architecture and internal parity; review potential ripple effects.
- Transparency and compliance: Share pay ranges where required; avoid salary history questions where prohibited.
- Speed with discipline: Target fast turnarounds on approvals while maintaining documented oversight.
- Limit rounds: Aim for no more than 2–3 negotiation iterations to maintain momentum.
- Offer calculators and explainers: Provide clear documentation on equity/variable compensation to reduce confusion.
- Document everything: Keep a clean audit trail in the ATS, including reasons for exceptions and declines.
- Candidate experience: Be respectful, responsive, and flexible where possible; set realistic deadlines without undue pressure.

## Common Challenges
- Internal equity vs. market pressure
  - Solution: Use structured exceptions with mitigation plans (e.g., planned market adjustment cycles); consider non-cash levers.
- Competing offers and exploding deadlines
  - Solution: Accelerate internal approvals; provide decision support materials; involve hiring leader early.
- Geo and remote work complexities
  - Solution: Apply geo-differentials consistently; clarify expectations and time zone requirements in the offer.
- Visa or relocation constraints
  - Solution: Engage immigration/mobility early; offer interim remote work if feasible; communicate timelines transparently.
- Misunderstanding of equity/variable comp
  - Solution: Provide plain-language explainers and scenarios; offer live walkthroughs.
- Budget caps
  - Solution: Trade sign-on bonuses or additional PTO where policy allows; revisit scope/level if justified.
- Counteroffers from current employer
  - Solution: Reinforce non-monetary value proposition; avoid bidding wars that cause inequity; set clear walk-away points.
- Delayed approvals
  - Solution: Use pre-defined approval matrices and SLAs; establish escalation channels; leverage automated workflows.
- Legal/compliance risks (e.g., pay transparency, salary history bans)
  - Solution: Train recruiters; use jurisdiction-specific templates and prompts within ATS.

## Performance Metrics
- Offer acceptance rate (overall, by role level, and by demographic group).
- Time-to-accept (from initial offer to signed acceptance).
- Number of negotiation rounds per offer.
- Approval cycle time for exceptions.
- Percent of offers within band vs. requiring exceptions.
- Cost of concessions per hire (sign-on, equity top-ups) and ongoing comp impact.
- Internal pay parity variance post-hire (e.g., standard deviation vs. peers).
- Candidate satisfaction/NPS post-offer.
- First-year retention of negotiated hires.
- Decline reasons distribution and competitive loss rate.
- Compliance incidents related to offers (target = zero).

## Technology and Tools
- Applicant Tracking System (ATS): Greenhouse, Lever, Workday Recruiting, SmartRecruiters for offer workflows, notes, and status tracking.
- Compensation tools: Market data (Radford, Mercer, Payscale), pay equity analytics (Syndio, PayScale Payfactors), internal comp planning tools.
- Document and e-signature: DocuSign, Adobe Acrobat Sign; jurisdiction-specific offer templates in a template library.
- Collaboration and workflow: Slack/Teams channels for rapid approvals; workflow automation (ServiceNow, Jira) to route exceptions.
- Background screening: Checkr, HireRight; integrate triggers post-acceptance.
- Equity administration: Carta, Shareworks for modeling and grant documentation.
- Mobility/immigration: Relocation vendors; immigration counsel management tools.
- Reporting/BI: HR analytics dashboards (Power BI, Tableau) tracking KPIs; ATS native analytics.
- Knowledge base/LMS: Playbooks, negotiation guides, and policy training modules.

This documentation is intended to guide consistent, fair, and compliant offer negotiations that balance business needs with candidate expectations while preserving a strong employer brand and organizational equity.

Process Details:
## Overview
Evaluate the effectiveness of the employee onboarding program is a continuous, evidence-based process that measures how well onboarding accelerates new-hire productivity, engagement, compliance, and retention. It gathers quantitative and qualitative data from new hires, managers, and stakeholders at multiple points in time; analyzes outcomes against goals; identifies improvement opportunities; and drives iterative enhancements to onboarding content, delivery, and supporting processes. This process ensures onboarding is aligned to business strategy, provides a consistent experience across roles and locations, and delivers measurable value (e.g., reduced time-to-productivity and early attrition).

Primary objectives:
- Validate whether onboarding achieves defined learning, behavioral, and business outcomes.
- Identify experience gaps, process bottlenecks, and root causes impacting new-hire success.
- Prioritize and implement improvements; confirm impact through re-measurement.
- Ensure fairness, accessibility, and compliance in onboarding.

Scope includes all onboarding modalities (preboarding, Day 1, first week, 30/60/90-day ramp), audiences (employees, interns, contractors where applicable), and delivery channels (in-person, virtual, hybrid).

## Key Activities
- Define evaluation strategy and success criteria aligned to onboarding goals and business outcomes.
- Design and maintain measurement instruments (surveys, interview guides, assessments, observation checklists).
- Establish data collection cadence (preboarding, Day 7, Day 30/60/90, Month 6) and sampling plan.
- Collect data from multiple sources: HRIS, LMS, ITSM, surveys, interviews, focus groups, performance systems.
- Analyze quantitative and qualitative data; conduct driver analysis and benchmarking.
- Produce findings and recommendations; maintain an improvements backlog with owners and timelines.
- Socialize results with stakeholders; close the loop with new hires and managers.
- Implement prioritized improvements; run pilots/A-B tests where feasible.
- Monitor and re-measure to confirm impact; update governance, standards, and artifacts.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Onboarding program design and curriculum (objectives, content map, delivery methods).
- New-hire cohorts and metadata (role, location, business unit, employment type, remote/on-site).
- Access to systems data: HRIS (start dates, attrition), LMS (course completions), ITSM (ticket volumes), provisioning status, performance checkpoints, helpdesk data.
- Existing feedback instruments and historical benchmarks.
- Policies on data privacy, confidentiality, consent, and retention.

Prerequisites:
- Clear onboarding goals and target KPIs (e.g., time-to-productivity target, 90-day retention).
- Stakeholder alignment and sponsorship (HR, L&D, IT, Security, Compliance, People Managers).
- Data access agreements and governance (GDPR/CCPA compliance; anonymity thresholds).
- Communication plan for soliciting feedback from new hires and managers.

Dependencies on other processes:
- 7.3.1.1 Design and deliver onboarding (content and process must exist to evaluate).
- 7.3.1.3 Improve onboarding program (uses evaluation outputs to implement changes).
- 7.3 Manage employee onboarding, training, and development (link to learning pathways).
- 7.2 Recruit employees (handoff data from ATS; preboarding touchpoints).
- IT provisioning, facilities access, security/compliance training processes.

## Process Steps
1. Define purpose and scope
   - Confirm evaluation objectives (e.g., accelerate productivity, reduce 90-day attrition).
   - Select framework(s): Kirkpatrick Levels 1–4 and Phillips ROI for economic impact.
   - Determine in-scope cohorts, geographies, roles, and timeline.

2. Establish success metrics and targets
   - Finalize KPIs and formulas (e.g., time-to-productivity definition by role).
   - Set baseline and targets using historical and external benchmarks.

3. Design the evaluation plan
   - Determine data sources, collection methods, cadences, and sample sizes.
   - Draft instruments: pulse surveys, manager check-in templates, interview guides.
   - Define segmentation for analysis (role, location, function, remote/hybrid, tenure).
   - Address ethics, anonymity, consent language, and data retention.

4. Build and test instruments
   - Configure survey and analytics tools; enable multi-language and accessibility.
   - Pilot with a small cohort; perform reliability checks and refine questions.

5. Execute data collection
   - Automate invitations and reminders aligned to milestones (Day 1, 7, 30/60/90, 180).
   - Capture operational data (LMS completions, IT provisioning SLAs, ticket volumes).
   - Conduct periodic interviews/focus groups with new hires, managers, and buddies.
   - Log issues and qualitative feedback in a centralized repository.

6. Analyze and synthesize
   - Perform descriptive stats, trend analysis, and cohort comparisons.
   - Run driver analysis to identify factors most correlated with outcomes (e.g., manager 1:1s with time-to-productivity).
   - Thematically code qualitative data; use text analytics for scale.
   - Triangulate findings across data sources; identify root causes and quick wins vs. systemic issues.

7. Benchmark and assess ROI
   - Compare results to internal historical performance and external benchmarks.
   - Calculate ROI/benefit: reduced ramp time, decreased early attrition, fewer IT tickets, etc.

8. Report and communicate
   - Produce an executive summary, dashboards, deep-dive analyses, and cohort heatmaps.
   - Share tailored insights with HR leadership, business leaders, managers, and enablement teams.
   - Close the loop with new hires: “You said, we did” communications.

9. Prioritize and plan improvements
   - Create an improvement backlog with value/effort scoring.
   - Assign owners, timelines, and success metrics for each initiative.
   - Integrate with change control and content governance processes.

10. Implement and monitor changes
   - Pilot improvements with select cohorts; use A/B testing where applicable.
   - Track leading indicators and re-measure impacted KPIs.
   - Document updates to onboarding content, playbooks, and checklists.

11. Governance and continual improvement
   - Review cadence (e.g., monthly operational review, quarterly strategic review).
   - Refresh instruments annually; recalibrate targets as the organization evolves.
   - Audit data quality, privacy compliance, and accessibility adherence.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Onboarding effectiveness report (executive summary, insights, recommendations).
- Live dashboards and scorecards (KPIs by cohort, trends, drill-downs).
- Improvements backlog with owners, timelines, and expected impact.
- Updated onboarding content, workflows, and manager enablement materials.
- Updated measurement instruments and standard operating procedures.
- Communication artifacts for stakeholders and new-hire feedback loops.
- Data dictionary and methodology documentation.

Success criteria:
- KPI targets met or trending positively (e.g., decreased time-to-productivity, improved 90-day retention).
- Clear, implemented improvements with measurable impact.
- Sustained or improved response rates and data quality.
- Stakeholder satisfaction with insights and actionability.
- Compliance with privacy and accessibility standards.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Onboarding Program Owner: Sponsors process, sets goals, approves changes, ensures cross-functional alignment.
- People Analytics/HR Analytics: Designs methodology, analyzes data, builds dashboards, conducts driver analysis.
- L&D/Onboarding Design Team: Updates content and learning paths based on findings; ensures alignment to competencies.
- HRIS/IT Analytics: Provides system data feeds, ensures data quality and integrations, maintains tooling.
- People Managers: Complete check-ins, provide feedback on new-hire ramp, support interventions.
- New Hires: Provide timely feedback via surveys/interviews; participate in pilots.
- Buddy/Mentor Leads: Offer qualitative insights; reinforce onboarding practices.
- Compliance/Legal/Privacy: Review instruments and processes for regulatory compliance; oversee consent and retention.
- DEI/Accessibility: Review for inclusivity, fairness, language/localization, and accessibility.
- Communications/Change Management: Craft messages, drive participation, manage “you said, we did.”

## Best Practices
- Use a mixed-methods approach: combine surveys, system data, interviews, and observation.
- Apply Kirkpatrick Levels 1–4 and Phillips ROI to connect learning to business outcomes.
- Measure longitudinally with pulses at key milestones (Day 1, 7, 30/60/90, 180).
- Segment analyses to uncover inequities and context-specific needs (role, region, remote).
- Ensure anonymity and confidentiality; enforce minimum n-size thresholds for reporting.
- Design concise, mobile-first surveys; limit to 3–7 minutes; rotate question banks to reduce fatigue.
- Tie evaluation to a clear logic model: inputs → activities → outputs → outcomes → impact.
- Automate data collection via HRIS/LMS/ITSM integrations; reduce manual effort and errors.
- Run pilots and A/B tests before global rollouts; use control cohorts where feasible.
- Close the loop: share actions taken and outcomes to build trust and increase response rates.
- Maintain a single source of truth for metrics definitions and methodology.
- Ensure accessibility (WCAG compliance) and localization for global populations.
- Enable managers with toolkits for effective check-ins and ramp plans; measure their adherence.
- Protect data privacy (GDPR/CCPA), obtain consent, and follow retention schedules.

## Common Challenges
- Low response rates: address with clear purpose messaging, mobile-friendly surveys, reminders, and manager advocacy; consider non-monetary incentives.
- Survey fatigue: use micro-pulses, rotate items, and leverage operational data to reduce asks.
- Attribution and confounders: use control groups, staged rollouts, and multivariate analysis.
- Small cohort sizes: aggregate across time/roles; use rolling windows; apply Bayesian or bootstrapped estimates cautiously.
- Data fragmentation: integrate systems; standardize identifiers; maintain a data dictionary.
- Inconsistent manager participation: set expectations, track adherence KPIs, provide training and nudges.
- Global and cultural differences: localize content; adapt cadence and channels; ensure translation quality.
- Qualitative data at scale: use text analytics for theming; validate with human review.
- Privacy and trust concerns: clearly communicate anonymity; apply reporting thresholds and secure storage.

## Performance Metrics
Experience and learning:
- New Hire Onboarding Satisfaction (average rating, CSAT).
- New Hire eNPS/NPS.
- Perceived Role Clarity and Confidence to Perform (Likert scales).
- Manager Satisfaction with New Hire Readiness.
- Training completion rates by due dates.

Operational and productivity:
- Time-to-Productivity: days from start to predefined productivity threshold per role.
- Ramp Plan Adherence: completion of 30/60/90-day milestones.
- Provisioning SLA adherence: time to laptop/account/access completion.
- Help desk tickets per new hire in first 30/60 days.
- Manager 1:1 completion rate in first 8 weeks.

Retention and quality:
- 30/90-day retention; 6- and 12-month regrettable attrition rate.
- First-year performance distribution vs. tenured peers.
- First-year internal mobility or progression (where relevant).
- Compliance completion rates (mandatory training) and audit findings.

Economic impact:
- ROI of onboarding improvements: (Benefits – Costs) / Costs.
- Cost of early attrition: (replacement cost + lost productivity) avoided vs. baseline.

Equity and accessibility:
- Experience and outcome parity across segments (role, location, demographic groups), respecting privacy thresholds.

Target setting:
- Establish baselines and annual improvement targets (e.g., 10% reduction in time-to-productivity; 3–5 point increase in eNPS).

## Technology and Tools
- HRIS/HCM: Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM (cohorts, transfers, attrition).
- ATS: Greenhouse, Workday Recruiting (handoff to preboarding).
- LMS/LXP: Cornerstone, Docebo, Degreed (training assignments and completions).
- Survey/VoE: Qualtrics, Medallia, Culture Amp, Glint (pulses, text analytics).
- Analytics and BI: Power BI, Tableau, Looker; statistical tools (R, Python) for advanced analysis.
- Collaboration and flow-of-work: Microsoft Teams, Slack (embedded pulses, nudges).
- ITSM/Provisioning: ServiceNow, Jira Service Management (access and device SLAs, ticket data).
- Digital Adoption Platforms: WalkMe, Pendo (in-app guidance and usage analytics).
- Knowledge base/Portals: SharePoint, Confluence, intranet hubs (content access metrics).
- Integration/Middleware: iPaaS (MuleSoft, Boomi) to automate data flows; RPA for reminders/data pulls where needed.
- Data governance and privacy: DLP tools, access controls, secure data lakes; consent management.

# 7.3.1.3 Execute Onboarding Program

## Overview
Execute Onboarding Program brings the organization’s onboarding design to life for each new employee. It operationalizes the onboarding plan defined in Create/Maintain Onboarding Program by coordinating people, systems, training, equipment, and engagement activities from pre-boarding through the first 90 days. The process ensures new hires are welcomed, provisioned, oriented to the company and role, trained for compliance and productivity, integrated socially, and supported through early performance milestones.

Purpose:
- Reduce time-to-productivity and enable a consistent, high-quality new hire experience.
- Meet legal, regulatory, and policy requirements (e.g., right-to-work, data privacy, safety).
- Embed culture, values, and ways of working.
- Establish early performance expectations and support structures (manager, buddy, mentors).

Role in the organization:
- Bridges talent acquisition and ongoing performance management.
- Coordinates cross-functional fulfillment (HR, IT, Facilities, Security, L&D, Payroll/Benefits, Compliance).
- Provides data and feedback to improve onboarding design and workforce planning.

## Key Activities
- Pre-boarding coordination and communications.
- Provisioning of access, equipment, workspace/badging.
- Day-1 welcome and corporate orientation.
- Role-specific onboarding and training plan execution.
- Assignment and enablement of buddy/mentor and manager check-ins.
- Compliance and policy training, acknowledgements, and documentation.
- Social and cultural integration, including ERG introductions and engagement events.
- Progress monitoring, issue resolution, and escalation.
- Feedback collection and continuous improvement loop.
- Reporting on completion, satisfaction, and time-to-productivity.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Signed offer/contract and start date.
- New hire profile in HRIS (personal data, job, location, manager, cost center).
- Background check/eligibility to work clearance; immigration approvals (if applicable).
- Onboarding program templates and curricula (corporate and role-based).
- Role/location-specific provisioning profiles (applications, hardware, facilities, training).
- Training assignments in LMS; compliance requirements by jurisdiction/function.
- 30-60-90 day role plan draft from hiring manager.
- Policies requiring acknowledgment (Code of Conduct, InfoSec, Privacy, Safety, etc.).
- Payroll and benefits enrollment windows and packets.

Prerequisites:
- “Create/Maintain Employee Onboarding Program” completed and approved, including content, schedule, and SLAs.
- Defined ownership: onboarding coordinator, hiring manager, L&D partner.
- Active vendor contracts for background checks, equipment, e-signature, etc.
- Data privacy and security controls in place for handling new hire data.
- Budget approvals for equipment, travel, relocation (if applicable).

Dependencies on other processes:
- Recruit and Hire Employees (offer acceptance, pre-employment checks).
- Provision IT/Facilities/Security Access (ITSM/IAM workflows).
- Administer Payroll and Benefits (enrollment setup).
- Manage Compliance and Risk (policy, regulatory training).
- Manage Employee Orientation and Deployment (parent process).
- Manage Employee Records (document retention and HRIS updates).

## Process Steps
1) Trigger and Intake (T-10 to T-5 business days)
- HRIS creates hire record; onboarding workflow auto-initiates.
- Onboarding coordinator validates start date, location, manager, and provisioning profile.
- Send welcome and pre-boarding email with portal access, schedule, and to-do list.

2) Pre-boarding Setup
- Identity and Access:
  - IAM pre-provisions accounts (email, SSO) with start-date activation.
  - IT assigns standard and role-based application entitlements.
- Equipment and Workspace:
  - IT orders devices and peripherals; Asset Mgmt tags and ships or stages pickup.
  - Facilities/Security set up desk, badge, parking, remote shipping logistics.
- Compliance Preparation:
  - Assign background/eligibility verification follow-ups as needed.
  - Prepare policy packets and I-9/RTW verification appointments (jurisdiction-specific).
- Training Assignments:
  - L&D assigns mandatory corporate and role-specific modules in LMS; set due dates aligned to SLA.
- Manager Readiness:
  - Manager finalizes 30-60-90 day plan, initial objectives, and first-week schedule.
  - Assign buddy/mentor and brief them on expectations.
- Communication and Engagement:
  - Send “What to expect Day 1,” IT setup instructions, benefits overview, and manager intro message.
  - Offer pre-start social touchpoint (team intro note or virtual coffee).

3) Day-1 Orientation
- Welcome session (live or virtual): company mission/values, org overview, policies, DEI, ERG introductions.
- Complete immediate admin tasks: I-9/RTW verification, tax forms, data privacy consent, direct deposit.
- IT activation: first login, MFA setup, workstation setup, collaboration tools orientation.
- Safety/information security briefings and required acknowledgements.
- Manager 1:1: role overview, team intro, review first-week plan, expectations, and communication norms.

4) First-Week Onboarding
- Corporate Training: begin compliance modules (ethics, security, privacy, safety) per timeline.
- Role-Specific Training: job tools, systems walkthrough, SOPs, shadowing schedule.
- Social Integration: team lunch/coffee, buddy check-ins, introductions to key stakeholders.
- Operational Readiness Checks: verify access works; resolve helpdesk tickets within SLA.
- Benefits Orientation: group session or guided self-enrollment with Q&A.
- Status Check: end-of-week pulse survey; onboarding coordinator reviews completion data and flags gaps.

5) Weeks 2–4 Ramp-Up
- Applied Learning: small tasks or simulations; supervised practice on core responsibilities.
- Ongoing Training: advanced role modules, process deep-dives; schedule assessments if required.
- Performance Foundations: finalize objectives and key results; confirm success metrics.
- Manager Touchpoints: weekly 1:1s; buddy check-ins 2–3x/week initially.
- Engagement: intro to communities of practice, ERGs, volunteering opportunities.
- Issue Management: track and resolve blockers; escalate cross-functional delays.

6) Months 2–3 Integration
- Increased Autonomy: assign end-to-end tasks; track quality, cycle time, and rework.
- Compliance Wrap-Up: ensure all mandatory trainings completed; capture attestations.
- Feedback and Coaching: 30- and 60-day surveys; manager provides structured feedback.
- Development Planning: discuss learning pathways and career plan; enroll in next modules.
- 90-Day Review: assess ramp milestones; confirm fit; adjust objectives; decide on probation status (where relevant).

7) Closure and Handover (end of onboarding period)
- Verify all deliverables complete (checklist signed by manager and onboarding coordinator).
- Archive documentation in HRIS/Document Mgmt per retention rules.
- Transition ownership to ongoing performance management and L&D for continuous development.
- Conduct after-action review; log lessons learned to improve program content and flow.

Controls and checkpoints embedded:
- Access provisioning SLAs (e.g., hardware ready by Day 1, all access within 48 hours).
- Mandatory training completion timelines (e.g., security within 7 days).
- Compliance verification points (I-9 within 3 days in U.S., equivalents elsewhere).
- Satisfaction and readiness checkpoints at Day 7, 30, 60, 90.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Provisioned access and equipment; workspace/badge active.
- Completed and recorded mandatory trainings with certificates/attestations.
- Signed policy acknowledgements and employment documents filed.
- 30-60-90 day plan and initial objectives captured in performance system.
- New hire and manager satisfaction survey results.
- Issue/ticket logs with resolution statuses.
- Onboarding completion checklist and report.
Success criteria:
- New hire productive on core tasks within target ramp time.
- 100% completion of mandatory training and policy acknowledgements within SLA.
- Access and equipment delivered by Day 1; minimal critical blockers.
- Positive new hire NPS and manager satisfaction threshold met.
- Compliance and audit requirements satisfied; no high-risk exceptions.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Onboarding Coordinator (HR/People Ops):
  - Owns end-to-end execution, timeline, and cross-functional coordination.
  - Monitors progress, manages communications, resolves/escalates issues, reports outcomes.
- Hiring Manager:
  - Defines role expectations, 30-60-90 plan, schedule; conducts regular 1:1s and feedback.
  - Requests non-standard access/equipment; ensures team integration and job readiness.
- Buddy/Mentor:
  - Provides day-to-day context, informal support, culture/ways-of-working guidance.
- IT Service Desk/End-User Computing:
  - Provisions hardware/software; enables accounts; supports setup and troubleshooting.
- Identity and Access Management (IAM):
  - Grants role-based access; enforces least privilege; audits access.
- Facilities and Security:
  - Prepares workspace; issues badges/parking; conducts safety orientation (onsite).
- Learning & Development (L&D):
  - Assigns curricula; tracks training; facilitates orientation; adapts content.
- Payroll and Benefits:
  - Ensures enrollment readiness; supports new hire sign-ups and queries.
- Legal/Compliance/Privacy:
  - Provides policy content; validates regulatory training; audits documentation.
- HRIS Administrator:
  - Maintains workflows, data integrity, notifications, and reporting.
- New Hire:
  - Completes tasks and trainings; sets up tools; seeks support; provides feedback.

## Best Practices
- Start early: pre-boarding begins upon acceptance with clear instructions and a single onboarding portal.
- Personalize: tailor content and provisioning by role, location, seniority, and work arrangement (onsite/remote/hybrid).
- Make managers accountable: track manager activities (plan, check-ins) with nudges and dashboards.
- Assign a buddy: proven to increase engagement and speed up ramp.
- Use modular, blended learning: microlearning, self-paced modules, and live practice; avoid information overload.
- Map “moments that matter”: Day 1, first week, first deliverable, first feedback, first social connection.
- Ensure accessibility and inclusion: WCAG-compliant content; closed captions; time-zone considerate scheduling.
- Automate provisioning: integrate HRIS, IAM, ITSM, LMS to reduce manual work and errors.
- Track compliance systematically: automatic assignments, due dates, reminders, and escalation paths.
- Provide a clear checklist for new hires and managers; visible progress tracker.
- Collect and act on feedback at 7/30/60/90 days; A/B test improvements.
- Measure outcomes, not just completions: tie onboarding to performance and retention metrics.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Delayed access or equipment:
  - Solution: auto-trigger tasks at T-10; enforce SLAs; maintain buffer inventory; provide loaners; proactive status dashboard.
- Information overload:
  - Solution: stagger content; use microlearning; prioritize just-in-time materials and searchable knowledge base.
- Inconsistent manager engagement:
  - Solution: manager enablement training; automated nudges; escalate non-compliance; tie to manager KPIs.
- Remote/hybrid onboarding gaps:
  - Solution: virtual orientation kits, welcome videos, structured virtual social events; ship equipment early; remote-friendly schedules.
- Compliance tracking gaps:
  - Solution: LMS integration with HRIS; mandatory gating for system access when legally permissible; audit trails.
- Data inaccuracies in HRIS:
  - Solution: validate data at intake; automate feeds from ATS; ownership for data stewardship and corrections.
- Cross-functional coordination breakdowns:
  - Solution: RACI clarity; weekly onboarding standup; shared Kanban/board; named single-threaded owner.
- Global and local policy misalignment:
  - Solution: global baseline with localized variants; content tagging by country; legal review cadence.
- New hire disengagement or early attrition:
  - Solution: buddy system, early impactful wins, frequent check-ins, clear expectations, visible career pathways.

## Performance Metrics
- Time-to-Productivity: days to complete first independent core task or hit defined performance threshold.
- Provisioning SLA Adherence: % of new hires with all required access/equipment by Day 1.
- Training Completion Rate and Timeliness: % completed within SLA; overdue counts.
- New Hire NPS/Satisfaction: at Day 7/30/90.
- Manager Satisfaction with Readiness: survey rating at Day 30/60.
- First-90/180/365-Day Retention: attrition rates compared to baseline.
- Ticket Volume and Resolution Time per New Hire: IT/HR support load.
- Onboarding Defect Rate: % of cohorts with critical issues (e.g., missing access, missed I-9).
- Buddy/Manager Engagement Metrics: % of required check-ins completed on time.
- Cost per Onboard: total execution cost per new hire.

## Technology and Tools
- HRIS/HCM: Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM, BambooHR.
- ATS integration: Greenhouse, Lever (for seamless data transfer).
- Workflow/ITSM: ServiceNow, Jira Service Management for task orchestration and SLAs.
- IAM/SSO: Okta, Azure AD; role-based access control and lifecycle management.
- LMS/LXP: Cornerstone, Docebo, Degreed for training delivery and tracking.
- Collaboration/Comms: Microsoft Teams, Slack, Zoom for meetings and communities.
- E-signature and Forms: DocuSign, Adobe Sign for policy acknowledgements and forms.
- Asset and Facilities Mgmt: JAMF/Intune for device mgmt; Envoy/Proxyclick for visitor/badge; space management tools.
- Document/Knowledge Management: SharePoint, Confluence for guides and checklists.
- Survey/Feedback: Qualtrics, CultureAmp for pulse checks and NPS.
- Analytics/Dashboards: Power BI, Tableau; HRIS/LMS native analytics for KPI tracking.
- Security and Compliance: DLP, endpoint protection, training content libraries; I-9 systems/E-Verify (US) and local equivalents.

Process Details:
## Overview
Define employee performance objectives is the foundational process that translates organizational strategy into clear, measurable goals for each employee. It ensures individual efforts align with enterprise, business unit, and team priorities while clarifying expectations, success measures, and development focus areas. Well-defined objectives drive execution, enable fair and consistent performance evaluation, support compensation and career decisions, and enhance engagement by making work meaningful and achievable.

This process applies to all employee types (full-time, part-time, temporary, and contingent as applicable) and is executed at the start of each performance cycle, upon role changes, and for new hires within their first 30–60 days.

## Key Activities
- Establish objective framework and calendar: Define categories (e.g., business results, customer, operational excellence, growth/development), weights, and deadlines.
- Cascade goals: Translate enterprise and department goals into team and role-specific objectives.
- Draft objectives: Manager and employee co-create SMART/OKR-style objectives with metrics and targets.
- Define measures and weights: Select KPIs, set baselines/targets, assign relative weights.
- Include competencies/behaviors: Add values-based and role-specific behavioral expectations.
- Align cross-functionally: Resolve interdependencies and prevent conflicting objectives.
- Approve and document: Route for approvals, finalize in the performance system, and confirm sign-off.
- Communicate and schedule check-ins: Share final objectives and plan recurring reviews.
- Monitor and revise: Manage controlled updates for material business changes.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs:
  - Organizational strategy and annual priorities
  - Department/team KPIs and budget/operating plan
  - Job description and competency framework
  - Prior-year performance data and development needs
  - Regulatory/contractual requirements (e.g., SLAs, union agreements)
  - Data sources for measurement (CRM, ERP, CSAT/NPS, financial systems)
- Prerequisites:
  - Defined performance cycle timeline, policies, and rating framework
  - Access to performance management system and goal library/template
  - Manager and employee trained on goal-setting methodology
- Dependencies on other processes:
  - Workforce planning and job design (role clarity)
  - Manage employee onboarding (for new hires’ initial objectives)
  - Manage compensation and rewards (alignment with incentives)
  - Manage employee performance program governance (calibration, policies)
  - Learning and development (development objectives/resources)

## Process Steps
1. Initiate the cycle
   - HR publishes the annual (or cycle) goal-setting calendar, objective categories, weighting guidance, and policy updates.
   - Performance system is configured (templates, workflows, deadlines).

2. Gather inputs
   - Manager reviews enterprise and department priorities, budget/targets, and team KPIs.
   - Employee reviews job responsibilities, prior feedback, and career aspirations.

3. Draft initial objectives
   - Manager proposes 3–6 result-oriented objectives and 1–3 development objectives.
   - Employee drafts/refines proposals, including stretch goals where appropriate.
   - Use SMART or OKR format:
     - Objective: qualitative aim aligned to strategy
     - Key results: 3–5 quantifiable outcomes (targets, dates)
     - Weighting: allocate total 100% across objectives

4. Define measures and targets
   - Specify metrics (leading and lagging), baselines, and data sources.
   - Set target ranges (threshold, target, stretch) and due dates/milestones.
   - Verify controllability (employee can meaningfully influence at least 70–80%).

5. Add behavioral and compliance expectations
   - Select 3–5 core competencies/values with clear behavioral indicators.
   - Include mandated compliance or safety objectives if applicable.

6. Align and resolve dependencies
   - Validate upstream/downstream dependencies with partner teams (e.g., Sales ↔ Operations).
   - Resolve conflicting targets; adjust weights and timelines as needed.

7. Risk and resource assessment
   - Document key risks, assumptions, and required resources/support.
   - Note cross-functional commitments (RACI where relevant).

8. Quality check and calibration
   - Manager applies a goal quality rubric (clarity, alignment, measurability, balance, feasibility).
   - Leaders/HR conduct calibration meetings to ensure consistency across teams.

9. Approvals and sign-off
   - Route in system to employee → manager → next-level leader (as required) → HR review for policy/compliance.
   - Capture electronic sign-offs and lock objectives for the cycle.

10. Communicate and plan cadence
    - Manager reviews final objectives with the employee, clarifies success criteria and check-in cadence (e.g., monthly/quarterly).
    - Schedule mid-year review and set alerts for milestones.

11. Baseline and monitor
    - Capture baseline values for each metric and confirm data feeds/reporting views.
    - Start tracking progress; document updates in check-ins.

12. Manage changes (if needed)
    - For material business changes, submit a change request documenting rationale, impact on weights/targets, and approval path.
    - Maintain version history and audit trail.

Edge cases:
- New hires mid-cycle: set provisional objectives within 30 days; proportionally weight to remaining cycle; emphasize onboarding/development.
- Role transfer/manager change: review and reapprove objectives within 30 days.
- Leave of absence: freeze objectives; adjust targets/weights upon return per policy.
- Collective bargaining/works council contexts: follow local consultation/approval procedures.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Individual performance plan: finalized list of objectives, key results, measures, weights, timelines, and competencies.
- Alignment map: linkage of individual objectives to team/department/enterprise goals.
- Check-in plan: cadence, milestone dates, and reporting views.
- Approval records: signatures, calibration notes, and change logs.
- Goal library updates: new or refined objectives templates for reuse.

Success criteria:
- Objectives are SMART/OKR-quality, balanced across categories, and approved on time.
- Clear line-of-sight to organizational goals.
- Data sources are defined and accessible for each metric.
- Employee and manager confirm shared understanding of expectations.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Employee
  - Co-create objectives, propose development goals, validate data sources, and commit to cadence.
- People Manager
  - Translate strategy to role objectives, ensure quality/feasibility, align cross-functionally, conduct reviews, and approve.
- Department/Function Leader
  - Provide cascading goals, resolve cross-team conflicts, set weighting norms, and lead calibration.
- HR Business Partner (HRBP)
  - Advise on design and alignment, ensure policy compliance, facilitate calibration, and coach managers.
- Learning & Development (L&D)
  - Provide development frameworks/resources and integrate learning plans with objectives.
- Total Rewards/Compensation
  - Align objectives with incentive plans, define payout mechanics, and ensure pay equity considerations.
- Legal/Compliance (incl. Works Council where applicable)
  - Ensure objectives meet legal/regulatory and collective agreement requirements.
- Performance System Administrator
  - Configure workflows, templates, permissions; manage audit logs and reporting.
- PMO/Strategy Office
  - Supply enterprise KPIs and priorities; support cascading and alignment mapping.
- Data/Analytics
  - Validate measurement definitions, baselines, and dashboards.

## Best Practices
- Use a balanced scorecard approach: include financial, customer, process/quality, and learning/development objectives.
- Limit to 4–6 primary objectives; avoid dilution.
- Ensure 70–80% of objectives are within the employee’s influence; use shared goals sparingly with clear accountability.
- Apply SMART/OKR rigor; define target ranges and unambiguous measurement methods.
- Weight objectives (e.g., 60–80% results; 20–40% behavioral/development based on role).
- Calibrate early: hold team calibration sessions before final approvals.
- Build a goal template library by role family; reuse to drive consistency.
- Tie development goals to specific skills/competencies with concrete learning activities and application milestones.
- Define change-control rules for in-year updates; maintain version history.
- Train managers on bias mitigation and inclusive goal-setting; use clear, non-discriminatory language.
- Integrate data sources and dashboards so progress is transparent and low-effort to track.
- Schedule recurring check-ins; treat goals as living commitments, not annual paperwork.

## Common Challenges
- Vague or unmeasurable goals
  - Solution: Use a goal-quality rubric, require metrics, and review by HRBP before approval.
- Misalignment or conflicting cross-team objectives
  - Solution: Run alignment workshops; use RACI and leader arbitration; standardize shared KPIs.
- Too many objectives
  - Solution: Enforce limits and weights; prioritize by impact and capacity.
- Gaming or perverse incentives
  - Solution: Use balanced metrics and target ranges; include qualitative assessment and behaviors.
- Data gaps or unreliable measures
  - Solution: Define data owners and sources; create interim proxies; invest in reporting integration.
- Mid-cycle business changes
  - Solution: Change-control process with documented rationale; adjust weights rather than add more goals.
- Low employee buy-in
  - Solution: Co-creation, transparency on how goals affect rewards/career, and regular feedback loops.
- Global/legal constraints (e.g., works councils)
  - Solution: Localize processes, consult early, and adhere to documentation and notice requirements.

## Performance Metrics
- On-time completion rate of objective setting (org, department, manager)
- Goal quality score (rubric-based) and percentage meeting SMART criteria
- Alignment rate (objectives mapped to enterprise/department goals)
- Average number of objectives per employee and weighting balance
- Percentage of objectives with defined data sources/baselines
- Mid-year and quarterly check-in adherence
- Revision rate and time-to-approve change requests
- Cross-functional conflict incidence and time-to-resolution
- Employee understanding and confidence (survey item scores)
- Variance in goal difficulty across teams (calibration dispersion)
- Correlation of objective attainment to business outcomes and incentive payouts
- Audit/compliance findings and legal disputes related to performance objectives
- Equity indicators (no adverse impact across demographics in goal difficulty or outcomes)

## Technology and Tools
- Performance management platforms: Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM, UKG, BambooHR, Lattice, 15Five
- OKR/goal platforms: Microsoft Viva Goals (Ally.io), Quantive (Gtmhub), Perdoo
- Analytics and BI: Power BI, Tableau, Looker for KPI dashboards and baselining
- Data sources: CRM (Salesforce), ERP (SAP/Oracle), service/CS tools (Zendesk), financial systems, data warehouse
- Collaboration and documentation: Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Slack/Teams for reviews and approvals
- Survey/engagement: Qualtrics, Culture Amp for understanding and buy-in metrics
- Learning systems: LMS/LXP (Cornerstone, Degreed) linked to development objectives
- Access/security: SSO, role-based access controls, audit logs, and data retention configurations

Implementation notes:
- Configure templates by role family with pre-defined objective examples and measures.
- Enable alignment mapping in the system to visualize cascades and dependencies.
- Automate reminders for deadlines and check-ins; surface progress widgets on manager dashboards.
- Maintain an auditable history of changes and approvals for legal defensibility.

Process Details:
# 7.3.2.2 Review Employee Performance

## Overview
Review Employee Performance is the cyclical process of assessing employees against agreed goals, competencies, and behavioral expectations, providing actionable feedback, and documenting outcomes. Its purpose is to improve individual and team performance, inform development and career decisions, and supply reliable inputs to related processes (e.g., learning and development, succession, rewards). It operates as part of the broader performance management framework and typically includes both frequent check-ins and more formal mid-year/annual reviews.

Effective performance reviews:
- Align individuals to organizational objectives
- Reinforce expected behaviors and culture
- Identify strengths, development needs, and potential
- Drive accountability and continuous improvement
- Provide defensible, consistent documentation for decisions

## Key Activities
- Cycle planning and communication (timelines, forms, rating scales)
- Gathering performance evidence (self-assessments, manager assessments, 360 feedback, objective metrics)
- Conducting regular check-ins (monthly/quarterly) and formal reviews (mid-year/annual)
- Performance rating and narrative feedback creation
- Calibration to ensure consistency and mitigate bias
- Review meetings between manager and employee
- Documentation, acknowledgment, and record retention
- Post-review follow-up (development plans, goals, coaching, PIPs if needed)
- Quality assurance and audit by HR
- Reporting and insights for leadership

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Current goals/objectives/OKRs with weightings and success criteria
- Role profile/job description and competency framework
- Performance evidence: KPIs, project outcomes, customer metrics, sales data, quality metrics, attendance/adherence, behavioral observations
- Employee self-assessment and supporting artifacts (work samples, dashboards)
- Peer/360 feedback (where applicable)
- Prior review history and development plan status
- Policies: rating definitions, calibration guidelines, documentation standards, data privacy and retention
- Review calendar, forms/templates in the performance system

Prerequisites:
- Goals set and agreed early in the cycle
- Managers and employees trained on the process, tools, and bias mitigation
- System access provisioned and validated; SSO and permissions confirmed
- Clear governance for escalations and exceptions
- Works council/union consultation where required (jurisdictional)

Dependencies on other processes:
- 7.3.2.1 Define performance objectives (inputs)
- 7.3.3 Manage employee training and development (post-review development actions)
- Manage employee relations (PIP and corrective actions)
- Workforce analytics/reporting (metrics and insights)
- Compensation and rewards (may consume outputs; handled via separate process)

## Process Steps
1) Plan and Launch the Cycle
- HRBP/HR Ops:
  - Finalize timelines, forms, rating scale, weightings, and calibration approach.
  - Update guidance, FAQs, examples of high-quality comments, and rubric.
  - Configure performance system, test workflows, and data integrations.
  - Communicate schedule, expectations, and resources to managers and employees.
- Managers:
  - Review team goals and ensure measurability and relevance.
  - Schedule check-ins and the formal review period on calendars.

2) Collect Inputs
- Employee:
  - Complete self-assessment, link goals and evidence, summarize outcomes and learnings.
  - Propose development objectives and career interests.
- Manager:
  - Compile objective data from systems (CRM, project trackers, QA reports).
  - Solicit peer/partner feedback as defined by policy.
  - Capture behavioral observations with examples (STAR: Situation-Task-Action-Result).
- System:
  - Aggregate performance data from integrated tools and surface nudges for missing data.

3) Conduct Ongoing Check-ins (Monthly/Quarterly)
- Manager and Employee:
  - Review progress on goals, adjust as needed, remove blockers.
  - Provide real-time feedback; log key outcomes in the system.
  - Update development plan actions (learning, stretch assignments, coaching).
- HR:
  - Monitor completion rates and send reminders; support managers where needed.

4) Draft Assessments
- Manager:
  - Evaluate performance against goals and competencies using evidence.
  - Draft narrative feedback highlighting strengths, impact, and growth areas.
  - Assign preliminary ratings; flag any potential PIP cases to HR early.
- Employee:
  - Finalize self-assessment comments; ask clarifying questions ahead of the meeting.

5) Calibration
- HR facilitates cross-team calibration sessions with managers and leaders:
  - Review distributions, outliers, and evidence to enhance fairness and consistency.
  - Adjust ratings where warranted; document rationale.
  - Confirm alignment to guidelines and legal considerations.

6) Review Meeting
- Manager and Employee:
  - Hold a structured discussion (typically 45–60 minutes):
    - Recognize achievements and impact.
    - Discuss gaps with specific examples and expectations.
    - Agree on development priorities, resources, and measurable next steps.
    - Discuss career trajectory; avoid conflating performance with pay if policy separates them.
  - Summarize key points, decisions, and commitments.

7) Documentation and Acknowledgment
- Manager:
  - Finalize ratings and feedback in the system; attach artifacts if allowed.
  - Create or update the Individual Development Plan (IDP); draft a PIP if needed in consultation with HR.
- Employee:
  - Add final comments and electronically acknowledge receipt (not necessarily agreement).
- HR:
  - Verify completeness and quality; ensure documentation meets policy standards.

8) Close the Cycle and Handoffs
- HR Ops:
  - Lock completed reviews; archive per retention policy.
  - Generate reports for leadership (completion, distribution, trends).
  - Provide data feeds to dependent processes (development planning, succession; compensation where applicable).
- People Analytics:
  - Analyze fairness, calibration adjustments, and correlation to outcomes; provide insights and recommendations.

9) Continuous Improvement
- HR:
  - Gather feedback on the process and tools; review cycle metrics and pain points.
  - Update guidance, training, and forms for the next cycle.
  - Coach managers with low quality scores or escalations.

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs:
- Completed, signed/acknowledged review forms with ratings and narratives
- Updated goals and development plans; PIPs where applicable
- Calibration records and decisions
- Audit trail and evidence repository
- Reports and dashboards (completion, distribution, quality indicators, sentiment)

Success criteria:
- On-time completion across the organization (e.g., >95% by deadline)
- High-quality feedback (specific, behavior-based, actionable)
- Consistent ratings across similar roles/levels after calibration
- Positive employee perceptions of fairness and usefulness
- Compliance with policy and regulatory requirements
- Actionable development commitments with follow-through

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Employee
  - Prepare self-assessment, provide evidence, engage in feedback, own development actions, acknowledge review.
- Manager/People Leader
  - Set clear expectations, observe and document performance, provide timely feedback, conduct reviews, assign ratings, create development actions, escalate issues.
- HR Business Partner (HRBP)
  - Advise on complex cases, enable bias mitigation, facilitate calibrations, ensure consistency and compliance.
- HR Operations/HRIS
  - Configure systems, manage workflow and data integrity, track progress, ensure security and retention.
- People Analytics
  - Provide metrics, insights, and fairness analyses; recommend improvements.
- Senior Leadership/Calibration Panel
  - Drive consistency, ensure alignment to business standards, approve final distributions as needed.
- Employee Relations/Legal (as needed)
  - Advise on PIPs, documentation sufficiency, and risk mitigation in sensitive cases.
- Learning & Development
  - Translate development needs into learning plans and programs; track follow-through.

## Best Practices
- Make it continuous: Pair formal reviews with frequent check-ins and real-time feedback.
- Use SMART goals and behaviorally anchored rating scales (BARS) for clarity.
- Train managers annually on effective feedback and bias mitigation (halo/recency/leniency/affinity).
- Separate performance discussion from compensation where possible to promote openness.
- Calibrate ratings with evidence; monitor distributions for fairness across demographics and roles.
- Require examples (STAR) for each competency and major goal; discourage vague statements.
- Enable 360 feedback selectively with clear guidance to enhance perspective.
- Leverage integrated data (OKR tools, CRM, project systems) to ground reviews in outcomes.
- Provide job aids: comment libraries, evidence checklists, and meeting agendas.
- Ensure accessibility, privacy, and regional compliance (GDPR/CCPA; works councils).
- Nudge and support: automated reminders, office hours, and QA sampling for feedback quality.
- Close the loop: convert development needs into concrete actions with due dates and owners.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Inconsistent ratings across teams
  - Solution: Robust calibration, clear rubrics, manager enablement, and analytics monitoring.
- Low-quality or vague feedback
  - Solution: Mandatory example count, templates, QA feedback to managers, and training with coaching.
- Recency bias overshadowing full-cycle performance
  - Solution: Require quarterly check-ins and evidence logs; prompt review of early-cycle achievements.
- Missed deadlines and low completion
  - Solution: Executive sponsorship, dashboards with tiered reminders, escalation protocol, and simplified forms.
- Manager discomfort with difficult conversations
  - Solution: Role-play training, scripts, HR support in meetings, and coaching resources.
- Employee distrust or perceived unfairness
  - Solution: Transparency in criteria, two-way dialogue, right to comment, appeal mechanisms, and data on calibration fairness.
- Tool usability issues
  - Solution: Pre-cycle testing, quick reference guides, helpdesk SLAs, and mobile access.
- Legal/ER risk due to poor documentation
  - Solution: Policy-enforced documentation standards, HR QA sampling, and ER review for low ratings/PIPs.

## Performance Metrics (KPIs)
- Timeliness and throughput
  - Review completion rate by deadline; average cycle time per review
- Quality
  - Percentage of reviews meeting documentation quality standards (e.g., examples per goal)
  - Average comment specificity score (text analytics)
- Consistency and fairness
  - Rating distribution vs. guidelines; calibration adjustment rate
  - Variance in ratings by comparable roles/levels; fairness indices across demographics (with privacy safeguards)
- Engagement and effectiveness
  - Employee and manager satisfaction with the process (survey CSAT)
  - Perceived fairness and usefulness scores
- Actionability
  - % of employees with active development plans; completion rate of development actions
  - PIP adherence and outcome rates (where applicable)
- Business linkage
  - Correlation between performance ratings and business outcomes (e.g., sales attainment, quality)
  - Voluntary attrition of top performers

## Technology and Tools
- Core HRIS/HCM: Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM (employee data, roles, org)
- Performance management platforms: Workday Performance, SAP PM/GM, SuccessFactors PM, Lattice, 15Five, Betterworks, Culture Amp Perform
- Goal/OKR tools: Betterworks, Quantive, Jira Align, Asana
- Feedback/360 tools: Culture Amp, Qualtrics, SurveyMonkey, Leapsome
- People analytics/BI: Workday Prism, Visier, Tableau, Power BI
- Collaboration and scheduling: Outlook/Google Calendar, MS Teams/Slack
- LMS: Cornerstone, Docebo, SAP SF Learning (to deliver development actions)
- Data integrations: CRM (Salesforce), project/engineering (Jira, GitHub), support (Zendesk)
- Security and compliance: SSO, role-based access control, audit logging, data retention tools
- Enablement: Knowledge base, microlearning modules, templates, comment libraries
- Optional AI assistance: Drafting support and sentiment checks with strict governance, human review, and privacy controls
