Process Details:
# [8.6.3.6] Approve Change/Release Deployment

## Overview
Approve Change/Release Deployment is the formal governance checkpoint that authorizes a change or release to proceed into the target environment(s) (e.g., production). Its purpose is to ensure the change/release is safe, compliant, value-aligned, and ready for execution based on documented risk, impact, testing evidence, rollback capability, and stakeholder readiness.

This process:
- Confirms business impact has been evaluated and risk is acceptable.
- Verifies all readiness criteria are met (technical, security, operational, and business).
- Ensures appropriate stakeholders have visibility and agree to the timing and implications.
- Provides an auditable authorization record and conditions of approval.
- Acts as a control to minimize service disruption and compliance breaches.

It sits within Manage Change Deployment Control and is tightly integrated with release management, change enablement (ITIL), DevOps pipelines, and IT risk/compliance management.

## Key Activities
- Intake and pre-screening of approval requests (change/release records).
- Risk- and impact-based routing (standard/normal/emergency; minor/major).
- Verification of readiness artifacts (test results, rollback plan, comms, runbooks).
- Conflict checks against release/change calendars and freeze windows.
- Security and compliance conformance checks.
- Capacity/performance and operational readiness assurance.
- Conduct of approval forum (CAB/eCAB/go-no-go) and decision capture.
- Conditional approvals and closure of pre-deployment actions.
- Issuance of formal authorization and stakeholder notification.
- Evidence archiving for audit and post-implementation review (PIR).

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs:
  - Approved Change Request (RFC) or Release record with scope, risk, and impact documented.
  - Business impact assessment and risk assessment (including risk rating).
  - Verified testing evidence: unit/integration, system, performance, security, UAT sign-offs.
  - Deployment plan/runbook and scheduled deployment window.
  - Validated rollback/back-out plan and recovery time estimate.
  - Implementation resources roster and on-call coverage.
  - Communication plan (stakeholder list, customer notices, service desk scripts).
  - Security review results (vulnerability scans, pen test results as applicable).
  - Operational readiness checklist (monitoring, alerting, capacity, DR/BC adjustments).
  - CMDB impact analysis (affected CIs, dependencies).
  - Change collision/conflict check and freeze window exceptions (if any).
  - Approvals to date (business, service owner, architecture as required).
- Prerequisites:
  - Change classified and risk-scored per policy (standard/normal/emergency).
  - All required testing completed and defects triaged within agreed thresholds.
  - Regression risk mitigations defined (e.g., feature flags, canary plan).
  - Segregation of duties observed (requester ≠ approver ≠ executor as per policy).
  - Release content baselined and version-controlled; deployment automation tested in lower envs.
  - Compliance requirements assessed (SOX, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001, etc.).
- Dependencies on other processes:
  - Change evaluation and planning; release planning and readiness.
  - Configuration management/CMDB updates and impact analysis.
  - Test management and quality assurance.
  - Security assessment and risk management.
  - Communications management and service continuity planning.
  - Deployment scheduling and calendar management.

## Process Steps
1. Initiate approval request
   - Change/Release Manager transitions RFC/Release to “Pending Approval” and compiles the approval package with all artifacts.
2. Pre-screen for completeness (Change Manager)
   - Validate required fields and artifacts using a standardized checklist.
   - Return to submitter if incomplete with specific gaps to close.
3. Determine approval path (risk-based routing)
   - Standard, low-risk: policy-based auto-approval if criteria met.
   - Normal: CAB review required.
   - Major/high-risk or customer-facing impact: Extended CAB and business owner review.
   - Emergency: eCAB expedited review with post-implementation PIR.
4. Conflict and schedule validation
   - Verify deployment window availability, freeze windows, and conflicts.
   - Update change calendar; secure maintenance notifications/approvals as needed.
5. Security, compliance, and SoD checks
   - Ensure security findings addressed or accepted risk documented.
   - Verify compliance controls; confirm SoD between author, tester, approver, deployer.
6. Distribute approval package
   - Send agenda and materials to CAB/eCAB at least 24–72 hours prior (per policy).
   - Include summary, impact, risk, test evidence, rollback plan, comms, and decision asks.
7. Conduct approval forum
   - Present change/release overview, business impact, readiness, and risk mitigations.
   - Q&A; confirm monitoring plan and success/abort criteria.
   - Capture decision: Approve, Approve with conditions, Defer, Reject.
8. Record decision and conditions
   - Update RFC/Release record with decision, approvers, timestamp, and conditions.
   - For conditional approvals, assign actions with owners and due times.
9. Final go/no-go checkpoint
   - Prior to window, confirm all conditions closed, no new conflicts, and stakeholders on-bridge.
   - Perform quick readiness checks (tools, access, backups, change freeze status).
10. Issue authorization
   - Change Manager/Release Manager changes status to “Approved for Deployment” and communicates authorization with reference number.
   - Notify Service Desk and impacted stakeholders; publish customer notices if applicable.
11. Archive evidence and handoff
   - Store the complete approval package and meeting minutes for audit.
   - Handoff to deployment execution process with clear rollback triggers and success metrics.

Emergency path (eCAB):
- Minimal viable review focusing on risk, impact, rollback, and customer impact.
- Document justification and risk acceptance; schedule mandatory PIR within defined SLA.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Approved Authorization
  - RFC/Release status updated to Approved for Deployment with approver list and decision rationale.
- Conditions and Action Items
  - Documented conditions with closure evidence.
- Communications
  - Stakeholder and customer communications issued per plan; Service Desk briefed.
- Audit Evidence
  - Approval package, minutes, checklists, risk acceptance, and SoD verification archived.
- Calendar Updates
  - Change/release calendar reflects approved window and blackout exceptions (if any).

Success criteria:
- Approvals granted before scheduled window with no unplanned escalations.
- All required artifacts complete; no critical exceptions outstanding.
- No unauthorized changes deployed; traceable audit trail exists.
- Post-deployment outcomes meet success criteria without major incidents or SLA breaches.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Change Manager
  - Owns process, performs pre-screening, coordinates CAB/eCAB, records decisions, issues authorization, ensures evidence retention.
- Release Manager
  - Assembles release approval package, confirms content readiness, aligns schedules, leads go/no-go calls.
- Change Advisory Board (CAB)
  - Cross-functional evaluation of risk, impact, readiness; provides approve/defer/reject decision.
- Emergency CAB (eCAB)
  - Rapid approval for emergencies; ensures minimal risk posture and mandates PIR.
- Service Owner/Application Owner
  - Confirms business impact, approves downtime/behavioral changes, validates success criteria.
- Business Owner/Stakeholder
  - Accepts business risk and customer impact; approves timing and communications.
- Security Officer/InfoSec
  - Reviews security implications, ensures vulnerabilities addressed or risks accepted.
- QA/Test Lead
  - Validates test coverage and results, defect disposition, and quality gates.
- Operations/SRE/Infrastructure Lead
  - Verifies operational readiness (monitoring, capacity, runbooks, on-call coverage).
- Enterprise/Domain Architect
  - Confirms architectural compliance and dependency impacts (as required).
- Risk/Compliance
  - Ensures regulatory controls and SoD compliance; records risk acceptances.
- Deployment Lead/DevOps Engineer
  - Ensures deployability and rollback feasibility; participates in go/no-go.
- Service Desk Lead/Communications
  - Prepares and issues notifications; updates knowledge and scripts.
- Vendor/Partner Representative (if applicable)
  - Provides vendor approvals, support commitments, and warranty coverage.

## Best Practices
- Use risk-based approvals with clearly defined thresholds and approval matrices.
- Pre-approve standard, low-risk, low-impact changes to reduce CAB load.
- Automate approval workflows integrated with CI/CD; require evidence links (tests, scans) to gates.
- Apply a consistent readiness/approval checklist including rollback, monitoring, and comms.
- Enforce segregation of duties and identity-based approvals (MFA-enabled).
- Maintain an effective CAB charter: scope, quorum, cadence, decision authority, SLAs.
- Time-box CAB decisions; provide pre-read packets to increase decision quality.
- Leverage feature flags, canary releases, and blue/green strategies to reduce risk.
- Maintain a living change calendar; proactively manage freeze windows and conflicts.
- Capture conditional approvals formally and validate closure before go-live.
- Record risk acceptances with business sign-off and expiry/review dates.
- Ensure all approvals are auditable (immutable logs) and traceable to individuals.
- Continuously improve using PIR data and metrics (e.g., reduce approval cycle time without increasing failure rate).

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Bottlenecks and delays
  - Solution: Risk-based automation, pre-approved standards, defined SLAs, parallel reviews.
- Incomplete or low-quality approval packages
  - Solution: Mandatory checklists, form validations, coaching/templates, gate automation.
- Stakeholder availability and quorum issues
  - Solution: Standing CAB cadence, virtual approvals, delegation matrix, asynchronous voting.
- Overuse of emergency changes
  - Solution: Tight eCAB criteria, root-cause analysis, metrics visibility, accountability.
- Conflicts and freeze violations
  - Solution: Centralized calendar, automated conflict detection, exception governance.
- DevOps vs. change control friction
  - Solution: Integrate change controls into pipelines; evidence-driven, policy-based approvals.
- Compliance and SoD violations
  - Solution: RBAC and workflow controls; periodic access reviews; audit sampling.
- Last-minute discovery of dependency risks
  - Solution: CMDB accuracy, automated dependency mapping, early architectural reviews.
- Global timezone coordination
  - Solution: Follow-the-sun CAB coverage, regional approvals, clear communication windows.

## Performance Metrics
- Approval cycle time (submission to decision).
- Percentage of changes auto-approved via policy (standard/low risk).
- First-pass approval rate (no rework required).
- Change failure rate (post-approval incidents, rollbacks).
- Emergency change rate and trend.
- CAB quorum/attendance rate and on-time decision SLA adherence.
- Percentage of approvals with complete evidence package at first submission.
- Unauthorized change count (audit nonconformities).
- Lead time from approval to deployment start.
- Conditional approval closure compliance (on-time, complete).
- Customer/business impact incidents attributable to approved changes.

## Technology and Tools
- ITSM/Change Management: ServiceNow, BMC Helix, Jira Service Management, Cherwell.
- Release and Deployment: Azure DevOps, GitLab CI/CD, Jenkins, Octopus Deploy, Harness, Argo CD, Spinnaker.
- Configuration and Dependency: CMDB (ServiceNow CMDB), Dynatrace Smartscape, Device42.
- Security and Compliance: Vulnerability scanners (Qualys, Tenable), SAST/DAST tools, GRC platforms (Archer), e-signature and approval logging.
- Observability and Readiness: Monitoring (Datadog, Prometheus, New Relic), logging (Splunk, ELK), alerting (PagerDuty, Opsgenie).
- Collaboration and Communications: Slack/Teams with approval bots, email integrations, ITSM notifications; Confluence/SharePoint for documentation.
- Policy/Workflow Engines: ITSM workflow designers, policy-as-code (OPA) for automated gates.
- Calendaring: Integrated change/release calendars with conflict detection and freeze management.

This process, when executed consistently and supported by automation and clear governance, reduces deployment risk while preserving delivery speed and compliance.

Process Details:
## Overview
Document IT change/release outcome is the process of formally capturing the results of a change or release after deployment. It establishes an authoritative record of what was deployed, how it performed against acceptance criteria, what variances occurred from the plan, and what follow-on actions are required. This process supports auditability, knowledge transfer, continuous improvement, regulatory compliance, and operational stability by ensuring every change/release leave-behind is accurate, complete, and traceable.

Within Manage change deployment control, outcome documentation is the final control point that:
- Confirms the status of the change/release (successful, partial, failed, rolled back).
- Links the change to incidents, problems, assets/CMDB items, and knowledge articles.
- Substantiates approvals and sign-offs with evidence.
- Feeds metrics to change governance (e.g., change failure rate, documentation completeness).
- Enables effective post-implementation reviews and learning cycles.

## Key Activities
- Gather deployment evidence: logs, screenshots, monitoring data, test results, approvals.
- Record planned versus actual: schedule adherence, scope variance, steps executed.
- Confirm acceptance criteria results and service validation/testing outcomes.
- Capture business impact: outage windows, customer impact, SLA effects, benefits realized.
- Document issues and remediation: incidents, defects, problems, rollbacks/back-outs.
- Update configuration and release data: versions, CI relationships, configuration parameter changes, CMDB updates.
- Record risk/compliance considerations: security scans, segregation of duties, approvals, SOX/ISO evidence.
- Produce or update release notes and knowledge articles (install/operate/rollback).
- Obtain stakeholder confirmations and close-out approvals.
- Archive artifacts per records retention and ensure discoverability.
- Trigger follow-on actions: PIR, problem investigation, technical debt items, change freeze exceptions.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs to begin:
- Approved change/release record with deployment plan and acceptance criteria.
- Execution artifacts: runbooks/playbooks, CI/CD job output, implementation logs.
- Test and validation results (functional, performance, security).
- Monitoring and observability data from the stabilization window.
- Incident/problem records generated during/after deployment.
- CMDB baseline snapshot (pre-change) and target state definition.
- Approvals and CAB decisions (including emergency approvals if applicable).

Prerequisites:
- Deployment execution completed (success, partial success, failure, or rollback).
- Access to ITSM tool, CMDB, logging/monitoring systems, and document repository.
- Named responsible person/team for outcome documentation.
- Defined templates and minimum evidence checklist.
- Time-synchronized systems to ensure accurate timestamps.

Dependencies on other processes:
- Execute change/release deployment.
- Service validation and testing.
- Incident management, problem management.
- Configuration management (CMDB updates).
- Knowledge management.
- Post-implementation review/retrospective.
- Release management and version control.

## Process Steps
1. Initiate documentation task
   - Triggered automatically upon deployment completion or stabilization window end.
   - Assign to Change Implementer or Release Manager; Change Manager oversees quality.

2. Consolidate evidence
   - Collect CI/CD pipeline logs, deployment console output, change scripts, and approvals.
   - Export monitoring snapshots (pre/post KPIs), error rates, latency, capacity.
   - Gather test evidence: test suites, coverage, security scan reports, data migration checks.
   - Capture chatops transcripts and bridge call notes if applicable.

3. Record planned vs. actual
   - Document actual start/end timestamps, environment(s), and scope executed.
   - Note variances: steps skipped/added, deviations from maintenance window, resource variances.

4. Declare outcome status
   - Categorize: Successful, Successful with issues, Partial (deferred items), Failed, Rolled back, Rolled forward.
   - Provide concise narrative summary and root cause if failure/rollback.

5. Confirm acceptance criteria results
   - Record each criterion with pass/fail and evidence link.
   - Include performance regressions/improvements and security posture changes.

6. Capture business and customer impact
   - Actual downtime, user impact, SLA breaches, transactions affected, error budgets consumed.
   - Benefits realized (e.g., performance gain, defect reduction).

7. Link operational records and artifacts
   - Link associated incidents, problems, and known errors.
   - Link release record, build numbers, artifact hashes, commit SHAs, feature flags toggled.
   - Identify affected CIs and relationships.

8. Update configuration information
   - Document version updates, configuration parameter changes, database schema versions.
   - Propose or execute CMDB updates per configuration management policy.
   - Obtain Configuration Manager validation where required.

9. Document rollback/back-out (if applicable)
   - Steps executed, duration, data restore verification, residual risks, and technical debt created.

10. Produce customer/operations documentation
   - Update release notes: features, fixes, breaking changes, deprecations, known issues.
   - Update or create knowledge articles: install, operate, troubleshoot, rollback.
   - Update runbooks with lessons learned and revised steps.

11. Compliance and approvals
   - Attach approvals (CAB, emergency CAB), SoD evidence, change tester signoff, security exceptions.
   - Redact secrets; classify documents per information security policy.
   - Obtain Service Owner/Business Owner acceptance where required.

12. Quality review and closure
   - Change Manager reviews for completeness and accuracy using checklist.
   - If gaps found, rework assigned; otherwise, close the change/release record.
   - Schedule PIR for significant or failed changes; create follow-up actions.

13. Archive and report
   - Archive artifacts to designated repository with retention tags.
   - Update dashboards/metrics; notify stakeholders of final outcome and links.

Process variations:
- Emergency changes: streamline evidence collection but enforce post-facto documentation within a defined SLA (e.g., 24 hours) and ECAB approval capture.
- Standard/pre-approved changes: leverage templated, automated evidence capture and simplified outcome fields.

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs:
- Completed change/release outcome record in the ITSM tool.
- Linked artifacts: logs, test results, monitoring screenshots, approvals, chat transcripts.
- Updated CMDB entries and relationships reflecting the deployed state.
- Release notes and knowledge articles.

Deliverables:
- Outcome summary report (exec and technical views).
- Variance log and issue list with assigned owners and due dates.
- Compliance evidence pack (audit-ready).
- PIR input package (for major/failed changes).

Success criteria:
- Outcome documented within defined SLA (e.g., 1 business day for standard, 24 hours for emergency).
- 100% completion of mandatory fields and evidence attachments.
- All related incidents/problems linked; CMDB updates validated.
- Stakeholder sign-offs recorded; change record closed without rework.
- No material audit nonconformities attributed to documentation gaps.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Change Implementer/Deployment Engineer: Collect evidence, draft outcome, link artifacts, propose CMDB updates.
- Release Manager: Ensure release scope/version accuracy, produce release notes, coordinate multi-team inputs.
- Change Manager: Govern process, review completeness/quality, ensure approvals, close records, drive metrics.
- Service Owner/Business Owner: Validate business impact and acceptance, approve outcome where required.
- Configuration Manager: Review and approve CMDB updates, ensure CI relationships are accurate.
- QA/Testing Lead: Validate test results and acceptance criteria status.
- Security/Compliance Officer: Verify security scans, exceptions, and regulatory evidence.
- SRE/Operations Lead: Validate operational stability, monitoring results, and runbook updates.
- Service Desk/Knowledge Manager: Publish/curate knowledge articles, update known errors.
- CAB/ECAB: Provide approvals and conditional requirements; review significant outcomes.
- Project/Product Manager: Communicate to stakeholders, confirm feature enablement/flags, track follow-ups.

## Best Practices
- Use standardized templates with mandatory fields and evidence checklists.
- Automate evidence capture from CI/CD, monitoring, and logging systems; auto-attach build IDs and commit SHAs.
- Define clear, measurable acceptance criteria pre-deployment; use the same criteria in outcome recording.
- Capture outcomes immediately (or within 24 hours) while context is fresh; embed prompts in deployment pipelines.
- Enforce strong linking discipline: change ↔ release ↔ incidents/problems ↔ CIs ↔ knowledge articles.
- Record both technical results and business impact; include downtime and benefits realized.
- Treat partial successes and workarounds explicitly; raise follow-up backlog items.
- Maintain data integrity: time-synchronized systems, immutable logs, and versioned documents.
- Protect sensitive information; redact secrets and follow information classification policies.
- Periodically audit a sample of records for completeness and quality; provide feedback and coaching.
- Incorporate lessons into runbooks and standard change templates to reduce repeat issues.
- For feature-flagged releases, document flag states and rollout cohorts at each stage.

## Common Challenges
- Incomplete or late documentation due to time pressure
  - Solution: SLA-backed tasks, pipeline gates, reminders, and management reporting.
- Evidence scattered across tools
  - Solution: Tool integrations and APIs to consolidate artifacts into the ITSM record automatically.
- Inconsistent definitions of “success”
  - Solution: Predefined acceptance criteria and outcome taxonomy approved by CAB/Service Owners.
- Missing CMDB updates or low CI accuracy
  - Solution: Integrate deployment tools with CMDB; require CMDB validation before closure.
- Poor linkage to incidents/problems/knowledge
  - Solution: Make linkages mandatory fields; enable quick search/attach in ITSM.
- Security and compliance gaps
  - Solution: Checklist items for SoD, approvals, scan results; periodic compliance reviews.
- Multi-team releases causing ownership confusion
  - Solution: RACI matrix, single Release Manager, and a unified outcome document.
- Over-documentation burden for standard changes
  - Solution: Lightweight templates and automation; tiered documentation by change risk level.

## Performance Metrics
- Documentation cycle time: average time from deployment completion to outcome record completion.
- First-pass approval rate: percentage of outcome records approved without rework.
- Completeness score: percentage of mandatory fields and required artifacts present.
- CMDB accuracy rate: percentage of changes with validated CI updates.
- Linkage rate: percentage of changes with associated incidents/problems/knowledge linked.
- Audit nonconformity rate: number of findings tied to change/release documentation per audit period.
- Change closure SLA adherence: percentage of changes closed within defined SLA.
- Post-change incident rate: number of incidents within stabilization window linked to “successful” changes (signals documentation accuracy and criteria quality).
- PIR trigger rate and actions closed: for significant/failed changes, percentage with PIR completed and action items closed on time.

## Technology and Tools
- ITSM and change/release management: ServiceNow, BMC Helix Remedy, Jira Service Management, Cherwell.
- CMDB and discovery: ServiceNow CMDB, BMC Atrium, Device42, Service Graph connectors.
- CI/CD and release orchestration: Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, Argo CD, Spinnaker.
- Configuration management/IaC: Ansible, Terraform, Puppet, Chef.
- Monitoring and observability: Datadog, New Relic, Prometheus/Grafana, Splunk Observability, CloudWatch/Azure Monitor/Stackdriver.
- Logging and evidence: Splunk, ELK/Opensearch, S3/Blob storage for artifact archiving.
- Security and compliance: SAST/DAST tools (e.g., SonarQube, OWASP ZAP), vulnerability scanners (e.g., Qualys, Tenable), approval workflow/e-signature tools.
- Knowledge and document repositories: Confluence, SharePoint, internal wikis, version-controlled docs in Git.
- ChatOps and collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams, with bots to capture deployment threads.
- Release artifact repositories: Nexus, Artifactory, Docker registries.
- Time synchronization and audit: NTP across systems; immutable storage or WORM for audit-critical logs.

This process ensures every IT change and release has a reliable, audit-ready, and operationally useful record, enabling safer, faster, and more compliant delivery of technology services.

# [8.6.4.1] Confirm hardware/software operational status

## Overview
This process validates that newly deployed or changed IT hardware and software are operational, secure, and meeting expected performance and availability targets. It is executed immediately after deployment and during the agreed hypercare period and serves as the formal “go-live confirmation” and readiness check for handover to steady-state operations.

Purpose:
- Ensure the deployed components (infrastructure, platforms, applications, endpoints, network devices) are installed correctly, configured as intended, and function within defined service levels.
- Detect and remediate defects early to minimize business disruption.
- Provide auditable evidence for Change/Release closure, CMDB updates, and compliance.

Role in the organization:
- Acts as the final quality gate within “Implement technology solutions” before business cutover or full production ramp-up.
- Feeds operational readiness data to Incident, Problem, Asset/CMDB, Monitoring/Observability, and Security processes.
- Supports ITIL Change Enablement, Release Management, and Service Validation and Testing.

## Key Activities
- Review and confirm approvals, maintenance window, and pre-conditions.
- Execute standardized operational validation plan (hardware and software).
- Perform health, availability, performance, security, and data integrity checks.
- Conduct smoke tests and functional validations with QA/business users where applicable.
- Verify monitoring, alerting, backups, logging, and support runbooks are in place and working.
- Capture evidence, resolve defects or execute rollback/backout if criteria not met.
- Update CMDB/asset records, documentation, and knowledge base.
- Obtain formal sign-off and close associated change/release records.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Approved change/release record and deployment plan with rollback/backout plan.
- Build artifacts, configuration baselines, IaC/manifests, and version identifiers.
- Operational validation plan/checklists, test scripts, and acceptance criteria.
- Monitoring/alert definitions and dashboards; logging configuration.
- Access credentials, connectivity details, and required approvals (CAB/security).
- Vendor documentation, runbooks, support contacts, and licenses/entitlements.

Prerequisites:
- Deployment completed per plan; environment accessible (including OOB/iDRAC/iLO).
- Successful backups/snapshots taken and verifiable restore test where applicable.
- Maintenance window active; on-call resources engaged.
- Baseline performance expectations defined; SLO/SLI thresholds documented.
- Certificates, secrets, and keys provisioned; DNS/NTP/time sync configured.

Dependencies on other processes:
- 8.6.3 Plan and administer release; Change Enablement.
- Environment provisioning and configuration management (IaC/CM).
- Test management and UAT sign-offs.
- Security management (vulnerability scanning, hardening, EDR).
- Asset/CMDB management; Knowledge management.
- Incident/Problem management for issue handling during validation.

## Process Steps
1) Initiate and review
- Confirm change window, scope, approvals, and rollback plan.
- Identify affected CIs and dependencies in CMDB; freeze scopes for validation.
- Align stakeholders: release manager, deployment engineers, app owner, QA, security, network/DB.

2) Prepare validation environment
- Verify access (privileged accounts, OOB console).
- Enable/confirm monitoring, logging, and alert routing; mute non-critical alerts during maintenance if needed.
- Stage test data and tools (e.g., synthetic transactions, API tests).

3) Execute pre-flight checks
- Connectivity: network reachability, firewall rules, DNS resolution, NTP/time sync.
- Licensing: license server reachability and activation status.
- Certificates: validity, trust chain, SANs, and expiration windows.
- Configuration drift: compare deployed configs to baseline (hash/signature or CM tool).

4) Hardware health validation (as applicable)
- Power, fans, thermals, ECC memory status, CPU health.
- Storage: RAID/array health, SMART, capacity thresholds, latency.
- NICs: link status, bonding/teaming, errors, MTU.
- Firmware/BIOS versions compliant with standards; no critical advisories.
- Hypervisor/virtualization platform health (vCenter/UCS/OneView).
- Out-of-band management health and access.

5) Operating system and platform checks
- Boot and service startup status; required daemons/processes active.
- Resource utilization within baseline: CPU, memory, disk IO, network.
- Kernel/modules/drivers compatible; no critical dmesg/Event Log errors.
- Package/patch level compliant with policy; reboots handled as required.

6) Application and middleware validation
- Configuration loaded and correct (env vars, feature flags, secrets).
- Services/containers/pods deployed with expected replicas; readiness/liveness probes passing.
- Ports listening, APIs responding with expected codes; health endpoints OK.
- Dependencies reachable: DBs, caches, message brokers, third-party services.
- Schema migrations applied and validated; data integrity verified.
- Scheduled jobs/CRONs/queues functioning; idempotency verified.

7) Security posture verification
- Host and application firewalls as per design; no unintended open ports.
- EDR/AV agent online and healthy; signatures current.
- Vulnerability scan initiated/completed with acceptable results or risk accepted.
- OS and app hardening benchmarks (e.g., CIS) met; secrets managed properly.
- SIEM log ingestion verified; critical detections tested where safe.

8) Observability and resilience checks
- Metrics visible on dashboards; SLI coverage (latency, errors, traffic, saturation).
- Alerts configured with proper thresholds and routing (PagerDuty/Opsgenie).
- Logs available, structured, and searchable; trace propagation/correlation IDs working.
- Backup/replication jobs scheduled and succeeding; sample restore validated.
- HA/failover behavior validated if in scope (cluster quorum, node drain, failback).
- Rate limiting, circuit breakers, and retries configured where applicable.

9) Performance and smoke testing
- Execute smoke tests to confirm core user journeys.
- Run light performance tests to compare to baseline; verify no abnormal regressions.
- Validate SLA/SLO conformance under normal load; confirm capacity headroom.

10) Business validation and sign-off
- Business/QA performs functional checks; confirm acceptance criteria met.
- Log defects; remediate during window or assess impact.
- If critical criteria fail: execute rollback/backout as per plan; notify stakeholders and create incidents/problems as needed.

11) Documentation and CMDB updates
- Update CMDB CIs: versions, relationships, locations, ownership, support groups.
- Attach evidence (screens, logs, reports) to change record.
- Update runbooks, knowledge articles, and support contact rotations.

12) Handover and hypercare
- Formal handover to operations with artifacts: validation report, known issues, monitoring dashboard links, and escalation paths.
- Hypercare period monitoring; tighten alert thresholds temporarily if required.
- Close change upon successful hypercare exit criteria.

13) Closure and retrospectives
- Record lessons learned; update checklists and automation.
- Feed issues into Problem Management and continuous improvement backlog.

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs:
- Operational Validation Report with pass/fail status and evidence.
- Updated CMDB/asset records and documentation.
- Configured and verified monitoring/alerting/logging.
- Security scan results and compliance attestations.
- Known issues list, remediation actions, and risk acceptances.

Deliverables:
- Signed acceptance/sign-off from technical owner and business (as needed).
- Runbooks/KB articles and updated deployment/rollback documentation.
- Change record closure with artifacts attached.

Success criteria:
- All mandatory validation checks passed; no P1/P2 incidents during and post-validation.
- SLO/SLI targets met; no critical security findings outstanding.
- CMDB accuracy confirmed; monitoring and backups verified.
- If issues arise, resolved within window or rollback executed cleanly.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Release Manager: Owns plan, approvals, communication, and change closure.
- Deployment/Implementation Engineer: Executes validations, remediates issues, documents evidence.
- Systems Administrator/SRE: OS/platform checks, automation, monitoring configuration.
- Application Owner/Technical Lead: Application validation, functional smoke tests, sign-off.
- QA/Test Engineer: Test execution, defect logging, business validation coordination.
- Security Engineer: Security controls verification, vulnerability scans, risk acceptance.
- Network Engineer: Connectivity, firewall, load balancer, DNS verifications.
- Database Administrator: DB availability, performance, schema migration validation, backups.
- Service Desk Lead: Receives handover, updates knowledge base, prepares for user contacts.
- Vendor/Third-Party Support (as needed): Specialized validation and troubleshooting.

## Best Practices
- Use standardized, version-controlled validation checklists and scripts; keep them idempotent.
- Automate health checks and evidence capture via CI/CD pipelines and CM tools.
- Define clear, measurable acceptance criteria and rollback triggers before deployment.
- Validate observability first; you can’t verify what you can’t see.
- Establish environment parity and immutable infrastructure where possible.
- Practice canary/blue-green or phased rollouts; leverage feature flags to decouple release from activation.
- Perform pre-production dry runs and disaster-recovery/restore tests periodically.
- Keep certificates, licenses, and secrets lifecycle-managed and monitored for expiry.
- Keep all changes traceable with configuration item relationships in CMDB.
- Run post-implementation reviews to improve checklists and automation continuously.

## Common Challenges
- Missing or misconfigured monitoring/logging: Mitigate with pre-deployment observability validation and templates.
- DNS, certificates, or time sync issues: Automate checks; enforce enterprise NTP/DNS/cert policies.
- Dependency failures (DB, message broker, external APIs): Include synthetic dependency checks; design retries and circuit breakers.
- Configuration drift and environment inconsistencies: Use configuration management and compliance scans; enforce drift remediation.
- Licensing/entitlement problems: Pre-validate entitlements; implement license server HA and monitoring.
- Performance regressions under real load: Maintain baselines and run targeted load tests in staging; enable load-shedding.
- Security findings discovered late: Integrate scanning into pipeline; define risk acceptance processes.
- Incomplete CMDB updates: Automate CI updates via pipelines and discovery tools; make change closure contingent on CMDB updates.

## Performance Metrics
- First-Pass Validation Rate (% of deployments passing without rework).
- Mean Time to Validate (MTTV) and to Detect issues (MTTD) post-deploy.
- Change Failure Rate attributable to post-deployment operational issues.
- SLO Conformance during hypercare (availability, latency, error rate).
- Post-deployment incident volume and severity within X days.
- Monitoring Coverage (% of components with active metrics, logs, and alerts).
- Security Compliance (% assets meeting patch/hardening/EDR policies).
- CMDB Update Timeliness (average time to update CIs after deployment).
- Mean Time to Remediate non-conformities or to rollback when criteria fail.
- Firmware/patch currency (% assets at approved versions).

## Technology and Tools
- Deployment/Automation: Ansible, Puppet, Chef, SCCM/MECM, Intune, Terraform, Helm, Argo CD, Jenkins/GitLab CI.
- Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, New Relic, Dynatrace, Splunk, ELK/Opensearch, CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, GCP Cloud Monitoring; PagerDuty/Opsgenie.
- Infrastructure/Endpoint Management: vCenter, HPE OneView, Dell OpenManage, Cisco UCS Manager, JAMF, WSUS, Chocolatey, Winget, apt/yum/zypper.
- Security: CrowdStrike/Defender, Nessus/Qualys/Tenable, Rapid7, OSQuery, SIEM platforms, Vault/Key Vault/Secrets Manager, Venafi/ACME.
- Networking: F5/NGINX/HAProxy, Infoblox, NS1, load balancers, firewall managers.
- Data Protection/DR: Veeam, Commvault, Rubrik, Zerto, SRM; snapshot/restore tools.
- Collaboration and ITSM: ServiceNow/Jira for change, CMDB, knowledge; Confluence/SharePoint for runbooks.
- Testing: Postman, k6/JMeter/Locust, Selenium/Cypress for functional and performance tests.

# [8.6.4.2] Confirm operational availability

## Overview
Confirm operational availability is the structured process used to verify that newly implemented or changed IT services/solutions can perform intended operational activities safely and reliably in the target environment (typically production). It ensures the service is available, stable, support-ready, secure, and compliant before full release or after cutover. This process mitigates business risk by validating that functional and non-functional requirements are met, monitoring and recovery mechanisms are in place, and all stakeholders are prepared to operate and support the service.

Role in the organization:
- Provides the go/no-go decision to proceed with or roll back a release.
- Establishes operational baselines and ensures observability, support readiness, and continuity.
- Creates audit evidence for change, security, and compliance requirements.
- Enables a smooth handover from project/engineering to operations (acceptance into service).

## Key Activities
- Plan and coordinate operational readiness validation during the deployment window.
- Execute post-deployment verification (PDV) and smoke tests for key business transactions.
- Validate non-functional requirements: availability, performance, capacity, resilience, and security.
- Confirm integrations, data integrity/migrations, and scheduled operations (jobs, feeds).
- Verify monitoring, alerting, logging, and synthetic checks are active and tuned.
- Validate backup, restore, and DR/replication status against RPO/RTO targets.
- Confirm service desk and operations readiness: runbooks, on-call, escalation paths, and knowledge articles.
- Update CMDB, service catalog, and documentation; capture evidence.
- Conduct a formal go/no-go review and communicate outcomes.
- Transition to steady-state operations and schedule a post-implementation review (PIR).

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Approved change/release record with deployment plan and backout plan.
- Release notes, implementation logs, version/build identifiers, and bill of materials (artifacts).
- Test plans/scripts for PDV (functional and non-functional).
- Service topology and dependencies (CMDB CI list, integration map).
- Monitoring dashboards, alert policies, logging queries, synthetic tests.
- Security controls checklist (IAM roles, certificates, vulnerability scan scopes).
- Business acceptance criteria and SLA/SLO targets.
- Access to environments, logs, dashboards, and necessary credentials (time-bound).

Prerequisites:
- Deployment to target environment completed (or ready for canary/blue-green cutover).
- All lower-environment tests passed; critical defects resolved or risk-accepted.
- Monitoring, logging, and tracing instrumentation implemented (pre-wired).
- Backout/rollback approach tested or validated; feature flags prepared when applicable.
- Change freeze for unrelated systems in the blast radius.
- Stakeholders (operations, service desk, security, business) are on standby.

Dependencies on other processes:
- 8.6.2 Plan and execute changes (Change Enablement/CAB).
- 8.6.3 Administer release (Release Management).
- 8.6.4 Implement technology solutions (deployment execution).
- Configuration Management (CMDB updates), Knowledge Management (runbooks/articles).
- Incident/Problem Management (issue handling), IT Service Continuity/DR, Availability/Capacity Management.

## Process Steps
1. Initiate readiness cycle
   - Confirm change window, participants, communication channels, and decision authority.
   - Review acceptance criteria and checklists; confirm preconditions met.

2. Verify deployment integrity
   - Confirm target versions/builds in all components (app, infra, DB, network, certs).
   - Validate configuration changes and feature flag states.
   - Review implementation logs for errors/warnings.

3. Establish observability
   - Enable/validate dashboards for golden signals (latency, traffic, errors, saturation).
   - Turn on synthetic tests and remove maintenance suppressions.
   - Verify log ingestion, tracing correlation, and SIEM forwarding.

4. Execute PDV/smoke tests (functional)
   - Validate login/SSO, critical user journeys, and APIs (200/expected responses).
   - Confirm scheduled jobs/cron tasks triggered or ready; queues/backlogs are healthy.
   - Validate integrations (payments, messaging, file transfers, partners) and DNS/TLS/cert validity.

5. Validate non-functional requirements
   - Run light performance probes (e.g., sample throughput, k6/JMeter smoke) to confirm headroom.
   - Check resource utilization, autoscaling, and capacity alarms.
   - Confirm resilience basics: instance/process restarts, load balancer health, zone/instance failover if within safe scope.

6. Security and compliance checks
   - Validate IAM policies/roles, least privilege, and access removals post-deploy.
   - Confirm secrets management, certificate chains, cipher policies, and expiry windows.
   - Trigger targeted vulnerability/config scans; verify log/audit coverage.

7. Data integrity and migration validation
   - Compare pre/post record counts, checksums, and data quality rules for migrations.
   - Verify reference data, indexing, archiving/retention, and PII handling.
   - Confirm no data loss, duplication, or orphaned records.

8. Backup, restore, and DR posture
   - Confirm successful backups post-change; retention and immutability policies applied.
   - Validate point-in-time recovery availability and perform a sample restore (where feasible).
   - Check replication/DR status, lag, and alignment to RPO/RTO targets.

9. Support readiness
   - Verify runbooks, SOPs, and escalation matrix; conduct a paging test if appropriate.
   - Ensure service desk routing, priorities, and knowledge articles are in place.
   - Confirm on-call coverage and vendor/third-party contacts.

10. Go/No-Go decision
   - Compare results against acceptance criteria and risk thresholds.
   - If Go: complete cutover (or widen canary), notify stakeholders, exit maintenance mode.
   - If No-Go: execute backout plan, stabilize, log root causes, and communicate.

11. Documentation and system updates
   - Update CMDB CIs, relationships, and service catalog entries automatically where possible.
   - Capture evidence: screenshots, logs, test results, monitoring baselines.
   - Close/annotate change record; record rationale and residual risks.

12. Hypercare and handover
   - Enter heightened monitoring for a defined period; track error budgets/SLOs.
   - Conduct knowledge transfer to operations; confirm ownership in ticketing queues.
   - Schedule and later conduct PIR to capture lessons learned and improvements.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Operational Readiness/PDV report with pass/fail and evidence.
- Go/No-Go decision log and communications to stakeholders.
- Acceptance into Service (AIS) or Service Readiness Certificate signed by required roles.
- Updated CMDB entries, service catalog items, runbooks, and knowledge articles.
- Monitoring dashboards, alert rules, and synthetic checks enabled and tuned.
- Backup/DR verification records; security and compliance check evidence.
- Closed/updated change record; PIR scheduled.
Success criteria:
- All critical PDV checks pass; no Sev1/Sev2 incidents during hypercare period.
- Key business transactions meet SLA/SLO targets.
- Monitoring and alerting coverage meets defined standard.
- Backup and DR objectives validated; security controls verified.
- CMDB and documentation updated within defined SLA.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Service Owner: Defines acceptance criteria, signs off AIS, aligns with business needs.
- Release/Change Manager: Orchestrates window, chairs go/no-go, ensures approvals and recordkeeping.
- Technical Lead/Application Owner: Leads PDV execution, validates functionality and integrations.
- SRE/Operations Engineer: Ensures observability, reliability checks, runbooks, and on-call readiness.
- Infrastructure Teams (Compute/Network/DB/Storage): Validate platform health, capacity, backups, and connectivity.
- Security/Compliance: Verify controls, scans, logging to SIEM, and audit evidence.
- QA/Test Engineer: Prepares automated PDV scripts and executes tests.
- Service Desk Manager: Ensures routing, KAs, SLAs, and escalation paths are ready.
- Business Representative/Process Owner: Confirms business-critical transaction readiness.
- Vendor/Third-Party Contacts: Confirm external integration availability and SLAs.
- DR/BCM Lead: Confirms continuity posture against RPO/RTO.

## Best Practices
- Define measurable acceptance criteria (functional and NFRs) early; align to SLOs/error budgets.
- Automate PDV checks in CI/CD; use repeatable, versioned checklists and evidence capture.
- Prefer progressive delivery (canary/blue-green) and feature flags to reduce blast radius.
- Maintain pre-prod/prod parity; rehearse cutover and backout.
- Standardize observability (golden signals, synthetic journeys, log schemas, traces).
- Enforce policy-as-code for security/compliance gates; rotate secrets on change.
- Validate backups and perform periodic restore exercises; use immutable backups where possible.
- Freeze unrelated changes; staff a war room with clear roles and a single comms channel.
- Auto-update CMDB from IaC/deployment pipelines; maintain traceability from change to CI.
- Keep a robust escalation matrix and conduct paging tests before go-live.

## Common Challenges
- Incomplete dependency visibility: Address with updated service maps, CMDB, and discovery tools.
- Environment drift: Use IaC and config management; enforce drift detection and remediation.
- Monitoring gaps or noisy alerts: Define monitoring standards, tuned thresholds, and synthetic tests.
- Third-party instability: Engage providers early, confirm windows, create fallbacks/mocks.
- Data migration errors: Perform dry runs, checksums, and snapshot backups; plan reversible changes where feasible.
- Rollback complexity (especially databases): Favor forward-fix and feature flags; test rollback scenarios.
- Tight windows and coordination: Rehearse, automate, and parallelize checks; strict timeboxing.
- Access delays: Pre-provision time-bound access and break-glass procedures with audit.
- Late security findings: Shift-left with pre-deployment scans; enforce change gates.
- Unclear ownership post-go-live: RACI clarity, ticket queue ownership, and named on-call.

## Performance Metrics
- Change success rate (% with no rollback/rework).
- Time to confirm operational availability (deployment end to AIS sign-off).
- Post-deployment incident rate (Sev1-3) within 7/30 days.
- PDV detection/repair metrics: MTTD for defects found, MTTR or time-to-rollback.
- Monitoring coverage (% services with APM/logging/synthetics) and alert fidelity (noise ratio).
- Business transaction success rate and performance during hypercare.
- DR/backup verification pass rate; RPO/RTO adherence.
- CMDB accuracy (% CIs updated within 24 hours) and documentation freshness.
- Security/compliance check pass rate; audit findings related to go-live readiness.
- Maintenance window adherence (% completed within window).

## Technology and Tools
- ITSM/Change: ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, BMC Remedy.
- CI/CD and release orchestration: Jenkins, GitLab CI/CD, Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, Spinnaker, Octopus Deploy.
- Progressive delivery: Argo Rollouts, Flagger, AWS CodeDeploy canary/blue-green.
- Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, New Relic, Dynatrace, AppDynamics; OpenTelemetry.
- Logging/SIEM: ELK/OpenSearch, Splunk, Sumo Logic, Microsoft Sentinel.
- Synthetic monitoring: Datadog Synthetics, Pingdom, Catchpoint, CloudWatch Synthetics.
- Infra/IaC/Config: Terraform, Ansible, Puppet, Chef, Helm, Kubernetes controllers.
- Secrets/IAM: HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault; Okta/Azure AD.
- Backup/DR: Veeam, Rubrik, Commvault, Zerto, native cloud backups/snapshots.
- Database and message platforms: OEM, Percona, pgAdmin, SolarWinds DPA; Kafka/RabbitMQ monitors.
- Network and traffic: F5/NGINX/ALB, ThousandEyes, NetFlow tools, DNS/cert managers.
- Testing: Selenium, Cypress, Postman/Newman, Pact (contract), k6/JMeter (performance).
- Collaboration and incident response: Slack/Teams, Zoom, PagerDuty/Opsgenie, Statuspage.
- Compliance/policy-as-code: Chef InSpec, Open Policy Agent, Prisma Cloud.

Process Details:
## Overview
Execute internal IT implementation plan is the process of deploying approved IT services and solutions into the internal enterprise environment so they are available, stable, secure, and supportable for employees and internal stakeholders. It sits within “Implement technology solutions” and focuses on controlled change execution, effective cutover, communication, and transition-to-operations.

Purpose:
- Deliver new or changed IT solutions to internal users with minimal risk and disruption.
- Ensure operational readiness (monitoring, support, documentation, licensing, access).
- Validate that deployed solutions meet business and compliance requirements.
- Capture lessons learned to continually improve deployment practices.

Scope includes:
- Enterprise applications, platforms, integrations, infrastructure (network, server, cloud), endpoints and configurations, security tooling, and data migrations.
- Planned, standard, and emergency/internal deployments (excluding external customer rollouts).

Value:
- Reduces change failure rate and downtime.
- Improves time-to-value and adoption.
- Ensures auditability and traceability of changes.

## Key Activities
- Finalize deployment strategy and schedule (including phased rollout approach).
- Change enablement and approvals (CAB, risk assessment).
- Environment readiness and configuration (non-prod parity, capacity, access).
- Backup/restore readiness and snapshotting.
- Data migration planning and rehearsal.
- Training and communications to impacted users and support teams.
- Deployment execution (automation-first, feature flags, blue/green/canary where applicable).
- Post-deployment validation (functional, security, performance) and business acceptance.
- Hypercare support and incident management.
- Transition to operations (runbooks, monitoring, CMDB updates).
- Post-implementation review and lessons learned.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Approved Internal IT Implementation Plan (scope, schedule, cutover, backout).
- Release package/baseline (versioned artifacts, dependencies, configuration).
- Test evidence and sign-offs (QA/UAT, security, performance, integration).
- Risk assessment and impact analysis.
- Communications and training materials drafts.
- Support model and runbooks (L1/L2 workflows, escalation matrix).
- Monitoring and alerting definitions and SLOs.
- Access provisioning matrix and role definitions.
- Licensing entitlements and capacity plans.
- Vendor/third-party support agreements (as needed).

Prerequisites:
- Change record created in ITSM with planned window; approvals obtained.
- Environments prepared and validated (non-prod→prod parity verified).
- Backout/rollback plan tested (restore procedure, data rollback, DNS reversion).
- Backup/DR readiness confirmed; snapshots/backups scheduled.
- CMDB baseline complete (CIs, relationships, ownership).
- Security controls in place (secrets management, certificates, firewall rules).
- Endpoint readiness (patch level, agent presence, connectivity).
- Coordination with other changes to prevent conflicts.

Dependencies on other processes:
- Release Management (8.6.4): packaging, release calendar.
- Change Enablement/Change Management (8.6.4/8.6.5): risk and approvals.
- Service Validation and Testing: test evidence and acceptance.
- Asset and Configuration Management: CMDB, inventory updates.
- Knowledge Management: KEDB, knowledge articles.
- Incident/Problem Management: hypercare and post-deploy issues.
- Vendor Management/Procurement: licenses, support SLAs.
- Information Security Management: security sign-offs and controls.

## Process Steps
1) Handover and readiness check
- Review implementation plan, release package, test sign-offs, and risk assessment.
- Validate prerequisites and entry criteria are met.
- Responsible: Implementation Lead, Release Manager, Service Owner.

2) Finalize rollout strategy and schedule
- Choose deployment pattern: phased pilot, canary, blue/green, big-bang (risk-based).
- Confirm change window, blackout periods, and maintenance notices.
- Align with release calendar and other changes.
- Responsible: Implementation Lead, Change Manager, Business Owner.

3) Confirm operational readiness
- Validate monitoring dashboards, alerts, logs, and SLOs.
- Verify support model, runbooks, and Service Desk knowledge articles.
- Confirm access provisioning workflows and license entitlements.
- Responsible: Operations Lead, Service Desk Manager, Security.

4) Approvals and communications
- Submit/secure CAB approvals; document risk treatments and backout plan.
- Issue stakeholder communications (what/when/impact/help channels).
- Schedule training sessions and publish materials.
- Responsible: Change Manager, OCM/Communications, Training Lead.

5) Pre-deployment activities
- Take system backups/snapshots; verify restore points and checksums.
- Pre-provision infrastructure (IaC), network changes, certificates, secrets.
- Perform data migration rehearsal or trial run if applicable.
- Lock down change windows and freeze non-essential changes.
- Responsible: Infra/Cloud Engineer, DBA, Network, Security.

6) Pilot or canary deployment (if selected)
- Deploy to a small cohort or non-critical segment.
- Run smoke tests and security checks; monitor for errors/performance.
- Gate decision: proceed, hold for fix, or roll back.
- Responsible: DevOps/SRE, QA, Service Owner.

7) Full deployment execution
- Execute automated deployment pipeline to production.
- Apply configuration via configuration management; enable feature flags progressively.
- Execute data migration scripts; validate record counts and integrity.
- Perform DNS/routing cutover or blue/green switch.
- Responsible: DevOps/SRE, DBA, Network.

8) Post-deployment validation
- Run functional smoke tests, integration checks, and security validation (scans/attestations).
- Validate performance baselines; verify logging/metrics/alerts.
- Confirm user access and role mappings; test key business scenarios with SMEs.
- Responsible: QA Lead, Security, Business SMEs.

9) Hypercare and issue management
- Elevate monitoring thresholds; war room/bridge as needed.
- Triage and resolve incidents; update KEDB.
- Make minor configuration fixes under approved change models.
- Responsible: Service Desk, SRE/Operations, Problem Manager.

10) Transition to steady-state operations
- Complete CMDB and asset updates; attach change and release records.
- Finalize runbooks, SOPs, and knowledge articles; confirm on-call readiness.
- Conduct handover session with Operations and Service Desk.
- Responsible: Implementation Lead, Ops Lead, Knowledge Manager.

11) Post-implementation review (PIR)
- Review outcomes vs. objectives, incidents, deployment metrics, and user feedback.
- Capture lessons learned; identify tech debt and improvement actions.
- Close change record and archive artifacts.
- Responsible: Project/Program Manager, Change Manager, Service Owner.

Exit criteria:
- Solution is available and stable; success metrics met.
- Operational acceptance confirmed; all documentation updated.
- Change record closed; PIR actions assigned.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Deployed and operational internal IT solution (versioned and traceable).
- Completed change record with approvals and evidence.
- Updated CMDB entries and asset inventory.
- Backups/snapshots and validated restore points.
- Runbooks/SOPs, monitoring dashboards, alert rules, on-call rota.
- User training artifacts and communications.
- Updated knowledge articles and KEDB entries.
- Data migration completion report and validation logs.
- PIR report with lessons learned and action items.
Success criteria:
- Deployment completed within window; no unplanned outages beyond SLA.
- Zero Sev-1 incidents attributable to the change within X days.
- Change failure rate within target; rollback not required or executed successfully.
- User access working; adoption/utilization meets target.
- Security and compliance checks passed; recoverability verified.
- Monitoring green and SLOs met.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Implementation Lead/Deployment Manager: Owns end-to-end execution, coordinates teams, ensures entry/exit criteria.
- Change Manager: Manages change records, risk assessment, approvals/CAB, scheduling.
- Release Manager: Manages release package integrity and calendar alignment.
- Service Owner/Product Owner: Defines acceptance criteria, owns business outcomes and budget.
- Project/Program Manager: Overall plan, dependencies, stakeholder management, PIR facilitation.
- DevOps/SRE/Platform Engineer: Automates deployment, ensures reliability, monitoring, and rollback capability.
- Infrastructure/Cloud Engineer: Provisioning, capacity, IaC, servers/VMs/storage.
- Network Engineer: DNS, load balancers, firewall rules, routing.
- Security/Identity Engineer: Security validation, certificates, secrets, IAM/SSO, policy compliance.
- DBA/Data Engineer: Data migration planning, execution, validation, rollback.
- QA/Test Manager: Test strategy, smoke/regression, sign-offs.
- Service Desk/Support Manager: L1 readiness, knowledge, comms to support staff, hypercare triage.
- OCM/Communications Lead: Stakeholder communications, training coordination.
- Business SMEs/Key Users: UAT and post-deploy validation of business scenarios.
- Architecture/Enterprise Architect: Conformance to standards, patterns, and non-functional requirements.
- Vendor/Partner: Advisory, support alignment, break-fix as contracted.

## Best Practices
- Use automation-first deployments (CI/CD, IaC, config management) to reduce human error.
- Prefer low-risk rollout patterns (canary, blue/green, feature flags) with measurable guardrails.
- Maintain environment parity; validate via automated configuration drift checks.
- Practice and document backout and restore; verify backups by test restores.
- Perform data migration rehearsals with anonymized or approved representative data.
- Integrate security early (shift-left): image scanning, IaC policy checks, secrets management.
- Establish clear go/no-go gates with objective criteria at pilot and full rollout.
- Pre-stage monitoring and alerting; define SLOs and error budgets.
- Prepare support: runbooks, knowledge articles, and escalation paths before go-live.
- Coordinate via a master change calendar; prevent change collisions with freeze windows.
- Communicate early and often: what’s changing, when, impacts, and where to get help.
- Track and remediate technical debt uncovered during implementation planning.
- Keep a well-defined RACI and a live war-room during critical cutovers.
- Update CMDB automatically from pipelines where possible for accuracy and speed.

## Common Challenges
- Environment drift causing unexpected behavior
  - Mitigation: Automated config validation, golden images, drift detection and remediation.
- Incomplete rollback plans or untested backups
  - Mitigation: Mandatory restore tests; documented, timed backout procedures.
- Data migration failures or performance degradation
  - Mitigation: Rehearsals, partitioned migrations, throttling, validation scripts, fallback strategies.
- Access provisioning delays
  - Mitigation: Pre-approved RBAC roles, JIT access, automated provisioning workflows.
- Change collisions and scheduling conflicts
  - Mitigation: Central change calendar, conflict checks, governance for blackouts.
- Insufficient stakeholder communication/training leading to poor adoption
  - Mitigation: Early OCM engagement, concise user guides, targeted training, champions network.
- Security control gaps post-deployment
  - Mitigation: Pre-deploy security checklist, automated policy-as-code, post-deploy scans.
- Vendor or dependency readiness issues
  - Mitigation: Confirm SLAs and on-call contacts; verify external API/integration windows.
- Endpoint variability (offline devices, patch levels)
  - Mitigation: Staged endpoint rollouts, retries, device health checks, remediation campaigns.
- Monitoring gaps and slow incident response
  - Mitigation: Observability standards, synthetic tests, runbooks with clear first-response steps.

## Performance Metrics
- Deployment frequency (per service/team) and lead time for changes.
- Change success rate and change failure rate (% requiring rollback/hotfix).
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) and Mean time to restore (MTTR) for post-deploy incidents.
- Percentage of deployments completed within approved window.
- Post-deployment incident volume and severity mix (7/30-day window).
- User adoption/utilization and training completion rates.
- Service availability and SLO attainment post-deploy.
- PIR completion rate and average closure time of action items.
- CMDB update accuracy and timeliness (audit pass rate).
- Compliance/security validation pass rate (scans, attestations).
- Variance to deployment budget/effort.

## Technology and Tools
- ITSM and Change/Release: ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, BMC Helix, Cherwell.
- CI/CD and Artifact Repositories: Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps; Artifactory/Nexus.
- Infrastructure as Code and Config Management: Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible, Puppet, Chef.
- Containerization and Orchestration: Docker, Kubernetes, OpenShift, Helm, ArgoCD/Flux.
- Feature Flags and Progressive Delivery: LaunchDarkly, Azure App Config, Split.
- Secrets and Certificates: HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, cert managers.
- Monitoring/Observability: Prometheus/Grafana, Datadog, New Relic, Dynatrace, AppDynamics, ELK/EFK, Splunk.
- Logging and APM: OpenTelemetry, Jaeger/Tempo, Sumo Logic.
- Database and Migration: Liquibase/Flyway, native DB tools, DMS (AWS DMS), backup/restore tools (Veeam).
- Network/DNS/LB: F5, NGINX, HAProxy, Cloudflare/Akamai, Infoblox.
- Endpoint and MDM: Microsoft Intune/Endpoint Manager, SCCM/MECM, Jamf.
- Identity/Access: Active Directory/Azure AD, Okta, Ping, SSO/SAML/OIDC tooling.
- Knowledge/Documentation: Confluence, SharePoint, wikis; runbook repositories.
- Testing and QA: Selenium/Cypress, Postman/Newman, JMeter/K6, security scanners (Snyk, Trivy).
- CMDB/Discovery: ServiceNow Discovery, Tanium, Lansweeper.
- Collaboration and War-room: Microsoft Teams, Slack, Zoom; incident bridges and status pages.

Process Details:
# [8.6.5.3] Support Organizational Changes

## Overview
Support Organizational Changes is the organizational change management (OCM) component of service/solution rollout. Its purpose is to prepare, equip, and support people through IT-related changes so that new services and solutions are adopted, used correctly, and deliver intended business outcomes. This process aligns people, process, and technology changes with clear communication, training, stakeholder engagement, readiness assessments, and post go‑live support (“hypercare”), ensuring a safe transition to steady-state operations.

Role in the organization:
- Reduces operational risk during deployments by proactively managing user adoption and resistance.
- Increases time-to-value by accelerating proficiency and effective use of new IT services.
- Ensures compliance, auditability, and traceability of change impacts, training, and approvals.
- Provides a feedback loop to improve releases, support models, and future changes.

## Key Activities
- Assess change impact and organizational readiness.
- Identify stakeholders and build a sponsorship/advocacy network.
- Develop change strategy, communications plan, and training plan.
- Prepare service desk and support functions for go‑live (knowledge, staffing, scripts).
- Execute communications, training, and enablement activities.
- Conduct pilots, rehearsals, and “train-the-trainer” enablement.
- Monitor adoption and sentiment; deliver hypercare support.
- Capture feedback, manage resistance, and mitigate change risks.
- Transition to business-as-usual (BAU) and conduct lessons learned.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Approved change request and deployment plan (scope, schedule, environments, blackout windows).
- Release notes and solution overview (capabilities, benefits, constraints).
- Change impact assessment inputs (process maps, roles, location data, user counts).
- Stakeholder registry and org charts (business units, sponsors, managers).
- Risk register and compliance requirements (audit, privacy, security, union considerations).
- Training baseline content and SME availability.
- Support model definition (SLAs/OLAs, escalation paths, service desk tooling).
- UAT results, go/no-go criteria, and pilot findings (if available).

Prerequisites:
- Executive sponsor identified and engaged.
- Change manager assigned; OCM budget and resources approved.
- Agreement on KPIs and success criteria (adoption and performance).
- Content repositories and platforms accessible (LMS, knowledge base, collaboration tools).
- Translations, accessibility needs, and regulatory training requirements identified.

Dependencies on other processes:
- Change Enablement/Management (CAB approvals; [8.6.x]).
- Release & Deployment Management ([8.6.5]).
- Service Desk Readiness, Incident & Problem Management ([8.x]).
- Training development/delivery ([8.6.5.2] Train users, if defined separately).
- Knowledge Management (knowledge articles and SOPs).
- Communications/Corporate Affairs (mass comms approvals).
- Security, Privacy, and Compliance reviews.

## Process Steps
Phase 1 – Plan and Analyze:
1) Initiate OCM
- Confirm scope, objectives, timeline, and constraints with Project/Release Manager and Service Owner.
- Establish governance: cadence, decision rights, RACI, and integration with CAB.

2) Stakeholder Identification and Analysis
- Map impacted groups, personas, and locations; identify sponsors, change champions, and managers.
- Assess change saturation (concurrent changes) and organizational risk hotspots.

3) Change Impact Assessment
- Identify process, role, policy, and technology impacts; categorize by severity and type.
- Document “what’s changing,” “why,” and “WIIFM” (what’s in it for me) by audience.
- Define critical behaviors and proficiency requirements.

4) Readiness Baseline and Risk Planning
- Survey or interview samples of impacted users/managers to gauge awareness and readiness.
- Create OCM risk register and resistance management plan with mitigation actions.

5) Change Strategy and Plan
- Select methodology (e.g., ADKAR aligned) and define approach: waves vs big bang, pilot scope, hypercare.
- Produce integrated OCM plan with milestones, budget, and resource plan.

Phase 2 – Design and Prepare:
6) Communication Planning
- Build a message map: purpose, benefits, impacts, timelines, support.
- Develop a channel mix (email, Teams/Slack, intranet, town halls, posters, video).
- Create comms calendar aligned to release milestones; secure approvals.

7) Training Strategy and Content Development
- Define learning objectives per role; decide modalities (eLearning, VILT, classroom, job aids, simulations).
- Develop curricula and assets: quick reference guides, videos, FAQs.
- Establish train-the-trainer and manager toolkits (talking points, checklists).

8) Support Readiness (Service Desk and Ops)
- Draft and publish knowledge articles; prepare call scripts and chatbots.
- Align SLAs/OLAs, staffing forecasts, and escalation paths for hypercare.
- Conduct tool updates (categorization, routing rules, priority matrices).

9) Pilot/Simulation and Rehearsals
- Run a pilot or user rehearsal; collect feedback and defect/adoption issues.
- Validate training effectiveness (pre/post tests) and refine materials.
- Conduct go-live dry run with end-to-end comms and support processes.

10) Compliance and Accessibility
- Review and document mandatory training completions (where required).
- Validate accessibility (e.g., WCAG) and translations.

Phase 3 – Execute and Support:
11) Execute Communications
- Send sequenced announcements, countdowns, and “day‑of” instructions.
- Leverage sponsors and managers for local reinforcement.

12) Deliver Training and Enablement
- Deliver role-based sessions; track attendance and proficiency.
- Provide office hours, coaching clinics, and self-service learning paths.

13) Go-Live and Hypercare
- Activate hypercare command center with defined hours, war room rituals, and dashboards.
- Monitor incidents, adoption, sentiment, training gaps; prioritize fixes.
- Provide field support and champion network amplification.

14) Resistance and Issue Management
- Identify resistance signals (low attendance, negative sentiment, circumvention).
- Apply targeted interventions: manager 1:1s, refresher microlearning, process tweaks.

Phase 4 – Reinforce and Transition:
15) Adoption Measurement and Benefits Tracking
- Track usage metrics, time-to-proficiency, and KPIs tied to business outcomes.
- Report to sponsors and CAB; compare actuals vs success criteria.

16) Reinforcement and Continuous Improvement
- Release tips, nudges, and “What’s New” updates; recognize adopters and champions.
- Update knowledge articles and SOPs based on lessons from hypercare.

17) Transition to BAU
- Exit hypercare when exit criteria are met; hand over to Service Owner and Operations.
- Archive OCM artifacts; close risks/issues or reassign to BAU governance.

18) Lessons Learned and Closure
- Conduct retrospective; capture what to replicate/avoid in future rollouts.
- Update OCM playbooks, templates, and metrics definitions.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- OCM strategy and integrated plan (timeline, resources, budget).
- Stakeholder map, sponsor plan, champion network roster.
- Change impact assessment and readiness assessments.
- Communications plan, calendar, and approved messages/assets.
- Training plan, curricula, content (eLearning, guides, videos) and completion logs.
- Support readiness pack: knowledge articles, scripts, FAQs, escalation matrices.
- Hypercare plan and operational dashboards.
- Adoption and sentiment reports; KPI dashboards.
- Compliance records (training completions, approvals).
- Transition-to-BAU documentation and lessons learned.

Success criteria:
- Adoption thresholds met (e.g., >85% active usage in targeted groups).
- Time-to-proficiency within target (e.g., 2 weeks for core roles).
- Training completion >95% for mandatory roles with satisfactory assessment scores.
- Hypercare incident volume and severity within forecast; MTTR within SLA.
- Positive stakeholder sentiment/NPS and benefits realization milestones achieved.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Executive Sponsor: Champion the change; remove roadblocks; communicate vision and urgency.
- Change Manager (OCM Lead): Own OCM strategy, plans, execution, metrics, and reporting.
- Project/Release Manager: Integrate OCM with project and release plans; manage dependencies.
- Service Owner: Define business outcomes; approve comms/training content; own BAU transition.
- Communications Lead: Develop and execute comms; ensure brand, tone, and approvals.
- Training/L&D Lead: Design curricula; develop and deliver training; track completion and proficiency.
- Business Managers/People Leaders: Localize messages; manage resistance; support training attendance.
- Change Champions/SMEs: Provide peer support, feedback, and advocacy; support pilots.
- Service Desk Manager: Prepare support; staff and manage hypercare; report support metrics.
- Knowledge Manager: Author and maintain KB articles and SOPs.
- HR/Org Development: Align changes with performance management and incentives; address workforce impacts.
- Security/Privacy/Compliance: Review content and process for regulatory compliance; approve when required.
- Data/Analytics Lead: Build adoption dashboards; instrument usage tracking.
- CAB/Change Authority: Approve change; govern risk thresholds and go/no-go decisions.

## Best Practices
- Integrate OCM from the outset; fund and resource it as a core workstream.
- Use a structured methodology (e.g., ADKAR, Kotter) and adapt to agile increments.
- Build a visible, active sponsorship coalition; equip managers with toolkits.
- Segment audiences and personalize messaging; focus on WIIFM and role impacts.
- Deliver blended, role-based learning; leverage microlearning and just-in-time job aids.
- Establish a champion network for peer influence and field intelligence.
- Prepare support thoroughly: knowledge up front, realistic staffing, and clear escalation.
- Pilot where possible; use findings to reduce risk before broad rollout.
- Ensure accessibility and inclusive design; translate content where needed.
- Instrument adoption analytics early; define clear, leading indicators (not just lagging).
- Maintain a single source of truth for comms and knowledge; prevent version drift.
- Plan reinforcement beyond go-live (nudges, recognition, refresher content).

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Insufficient sponsorship: Secure explicit commitments, regular sponsor messaging, and visible engagement.
- Change saturation: Maintain a change calendar; sequence/wave deployments; coordinate with enterprise portfolio.
- Resistance and low engagement: Use manager-led conversations, targeted coaching, and address pain points quickly.
- Training not aligned to roles: Conduct task analysis; build role-specific paths; validate with SMEs and pilots.
- Distributed/remote workforce: Use multiple channels and asynchronous learning; leverage collaboration tools.
- Inadequate support readiness: Shift-left knowledge; create targeted scripts; staff hypercare; simulate call scenarios.
- Poor data on impacted users: Reconcile HRIS, AD, and application data; validate with business leaders.
- Language and accessibility gaps: Plan translations; meet accessibility standards; test with diverse users.
- Scope creep and timeline compression: Protect critical OCM milestones; negotiate MVP and phased adoption.

## Performance Metrics
Adoption and proficiency:
- Active usage rate by role/group within defined timeframes.
- Time-to-proficiency (assessment pass rates, task completion accuracy and time).
- Feature adoption rates for critical capabilities.

Readiness and training:
- Training completion and assessment scores by role/location.
- Readiness index (awareness, desire, knowledge, ability scores from surveys).

Support effectiveness:
- Change-related incidents/requests volume and trend; proportion resolved by knowledge articles.
- First Contact Resolution and MTTR during hypercare.
- Knowledge article views, helpfulness ratings, and search success.

Sentiment and stakeholder health:
- Stakeholder NPS/CSAT; manager confidence scores.
- Resistance indicators (declines in attendance, negative feedback trends).

Business outcomes (tie to value):
- Process KPIs impacted by the change (e.g., cycle time, error rate).
- Benefits realization milestones vs plan.

Governance:
- Compliance with comms/training schedule; audit trail completeness.

## Technology and Tools
- ITSM platforms: ServiceNow, Jira Service Management (incidents, changes, knowledge, SLAs).
- Knowledge base and documentation: Confluence, SharePoint, Guru.
- Collaboration and comms: Microsoft Teams, Slack, email platforms, intranet/CMS, town hall tools (e.g., Zoom/Webinar).
- Learning management and content: LMS (Cornerstone, SuccessFactors, Docebo), content tools (Articulate, Camtasia), virtual labs/sandboxes.
- Digital adoption platforms: WalkMe, Pendo, Whatfix for in-app guidance and analytics.
- Survey and sentiment: Qualtrics, Medallia, MS Forms, Pulse surveys.
- Analytics/BI: Power BI, Tableau, Looker for adoption dashboards and KPI tracking.
- Scheduling and resource planning: Smartsheet, MS Project, Jira for integrated plans.
- Chatbots/virtual agents: Deflect common “how-to” queries post go-live.
- Translation and accessibility: Localization tools; accessibility checkers (e.g., WAVE).

This process ensures people are ready, willing, and able to use new IT services and solutions, lowering risk and accelerating value realization from technology investments.
