Process Details:
## Overview
Provide IT infrastructure service and capabilities is the end-to-end process by which the IT function delivers and operates foundational infrastructure services that enable business applications and day-to-day operations. It covers provisioning, configuring, securing, monitoring, maintaining, optimizing, and retiring infrastructure components and platform capabilities.

Scope includes:
- Compute (virtual machines, containers, serverless runtimes), storage, databases, and data platforms
- Networking (LAN/WAN, VPN, load balancers, DNS/DHCP/IPAM)
- Identity and access (directory, SSO, MFA), secrets management
- Observability (monitoring, logging, APM, event management)
- Platform services (Kubernetes, middleware, message queues)
- Backup, recovery, and disaster recovery
- Endpoint management for servers and shared infrastructure devices
- Cloud and on-premise infrastructure (hybrid/multi-cloud)

Purpose:
- Deliver reliable, secure, scalable, and cost-effective infrastructure services aligned to business needs and SLAs
- Provide standardized, automated capabilities to accelerate product and application delivery
- Ensure compliance with security and regulatory requirements
- Maintain accurate asset and configuration records to support supportability and audits

Role in the organization:
- Foundational enabler for all digital services and internal operations
- Partner to application, data, and security teams, providing platforms and shared capabilities
- Key contributor to business continuity, resilience, and risk management


## Key Activities
- Service catalog management: Define, publish, and maintain standard infrastructure service offerings and SLAs/SLOs
- Demand intake and fulfillment: Triage and fulfill service requests and provisioning demands
- Capacity and availability management: Plan, forecast, and ensure capacity and HA/DR are adequate
- Provisioning and configuration: Build and configure infrastructure using automation and standards
- Security and compliance: Apply baselines, hardening, vulnerability remediation, and policy enforcement
- Observability and event management: Implement monitoring, logging, alerting, and SRE practices
- Backup and disaster recovery: Configure, test, and operate backup/restore and DR runbooks
- Change, release, and patch management: Govern updates with minimal risk and downtime
- Access management: Provision least-privilege access and manage credentials/secrets
- Cost and asset management: Tagging, showback/chargeback, license governance, CMDB/asset updates
- Documentation and knowledge: Runbooks, diagrams, SOPs, and knowledge articles
- Lifecycle management: Evergreen upgrades, tech refresh, and decommissioning
- Continuous improvement: Post-incident reviews, optimization, and automation expansion


## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs
  - Approved infrastructure service definitions with SLAs/SLOs and support tiers
  - Architecture standards, reference designs, and security baselines (CIS, hardening guides)
  - Capacity plans and forecasts; approved budgets
  - Approved service requests/work orders and change records
  - Access approvals and role definitions for IAM
  - Vendor contracts, licenses, and support entitlements
  - Network addressing plans, DNS/DHCP scopes, and firewall policies
  - CMDB data model and naming/tagging standards
  - Backup/DR policies including RPO/RTO targets

- Prerequisites
  - Operational ITSM platform (incident, change, request, CMDB)
  - Automation toolchains (IaC, CI/CD, configuration management)
  - Monitoring/logging platforms and alert routing
  - Segregated environments (dev/test/stage/prod) and landing zones/tenants
  - Security tooling (EDR, vulnerability scanners, secrets vault) integrated with pipelines
  - Governance guardrails (e.g., cloud policies, RBAC, quotas)
  - Network connectivity established (on-prem, cloud, hybrid)

- Dependencies on other processes
  - 8.7.7 Manage infrastructure resource administration (asset, inventory, capacity)
  - Change and release management
  - Incident, problem, and request fulfillment
  - Information security management and risk/compliance
  - Supplier/vendor and license management
  - Financial management/FinOps and budgeting
  - Business continuity/disaster recovery management
  - Enterprise architecture and standards


## Process Steps
1) Plan and prepare
- Review demand pipeline, capacity forecasts, and SLAs/SLOs
- Validate architecture alignment and security baselines for requested services
- Confirm budgets, licenses, and vendor capacity
- Define success metrics and acceptance criteria for the request
- Artifacts: Delivery plan, risk assessment, change record (if required)

2) Intake and triage
- Receive request via catalog/work order with required details (environment, sizing, data classification, connectivity, tags, RPO/RTO, timeline)
- Validate completeness; route to appropriate platform team (cloud, network, storage, DB, Kubernetes)
- Determine if standard offering fits or if exception/engineering is needed
- Artifacts: Triage log, request validation checklist

3) Design and capacity check
- Map request to standard patterns (golden images, modules, Helm charts, blueprints)
- Evaluate capacity and availability; trigger capacity expansion if needed
- Define network placement, segmentation, firewall rules, and DNS/DHCP
- Select backup/DR tiers and observability coverage
- Artifacts: Low-level design (LLD), bill of materials, cost estimate, change proposal

4) Authorization and scheduling
- Submit or update change record (normal/standard/emergency) with back-out plans
- Obtain security approval for data classification and connectivity
- Coordinate maintenance windows and stakeholder communications
- Artifacts: Approved change, comms plan

5) Provisioning and configuration (automated by default)
- Use IaC to provision infrastructure (e.g., Terraform, ARM, CloudFormation, vSphere)
- Configure OS/hypervisor/container runtime; join domain if required
- Apply configuration management (Ansible/Puppet/Chef) for baseline hardening, packages, and agents (monitoring, backup, EDR)
- Implement network rules, load balancers, TLS certificates, and DNS
- Configure IAM roles/policies and secrets in vault; enforce least privilege
- Artifacts: Pipeline run logs, configuration state files, assigned asset IDs

6) Integration and observability
- Register assets/config items in CMDB with relationships and tags
- Configure monitoring, metrics, logs, traces, and SLOs/error budgets
- Set alert thresholds, notification routes, and on-call schedules
- Enable backups per policy and test initial restore for critical systems
- Artifacts: CMDB updates, monitoring dashboards, backup job records

7) Verification and acceptance
- Execute functional verification (ping, port checks, dependency checks)
- Perform security scans and policy-as-code evaluations; remediate findings
- Validate RPO/RTO, performance baselines, and access controls
- Obtain Operational Readiness Review (ORR) sign-off from stakeholders
- Artifacts: Test results, ORR checklist, signed acceptance

8) Handover and documentation
- Update runbooks, SOPs, topology diagrams, and knowledge articles
- Provide access to support teams and customers via the service catalog
- Confirm support model (L1/L2/L3), escalation paths, and SLAs
- Artifacts: Runbooks, knowledge articles, support model document

9) Operate and support
- Monitor and respond to events/incidents; follow incident and problem management
- Perform routine maintenance: patching, certificate rotation, capacity tuning
- Execute backups and DR drills; track success and remediate failures
- Manage cost optimization (rightsizing, scheduling, reserved instances)
- Artifacts: Incident/problem records, maintenance logs, DR drill reports, FinOps reports

10) Continuous improvement and lifecycle
- Review SLOs, incidents, and change outcomes; identify improvement actions
- Reduce toil via additional automation and self-service enhancements
- Plan lifecycle refresh or decommission when services are no longer needed
- Securely decommission: data sanitization, revoke access, release resources, update CMDB
- Artifacts: PIRs, improvement backlog, decommission checklist and evidence


## Outputs and Deliverables
- Provisioned and operational infrastructure services/capabilities per request
- Updated CMDB/asset inventory with accurate relationships and tags
- Monitoring dashboards, alerts, and SLO/error budget definitions
- Configured backup/DR with tested restore points; DR runbooks
- Security baselines, scan reports, and compliance attestations
- Runbooks, SOPs, and knowledge articles; architecture and network diagrams
- Change, incident, and maintenance records
- Cost/showback/chargeback reports and tagging compliance

Success criteria:
- Services meet agreed SLAs/SLOs and security/compliance requirements
- Provisioning delivered within defined lead times with minimal rework
- CMDB accuracy > 95% and zero unauthorized changes
- Backup success rate and RPO/RTO adherence
- Positive customer satisfaction (CSAT) and reduced incident rates
- Cost efficiency targets met (e.g., rightsizing savings, reserved coverage)


## Roles and Responsibilities
- Infrastructure service owner
  - Owns service strategy, SLAs/SLOs, roadmap, and continuous improvement
- Platform engineers (cloud/compute/storage/network/database/Kubernetes)
  - Design, build, automate, and operate respective platforms; maintain standards and modules
- Site reliability engineer (SRE)
  - Define SLOs/error budgets; implement observability; lead reliability improvements and toil reduction
- Security/IAM engineer
  - Define and enforce security baselines, IAM policies, secrets management, and vulnerability remediation
- Change/release manager
  - Govern change process, approvals, and deployment windows; track success rates
- Configuration/CMDB manager
  - Maintain CMDB data model, discovery, and CI relationships; ensure accuracy
- Service desk (L1) and operations (L2/L3)
  - Handle requests, incidents, and escalations; execute runbooks
- DR/BCP lead
  - Ensure backup/DR plans, tests, and RPO/RTO compliance
- Vendor/license manager
  - Manage supplier SLAs, license compliance, and support escalations
- FinOps/IT finance analyst
  - Monitor and optimize cost; manage showback/chargeback, budgeting
- QA/test engineer
  - Validate builds against requirements and security/compliance
- Application/product team (customer)
  - Provide requirements, data classification, and participate in ORR; own application-level configuration


## Best Practices
- Standardize offerings and patterns
  - Publish well-defined catalog items with golden images, blueprints, and reference architectures
- Automate everything
  - Use IaC, configuration management, and pipelines; keep automation idempotent and tested
- Implement policy and governance as code
  - Enforce guardrails (cloud policies, OPA/Sentinel), tagging, RBAC, and quotas programmatically
- Build secure-by-default
  - Harden baselines, zero-trust networking, MFA/SSO, secrets vaults, and continuous vulnerability scanning
- Design for reliability
  - Multi-AZ/region, HA patterns, chaos testing where appropriate, DR drills, and capacity headroom
- Observability-first
  - Standard metrics/logs/traces; SLOs with alerting tied to user impact; reduce noise via event correlation
- Self-service enablement
  - Provide curated blueprints and guardrailed portals for faster, safer provisioning
- Cost-awareness (FinOps)
  - Rightsize, schedule non-prod, reserved/savings plans, storage tiering, and regular cost reviews
- Documentation and knowledge
  - Keep runbooks close to code (docs-as-code), versioned and reviewed; maintain accurate diagrams
- Continuous compliance
  - Integrate compliance checks into pipelines; remediate drift automatically
- Segregation and least privilege
  - Environment isolation, network segmentation, and minimal access with JIT/JEA controls
- Lifecycle discipline
  - Patch regularly, track EOL/EOS, execute tech refresh plans, and decommission cleanly


## Common Challenges
- Configuration drift and manual changes
  - Solution: Enforce changes via automation only; detect drift with config scanners and correct automatically
- Shadow IT and sprawl
  - Solution: Strengthen catalog offerings, tagging, and guardrails; implement discovery and showback
- Capacity shortages or overprovisioning
  - Solution: Improve forecasting, autoscaling, and rightsizing; regularly review utilization
- Siloed teams and slow handoffs
  - Solution: Cross-functional squads, shared backlogs, and platform product ownership; automate approvals for standard changes
- Alert fatigue and noisy monitoring
  - Solution: Event correlation, SLO-based alerting, runbook automation, and continuous tuning
- Security misconfigurations
  - Solution: Baselines as code, pre-deployment checks, continuous scanning, and least-privilege IAM templates
- Complex multi-cloud/hybrid operations
  - Solution: Standardize abstractions, landing zones, and common toolchains; central policy and identity
- License and compliance risks
  - Solution: Centralized license management, continuous compliance scanning, and audit-ready CMDB
- Long lead times to provision
  - Solution: Expand self-service blueprints, pre-approved standard changes, and reusable modules
- Backup/DR gaps discovered during incidents
  - Solution: Automated backup verification, periodic restore tests, and DR exercises with executives


## Performance Metrics
- Provisioning lead time: Request to ready-for-use (by service type and environment)
- Change success rate: Percentage of infra changes with no incidents or rollbacks
- SLA/SLO attainment: Availability, latency, and error budget consumption per service
- Incident metrics: MTTR, MTTD, incident rate per 1,000 CIs, repeat incidents
- Configuration drift rate: Number of drift events detected and auto-remediated
- Patch currency: Percentage of infrastructure within patch SLA
- Backup/DR effectiveness: Backup success rate, time-to-restore tests, RPO/RTO adherence
- Capacity/utilization: CPU/memory/storage/network utilization vs. thresholds; saturation alerts
- Cost efficiency: Cost per workload, rightsizing savings, reserved coverage %, idle resource rate
- Security posture: Vulnerability remediation time, baseline compliance %, IAM policy violations
- CMDB accuracy: Completeness and correctness of CIs and relationships
- Self-service adoption: Percentage of requests fulfilled via automated catalog blueprints
- Customer satisfaction (CSAT): Post-fulfillment and post-incident surveys


## Technology and Tools
- ITSM and CMDB: ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, BMC Remedy; discovery tools for CMDB
- IaC and pipelines: Terraform, CloudFormation/ARM/Bicep, Pulumi; Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps
- Configuration management: Ansible, Puppet, Chef, DSC
- Container platforms: Kubernetes, OpenShift; Helm, Argo CD, Flux
- Virtualization and hyperconverged: VMware vSphere/NSX/vSAN, Nutanix
- Cloud providers and governance: AWS, Azure, GCP; AWS Control Tower, Azure Policy, GCP Organization Policy
- Observability: Prometheus/Grafana, Datadog, New Relic, Dynatrace; ELK/Opensearch, Splunk; ServiceNow Event Mgmt, Moogsoft
- Network and delivery: F5/NGINX load balancers, SD-WAN, Cisco/Arista; DNS/DHCP/IPAM (Infoblox)
- Identity and secrets: Azure AD/Entra, Okta, Keycloak; HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS/Secrets Manager
- Security: EDR (CrowdStrike, Defender), vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys), compliance as code (OPA, Sentinel), SAST/secret scanning
- Backup and DR: Veeam, Commvault, Rubrik, Druva; Zerto, VMware SRM; cloud-native backups
- Endpoint/server management: Microsoft MECM/Intune, WSUS/Ivanti, Jamf (for shared infra endpoints)
- Cost management: Apptio/Cloudability, CloudHealth, native cloud cost tools
- Documentation and runbooks: Docs-as-code in Git, Confluence; diagramming (draw.io, Lucidchart)

Process Details:
## Overview
Provide IT resolution capabilities is the systematic establishment, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the people, knowledge, tools, and procedures required to resolve IT incidents and service requests efficiently and reliably. It ensures that the support organization (service desk, technical support, engineering, and vendors) possesses the right skills, documented playbooks, access rights, and automation to restore service, fulfill requests, and meet SLAs/OLAs.

This process sits within Operate IT user support and underpins incident, service request, change, and problem management by:
- Defining the resolution model (tiers or swarming), escalation paths, and vendor engagement.
- Building and curating resolution knowledge (runbooks, KB articles, diagnostics).
- Equipping teams with the tools, environments, and access they need to act.
- Developing people (skills matrix, training, certification, coaching).
- Embedding automation and “shift-left” to increase first-contact resolution and self-service.

## Key Activities
- Capability assessment and planning: assess skill gaps, tooling needs, and coverage; create improvement plan.
- Resolution model design: define tiers/swarms, assignment rules, escalation criteria, and handoff standards.
- Knowledge creation and curation: develop SOPs, runbooks, KB articles, decision trees; adopt KCS practices.
- Tooling and access enablement: provision ITSM, remote support, monitoring, diagnostic tools; set least-privilege access and JIT workflows.
- Automation and self-heal: implement standard changes, scripts, and runbook automation; expose self-service fixes.
- Training and certification: role-based curricula, labs, simulations, shadowing, and certification tracking.
- Vendor and third-party enablement: maintain support contracts, support accounts, and engagement procedures.
- On-call and major-incident readiness: rosters, paging, communication templates, and war-room practices.
- Quality assurance and continuous improvement: audits, ticket reviews, RCA feedback loops, and metric-driven enhancements.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs
  - Incident and request volume/typology, trends, peak patterns.
  - SLAs/OLAs, service catalog, support hours, languages.
  - Current skill matrix and training records.
  - Service architecture, CMDB, dependency maps, known errors/workarounds.
  - Tool inventories, licenses, vendor support contracts/SLAs.
  - Security, compliance, and change control policies.
  - Historical performance metrics (FCR, MTTR, escalations, reopens).

- Prerequisites
  - Defined support operating model (tiered or swarming) and governance.
  - ITSM platform and integrated knowledge base in place.
  - Access governance model (RBAC, PAM, JIT approvals).
  - Budget and leadership sponsorship for enablement, tools, and training.
  - Baseline documentation standards and version control.

- Dependencies on other processes
  - Incident and Service Request Management (intake and prioritization).
  - Knowledge Management (KCS methodology, article lifecycle).
  - Problem Management (RCA, known errors).
  - Change Enablement (standard changes for fixes; emergency changes).
  - Configuration/Asset Management (CMDB accuracy, asset details).
  - Vendor/Supplier Management (support contracts, escalation).
  - Security Operations and IAM (privileged access, secure handling).
  - Release and Deployment Management (new/changed services and runbooks).
  - Capacity and Availability Management (preventive improvements).
  - Workforce Management/HR (hiring, scheduling, performance).

## Process Steps
1) Assess and plan capabilities (quarterly and on change)
- Analyze ticket data by service, priority, time, and resolution path.
- Map skills-to-demand; identify gaps in people, tools, access, and knowledge.
- Prioritize improvements with business impact and risk; create a roadmap with owners and timelines.

2) Define or validate the resolution operating model
- Choose tiered support or swarming model (or hybrid) per service.
- Document assignment rules, escalation criteria (time, priority, complexity), and swarming triggers.
- Define handoff quality criteria (required diagnostics, reproduction steps, logs).
- Establish OLAs between groups; publish escalation matrices and contact trees.

3) Build and maintain resolution knowledge
- For top incident types and requests, create SOPs/runbooks/KBs using KCS.
- Standardize structure: purpose, symptoms, diagnostics, steps, rollback, verification, comms templates.
- Tag with services/CIs, keywords; link to known errors and standard changes.
- Implement review cycles (e.g., every 6–12 months or after 5 uses/first failure) and retirement criteria.

4) Enable tools, environments, and access
- Provision ITSM integrations with monitoring, logs, CMDB, and chat/telephony.
- Set up remote support tools, diagnostic utilities, and test/sandbox environments mirroring prod.
- Configure AIOps triage, alert correlation, and event-to-incident workflows.
- Implement PAM and JIT access for privileged tasks; pre-approve standard changes and scripts.

5) Develop people and validate competency
- Create role-based learning paths per service (L1/L2/L3; product-specific).
- Deliver blended training: e-learning, labs, shadowing, simulations, certification.
- Maintain an updated skills matrix; schedule cross-training and mentoring.
- Conduct periodic capability validations (skills assessments, scenario drills).

6) Implement automation and shift-left
- Convert frequent, low-risk fixes into automated runbooks/self-heal jobs.
- Publish self-service request/resolution items with guardrails and dynamic approvals.
- Embed decision trees and suggested actions in agent desktop; use virtual agents for triage/resolution.

7) Establish on-call, major-incident, and vendor engagement readiness
- Publish on-call rosters, paging policies, and time-to-engage targets.
- Prepare major-incident runbooks, comms templates, and war-room standards.
- Maintain vendor support contacts, SSO accounts, runbooks, and data-sharing agreements.
- Test failover communications and vendor engagement quarterly.

8) Pilot and operationalize
- Pilot new capabilities with a subset of services; collect feedback and adjust.
- Roll out widely with release notes, quick reference guides, and office hours.
- Update the service catalog and knowledge repository accordingly.

9) Monitor, audit, and improve
- Track KPIs/KRIs; perform ticket QA reviews and knowledge audits.
- Run RCAs on major incidents and chronic issues; feed outcomes into knowledge and training.
- Retire obsolete content; version and communicate updates.
- Reassess quarterly; update the roadmap.

Governance checkpoints
- Change Advisory Board approval for changes to automation and standard changes as required.
- Security review for privileged access and data handling in tooling.
- Vendor management review for contract changes and escalations.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Documented resolution model (tiers/swarms), escalation matrix, and OLAs.
- Skills matrix by team/member; training curricula; certification records.
- Resolution knowledge: SOPs, runbooks, KB articles, decision trees.
- Tooling: configured ITSM workflows, automations, integrations; remote support and diagnostics toolkits.
- Access enablement: PAM/JIT configurations, role profiles, standard change templates.
- On-call schedules, major-incident playbooks, communication templates.
- Vendor engagement artifacts: support contracts, contact lists, runbooks.
- Performance reports and improvement backlog with owners and due dates.

Success criteria
- SLA adherence and improved MTTR/FCR versus baseline.
- Reduced escalations and re-open rates; higher self-service deflection.
- Positive customer satisfaction (CSAT) and agent productivity gains.
- Audit compliance for access, documentation, and change handling.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- IT Resolution Capability Owner: accountable for this process, roadmap, KPI performance, and governance.
- Service Owners: define service-specific resolution requirements; approve runbooks and standard changes.
- Incident Manager/Major Incident Manager: ensure rapid triage, engagement, comms, and post-incident actions.
- Knowledge Manager: govern KCS practices, article quality, and lifecycle.
- Problem Manager: drive RCAs; create known errors/workarounds feeding knowledge base.
- L1 Service Desk: initial triage, FCR using scripts/KB; escalate with complete diagnostics.
- L2/L3 Support Engineers: advanced diagnostics and resolution; author runbooks; mentor L1.
- Tooling/Platform Administrators (ITSM, monitoring, AIOps, remote support): implement and maintain tools/integrations and automations.
- Security/IAM/PAM Administrators: manage privileged access, JIT workflows, and audit.
- Vendor Manager: maintain contracts, SLAs, and escalation paths; coordinate vendor support.
- Training/Enablement Lead: design and deliver training; track competencies.
- Workforce Management: staffing, scheduling, on-call administration; capacity planning.
- QA/Process Analyst: ticket quality audits; compliance checks; continuous improvement facilitation.

## Best Practices
- Adopt KCS to embed knowledge capture and reuse in the resolution workflow.
- Use a shift-left strategy: move resolvable work closer to the user via self-service and empower L1 with better tools and access.
- Choose a swarming model for complex, cross-domain incidents to reduce handoffs.
- Standardize diagnostics and handoff checklists to minimize “ping-pong.”
- Treat runbooks and KB as versioned products with owners, SLAs for updates, and usage analytics.
- Implement least-privilege and JIT access with privileged session recording for audit.
- Align automations to standard changes; include clear rollback and safety checks.
- Integrate observability (monitoring, logs, traces) into the agent desktop for faster triage.
- Regularly conduct incident simulations and game days to validate readiness.
- Close the loop: make RCA outcomes mandatory inputs to knowledge, automation, and training updates.
- Measure what matters; publish dashboards and review in operational cadence.
- Ensure inclusive global coverage: language support, time zones, and accessibility considerations.

## Common Challenges
- Skill gaps and high turnover: mitigate with structured curricula, career pathways, and mentoring; maintain an evergreen skills matrix.
- Tool sprawl and poor integration: rationalize tools; integrate ITSM with monitoring, logs, CMDB, and chat; standardize agent workspace.
- Access delays: implement pre-approved JIT access and standard changes for common privileged tasks.
- Knowledge decay and inconsistency: enforce KCS, ownership, and review cadences; use templates and quality checks.
- Escalation “ping-pong”: define clear handoff criteria; adopt swarming for multi-domain issues; measure and coach on incomplete escalations.
- Incomplete CMDB/dependency data: invest in discovery and service mapping; require CI linkage in tickets.
- Vendor bottlenecks: negotiate OLAs with vendors; maintain good engagement practices and clear escalation paths.
- Security constraints vs. speed: involve security early; pre-authorize low-risk automations; use PAM to balance speed and control.
- Changes breaking runbooks: tie runbook updates to release/change processes; validate in pre-prod; include rollback guidance.
- Language/time-zone issues in global teams: provide multilingual KB and follow-the-sun scheduling.

## Performance Metrics
- Effectiveness and speed
  - MTTR by priority and service.
  - Mean time to engage correct resolver; time at each tier.
  - First contact resolution rate and remote fix rate.
  - Escalation rate and average number of handoffs per ticket.
  - Reopen/recurrence rate within 7/30 days.

- Quality and customer experience
  - CSAT post-resolution; complaint rate.
  - Ticket quality score (completeness of diagnostics, CI linkage, KB usage).
  - % incidents linked to known errors/workarounds.

- Knowledge and shift-left
  - KB reuse rate per ticket; KB contribution rate; article health (age, last review).
  - Self-service deflection rate; virtual agent resolution rate.
  - Automation success rate and volume of automated fixes.

- Compliance and readiness
  - % of privileged actions using PAM/JIT; access approval SLA.
  - On-call coverage adherence; major-incident response time.
  - Audit findings closure rate for documentation and access controls.

- Efficiency and cost
  - Cost per ticket; agent utilization; backlog age distribution.

Set targets per service criticality and review in weekly operational reviews and quarterly capability reviews.

## Technology and Tools
- ITSM platform: ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, BMC Helix, Freshservice.
- Knowledge management: integrated KB with KCS support; Confluence or equivalent for design docs; search relevance tuning.
- Observability and diagnostics: APM (Dynatrace, AppDynamics, New Relic), infrastructure monitoring (Datadog, Zabbix, Prometheus/Grafana), log analytics (Splunk, ELK), network tools (Wireshark), database clients.
- AIOps/event management: Moogsoft, BigPanda, ServiceNow ITOM, Azure Monitor/Action Groups.
- Remote support: BeyondTrust/Bomgar, TeamViewer, Splashtop, Microsoft Quick Assist; secure file transfer tools.
- Endpoint and configuration management: Microsoft Intune, SCCM/MECM, Jamf, Ansible, Puppet, Chef.
- Runbook automation and orchestration: Ansible Tower/AWX, Rundeck, Power Automate, ServiceNow Flow Designer, PagerDuty Automation.
- ChatOps and collaboration: Microsoft Teams, Slack, Zoom; incident comms add-ons; virtual agents.
- Major incident management and paging: PagerDuty, Opsgenie, xMatters.
- CMDB and discovery/service mapping: ServiceNow Discovery/Service Mapping, Device42.
- Identity, access, and PAM: Okta/Azure AD for SSO; CyberArk, Thycotic/Delinea for PAM; JIT access workflows.
- Version control and documentation: Git, GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket for runbooks and scripts; controlled releases.
- Test/sandbox environments: representative non-prod stacks; synthetic transaction tools.

# [8.7.8.4] Escalate IT Requests

## Overview
Escalate IT Requests is the codified procedure for transferring ownership, decision-making, or action of an IT request (incident, service request, access request, problem, or change-related issue) to a higher support tier, another functional team, supplier, or management level when predefined criteria are met. The purpose is to ensure timely, effective resolution and risk-appropriate decision-making, protecting business operations and meeting SLAs/OLAs/UCs.

This process:
- Ensures issues exceeding the scope, permissions, or time constraints of the current resolver are promptly routed to the most capable group.
- Provides a consistent, auditable escalation pathway across functional, hierarchical, and supplier domains.
- Integrates with major incident, problem, change, access, and security response processes.
- Improves customer experience through timely communication and expectations management.

Scope includes all IT user support channels (service desk, self-service portal, chat/virtual agent, email, phone) and all severity levels, with special handling for Major Incidents (P1) and security/privacy events.

## Key Activities
- Triage and escalation need assessment based on impact, urgency, risk, and SLA timers.
- Selection of escalation type: functional/technical, hierarchical/managerial, vendor/supplier, or major incident/security.
- Preparation of escalation package (context, reproduction steps, logs, diagnostics, attempted steps, impact analysis).
- Execution of escalation via ITSM tool reassignment, paging/on-call, bridge initiation.
- Stakeholder communications and updates per cadence.
- Monitoring acceptance, progress, and further escalation triggers.
- Handover management and warm transfer coordination.
- Closure, documentation, knowledge capture, and post-incident/problem follow-up.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs:
  - An active ticket with categorization, priority (impact x urgency), and SLA/SLO attached.
  - Current troubleshooting notes, diagnostics, and evidence of steps attempted.
  - CMDB/service map references and affected CIs or services.
  - Business impact statement, user contact details, and stakeholder list.
  - Relevant runbooks/KB articles consulted and outcomes.
  - Vendor contracts/UCs and on-call schedules for target groups.

- Prerequisites:
  - Approved escalation policy and matrix (who/when/how, by severity).
  - Defined SLAs/OLAs/UCs and associated timers/thresholds.
  - RACI for incident/request handling and major incident management.
  - Up-to-date on-call rosters and contact lists.
  - Configured ITSM platform enabling reassignment, notifications, and audit trail.
  - Knowledge base and runbooks available to Level 1 before escalation.
  - Integration to collaboration/paging tools (e.g., Slack/Teams, PagerDuty).
  - Major Incident, Security Incident, and Change processes defined and trained.

- Dependencies on other processes:
  - Incident Management and Request Fulfillment (primary owning processes).
  - Major Incident Management (P1/P0 handling).
  - Problem Management (recurrence/structural fix).
  - Change Enablement (if remediation requires change).
  - Access Management (permission-related requests).
  - Knowledge Management (articles and post-resolution updates).
  - Service Level Management (SLA/OLA governance).
  - Supplier/Vendor Management (UCs, escalation contacts).
  - Configuration Management (CMDB accuracy).

## Process Steps
1. Detect Escalation Need
   - Trigger conditions include:
     - Impending or actual SLA breach at current level (e.g., 50% resolution time consumed with no viable path).
     - Required skills, tools, or permissions exceed current resolver scope.
     - Higher business risk or broader impact identified (multiple users/services affected).
     - Dependency on another team or supplier to proceed.
     - Security/privacy indicators present.
     - VIP/Executive impact requiring priority handling.
2. Validate Ticket Quality (Quality Gate)
   - Confirm mandatory fields: category, CI/service, impact/urgency, detailed symptoms, user details.
   - Document steps attempted, error messages/logs, screenshots/attachments.
   - Link related tickets, alerts, and known problems; deduplicate if applicable.
   - Apply standardized escalation template/checklist to prevent “blind” escalations.
3. Determine Escalation Type
   - Functional escalation: to the correct technical group or higher tier (L2/L3/SME).
   - Hierarchical/managerial escalation: to team lead/incident manager for prioritization/resource decisions.
   - Supplier/vendor escalation: to external support per UC/warranty.
   - Major Incident escalation: activate Major Incident Management if P1 threshold met.
   - Security escalation: hand off to Security Incident Response for suspected breach.
4. Set Priority and Target Timers
   - Confirm or adjust priority (impact x urgency). Example thresholds:
     - P1: escalate immediately; target acknowledgment ≤ 10 minutes by target group.
     - P2: escalate within 30 minutes; acknowledgment ≤ 30 minutes.
     - P3: escalate if unresolved after 2 hours; acknowledgment ≤ 4 business hours.
     - P4: escalate if unresolved after 1 business day.
   - Ensure OLA/UC timers for target group are applied.
5. Prepare Escalation Package
   - Concise summary: business impact, scope, symptoms, timeline.
   - Technical detail: logs, metrics, topology/service map, change history, runbook results.
   - Reproduction steps and what has been ruled out.
   - Requested action and urgency.
   - Contacts and availability for live handoff.
6. Execute Escalation
   - Reassign ticket to target group, set correct assignment and priority fields.
   - Trigger notifications/paging per on-call schedule; for P1, start a bridge/war room.
   - For vendor: open case on vendor portal, include diagnostics; link vendor case ID to ticket.
   - For security: open SIR in security tool and relate to incident.
7. Confirm Acceptance and Ownership
   - Ensure target group acknowledges within OLA; if no response, auto-escalate per matrix.
   - Perform warm handoff for live incidents: introduce SME to user/bridge, transfer context verbally.
   - Update ticket with owner and next steps.
8. Coordinate and Communicate
   - Set stakeholder update cadence (e.g., P1: every 15–30 min; P2: hourly).
   - Provide estimated time to restore (ETR) or next checkpoint time.
   - Maintain customer comms via approved channels; log all comms in ticket.
9. Monitor Progress and Re-Escalate if Needed
   - Track progress against work plan and timers.
   - If blocked or risk increases, escalate to next tier/manager or invoke Major Incident.
   - Avoid ping-pong: if reassignment back is attempted, convene quick triage to resolve ownership.
10. Resolution/Handover
    - Once resolved or workaround applied, validate service restoration with user/business.
    - If permanent fix requires change, raise change and coordinate via Change Enablement.
    - For recurring/systemic issues, raise a Problem record and link.
11. Document and Close
    - Complete resolution notes, root cause (if known), and prevention recommendations.
    - Update or create KB article/runbook if a new pattern was discovered.
    - Record SLA outcomes, breach reason codes, and escalation path taken.
    - For P1/P2, schedule post-incident review; log actions and lessons learned.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Updated ticket with:
  - Escalation path, timestamps, and ownership history.
  - Complete diagnostic package and decisions taken.
  - Communications log and stakeholder updates.
  - Resolution details, workaround (if applicable), and validation evidence.
- Vendor case records, bridge recordings/notes (where applicable).
- Problem records and/or change requests raised and linked.
- Knowledge base updates or new articles.
- Post-incident review report for major/high-impact cases.

Success criteria:
- Correct target group engaged on first escalation with timely acknowledgment per OLA.
- Restoration or effective workaround within SLA/SLO.
- No unnecessary handoffs or ping-pong; minimal reassignments.
- Stakeholder communications met cadence standards.
- Complete, auditable documentation with clear rationale.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Service Desk Agent (L1)
  - Triage, initial troubleshooting, ticket quality, determine and trigger escalation.
  - Prepare escalation package; perform warm handoffs.
- Resolver Groups (L2/L3/SMEs)
  - Accept escalations within OLA; lead technical diagnosis and resolution.
  - Escalate further when appropriate; document technical findings.
- Incident Manager
  - Oversee escalations for high-priority cases; ensure adherence to process.
  - Initiate and run bridges; coordinate cross-team efforts.
- Major Incident Manager (for P1)
  - Lead Major Incident process; communications, stakeholder management, ETR setting.
- Team Leads/Shift Leads
  - Provide approvals/prioritization and resource allocation; remove blockers.
- Service Owner
  - Business impact validation; accept risk decisions and post-incident actions.
- Supplier/Vendor Support
  - Respond and resolve within UC; participate in bridges; provide RCAs where required.
- Security Officer/IR Team
  - Lead security escalations; containment and forensic steps.
- Change Manager
  - Assess and schedule emergency/normal changes required for remediation.
- Problem Manager
  - Analyze trends; facilitate root cause and preventive actions post-restoration.
- Service Level Manager
  - Monitor SLA/OLA performance; drive improvements with teams and suppliers.
- Communications/PMO (as needed)
  - Manage executive and broad communications for significant events.

## Best Practices
- Define a clear, visual escalation matrix with contacts, timers, and criteria; keep it current and accessible.
- Automate wherever possible: SLA timers, auto-escalations, paging, assignment suggestions based on AI and CMDB.
- Use impact/urgency matrices consistently; enable dynamic priority upgrades based on telemetry and business events.
- Enforce ticket quality gates with templates and mandatory fields for escalations.
- Favor warm handoffs and swarming over cold reassignments to reduce context loss.
- Establish standardized communication cadences and templates per severity; communicate early and often.
- Integrate monitoring/AIOps with ITSM to correlate alerts and reduce duplicate escalations.
- Pre-approve emergency change pathways for common fixes to avoid delays.
- Maintain robust on-call coverage with rotations, handover notes, and burnout safeguards.
- Protect against “ping-pong”: require joint triage before reassigning back; measure and act on bounce rates.
- Conduct post-incident reviews for P1/P2 and feed improvements into KB, runbooks, and training.
- Include VIP handling rules and privacy/security escalation triggers in policy.
- Align OLAs with SLAs and vendor UCs; avoid gaps that cause systemic breaches.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Unclear ownership leading to delays
  - Solution: RACI, clear service-to-group mapping, assignment rules powered by CMDB/service maps.
- Poor ticket quality on escalation
  - Solution: Mandatory templates, validation checklists, QA spot checks, coaching.
- Delayed acknowledgments by target groups
  - Solution: On-call paging integration, OLA tracking with automated reminders and auto-escalation.
- Over/under-escalation (wrong severity)
  - Solution: Training on impact/urgency; tool-guided priority calculators; business validation.
- Ping-pong between teams
  - Solution: Swarming, joint triage huddles, ownership rules, bounce-rate KPI with corrective actions.
- Vendor slow response
  - Solution: UC SLAs with penalties, vendor scorecards, named TAMs, pre-shared diagnostics packages.
- Time zone and coverage gaps
  - Solution: Follow-the-sun model, handover protocols, regional escalation matrices.
- Communication gaps with stakeholders
  - Solution: Standard comms cadence, templates, comms lead for major incidents, status pages.
- Security incidents misrouted
  - Solution: Clear indicators in forms, SOC triage integration, mandatory security review checklist.
- Changes needed but delayed approvals
  - Solution: Emergency change policies, predefined guardrails, delegated approval thresholds.

## Performance Metrics
- Mean Time to Escalate (MTTE): from ticket open to first qualified escalation.
- Acknowledgment Time by Target Group: time to accept ownership post-escalation.
- Percentage of Tickets Escalated: by service and severity; target healthy range (e.g., L1 FCR > 70% for standard requests).
- First Escalation Success Rate: resolved by first target group without further reassignment.
- Reassignment/Ping-Pong Rate: average reassignments per escalated ticket.
- SLA Compliance for Escalated Tickets: resolution and response adherence by severity.
- Time in Queue per Tier: L1/L2/L3 wait times; identify bottlenecks.
- Major Incident Trigger Latency: time from qualifying event to MIM activation.
- Communication Cadence Compliance: percent of updates delivered on time during escalations.
- Vendor OLA/UC Compliance: response and resolution vs contract.
- Knowledge Capture Rate: percent of escalated tickets resulting in KB updates.
- Customer Satisfaction (CSAT/NPS) for escalated tickets.
- Post-Incident Action Closure Rate: completion of PIR actions within target timeframe.

## Technology and Tools
- ITSM Platforms: ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, BMC Helix/Remedy, Ivanti, Freshservice.
- Monitoring/Observability: Datadog, Dynatrace, New Relic, AppDynamics, Splunk, Prometheus/Grafana, CloudWatch/Azure Monitor.
- AIOps/Event Correlation: Moogsoft, BigPanda, ServiceNow ITOM, PagerDuty Event Intelligence.
- On-Call and Paging: PagerDuty, Atlassian Opsgenie, xMatters.
- Collaboration/Bridges: Microsoft Teams, Slack, Zoom; integrated with ITSM for war rooms.
- Runbook Automation/Orchestration: Ansible Tower/AWX, Rundeck, ServiceNow Orchestration.
- CMDB and Service Mapping: ServiceNow Discovery/Service Mapping, Device42.
- Knowledge Management: ITSM-native KBs, Confluence.
- Contact Center/Telephony: Genesys, Five9, Amazon Connect (for hot transfers and call logging).
- Vendor Portals and Case Management: per supplier (e.g., AWS Support, Microsoft Premier, hardware OEM portals).
- Dashboards/BI: Power BI, Tableau, Grafana (for SLA/OLA and escalation metrics).
- Status Communication: Statuspage, Service Status portals, email/SMS gateways.

# [8.7.8.5] Resolve IT issues/requests

## Overview
Resolve IT issues/requests is the operational process that restores service when something breaks (incidents) and fulfills standard user requests (service requests) within agreed service levels. It spans investigation, diagnosis, resolution or fulfillment, communication, and closure. The process is central to user satisfaction and business continuity, ensuring minimal disruption, predictable delivery, and continuous learning through knowledge management and root-cause linkage.

Scope and boundaries:
- Starts when an incident/request is received or assigned to a resolver group (via service desk, self-service, monitoring, or integration) and the ticket contains sufficient information to act.
- Ends when the user’s service is restored/request fulfilled, documentation is complete, customer confirmation is obtained (when required), and linked follow-up items (e.g., problem record, change) are created.
- Includes major incident handling trigger/participation, functional/hierarchical escalation, vendor engagement, change execution for fixes, and knowledge updates.
- Excludes creation of tickets (handled upstream by logging/intake), preventive problem management, and deployment/release activities unless needed to resolve a ticket.

Objectives:
- Restore service quickly and safely; fulfill requests accurately and on time.
- Meet SLAs/OLAs/UCs, reduce mean time to resolve, increase first-contact resolution.
- Communicate effectively with stakeholders and keep accurate records.
- Feed continuous improvement via knowledge, problem management, and trend analysis.

## Key Activities
- Triage and prioritization based on business impact and urgency.
- Initial diagnosis and first-contact resolution using KB/runbooks.
- Detailed technical troubleshooting and execution of workarounds or permanent fixes.
- Service request fulfillment (tasking, approvals, provisioning, delivery).
- Functional, hierarchical, and vendor escalation when needed.
- Major incident participation/trigger for high-impact cases.
- Change execution coordination (standard/emergency/normal) to implement fixes.
- Communication: acknowledgments, status updates, ETAs, closure confirmations.
- Validation and quality checks prior to closure.
- Documentation: work notes, time entry, resolution codes, asset/CI updates.
- Knowledge contribution and maintenance (KCS).
- Hand-offs to Problem Management for recurring/significant issues.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- A logged ticket with unique ID, category (incident/request), priority, detailed description, contact info, affected service/CI, impact/urgency, attachments/logs as applicable.
- Applicable SLA/OLA and business hours; on-call rota.
- Knowledge articles, diagnostic runbooks, known error database.
- Configuration/asset data (CMDB), service maps, monitoring alerts/events.
- Access to required environments, tools, and credentials.
- Approval artifacts for request items requiring authorization.
- Vendor contract details and escalation paths.

Prerequisites:
- ITSM tool configured with workflows, priority matrix, categories, templates.
- Defined resolver groups, on-call schedules, and escalation paths.
- Published standard request catalog with fulfillment workflows and SLAs.
- Integrated monitoring and event correlation where applicable.
- Security, change, and problem management policies in place.
- Compliance guardrails (logging, PII handling, SoD) and training.

Dependencies on other processes:
- Operate IT user support (intake/logging, categorization/prioritization).
- Major Incident Management.
- Change Enablement/Management.
- Problem Management and Known Error process.
- Knowledge Management.
- Access Management/Identity Governance for provisioning and permissions.
- Asset/Configuration Management (CMDB accuracy).
- Supplier/Vendor Management.
- Release/Deployment Management when fixes require deployment.
- Communications Management for incident updates.
- Information Security Incident Response (for suspected security events).

## Process Steps
1) Receive and verify ticket
- Confirm incident vs service request classification and priority using defined matrix.
- Validate required fields; if incomplete, contact user or service desk to obtain details; add diagnostic attachments (logs, screenshots).
- For alerts/events: deduplicate and correlate to reduce noise; link to existing parent incident if applicable.

2) Acknowledge and communicate
- Send acknowledgment within SLA/OLA (automated where possible).
- Provide initial status/ETA or next update time; set user expectations and impact statement.

3) Triage
- Confirm affected service/CI; check monitoring dashboards and recent changes/releases.
- Consult KB/known errors; attempt first-contact resolution using scripts/runbooks.
- If suspected security incident, follow security IR procedures and reclassify/escalate.

4) Decide path
- Incident resolution path: restore service.
- Request fulfillment path: deliver the approved service item.
- Major incident path: if impact/urgency meets threshold, trigger major incident process and join the bridge; proceed in parallel with resolution steps.

5a) Incident resolution path
- Diagnosis: replicate issue if safe, review logs, metrics, last changes, capacity/availability data; engage swarming if needed.
- Workaround: apply safe workaround to restore service quickly; document clearly.
- Determine if change is required:
  - Standard change: execute pre-approved steps as per catalog.
  - Emergency change: invoke emergency procedure and approvals; ensure rollback plan.
  - Normal change: raise RFC; if waiting would breach SLA/significant impact, consider emergency path per policy.
- Implement fix: configuration update, patch, restart, rollback, data correction, or code hotfix per governance.
- Test/validate: confirm service restoration; monitor for stability; run smoke tests.

5b) Service request fulfillment path
- Validate request type, entitlements, and completeness.
- Route for approvals or auto-approve per policy; track SLAs for approval turnaround.
- Create and assign fulfillment tasks (e.g., access provisioning, hardware dispatch, software install, mailbox changes).
- Execute via automation/orchestration where possible; otherwise, L1/L2/L3 or field techs perform tasks.
- Validate delivery with requestor; ensure compliance (SoD, least privilege, audit logs).

6) Escalation and vendor engagement
- Functional escalation: transfer to the correct resolver group when expertise required; include complete context to avoid rework.
- Hierarchical escalation: engage leadership if SLAs at risk, blockers persist, or cross-team coordination needed.
- Vendor escalation: initiate per UC; provide logs, environment details, and business impact; track vendor SLAs.

7) Communication management
- Provide regular updates based on ticket priority; maintain a comms timeline for major incidents.
- Update status page or service communications channels as appropriate.
- Coordinate with business stakeholders for high-impact incidents.

8) Documentation and knowledge
- Record detailed work notes, diagnostics performed, decisions, and outcomes.
- Select accurate closure categorization codes and cause codes.
- Update/create knowledge articles (KCS): problem statement, environment, symptoms, steps, workaround, fix, references.

9) Validation and closure
- Confirm with user that the issue is resolved/request fulfilled; obtain explicit confirmation for incidents unless auto-closure is approved by policy.
- Ensure no open tasks, approvals, or change records remain; ensure asset/CI updates are complete.
- Close the ticket; trigger customer satisfaction survey where applicable.

10) Post-resolution follow-up
- For significant or recurring issues, create/link a Problem record and capture known error/workaround.
- Participate in post-incident review (blameless) for P1/P2 incidents; publish RFO/RCA within agreed time.
- Raise continuous improvement items (automation candidates, catalog updates, monitoring gaps).

Exception flows:
- User unavailable for validation: attempt per policy (e.g., 3 contact attempts in 5 business days), then close with communication and reopen grace period.
- Duplicate tickets: link/mark as child; communicate via parent.
- Misrouted tickets: reassign with context; notify service desk.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Resolved incidents with documented root cause or workaround.
- Fulfilled service requests with completion evidence and audit trail.
- Communication records: acknowledgments, status updates, closure notes; status page entries where applicable.
- Change records executed and closed; rollback documentation if used.
- Knowledge artifacts: new/updated KB articles, known errors.
- Problem records created/linked for recurring or high-impact issues.
- Updated CMDB/asset records as needed.
- Post-incident reports/RFO/RCA for major incidents.
- Metrics and dashboards for process performance.

Success criteria:
- Service restored or request fulfilled within SLA/OLA.
- Accurate classification and documentation; zero critical fields missing.
- User confirms resolution; CSAT meets target.
- Low reopen/transfer rates; minimal SLA breaches.
- Knowledge captured for reuse; reduction in repeat incidents.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Service Desk Analyst (L1): initial triage, first-contact resolution, ticket enrichment, user comms, routing, simple request fulfillment.
- Resolver Group Engineer (L2/L3): advanced diagnosis, resolution, fulfillment tasks, change execution, documentation, knowledge contribution.
- Incident Manager: coordinates high-priority incidents, runs bridges, ensures comms, tracks SLAs, drives restoration.
- Request Fulfillment Coordinator: oversees request workflows, approvals, tasking, SLA adherence.
- Major Incident Manager: leads major incidents, stakeholder management, RFO delivery.
- Problem Manager: receives escalations for recurring/significant issues, drives RCA and corrective actions.
- Change Manager: governs emergency/normal change approvals and scheduling; ensures proper risk and rollback planning.
- Knowledge Manager: facilitates KCS practices, quality reviews, publication lifecycle.
- Service Owner/Product Owner: prioritizes fixes, accepts risk, approves changes where required, communicates business impact.
- Vendor Manager/Supplier liaison: manages vendor escalations and contract performance.
- Security Operations/SIRT: handles suspected security incidents, coordinates containment/eradication.
- Field Support Technician: on-site hardware swaps, cabling, physical diagnostics.
- NOC/Monitoring Analyst: event correlation, proactive incident creation, health dashboards.
- ITSM Tool Administrator: maintains workflows, automations, queues, and reporting.

## Best Practices
- Shift-left: empower L1 and self-service with high-quality knowledge, diagnostics, and automation.
- Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS): capture, structure, reuse, and improve knowledge as part of work.
- Swarming: collaborative, time-boxed cross-functional troubleshooting to avoid ping-pong handoffs.
- Standardization: use standard change models and request catalog items with clear SLAs and fulfillment steps.
- Automation and orchestration: automate repetitive tasks (password resets, provisioning, reboots), ChatOps integrations, auto-remediation.
- Clear prioritization: impact/urgency matrix tied to business outcomes and service levels; avoid priority inflation.
- Communication discipline: early acknowledgment, consistent updates, clear ETAs, plain language; maintain a single source of truth for status.
- Strong linkage to Change/Problem: verify recent changes during triage, create problems for patterns, minimize change-induced incidents.
- Quality documentation: detailed work notes, accurate closure codes, CI linkage; use templates.
- Post-incident reviews: blameless, timely, with concrete action items and owners; share broadly for learning.
- Environment observability: service maps, dashboards, SLOs/error budgets; correlate incidents to telemetry.
- Access and approvals: pre-approve low-risk items; enforce least privilege and SoD for access-related requests.
- Continual improvement: review metrics and feedback, retire low-value catalog items, refine runbooks, prune noisy alerts.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Incomplete ticket information
  - Solution: mandatory fields, dynamic forms with context-specific questions, intake validation scripts, virtual agent prompts.
- High handoff/transfer rates
  - Solution: skill-based routing, swarming, enriched tickets, resolver group taxonomy cleanup.
- SLA breaches due to bottlenecks
  - Solution: WIP limits, real-time queue monitoring, auto-escalations, on-call optimization, capacity planning.
- Noisy/duplicate alerts
  - Solution: event correlation, deduplication rules, AIOps, tune monitoring thresholds with SLOs.
- Vendor delays
  - Solution: clear UCs with SLAs, escalation paths, contract governance, parallel workstreams when possible.
- Recurring incidents
  - Solution: proactive Problem Management, known error database, permanent fixes prioritized through Change/Release.
- Knowledge gaps/low reuse
  - Solution: KCS coaching, peer reviews, incentives, embed knowledge tasks in DoD for closure.
- Access approval delays
  - Solution: role-based access control, pre-approved standard access, automated approval routing and reminders.
- Documentation drift
  - Solution: versioned runbooks, ownership, regular review cadence tied to PIRs and changes.
- Communication breakdowns in major incidents
  - Solution: defined comms roles, update cadence by priority, templates, status page automation.

## Performance Metrics
- MTTA (Mean Time to Acknowledge) by priority.
- MTTD (Mean Time to Detect) for monitoring-originated incidents.
- MTTR (Mean/Median Time to Resolve) by priority and service.
- First Contact Resolution rate (FCR) and First Level Resolution rate.
- SLA attainment rate (response and resolution); breach count by cause.
- Reopen rate and transfer/reassignment count per ticket.
- Escalation rate (functional/hierarchical) and major incident frequency.
- Backlog volume and age (90th percentile time in queue).
- Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) and Net Effort Score after closure.
- Knowledge metrics: reuse rate, article creation/maintenance throughput, link rate to tickets.
- Automation impact: tickets auto-resolved/fulfilled, mean savings per automation.
- Change-induced incident rate and emergency change count related to incident fixes.
- Vendor performance: vendor MTTR, SLA attainment.
- After-hours load: percentage of work outside business hours, overtime.

Target examples (adjust to context):
- MTTA P1 < 10 minutes; MTTR P1 < 4 hours.
- FCR > 70% for service desk addressable categories.
- SLA attainment > 90%; Reopen rate < 5%.
- CSAT > 4.5/5.

## Technology and Tools
- ITSM platform: ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, BMC Helix/Remedy, Cherwell/Freshservice for ticketing, workflows, SLAs, and knowledge.
- Omnichannel intake: portal, email, phone/IVR, chat/virtual agent, APIs.
- Monitoring/observability: Datadog, New Relic, Dynatrace, Prometheus/Grafana, AppDynamics; service maps.
- Log and APM: Splunk, Elastic, Sumo Logic; distributed tracing.
- Event correlation/AIOps: Moogsoft, BigPanda, ServiceNow ITOM, Opsgenie events.
- Remote support: BeyondTrust/Bomgar, TeamViewer, Quick Assist, Dameware.
- Endpoint and RMM: Microsoft Intune/Endpoint Manager, SCCM/MECM, Jamf, Kaseya, NinjaOne.
- CMDB/Asset: integrated ITSM CMDB, Lansweeper, Device42, Service Graph.
- Identity and access: Active Directory/Azure AD, Okta, SailPoint; PAM tools (CyberArk).
- Orchestration and automation: Ansible, Puppet, Chef, Salt, Rundeck, Power Automate, ServiceNow Flow Designer; ChatOps (Slack, MS Teams) with bots.
- Change/Release: integrated change modules, CI/CD tools (Jenkins, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps) for fix deployment.
- Major incident coordination: bridge/conference tools, PagerDuty/Opsgenie xMatters for on-call and paging, status page tools.
- Knowledge and documentation: Confluence, integrated KB, runbook repositories.
- Security and compliance: SIEM (Splunk ES, QRadar), EDR (Defender, CrowdStrike), ticket tagging and secure fields for sensitive data.
- Analytics and reporting: ITSM dashboards, BI tools (Power BI/Tableau), heatmaps for trends.

[9.1.1.1] Develop and maintain budget policies and procedures
Level: 4

Process Details:
## Overview
Develop and maintain budget policies and procedures is the foundational process that defines how an organization plans, constructs, approves, communicates, and monitors its budgets. It creates a standardized, repeatable, and controlled framework that guides all budget participants across operating expense, headcount, capital expenditure, and cash planning. The process ensures alignment with corporate strategy, financial controls, regulatory requirements, and enterprise performance management tools.

Purpose:
- Establish clear principles, rules, and step-by-step procedures for budgeting to drive consistency, transparency, and accountability.
- Define roles, responsibilities, timelines, templates, and controls that reduce cycle time, errors, and rework.
- Provide governance (approval rights, exception handling, version control) for ongoing maintenance as business conditions, regulations, and systems evolve.

Role in the organization:
- Serves as the backbone for [9.1] Perform planning and management accounting and directly enables [9.1.1] Perform planning/budgeting/forecasting.
- Connects strategic planning, operational planning, and financial targets; integrates with procurement, HR, capital planning, treasury, and accounting.
- Supports compliance with internal control frameworks (e.g., COSO), financial reporting standards (IFRS/US GAAP), and industry or public-sector budgeting requirements.

## Key Activities
- Define budgeting principles and scope (e.g., zero-based vs. incremental; driver-based modeling; rolling horizon).
- Draft and maintain policy documents, procedures, and work instructions.
- Establish governance: approval authorities, RACI, escalation and exception processes, change control and versioning.
- Specify data standards: chart of accounts, cost centers, project codes, fiscal calendar, scenario definitions, and assumptions library.
- Design the budget cycle calendar and milestones; set deliverables by function/business unit.
- Develop standard templates, forms, and guidance (Opex, Capex, headcount, revenue drivers).
- Configure supporting systems (EPM/ERP), workflows, and access controls aligned to the policy.
- Train and communicate to stakeholders; provide a helpdesk/FAQ.
- Monitor compliance, analyze effectiveness, and implement continuous improvements.
- Conduct periodic reviews and audits; remediate issues.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Corporate strategy, objectives, and risk appetite.
- Historical financials, actuals vs. prior budget, and key performance metrics.
- Forecasting methodologies and planning assumptions (inflation, FX, growth rates).
- Organizational structure, chart of accounts, entity hierarchies, fiscal calendar.
- Policies that intersect with budgeting: capital approval, procurement, travel and expense, revenue recognition, headcount/compensation, tax, treasury guidelines.
- Regulatory and compliance requirements (e.g., grant rules, public-sector budgeting laws, industry-specific mandates).
- Technology landscape and system capabilities (ERP, EPM, BI, workflow tools).

Prerequisites:
- Executive sponsorship (CFO) and a cross-functional Budget Governance Committee.
- Designated policy/process owner in FP&A.
- Approved policy template, document taxonomy, and version control standards.
- Defined planning methodology (e.g., rolling 18-month forecast with annual budget; top-down targets with bottom-up build).
- Security model and segregation of duties principles for budgeting systems.
- Resourced project team (FP&A, IT/EPM admin, HR, Procurement, Accounting, Internal Audit).

Dependencies on other processes:
- Strategic planning and target-setting.
- General accounting and reporting (to ensure master data alignment and close calendar).
- Workforce planning (HR) for headcount and compensation.
- Capital planning and project portfolio management.
- Procurement and vendor management for spend baselines and commitments.
- Treasury and cash forecasting.
- Risk and compliance, internal audit (control design and assurance).
- Master data management and IT change management.

## Process Steps
1) Initiate annual/biennial policy cycle
- Trigger: strategy refresh, regulatory change, system change, or planned annual review.
- Confirm scope (what policies/procedures to create/update) and timeline.
- Establish working group and governance cadence.

2) Gather requirements and constraints
- Compile strategy, risk appetite, regulatory requirements, audit findings, and business requests.
- Identify mandatory control requirements (e.g., approvals, documentation retention).

3) Assess current state and gaps
- Review existing policies, procedures, templates, and system configuration.
- Map pain points: cycle delays, variance volatility, compliance breaches, manual workarounds.

4) Define budgeting framework and principles
- Choose methodology: incremental vs. zero-based vs. activity-based; driver-based planning; rolling forecast cadence.
- Set scope: Opex, Capex, headcount, revenue, cash; entity and function coverage.
- Define tolerance thresholds (e.g., variance limits, target reset rules).

5) Draft policy architecture
- Policy hierarchy: policy (what/why), standard (musts), procedures (how), work instructions (detailed steps).
- Write clear, plain-language policy statements referencing controls, roles, and exceptions.
- Include policy elements: purpose, scope, definitions, responsibilities, calendar, approval matrix, controls, exceptions, document control, effective date.

6) Design controls and compliance mapping
- Align to COSO components: control environment, risk assessment, control activities, information/communication, monitoring.
- Define key controls: authorization thresholds, segregation of duties, audit trails, change logs, reconciliation checks, data validation rules.
- Map controls to risks (e.g., unauthorized budget changes, misclassification, late submissions).

7) Define data standards and master data governance
- Standardize chart of accounts, cost centers, product/customer hierarchies, project codes.
- Set naming conventions, effective dating, and ownership for master data changes.
- Establish assumptions library and scenario taxonomy (Base, Stretch, Downside).

8) Build the budget calendar and deliverables
- Establish milestones: issuance, top-down targets, submissions, consolidations, challenge rounds, executive review, board approval, system lock.
- Publish deadlines, dependencies (e.g., accounting close), and blackout periods.

9) Create templates, guidance, and procedures
- Develop standardized templates for Opex, Capex, headcount, revenue drivers, allocations.
- Draft procedures for each participant role (e.g., BU finance, cost center owner).
- Create job aids, FAQs, and examples (e.g., driver sheet usage, allocation methods).

10) Define roles, responsibilities, and approval matrix
- Document RACI across CFO, FP&A, BU finance, cost center managers, HR, Procurement, IT, Internal Audit.
- Specify approval thresholds (e.g., Capex > $1M requires CFO and Capex Committee).
- Configure segregation of duties in systems to match policy.

11) Align systems and configure workflows
- Configure EPM models, forms, data validations, locks, and workflow tasks per policy.
- Integrate with ERP, HRIS, PPM, and procurement data.
- Set up audit trails, versioning, and e-signature/approvals.

12) Stakeholder review, pilot, and refine
- Conduct targeted pilots with selected BUs.
- Capture feedback on clarity, usability, and system behavior; adjust documents and configuration.

13) Approvals and publication
- Route for formal approvals (Budget Governance Committee, CFO, Board as applicable).
- Apply version control, assign effective date, archive superseded versions.
- Publish to a single authoritative repository and notify stakeholders.

14) Training and communication
- Deliver role-based training (live sessions, e-learning).
- Require acknowledgement for policy receipt and understanding.
- Provide support channels and office hours.

15) Execution monitoring and compliance
- Track submissions, on-time completion, exceptions, and policy deviations.
- Run control checks (data validations, approval completeness) and remediate issues.

16) Maintenance and continuous improvement
- Operate a change request process with impact assessment and controlled releases.
- Conduct post-cycle review; analyze KPIs; implement improvements.
- Schedule periodic (at least annual) policy review and trigger ad-hoc updates for regulatory/system changes.

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs:
- Budget Policy document and companion Standards.
- Detailed Procedures and Work Instructions by role and process area.
- Budget calendar and milestone plan.
- RACI/roles documentation and approval matrix.
- Control matrix mapped to risks and test plans.
- Templates and forms (Opex, Capex, headcount, revenue drivers).
- Assumptions library and scenario definitions.
- System configuration specifications and workflow design.
- Training materials, FAQs, and communications.
- Policy repository with version history and audit trail.

Success criteria:
- Policy approved by required governance bodies and published before cycle start.
- >95% on-time submissions; minimal exception requests.
- Reduction in cycle time and rework compared to prior year.
- Fewer audit findings and control deficiencies.
- High user satisfaction/adoption; training completion >90%.
- Budget variances within defined tolerance bands attributable to genuine performance, not process issues.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- CFO (Executive Sponsor): Approves policy; sets financial strategy and targets; chairs governance for major decisions.
- Head of FP&A (Policy Owner): Authors and maintains policy; manages governance, calendar, and continuous improvement; ensures integration across functions.
- Budget Governance Committee (Cross-functional): Reviews and approves policy changes; adjudicates exceptions; ensures alignment with strategy and risk.
- BU Finance Leads: Localize procedures; coach cost center owners; ensure data quality; enforce timelines.
- Cost Center/Project Owners: Prepare submissions per policy; justify assumptions; comply with approvals.
- HR/Workforce Planning: Provide headcount plans, comp guidelines, and workforce cost drivers; align hiring plans with budget cycles.
- Procurement/Sourcing: Provide spend baselines and contract commitments; enforce pre-PO budget checks if required by policy.
- Accounting/Controllership: Align master data and fiscal calendar; validate mapping and classification; provide actuals for baselines.
- Treasury: Provide cash/FX assumptions; align liquidity constraints and funding costs.
- IT/EPM Administration: Configure and maintain planning tools; manage access controls, integrations, and audit trails.
- Risk & Compliance/Internal Audit: Review control design; test effectiveness; report findings; advise on remediation.
- Legal/Tax: Review for regulatory/tax implications; ensure compliance with statutory budgeting requirements where applicable.
- Data Governance/Master Data Management: Own data standards; manage change control for hierarchies and codes.
- PMO/Capital Committee: Govern Capex intake, prioritization, and approvals consistent with the policy.

## Best Practices
- Anchor on principles, then codify procedures; keep language clear and non-technical where possible.
- Standardize templates and definitions; maintain a single source of truth for assumptions and master data.
- Use driver-based and scenario planning to improve agility and insight.
- Limit exceptions; require documented business justification, time-bound validity, and senior approval.
- Align budget and close calendars; avoid conflicts and include blackout periods.
- Enforce segregation of duties and least-privilege access in planning systems.
- Implement automated validations and workflow to reduce manual errors.
- Version control all documents; maintain an accessible policy repository with search and metadata.
- Provide role-based training and certification for key users; refresh annually.
- Review and update policies at least annually, and after major events (M&A, ERP/EPM changes, regulatory changes).
- Measure and act on KPIs; publish a post-mortem with improvement actions.
- Pilot changes with select BUs before global rollout.

## Common Challenges
- Overcomplex policies and forms cause low adoption.
  - Solution: Simplify; use role-based views and progressive disclosure of detail.
- Shadow spreadsheets and off-system workarounds undermine controls.
  - Solution: Strengthen system capability and mandate use; disable uncontrolled file exchanges; integrate key data sources.
- Inconsistent definitions and master data lead to reconciliation issues.
  - Solution: Enforce data standards and MDM governance; lock dimensions during cycles.
- Weak governance and unclear roles cause delays.
  - Solution: Formalize RACI and escalation paths; publish calendars early; hold weekly governance standups during cycles.
- Excessive exceptions create uneven enforcement.
  - Solution: Institute strict exception criteria, time limits, and reporting; reduce via root-cause remediation.
- Insufficient training and communication.
  - Solution: Deliver mandatory, role-based training with assessments; maintain FAQs and help channels.
- Technology limitations or misconfiguration.
  - Solution: Invest in fit-for-purpose EPM; configure workflows, validations, and audit trails to mirror policy.

## Performance Metrics
- Policy readiness: Publication lead time before cycle start; number of open issues at launch.
- Cycle efficiency: Budget cycle duration; on-time submission rate; number of consolidation iterations.
- Quality and compliance: Data validation failure rate; number of policy deviations/exceptions; audit findings; completeness of approvals.
- Adoption and enablement: Training completion rate; user satisfaction (survey); system utilization (active users, time in system).
- Outcomes impact: Variance adherence vs. tolerance; reforecast frequency due to process errors; reduction in manual adjustments.
- Control effectiveness: SoD violations prevented; percentage of actions with full audit trail; access review remediation time.
- Maintenance health: Time to process change requests; cadence adherence to annual reviews; proportion of improvements implemented.

## Technology and Tools
- Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) platforms: Oracle EPM Cloud, SAP Analytics Cloud Planning/SAP BPC, Anaplan, Workday Adaptive Planning, Prophix.
- ERP/Financial Systems: SAP S/4HANA, Oracle ERP Cloud, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance, NetSuite for actuals and master data.
- Policy and document management: SharePoint/Teams, Confluence, PowerDMS, ConvergePoint; e-signature (DocuSign/Adobe Sign) for approvals.
- Workflow and automation: ServiceNow, Nintex, Microsoft Power Automate; intake for exceptions and change requests.
- GRC/Internal control tools: ServiceNow GRC, RSA Archer, MetricStream for control mapping, testing, and issues.
- Master Data Management: Informatica MDM, SAP MDG for governance of COA and hierarchies.
- BI/Analytics: Power BI, Tableau, Qlik for KPI dashboards and variance analysis.
- Collaboration and training: LMS platforms for courses and tracking; Slack/Teams channels for support.
- Access management: IAM/SSO (Okta, Azure AD) to enforce least-privilege and SoD in EPM/ERP.

This process, when executed rigorously, creates a durable, well-governed budgeting environment that accelerates planning cycles, improves decision quality, withstands audits, and adapts to change with minimal disruption.

## Overview
Operationalize and implement plans to achieve budget is the process of translating the approved budget and forecast into executable operating plans, governance, and controls that guide daily decisions, spending, hiring, and project execution. It ensures resources are allocated to priorities, spending authority is set, systems are configured to enforce the plan, and performance is monitored and corrected to meet financial targets.
