Process Details:
## Overview
Manage default accounts is the focused process for handling customer accounts that have breached agreed payment terms and are in default. The purpose is to maximize recoveries, minimize credit losses, and ensure regulatory compliance while protecting customer relationships and organizational reputation. It sits within the collections domain of revenue accounting, translating delinquency into structured action: validating debt, segmenting risk, negotiating or enforcing remedies, executing the necessary accounting treatments (provisions, charge-offs, recoveries), and closing cases with complete audit trails. The process interacts closely with credit risk management, disputes/deductions, cash application, legal, and financial reporting to ensure accurate books and timely decision-making.

## Key Activities
- Identify and qualify default accounts
  - Trigger on aging thresholds, broken promises-to-pay (PTP), insolvency notices, or policy-defined events of default.
- Validate balance and eligibility
  - Confirm invoice accuracy, dispute status, cash application, fees/interest, and statute-of-limitations considerations.
- Segment and prioritize portfolio
  - Rank by risk, balance, likelihood of recovery, customer value, collateral/security, region, and regulatory regime.
- Apply account controls
  - Credit hold/stop-supply, suspension of services where permitted, update risk ratings, and notify stakeholders.
- Outreach and negotiation
  - Final demands, hardship assessment, structured payment plans, settlements, fee waivers per policy, and approvals.
- Escalation and enforcement
  - Place with third-party collectors or legal counsel; initiate litigation or security enforcement where applicable.
- Accounting treatments
  - Record impairment/provisions (e.g., ECL/CECL), charge-offs/write-offs per policy, recoveries, and fee accounting.
- Monitoring and compliance
  - Track PTP adherence, agency performance, legal case progress, consumer protection compliance, and complaints.
- Closure and feedback
  - Cure and reinstate or write-off and close; update master data, reports, and feed lessons learned to credit strategy.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs
  - AR aging reports and default triggers (DPD buckets, broken PTP)
  - Customer contract, terms, and credit policy
  - Invoices, statements, and dunning history
  - Dispute/deduction status and resolutions
  - Cash application status and unapplied cash
  - Customer contact and ownership details; communication logs
  - Collateral/security documentation (if secured credit)
  - Credit scores/bureau data or internal risk ratings
  - Legal notices (bankruptcy, receivership), and governance/legal guidelines
- Prerequisites
  - Documented default management policy, approval matrix, and authority limits
  - Configured systems for case management, dunning, and collections workflows
  - Verified, current customer contact data and consent preferences
  - Compliance framework (e.g., FDCPA/TCPA in US, FCA CONC in UK, GDPR/CCPA for privacy)
  - Defined write-off criteria and provisioning methodology
- Dependencies on other processes
  - Invoice to cash: Billing accuracy, cash application (to avoid chasing paid items)
  - Dispute and deduction management: Resolve billing/quality disputes prior to enforcement
  - Credit risk management: Policy, risk scoring, credit holds, limit adjustments
  - Legal and compliance: Regulated contact rules, litigation intake, bankruptcy handling
  - Financial reporting: Provisioning, write-offs, recoveries, revenue and impairment reporting

## Process Steps
1. Detect and intake
   - Run daily/weekly default triggers (e.g., 60/90+ DPD, broken PTP, insolvency filing).
   - Auto-create default cases with current balance, fees/interest, prior actions, and contact info.
2. Validate the debt
   - Confirm invoice and pricing accuracy; reconcile unapplied cash.
   - Check for open disputes/deductions; pause collections until resolved.
   - Verify contractual terms, late fee clauses, jurisdiction, and statute-of-limitations.
   - Calculate current balance including interest/fees per policy; obtain internal sign-off.
3. Segment and prioritize
   - Classify by risk tier, balance size, B2B vs. B2C, secured vs. unsecured, and likelihood of cure.
   - Assign account strategy (e.g., intensive outreach, settlement path, agency placement, legal evaluation).
4. Apply controls and update status
   - Place on credit hold/stop-supply where permitted; communicate to Sales/Service.
   - Update internal risk ratings and expected credit loss (ECL/CECL) parameters.
   - Record final demand date and compliance-required notices.
5. Outreach and assessment
   - Send final demand letter/email/SMS per legal standard; document delivery.
   - Attempt right-party contact (RPC) using compliant channels and times.
   - Assess hardship and intent; verify identity; capture financial capability for B2C or cash flow for B2B.
6. Offer and negotiate resolution
   - Options: Short-term PTP, structured payment plan, settlement discount, fee/interest waiver, term extension.
   - Validate within approval thresholds; escalate exceptions to Credit Risk Manager.
   - Generate agreement documents; obtain e-signature; set up auto-pay where possible.
7. Monitor and enforce agreements
   - Track PTP/payment plan adherence; send reminders; intervene on misses.
   - If agreement breaks, re-segment for next action (agency or legal).
8. Escalation path
   - Third-party collections: Prepare placement packet (debt validation, communications log, invoices, consent settings); execute data-sharing agreements; monitor performance and compliance.
   - Legal action: Legal review for viability; prepare case file; file suit, liens, or security enforcement as appropriate; respect bankruptcy automatic stay and consumer protection rules.
9. Accounting and reporting
   - Update provisions based on aging/risk; book impairment entries.
   - When criteria met, process write-off/charge-off; maintain recoverability tracking.
   - Record recoveries, agency fees, legal costs; ensure net presentation per policy.
   - Update dashboards on portfolio status, roll rates, cure rates.
10. Close and reinstate or exit
   - Cured accounts: Remove credit hold, restore terms, remove default flags, and notify stakeholders.
   - Non-recoverable: Close post write-off; retain records per retention policy.
   - Conduct root-cause analysis; feed insights to credit policy and sales.
11. Compliance, quality, and audit
   - Ensure contact frequency/time/channel rules adhered to; maintain call recordings and consent logs.
   - Manage and resolve complaints; perform sample QA.
   - Retain evidence for audits and regulatory inquiries.

Alternate flows:
- Bankruptcy/insolvency: Immediately stop collection attempts; route to legal; file proofs of claim; adjust provisioning.
- Deceased consumer: Work through estate procedures; special compliance handling.
- Government/public sector: Follow agency-specific claim and dispute processes.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Outputs
  - Updated account status (default, payment plan, agency, legal, cured, written-off)
  - Adjusted provisions, write-off entries, and recovery postings
  - Credit holds and risk ratings updated across systems
  - Placement files to agencies or legal case packets
  - Documented payment plan/settlement agreements and e-signatures
- Deliverables
  - Final demand notices and communications log
  - Exception approval records (waivers, settlements)
  - Monthly default portfolio report (aging, roll rates, cure rates, losses, recoveries)
  - Compliance and QA reports; complaint logs
  - Lessons learned/action items for credit policy
- Success criteria
  - Increased cure and recovery rates with controlled cost-to-collect
  - Reduced roll rates to later DPD buckets
  - Accurate, timely provisioning and write-off accounting
  - Zero material compliance violations and low complaint rates
  - Complete, auditable documentation for all cases

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Collections/Default Management Specialist
  - Manage cases end-to-end; outreach, negotiation, documentation, monitoring.
- Credit Risk Manager
  - Define policy; approve exceptions/settlements; oversee provisioning and risk segmentation.
- AR Accountant
  - Post provisions, write-offs, recoveries; reconcile ledger; support reporting and audits.
- Dispute Resolution Analyst
  - Resolve billing/quality issues blocking collections; coordinate credits/adjustments.
- Sales/Account Manager
  - Provide relationship context; support remediation; align on stop-supply decisions.
- Compliance Officer
  - Ensure adherence to laws and internal policies; oversee complaints and QA.
- Legal Counsel
  - Advise on litigation viability; handle bankruptcy, settlements, and court actions.
- Third-Party Collection Agency
  - Execute placements per SLA; report performance and compliance; return accounts as needed.
- Data/Analytics Lead
  - Build risk scores, strategy optimization, dashboards, champion–challenger tests.
- IT/System Administrator
  - Maintain collection systems, integrations, dialers, templates, and security.

## Best Practices
- Segment and prioritize using data-driven risk models; tailor strategies by segment.
- Validate debt before escalation; resolve disputes early to avoid wasted effort and risk.
- Use omnichannel, compliant contact strategies; maximize right-party contact rate.
- Standardize decision trees for settlements, waivers, and restructures with clear approval limits.
- Offer self-service digital options for payment plans and settlements with e-sign and auto-pay.
- Apply early warning indicators (missed micro-events, declines in spend) for pre-default intervention.
- Maintain complete audit trails: communications, approvals, documents, and system actions.
- Manage third-party agencies with SLAs, compliance audits, and rotation/recall strategies.
- Align with legal/regulatory requirements per jurisdiction and consumer vs. commercial accounts.
- Continuously improve using analytics: champion–challenger tests, score recalibration, and root-cause loops.
- Coordinate with Sales/Service on stop-supply and customer messaging to protect brand.
- Train staff on empathy, negotiation, and compliance; enable scripts and knowledge bases.
- Ensure data privacy and security in all communications and data sharing.

## Common Challenges
- Inaccurate or incomplete contact information
  - Solution: Enrich via bureaus/skip-trace vendors; verify during each contact; maintain consent records.
- Chasing disputed or already-paid balances
  - Solution: Tight integration with billing, disputes, and cash application; pre-collection validation checklist.
- Fragmented systems and poor visibility
  - Solution: Centralized case management; integration between ERP, CRM, dialers, and document management.
- Regulatory complexity across regions
  - Solution: Rule-driven contact engines; jurisdiction-specific templates; compliance monitoring and training.
- Broken promises-to-pay and plan defaults
  - Solution: Auto-reminders, nudges, and reinforcement; risk-based deposits; proactive outreach before due dates.
- Low recovery on small-balance, late-stage accounts
  - Solution: Automation, batch settlements, agency placements, and cost-to-collect modeling.
- Bankruptcy/insolvency risks
  - Solution: Automated stay detection, legal workflows, and specialized handling.
- Reputational and complaint risks
  - Solution: Tone-appropriate scripts, QA review of calls, and rapid complaint resolution.
- Provisioning accuracy
  - Solution: Regular ECL/CECL model back-testing; governance over assumptions and overlays.

## Performance Metrics
- Cure rate: Percent of default accounts returning to current within 30/60/90 days.
- Roll rate: Movement from 60→90→120+ DPD; minimize late-stage migration.
- Right-party contact (RPC) rate and contact-to-cure conversion rate.
- Promise-to-pay kept ratio and average days to cure.
- Liquidation/recovery rate (gross and net of costs) and average recovery per account.
- Cost-to-collect per dollar recovered; agency/legal ROI.
- Time to placement and time to write-off.
- Provisioning accuracy: Variance between expected and actual losses; back-testing results.
- Compliance KPIs: Complaints per 1,000 contacts, QA pass rate, violations/incidents.
- Agent productivity: Cases handled, resolutions per FTE, and utilization.
- Data quality: Percentage of accounts with verified contact info and consent status.

## Technology and Tools
- ERP/AR and collections platforms: SAP S/4HANA FSCM Collections, SAP FI-AR, Oracle Receivables, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance, Workday.
- AR automation and collections suites: HighRadius, Billtrust, Esker, BlackLine AR, FIS GETPAID, Serrala.
- Case management and CRM: Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zendesk.
- Dialers/omnichannel communication: Genesys, Five9, Twilio; compliant SMS/email; call recording.
- E-signature: DocuSign, Adobe Acrobat Sign for agreements.
- Payment gateways and portals: Stripe, Adyen, Cybersource; customer self-service portals for payments/plans.
- Credit/risk and data enrichment: Experian, Equifax, TransUnion, Dun & Bradstreet; skip-trace services.
- Analytics and BI: Power BI, Tableau; data science platforms for scoring and strategy optimization.
- Document and records management: SharePoint, Box; secure retention and audit trails.
- Legal and bankruptcy monitoring: Legal case management tools; PACER/insolvency feeds where available.
- Compliance monitoring: Call QA tools, consent management, contact rule engines.
- RPA/automation: Bots to generate letters, assemble placement packets, and update statuses across systems.

# Process Documentation: [9.2.5.3] Correspond/Negotiate with Customer

## Overview
This process governs how the organization communicates and negotiates with customers to resolve revenue-related adjustments and deductions (e.g., short-pays, chargebacks, price concessions, rebates, returns, promotional allowances, billing errors). It ensures disputes are handled promptly, fairly, and in compliance with accounting standards, while minimizing revenue leakage and maintaining customer satisfaction.

Purpose:
- Resolve customer-initiated deductions and requests for adjustments through structured correspondence and negotiation.
- Determine appropriate concessions (if any), secure internal approvals, formalize agreements, and record accurate accounting entries.
- Provide a consistent, auditable approach that supports revenue recognition rules (e.g., ASC 606/IFRS 15), internal controls, and SOX compliance.

Role in the organization:
- Bridges Finance/Revenue Accounting, Sales/Account Management, Credit & Collections, Pricing/Trade, Customer Service, and Legal.
- Protects margin and cash flow by reducing unwarranted deductions and accelerating dispute resolution.
- Feeds root-cause insights back to upstream processes (order-to-cash, pricing, promotions, fulfillment) to prevent recurrence.

## Key Activities
- Intake and triage of customer deductions/disputes and requests for concessions.
- Fact-finding and validation against contracts, price lists, promotions, invoices, delivery, and returns.
- Financial and accounting impact assessment (revenue vs. expense, tax, accruals).
- Offer strategy design (options, ranges, settlement terms) aligned to Delegation of Authority (DoA).
- Correspondence and negotiation with the customer; meeting scheduling and communication.
- Internal approvals for proposed concessions/settlements.
- Agreement formalization (e.g., credit memo, settlement letter, payment plan).
- ERP updates, dispute closure, and accounting postings.
- Stakeholder communication and learnings capture.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Customer claim artifacts: remittance advices (including EDI 820), deduction backup, debit memos, claim forms, chargeback codes.
- Contractual documents: master agreements, order confirmations, price lists, promotional/rebate agreements, trade spend commitments, SLAs.
- Transaction data: invoices, delivery notes/POD, RMA/returns, credit/debit memos, tax details, payment history, collection notes.
- Internal policies: discounting policy, settlement playbooks, DoA thresholds, accounting policy for revenue adjustments, dispute coding standards.
- Analytics: customer deduction history, dispute reason trends, recovery rates.

Prerequisites:
- Deduction/dispute record created in the dispute management system and assigned to an owner.
- Dunning suppression applied only to disputed items (not unrelated overdue invoices).
- Up-to-date DoA matrix and approver availability.
- Defined negotiation templates and approved offer catalog (e.g., early-pay discounts, partial credits, replacements).

Dependencies on other processes:
- 9.2.5 Manage and process adjustments/deductions (case creation, coding, and posting).
- Billing and Invoicing (9.2.2) for invoice accuracy and corrections.
- Pricing/Promotions/Rebates management for validation and approvals.
- Returns and RMA processing for physical product issues.
- Credit & Collections for payment coordination and dunning controls.
- Legal for settlement language and dispute escalation.
- Revenue recognition and general accounting for correct postings and disclosures.

## Process Steps
1. Intake and Triage
   - Receive deduction/adjustment request via EDI/email/portal/phone.
   - Create or confirm dispute case with reason code; link all related invoices and documents.
   - Triage severity and value; assign priority and owner; set SLA based on policy.

2. Fact-Finding and Validation
   - Retrieve and review contract, pricing, promo agreements, rebates accruals, invoice copies, delivery/POD, returns/RMA, service tickets.
   - Verify legitimacy: compare claimed reason and amounts to contract terms and evidence.
   - Identify root cause (pricing error, shortage, damage, late delivery, unauthorized deduction).
   - Quantify financial impact including tax and freight. Determine preliminary accounting treatment (contra-revenue vs. SG&A vs. other).

3. Strategy and Offer Design
   - Define objectives, BATNA (best alternative to negotiated agreement), walk-away point, and desired outcome.
   - Select offer options from approved catalog (e.g., partial credit, credit upon return, replacements, expedited reship at shared cost, early payment discount for prompt settlement, payment plan).
   - Consider revenue recognition implications (e.g., price concession = variable consideration; ensure consistency with ASC 606/IFRS 15) and any need for contract modification.
   - Draft proposed terms: amount, conditions precedent (e.g., return received), timeline, how it will be settled (credit memo vs. write-off), and tax treatment.
   - Perform margin impact analysis and alignment with customer lifetime value and precedent risk.

4. Internal Alignment and Pre-Approval
   - Review with Sales/Account Management for relationship context and trade terms.
   - Consult Pricing/Trade/Marketing for promo eligibility and rebate implications.
   - Engage Legal if settlement includes release language or non-standard terms.
   - Obtain approvals per DoA (value/percentage thresholds, exceptions). Document approvals in workflow.

5. Customer Correspondence & Negotiation
   - Initiate contact: acknowledge receipt within SLA; schedule call or exchange proposed resolution via email/portal.
   - Present evidence and rationale; propose options; listen to customer constraints.
   - Negotiate within approved parameters; use concessions sequencing (non-cash, conditional, time-bound).
   - If negotiation exceeds authority, pause and seek additional approval or escalate.
   - Capture meeting minutes, decisions, and customer commitments in CRM/dispute system.

6. Agreement Formalization
   - Draft settlement letter or email with agreed terms, including:
     - Amount and nature of adjustment
     - Invoices impacted and reason codes
     - Conditions (e.g., return receipt, payment deadline)
     - Mutual releases (if applicable)
     - How the adjustment will be processed (credit memo/write-off/offset)
   - Secure signatures/acknowledgment (e-signature if required); attach to case.

7. Execution and Accounting
   - Create credit memo or adjustment in ERP; ensure correct GL accounts (contra-revenue vs. expense), tax handling, and revenue recognition adjustments.
   - Update rebate accruals or promo settlements as needed.
   - Apply credit to open items; clear deductions from AR; update DSO impact.
   - For invalid deductions: issue debit memo and recommence collections on disputed amount.

8. Communication and Closure
   - Notify customer of postings and net balance due; share statement if needed.
   - Inform internal stakeholders (Sales, Collections, Customer Service, Trade) of outcome and any ongoing actions (e.g., updated terms).
   - Close dispute case with final reason code; log recovery vs. claim, cycle time, and root cause.
   - Trigger corrective actions upstream (pricing master update, delivery process fix, contract clarification).

9. Post-Case Review and Continuous Improvement
   - Include case in periodic deduction reviews; analyze trends, top offenders, leakages.
   - Update playbooks and offer catalog based on lessons learned.
   - Train teams on recurring issues and prevention.

Decision points:
- Legitimate vs. invalid claim
- Authority threshold exceeded
- Need for legal involvement
- Contract modification implications under revenue recognition standards

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs:
- Customer-facing correspondence and settlement agreement/acknowledgment.
- Approved credit memos/debit memos/write-offs and associated journal entries.
- Updated dispute case with documents, approvals, and closure notes.
- Adjusted revenue/expense accounts and rebate accruals as applicable.
- Updated customer payment status and AR aging; dunning status corrected.
- Root-cause tags and insights for upstream remediation.

Success criteria:
- Resolution within SLA; accurate accounting treatment; minimized concession vs. claim.
- Customer acceptance and payment behavior improvement.
- Complete audit trail and compliance with policies and DoA.
- Reduction in recurrence of similar deductions.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Deductions/Dispute Analyst (Process Owner): Case intake, validation, analysis; lead negotiation; coordinate approvals; maintain documentation; post settlement entries or coordinate with AR.
- Revenue Accountant: Determine accounting treatment, revenue recognition implications, and ensure correct postings.
- Sales/Account Manager: Provide relationship context; support negotiation strategy; ensure consistency with commercial commitments; communicate with customer as needed.
- Pricing/Trade/Promotions Manager: Validate promo eligibility, rebate calculations; approve related concessions; update programs.
- Credit & Collections Specialist: Manage dunning, payment application, and follow-up on recovered amounts; issue debit memos for invalid deductions.
- Legal Counsel: Review and approve settlement language, releases, and high-value or high-risk cases.
- Tax Specialist: Validate tax implications of credits/returns and cross-border impacts.
- Controller/Finance Approver: Approve concessions per DoA; oversee compliance and materiality considerations.
- Customer Service/Logistics: Provide delivery/POD evidence, manage returns/RMA and replacements.
- Systems/ERP Administrator: Maintain workflows, reason codes, and user access; ensure audit logging.

## Best Practices
- Standardize reason codes and documentation requirements; require customer backup before negotiation.
- Maintain a tiered DoA and pre-approved offer catalog to expedite decisions.
- Use playbooks by scenario (pricing error, short-ship, damage, late delivery, promo dispute) with evidence checklists and negotiation scripts.
- Separate duties: negotiator vs. approver; accounting entry review by Revenue Accounting.
- Control dunning smartly: suppress for disputed items only.
- Quantify and communicate financial impact of options during approvals (margin, revenue recognition, tax).
- Align settlements with ASC 606/IFRS 15: treat price concessions as variable consideration; assess contract modifications.
- Time-bound, conditional concessions (e.g., credit upon return receipt) to reduce leakage.
- Keep communications professional and evidence-based; confirm agreements in writing.
- Maintain a centralized repository of contracts and promo agreements for quick validation.
- Conduct root-cause reviews and feed fixes upstream (e.g., pricing master data, delivery quality, policy clarity).
- Track precedents to avoid setting unfavorable expectations with customers.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Incomplete or late customer documentation: Enforce submission standards; provide a checklist; pause negotiations pending evidence.
- Unauthorized deductions/short-pays: Use debit memos and collections; escalate with Sales; apply late fees per contract where appropriate.
- Poor contract/promotions visibility: Implement CLM and trade spend systems; link agreements to ERP and dispute cases.
- Long cycle times due to approvals: Implement tiered thresholds, auto-approvals for low-value standard cases, and clear SLAs.
- Revenue recognition complexity: Involve Revenue Accounting early; use guidance notes for common scenarios.
- Cross-functional misalignment: Establish weekly dispute huddles and clear RACI; maintain shared dashboards.
- System fragmentation: Integrate ERP, CRM, dispute management, and trade systems; use APIs and RPA to gather evidence.
- Customer power and precedent risk: Use playbooks and approval gates; escalate strategic accounts to leadership with holistic view (profitability, growth).

## Performance Metrics
- Dispute resolution cycle time (receipt to closure).
- Percentage resolved within SLA.
- Recovery rate: amount recovered vs. claimed.
- Concessions as % of sales (overall and by reason code).
- Invalid deduction rate and time to rebill.
- Offer acceptance rate and number of negotiation rounds.
- Reopen rate of closed disputes.
- DSO impact attributable to disputes.
- Revenue leakage prevented (vs. baseline).
- First-contact response time to customer.
- Audit exceptions and policy compliance rate.
- Root-cause distribution and recurrence rate.

Targets and thresholds should be tailored by customer tier, region, and product line.

## Technology and Tools
- ERP/Financials with AR and Credit/Collections (e.g., SAP S/4HANA, Oracle Cloud ERP, Microsoft D365).
- Dispute/Deduction Management (e.g., SAP FSCM Dispute Management, HighRadius, BlackLine AR Automation, Billtrust).
- Trade Promotion/Rebate Management (e.g., Vistex, Model N, Oracle TPM).
- Contract Lifecycle Management (e.g., Icertis, DocuSign CLM) linked to pricing and promo terms.
- CRM and case management (e.g., Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics) for correspondence tracking.
- EDI and payment processing (EDI 810/820, portals) with remittance reason code ingestion.
- Document management and e-signature (e.g., SharePoint, DocuSign, Adobe Sign).
- Analytics/BI and dashboarding (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) for KPIs and root-cause analysis.
- RPA/Automation for evidence gathering, coding, and generating standard responses.
- Access controls, workflow, and audit logging to support SOX and internal controls.

# [9.2.5.5] Prepare Chargeback Invoices

## Overview
Prepare Chargeback Invoices is the process of creating and submitting formal claims to suppliers/manufacturers to recover the difference between a distributor’s acquisition price and a lower end-customer contract or promotional price. This process is common in industries with indirect sales models and customer-specific pricing (e.g., pharmaceuticals, medical devices, electronics, CPG).

Purpose:
- Recover funds when products are sold downstream at approved prices below the distributor’s acquisition cost (e.g., ship-and-debit scenarios, contract pricing, promotional price protection).
- Ensure revenue accuracy and margin integrity by aligning realized selling prices with supplier funding.
- Provide audit-ready documentation to support claims, reduce disputes, and comply with contractual and regulatory requirements.

Role in the organization:
- Supports revenue accounting accuracy (net sales, deductions, and adjustments).
- Reduces DSO and write-offs by accelerating and improving claim recovery.
- Enables pricing/contract compliance insights and drives upstream process improvements (pricing governance, contract management, master data).

## Key Activities
- Identify eligible transactions and chargeback programs (contract, promo, price protection).
- Validate eligibility against supplier agreements and customer/product master data.
- Calculate claim amounts (price deltas, applicable taxes/freight per contract rules).
- Compile supporting documentation (invoices, POS/sell-through reports, shipping docs).
- Generate chargeback invoice(s) and claim package with required fields and attachments.
- Obtain approvals as per delegation of authority and internal controls.
- Transmit claims to suppliers (EDI/portal/email) and track acknowledgements.
- Record accounting entries and update subledgers/accruals.
- Monitor, reconcile, and resolve supplier responses, disputes, and partial approvals.
- Close and archive claims; report on performance and exceptions.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Executed supplier pricing/chargeback agreements (program terms, eligible SKUs, customers, effective dates, calculation rules, submission windows).
- Customer and product master data (sold-to/ship-to hierarchy, end-customer IDs, SKU mappings, UoM conversions).
- Distributor acquisition data (supplier invoices, contract buy price, effective dates).
- Downstream sales data (distributor invoices to end-customers, POS/sell-through, shipment confirmations).
- Pricing data (end-customer contract price, promotional price lists, rebates vs. chargeback delineation).
- Tax and freight rules per contract and jurisdiction (tax engine outputs when applicable).
- FX rates (for multi-currency scenarios).
- Prior claims history to prevent duplicates.
- Approval thresholds/authority matrix.

Prerequisites:
- Master data governance in place (validated SKUs, customer eligibility).
- Defined submission timelines (e.g., claims must be filed within 30/60/90 days of sale).
- Supplier transmission method established (EDI 844/849, cXML, portal, email).
- Internal controls established (segregation of duties, review workflows).

Dependencies on other processes:
- Contract and price agreement administration (pricing setup and changes).
- Sales order processing and billing (accuracy of downstream invoices).
- Deductions and adjustments management (application of credits, dispute handling).
- General accounting and reporting (GL postings, revenue recognition, accruals).
- Master data management (customer/product hierarchies).
- Tax determination and compliance.

## Process Steps
1. Trigger and Intake
   - Identify transactions where end-customer contract price < distributor acquisition price.
   - Trigger can be periodic batch (e.g., weekly) or event-based (sale posted).

2. Eligibility Validation
   - Verify active supplier contract/promo covers the SKU, customer, region, channel, and sale date.
   - Check volume caps, tier thresholds, and any exclusions.
   - Validate ship-to vs. end-customer mapping and any required reseller IDs.

3. Data Collection and Normalization
   - Consolidate acquisition cost, downstream sale price, quantities, UoM conversions.
   - Normalize currencies using contract-specified FX rate/date basis.
   - Pull taxes/freight/handling values and apply contract rules (e.g., pre-tax delta only).

4. Duplicate and Conflict Checks
   - Compare to previously submitted claims to prevent duplicates.
   - Identify overlapping programs (promo vs. contract) and apply hierarchy rules.
   - Check for returns/credits that reduce quantities eligible for claim.

5. Calculate Claim Amounts
   - Line-level calculation: Eligible Qty x (Distributor Acquisition Price – Approved End-Customer Price).
   - Apply rounding rules, tiered pricing, minimum/maximum caps, and tolerances.
   - Determine handling of taxes and freight per agreement (include/exclude; method).
   - Summarize by contract, product, customer, and period per supplier instructions.

6. Compile Supporting Documentation
   - Required attachments: distributor invoices to end customers, shipment docs, proof of delivery (if required), price agreement/contract ID, POS/sell-through reports, supplier invoice showing acquisition cost, tax calculations, and any required certifications.
   - Redact PII as appropriate; ensure file naming and structure align with supplier guidelines.

7. Prepare Chargeback Invoice
   - Create header: Supplier name and ID, Distributor bill-to/sold-by, Claim/Invoice number, Contract/Promo ID, Claim period, Currency, Submission date, Contact info.
   - Create lines: SKU/UPC, Description, UoM, Qty, Acquisition Price, Approved Price, Delta, Tax/Freight treatment, Line total, End-customer ID/name, Ship-to, Invoice references, Shipment dates.
   - Include summary totals and reason code (e.g., Ship-and-Debit, Contract Price, Promo).
   - Cross-reference internal documents (SO/DO/Invoice numbers).

8. Internal Review and Approval
   - Automated validation checks (completeness, pricing match, tolerance thresholds).
   - Manual review for exceptions or high-value claims per approval matrix.
   - Approver attests to eligibility, accuracy, and documentation sufficiency.

9. Post Accounting Entries
   - Record receivable from supplier or reduction in COGS as per policy.
   - Adjust revenue/contra-revenue and chargeback accruals if required (ASC 606 impact).
   - Tag entries with claim number for traceability.

10. Transmit to Supplier
   - Preferred: EDI 844 Product Transfer Account Adjustment with attachments; receive 997/824 acknowledgements and 849 response for dispositions.
   - Alternatives: Supplier portal submission, cXML, or secure email.
   - Confirm receipt and obtain claim ID from supplier if different.

11. Track, Reconcile, and Resolve
   - Monitor supplier responses: approved, partially approved, denied, need-more-info.
   - Address disputes: provide clarifications, corrected documents, or withdraw ineligible lines.
   - Reconcile remittances/credit memos (e.g., EDI 820) to claim lines; apply to AR/deductions.
   - Escalate per SLA if aging exceeds thresholds.

12. Close and Archive
   - Mark claim as closed once fully paid/credited or written off per policy.
   - Archive full audit trail (inputs, calculations, approvals, transmissions, responses) per retention policy.
   - Capture root causes for denials/adjustments and feed upstream improvements.

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs:
- Chargeback invoice(s) with itemized claim lines and summary totals.
- Complete claim package (supporting documentation).
- Transmission receipts and supplier acknowledgements.

Deliverables produced:
- GL postings and subledger updates (AR, deductions, accruals).
- Reconciliation records (credit memos, remittance advice).
- Status reports/dashboards on claims submitted, approved, disputed, closed.

Success criteria:
- First-pass acceptance rate meets/exceeds target (e.g., ≥95%).
- Average submission cycle time within SLA (e.g., ≤7 days from sale period close).
- Recovery rate vs. claimed amount (e.g., ≥98% approved).
- Low percentage of aged claims >30/60/90 days.
- Compliance: zero material audit findings; complete, accurate audit trails.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Chargeback Specialist/Analyst: Execute validations, calculations, documentation, invoice preparation, submission, and tracking.
- Pricing/Contract Administration: Maintain contract terms, eligibility lists, price files; resolve discrepancies.
- Sales Operations/Customer Service: Provide POS/sell-through data, assist with end-customer verification.
- Accounts Receivable/Deductions Analyst: Apply credits, reconcile remittances, manage disputes and write-offs.
- Revenue Accountant: Ensure proper recognition/contra-revenue, accrual adjustments, and GL postings.
- Master Data Management: Maintain accurate customer/product mappings, hierarchies, and IDs.
- IT/EDI Analyst: Maintain integrations, EDI mappings (844/849/820), portals, and transmission monitoring.
- Supplier Account Manager: Liaise with supplier counterparts, negotiate resolutions, escalate disputes.
- Internal Audit/Compliance: Test controls, review samples, ensure policy adherence.
- Finance Manager/Controller: Approve high-value claims, oversee policy and performance.

## Best Practices
- Standardize submission formats and field definitions aligned to each supplier’s specifications.
- Automate eligibility checks and calculations with configurable rules; use tolerance thresholds to auto-approve low-risk items.
- Leverage EDI for high-volume suppliers (844/849) with automated acknowledgement handling.
- Maintain airtight master data governance; synchronize contract/customer/SKU mappings.
- Enforce segregation of duties (preparer vs. approver vs. AR application).
- Implement submission calendars with cut-offs; avoid stale claims beyond contract windows.
- Maintain comprehensive audit trails and document retention; include versioned contract terms.
- Use reason codes and root-cause analysis of denials to drive upstream fixes (pricing setup, contract clarity, sales discipline).
- Apply clear rules for taxes, freight, and currency; codify in system configuration and SOPs.
- Establish SLAs with suppliers (acknowledgement, disposition, payment timelines) and a playbook for disputes.
- Periodically sample-test claims for accuracy and eligibility; incorporate continuous improvement.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Data quality issues (misaligned SKUs/customers): Implement master data stewardship, automated cross-references, and validation rules.
- Contract ambiguities: Tighten contract language; maintain a centralized, searchable repository; involve Legal/Contracts in disputes.
- Duplicate or overlapping claims: Use claim numbering, duplicate checks, and program hierarchy rules (contract > promo or vice versa).
- Denials due to documentation gaps: Use submission checklists; pre-generate document packages; enforce completeness checks.
- Timing/cutoff misses: Calendar-driven reminders; dashboard alerts; capacity planning around period ends.
- Tax/freight handling inconsistencies: Codify rules in tax engine and chargeback configuration; test scenarios regularly.
- Multi-currency complexities: Standardize FX sources and valuation dates; lock FX rates per period when allowed.
- Systems integration failures (EDI): Proactive monitoring, error queues, and retry logic; maintain updated EDI maps.
- High manual touch: Deploy RPA for data gathering/attachment collation; exception-based worklists for analysts.
- Aging and cash application delays: Dedicated reconciliation cadence; auto-match using claim/line IDs; escalate per SLA.

## Performance Metrics
- First-pass acceptance rate (% claims approved without rework).
- Average days from period close to submission.
- Recovery rate (% of claimed dollars recovered).
- Dispute/denial rate (% lines or $ denied).
- Average resolution time (submission to final disposition).
- Claims aging (0–30, 31–60, 61–90, >90 days outstanding).
- Manual touch rate (% lines requiring manual intervention).
- Cost per claim (labor, system costs).
- Duplicate claim rate.
- Adjustment/write-off rate (% $ written off post-denial).
- Audit exceptions (count/severity) and control effectiveness.

## Technology and Tools
- ERP: SAP (SD, FI/AR, Vistex), Oracle (E-Business Cloud/Fusion), Microsoft Dynamics 365.
- Revenue/Contract and Chargeback Management: Model N, Vistex, Revitas/Model N CARS, Pricefx, Vendavo.
- EDI/Integration: 844 (Product Transfer Account Adjustment), 849 (Response), 820 (Payment/Remittance), 997/824 (Acknowledgements), 852/867 (POS/Sales/Inventory where used); iPaaS (MuleSoft, Boomi), B2B gateways.
- Workflow/BPM and RPA: ServiceNow, Nintex, UiPath, Automation Anywhere, Power Automate.
- Tax Engines: Avalara, Vertex.
- Document and Records Management: SharePoint, OpenText, Box; e-signature for approvals (DocuSign, Adobe Sign).
- Analytics/Dashboards: Power BI, Tableau; exception dashboards and SLA monitors.
- Master Data Management: Informatica MDM, SAP MDG.
- Supplier Portals: Manufacturer-specific portals for claim submission and tracking.

Process Details:
## Overview
Process 9.2.5.6 Process related entries is the operational execution of recording all accounting entries tied to revenue adjustments and deductions so that the general ledger and subledgers fairly present revenue and contra-revenue for financial reporting. It translates approved adjustments—such as credits, rebates, chargebacks, customer short‑pays, sales returns, variable consideration accruals, and deferrals—into accurate, timely journal entries with complete audit support.

This process:
- Ensures revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC 606/IFRS 15 and company policy.
- Provides a balanced and reconcilable ledger by posting entries to the correct accounts, cost objects, entities, and periods, with appropriate reversals when applicable.
- Supports period-end close, management reporting, external financial statements, audit readiness, and compliance (e.g., SOX).

It sits within 9.2 Perform revenue accounting and specifically under 9.2.5 Manage and process adjustments/deductions, following upstream activities that identify, validate, calculate, and approve adjustments, and preceding reconciliations, analytics, and reporting.

## Key Activities
- Intake and triage of adjustment/deduction requests (manual and system-generated).
- Validation of completeness and eligibility (supporting documents, approvals).
- Accounting determination (nature of entry, debit/credit accounts, dimensions, tax/FX).
- Journal preparation (one-time, recurring, reversing, mass upload).
- Routing for approval per Delegation of Authority (DOA) and control requirements.
- Posting entries to the revenue subledger and/or general ledger.
- Linking entries to source transactions and reason codes for traceability.
- Exception handling and error correction.
- Reconciliation of postings with subledgers and supporting schedules.
- Period-end activities (accruals, reversals, true-ups, flux analysis).
- Documentation and retention for audit and compliance.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs:
  - Approved adjustment requests (credit memos, rebates, MDF/co-op claims, chargebacks, short-pay resolutions, price protection, returns RMAs).
  - Calculations and schedules (rebate accrual models, variable consideration estimates, returns provisions, allocation files).
  - Source data from systems (ERP/Revenue Management, Billing, AR, CRM/Order Management, Warehouse/Returns, Deduction management).
  - Master data (chart of accounts, cost centers/profit centers, product/customer, legal entity, posting periods).
  - Policy references (revenue recognition, reserves, materiality, DOA, documentation standards).
  - FX rates, tax parameters, and accounting calendars.

- Prerequisites:
  - Prior steps completed: identification, validation, calculation, and approval of adjustments (9.2.5.1–9.2.5.5).
  - Open posting period and access rights configured.
  - Up-to-date master data and exchange rates.
  - Configured journal templates, reason codes, and integration mappings.

- Dependencies on other processes:
  - 9.2.1 Revenue recognition (contract modifications, performance obligations).
  - 9.2.3 Accounts receivable and cash application (deduction identification, short-pays).
  - 9.1 Planning and management accounting (profit center allocations, margin reporting).
  - 9.4 General accounting and reporting (GL close, reconciliations).
  - Sales operations/trade promotions management (rebates, co-op).
  - Tax and treasury (indirect tax on credits, FX revaluation).
  - IT/MDM (systems availability, data quality).

## Process Steps
1. Intake and queue creation
   - Capture requests from systems (auto-generated accruals, deduction tool) and manual submissions via standardized form.
   - Assign unique ID, categorize by type (rebate, return, chargeback, credit correction, reclass, accrual/deferral), and tag with reason code and priority/SLA.

2. Completeness and policy check
   - Verify required support is attached: agreement/contract, claim/settlement, RMA, proof of performance, calculation workbook, approvals.
   - Confirm eligibility per policy (terms, validity window, customer/product scope, materiality thresholds).

3. Accounting assessment
   - Determine accounting treatment under ASC 606/IFRS 15:
     - Contra-revenue (sales discounts, rebates, returns, price protection).
     - Revenue deferral/recognition (contract modifications, variable consideration constraint).
     - AR adjustments (short-pay, write-off within policy), with bad debt handled per policy if credit-related.
     - Reclassifications between revenue accounts or to other income/expense where appropriate.
   - Identify accounts and dimensions (GL account, cost/profit center, product/region, project, legal entity).
   - Determine tax impact (credit tax adjustments where applicable).
   - Determine FX handling and spot rate if multi-currency.

4. Calculate and allocate
   - Validate calculation logic or recompute as needed.
   - Allocate amounts across customers/products/cost centers based on the underlying driver (e.g., sales mix) and attach allocation file.
   - Determine reversal date for accruals/deferrals and whether entry is recurring.

5. Prepare journal entry
   - Populate standardized journal template with:
     - Document date, posting date, period.
     - Entry type (standard/reversing/recurring), source system, reference to source doc/contract.
     - Lines with accounts, dimensions, currency, amount (debit/credit), tax code if needed.
     - Reason code and detailed description.
   - Attach supporting documents and calculations.

6. Control checks
   - Automated validations: balanced entry, open period, valid accounts/dimensions, duplicate check, amount thresholds, required attachments present.
   - Manual review by preparer for completeness and narrative clarity.

7. Approval workflow
   - Route for approval based on DOA and control level (e.g., high-value, sensitive accounts).
   - Capture approver comments and electronic sign-off. Resolve any queries.

8. Post to ledger
   - Post to subledger (e.g., AR/revenue module) when entry affects customer-level balances; otherwise post to GL.
   - Ensure linkage to customer/invoice/contract where relevant for traceability and downstream analytics.
   - Record journal ID and update the request status to Posted.

9. Notification and stakeholder update
   - Notify requestor and impacted stakeholders (AR, Sales Ops, Rev Rec) of posting details.
   - Update dashboards and deduction aging with resolution codes.

10. Reconciliation and review
    - Reconcile posted entries to:
      - Subledger reports (AR balance, deduction aging).
      - Accrual and provision rollforwards.
      - Rebate and return reserve schedules.
    - Investigate and clear exceptions.

11. Period-end close activities
    - Post required accruals/true-ups for variable consideration and returns reserves.
    - Execute scheduled reversals; review recurring entries and adjust if assumptions changed.
    - Perform flux analysis on revenue and contra-revenue; document explanations.
    - Obtain management sign-off; lock period and archive documentation.

12. Record retention and audit support
    - Store journals and all support per retention policy with immutable links to source artifacts.
    - Maintain an audit trail of preparer/approver actions and any subsequent adjustments.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Posted journal entries in GL/subledgers with complete metadata and attachments.
- Updated deduction aging and resolution codes.
- Rollforward schedules for rebates, returns, and other reserves.
- Reconciliations between subledgers and GL; exception logs.
- Period-end close package (journal listing, flux analysis, sign-offs).
- Audit evidence (approval logs, calculations, policy references).

Success criteria:
- 100% of entries posted within SLA and within the correct period.
- Zero unexplained differences between subledgers and GL.
- Compliance with ASC 606/IFRS 15, tax rules, DOA, and SOX controls.
- Complete documentation and traceability; no audit findings.
- Accurate, timely reversals and minimal rework/error rate.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Revenue Accountant
  - Prepare and post journals; ensure correct accounting treatment; maintain schedules; perform reconciliations.
- Deductions Analyst (AR)
  - Investigate customer deductions/short-pays; assemble support; recommend accounting disposition and coding.
- Revenue Recognition Specialist
  - Advise on ASC 606/IFRS 15 implications; review variable consideration, deferrals, and contract modifications.
- Finance Manager/Controller
  - Approve journals per DOA; review flux analyses and reconciliations; oversee period-end close.
- Sales Operations/Trade Promotions Manager
  - Provide rebate/COOP agreement terms and approvals; validate accrual calculations and claim settlements.
- Tax Analyst
  - Review tax implications on credits/adjustments; ensure proper tax coding and reporting.
- GL Accountant
  - Ensure GL integrity; manage open/close periods; coordinate with consolidation/reporting.
- IT/ERP Support
  - Maintain journal workflows, master data integrity, integrations, and user access controls.
- Internal Audit/Compliance
  - Test key controls; review documentation and adherence to policy.

## Best Practices
- Standardize journal templates, reason codes, and narratives to improve clarity and analytics.
- Enforce maker-checker segregation and automated DOA workflows; minimize manual journal postings.
- Automate intake and posting for recurring/low-risk items using rules and RPA; retain manual review for high-risk entries.
- Link every entry to a source artifact (invoice, contract, claim, RMA) and maintain a consistent reference ID.
- Use reversing journals for accruals/deferrals and maintain a documented reversal schedule.
- Maintain robust variable consideration models with periodic back-testing and true-ups.
- Implement daily or near-real-time reconciliations between subledgers and GL.
- Establish a close calendar with cutoffs, checklists, and cross-functional sign-offs.
- Apply reason codes consistently to enable root-cause analysis and deduction reduction initiatives.
- Govern master data tightly (COA, dimensions, customers/products) to prevent mispostings.
- Monitor FX and tax impacts; use system-driven rates and tax engines where possible.
- Train stakeholders on documentation standards and revenue policies.

## Common Challenges
- High volume of small deductions and short-pays leading to backlog
  - Solution: Deduction management tools with auto-classification and reason codes; triage by materiality and automate low-value write-offs within policy.
- Misclassification between contra-revenue and bad debt/expense
  - Solution: Clear policy decision trees; mandatory Revenue Recognition review for edge cases; periodic sample audits.
- Manual errors and duplicate postings
  - Solution: Pre-posting duplicate checks, template validation rules, and posting locks; RPA with exception handling.
- Incomplete/late documentation
  - Solution: Required fields/attachments in intake; reject/return workflow; SLA tracking and escalation.
- Timing mismatches and out-of-period postings
  - Solution: Close calendar enforcement, cutoffs, reversing entries, and post-close adjustment review.
- Complex rebate calculations and allocations
  - Solution: Use specialized rebate/claim systems; standardized allocation drivers; independent review of models.
- System integration gaps (CRM/ERP/deduction tools)
  - Solution: API-based integrations, middleware, and reconciliation controls; reference IDs across systems.
- FX and tax misapplication
  - Solution: Use central rate sources and tax engines; automated determination; Tax review for non-standard entries.

## Performance Metrics
- Cycle time: average and 90th percentile from intake to posting.
- On-time posting rate: % entries posted within SLA and within period.
- Error/rework rate: % of journals requiring correction or reversal.
- Approval compliance: % journals approved per DOA before posting.
- Auto-post/straight-through processing rate for eligible items.
- Reconciliation breaks: count and value; time to resolve.
- Aged deductions: volume and value by aging bucket; resolution rate.
- Reserve accuracy: variance between accruals and actuals; back-testing results.
- Documentation completeness: % journals with required attachments and narratives.
- Close timeliness: time to complete revenue-related close tasks.
- Audit findings: number and severity related to this process.

## Technology and Tools
- ERP/Financials: SAP S/4HANA, Oracle ERP Cloud, Microsoft Dynamics 365 (GL, AR, revenue subledgers).
- Revenue recognition modules: SAP RAR, Oracle RMCS, Zuora Revenue for ASC 606/IFRS 15 treatment.
- Deduction and cash application tools: HighRadius, Billtrust, Serrala for identification, matching, and resolution.
- Rebate/trade promotion management: Vistex, Model N, Enable for accruals and settlements.
- Close and reconciliation management: BlackLine, Trintech Cadency for journal workflows, reconciliations, and certifications.
- Workflow/Intake: ServiceNow, Jira, or ERP-native workflows for requests and approvals.
- RPA/Automation: UiPath, Automation Anywhere for template population and posting.
- BI/Analytics: Power BI, Tableau for KPIs, flux analysis, and dashboards.
- Document management: SharePoint, OpenText for secure storage and audit trails.
- Integration/Master data: MuleSoft, Boomi; MDM tools for COA/dimensions consistency.
- FX and tax engines: Reuters/Refinitiv rate feeds; Vertex, Avalara for indirect tax.

# [9.3.1.1] Negotiate service-level agreements

## Overview
Negotiate service-level agreements (SLAs) is the process of defining, agreeing, and formalizing the scope, quality, and responsibilities between the Finance function (as customer) and internal or external service providers who support General Accounting and Reporting. Within Manage financial policies and procedures, SLA negotiation ensures that services critical to financial integrity (e.g., general ledger maintenance, journal processing, account reconciliations, close and reporting support, master data management) are delivered consistently, measurably, and in compliance with regulatory and policy requirements.

Purpose:
- Align service performance with financial policy, regulatory deadlines (e.g., month-end close, statutory reporting), and control requirements (e.g., SOX).
- Define clear expectations, mutual obligations, metrics, governance, and escalation paths.
- Enable predictable service quality, transparency, and continuous improvement.

Role in the organization:
- Anchors performance management for finance shared services, BPO providers, and enabling functions (IT, data, risk).
- Ensures underpinning contracts and operational-level agreements (OLAs) support end-to-end Finance outcomes (e.g., close cycle time, reporting accuracy).
- Provides auditable documentation for internal control and vendor risk management.

## Key Activities
- Identify service need and scope (e.g., GL close support, reconciliations).
- Gather and baseline requirements (volumes, complexity, seasonality, geographies).
- Define metrics, targets, measurement methods, and reporting cadence.
- Assess risks, controls, and compliance obligations (SOX, data privacy, audit rights).
- Negotiate commercial and non-commercial terms (pricing, credits, earn-backs, change control).
- Establish governance, roles, escalation paths, and issue management.
- Coordinate cross-functional review (Finance, Procurement, Legal, Risk, InfoSec, IT).
- Finalize and execute the SLA; implement measurement and governance mechanisms.
- Communicate, onboard, and monitor initial performance; refine via continuous improvement.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Documented service requirements and use cases (e.g., month-end close tasks, reconciliation types).
- Historical performance and volume data (baseline metrics, seasonality).
- Applicable policies and regulatory requirements (SOX, GAAP/IFRS, data retention).
- Standard SLA templates, definitions, and approved KPI library.
- Budgetary constraints and pricing benchmarks.
- Risk assessments, BCP/DR requirements, data privacy and security requirements.
- Enterprise sourcing strategy and preferred supplier list/service catalog.

Prerequisites:
- Delegation of Authority (DoA) and approval thresholds defined.
- Governance framework and RACI for negotiation and ongoing oversight.
- Contract lifecycle management (CLM) and document repositories configured.
- Measurement capability identified (tools, data sources, ownership).

Dependencies on other processes:
- Vendor selection and contracting (Procurement/Sourcing).
- Manage service catalog and define financial policies and procedures.
- Risk management, InfoSec assessment, and privacy impact assessments.
- IT service management (where services depend on ERP or platforms).
- Record to report and close processes that the SLA underpins.

## Process Steps
1. Trigger and initiation
   - Identify need (new service, renewal, scope change, performance issue).
   - Assign SLA Owner (typically Finance Service Owner or Process Owner).
   - Create negotiation plan, timeline aligned to contract expiry/close calendar.

2. Define scope and service boundaries
   - Draft service scope: processes, geographies, entities, languages, in/out of scope.
   - Document dependencies and required inputs from Finance, IT, or third parties.
   - Identify peak periods (e.g., quarter-end, year-end) and blackout windows.

3. Baseline and requirements gathering
   - Collect historical volume, cycle time, error rates, and workload drivers.
   - Determine control and compliance requirements (SOX key controls, audit evidence).
   - Validate data collection feasibility for each proposed metric.

4. Draft service levels and measurement model
   - Select KPIs and SLTs (service level targets) with clear definitions and formulas.
   - Define measurement sources, sampling, exclusions, and calculation timing.
   - Set reporting cadence (weekly, MBR/QBR), dashboards, and data ownership.
   - Example metrics for General Accounting:
     - Month-end close cycle time (business days).
     - On-time completion of reconciliations (% by due date).
     - Journal entry rework rate (% requiring correction).
     - Intercompany mismatch resolution turnaround (hours/days).
     - Master data change turnaround time (hours/days) and right-first-time (%).
     - Financial statement delivery timeliness and accuracy (%).
     - PBC request turnaround during audits (days).

5. Risk, control, and compliance embedding
   - Define control obligations (segregation of duties, maker-checker, evidence retention).
   - Specify audit rights, data privacy clauses, breach notification SLAs.
   - Require BCP/DR: RTO/RPO, failover tests, location resilience, staffing coverage.

6. Commercial and contractual terms
   - Choose pricing model (per-transaction, FTE-based, fixed fee, tiered).
   - Define service credits/penalties, earn-backs, caps, chronic failure clauses.
   - Include indexation, benchmarking, transition/termination assistance, IP/confidentiality.
   - Establish change control for scope or metric modifications.

7. Governance model and RACI
   - Define roles: Service Owner, Provider Lead, Governance Board, VMO, Escalation points.
   - Set cadence for MBR/QBR, continuous improvement plans (CIPs), and root-cause analysis.
   - Agree issue prioritization, ticketing, and escalation timelines.

8. Negotiation sessions
   - Circulate draft SLA and negotiation agenda; maintain issues and decisions log.
   - Conduct structured sessions; reconcile positions with data and benchmarks.
   - Validate feasibility during peak periods; stress-test staffing and capacity plans.

9. Cross-functional review and approvals
   - Legal redline (liability, indemnity, confidentiality, audit rights).
   - Procurement review (rate cards, commercial reasonableness).
   - InfoSec/privacy sign-off; Risk/Compliance and Internal Audit review as needed.
   - Obtain approvals per DoA; finalize exhibits (service catalog, OLAs/UCs).

10. Execution and enablement
    - Execute via e-signature; store in CLM/repository with metadata and review dates.
    - Configure measurement dashboards, data pipelines, and alert thresholds.
    - Onboard teams; train on SLA obligations, definitions, and governance.

11. Baseline period and stabilization
    - Run a shakedown/baselining period (e.g., 1–2 cycles) to validate metrics.
    - Calibrate targets if baseline differs materially and both parties agree.

12. Operate and improve
    - Monitor performance; conduct MBR/QBR; log and execute CIPs.
    - Manage changes through formal change control; re-baseline metrics as needed.
    - Plan periodic SLA reviews (e.g., annually) or trigger on material events.

13. Audit and renewal
    - Perform periodic compliance audits; remediate findings.
    - Begin renewal/renegotiation 90–180 days before expiry based on complexity.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Executed SLA and associated exhibits (service scope, KPI definitions, OLAs, UCs).
- Governance charter, RACI, and escalation matrix.
- Performance measurement setup (dashboards, data definitions).
- Risk and compliance register specific to the service.
- Communication and training materials.
- Transition/implementation plan and stabilization report.

Success criteria:
- SLA signed within planned timeline and budget.
- Metrics are measurable, achievable, and aligned to Finance outcomes.
- Compliance requirements embedded and approved by Risk/Legal/Privacy.
- Measurement is live before service go-live; first cycles meet or exceed targets.
- Stakeholders acknowledge clarity of roles and obligations.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Finance Service Owner / Process Owner (R2R): Leads scope, metrics, governance; accountable for outcomes.
- Provider Lead (Internal SSC or BPO): Commits capacity, quality, and continuous improvement; owns delivery.
- Procurement/Sourcing: Manages commercial negotiation, supplier diligence, and contracting workflow.
- Legal Counsel: Reviews and negotiates legal terms, audit rights, liability, confidentiality, data use.
- Risk and Compliance / Internal Audit: Ensures controls, SOX, and auditability are embedded.
- Information Security / Data Privacy Officer: Validates security, access, and data protection requirements.
- IT/ERP Owner: Confirms system-related SLAs/OLAs and measurement feasibility.
- Vendor Management Office (VMO): Oversees supplier performance, governance cadence, and remediation.
- Finance Leadership (Controller/CFO): Provides approvals per DoA; ensures alignment to financial strategy.

## Best Practices
- Use standard SLA templates and a common KPI glossary to avoid ambiguity.
- Tie SLAs to business outcomes (e.g., financial close and reporting timeliness), not only activity metrics.
- Define measurement methods, data sources, exclusions, and rounding rules explicitly.
- Include mutual obligations and dependencies (e.g., timely approvals and inputs from Finance) to prevent unfair breaches.
- Keep the metric set focused (10–15 meaningful KPIs), with clear weighting and critical service levels.
- Calibrate targets using actual baselines and industry benchmarks; allow a short stabilization period.
- Implement OLAs and Underpinning Contracts for internal dependencies (IT, data, HR) to support end-to-end SLAs.
- Include structured escalation and root-cause analysis requirements; mandate corrective action plans with timelines.
- Design service credits that discourage gaming (e.g., caps, chronic failure clauses) and reward sustained improvements.
- Schedule periodic formal reviews to adjust for scope, volume, or regulatory changes.
- Ensure BCP/DR testing cadence and outcomes are reported in governance forums.

## Common Challenges
- Ambiguous definitions leading to disputes
  - Solution: Use standard definitions; include examples and calculation formulas; run a pilot measurement.
- Unrealistic targets or insufficient baseline data
  - Solution: Perform data-driven baselining; phase-in targets; revisit after stabilization.
- Measurement gaps and data quality issues
  - Solution: Validate data availability up front; assign data owners; automate collection; audit the metric pipeline.
- Misaligned incentives and excessive metrics
  - Solution: Focus on a balanced scorecard; weight critical outcomes; tie credits to customer impact.
- Multi-party dependencies causing E2E failures
  - Solution: Establish OLAs/UCs; define joint accountability and cross-provider governance.
- Compliance and control omissions
  - Solution: Embed Risk/Compliance/IA early; require control mapping and evidence retention.
- Scope creep and change management issues
  - Solution: Enforce formal change control; maintain a service catalog; adjust pricing and metrics when scope changes.
- Geographical and time-zone coverage problems during peak cycles
  - Solution: Agree staffing models, holiday calendars, and surge capacity plans; define blackout windows.

## Performance Metrics
Negotiation and setup effectiveness:
- SLA negotiation cycle time (days) vs. plan.
- Number of negotiation iterations/redlines.
- On-time approval rate and compliance sign-offs achieved first pass (%).
- Stakeholder satisfaction with clarity and completeness (CSAT).

Operational performance post-go-live:
- SLA attainment rate (% KPIs meeting targets per period).
- Critical service level breaches (count/severity) and time to resolution.
- Service credits incurred ($) and trend; root-cause distribution of breaches.
- Close cycle time (days) and on-time reporting (%).
- Reconciliation on-time completion (%) and aged unreconciled items (count/value).
- Journal entry right-first-time (%) and rework volume (%).
- Audit PBC on-time (%), audit findings related to service (count).
- Change request volume and average lead time (days).
- BCP/DR test pass rate (%) and RTO/RPO adherence.

## Technology and Tools
- Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) and e-signature: Icertis, DocuSign CLM, Adobe Sign.
- IT Service Management and ticketing: ServiceNow, Jira Service Management.
- Performance reporting and analytics: Power BI, Tableau; data pipelines via SQL/ETL tools.
- ERP and Finance systems: SAP S/4HANA, Oracle Cloud ERP, Workday; close/reconciliation tools (BlackLine, Trintech Cadency).
- Vendor management and sourcing: SAP Ariba, Coupa, GEP; supplier risk platforms (ProcessUnity, OneTrust).
- GRC and compliance: ServiceNow GRC, SAP GRC, AuditBoard.
- Collaboration and repositories: Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, Confluence.
- Requirements and workflow: Confluence, Jira; approval workflows aligned to DoA.
