# [9.3.2.8] Prepare Trial Balance

## Overview
Prepare Trial Balance is the core general accounting activity that compiles the ending balances of all general ledger (GL) accounts for a defined period and verifies that total debits equal total credits. It produces the unadjusted and adjusted trial balances that serve as the foundation for financial statement preparation, management reporting, regulatory filings, and audits.

Purpose and role in the organization:
- Ensures the GL is complete and internally consistent (debits = credits) before reporting.
- Surfaces errors, omissions, or misclassifications that require adjusting journal entries (AJEs).
- Validates that control accounts (e.g., cash, AR, AP, payroll, inventory, fixed assets) agree with their subledgers and reconciliations.
- Provides a standardized dataset for consolidation, analysis, and disclosures.
- Supports internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR/SOX), enabling documented preparation and review.

Typical frequency: monthly, quarterly, and annually; ad hoc for special reporting and audits.

Scope: Entity-level or business unit GL; may include currency translation to group currency for consolidation; excludes consolidation eliminations (performed in consolidation).

## Key Activities
- Extract and compile GL period-end balances for all accounts.
- Generate the unadjusted trial balance (UTB).
- Perform integrity checks: debits vs credits, missing accounts, suspended/unposted items.
- Tie key control accounts to subledgers and reconciliations (cash, AR, AP, inventory, FA, payroll).
- Perform variance analytics vs prior periods, forecast/budget; identify anomalies.
- Prepare and post adjusting, accrual, deferral, reclassification, and error-correction entries.
- Generate the adjusted trial balance (ATB); confirm debits = credits.
- Lock/freeze the ATB and publish to reporting and consolidation tools.
- Archive supporting documentation and evidence of review/approval.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Finalized GL postings for the period (regular and subledger-interface journals).
- Chart of accounts (COA), posting rules, account attributes (natural/functional).
- Prior period TB and roll-forward schedules.
- Subledger outputs: AR, AP, FA, Inventory/Costing, Projects, Payroll, Bank.
- Period FX rates (for remeasurement/translation where applicable).
- Close calendar and materiality thresholds.
- Journal entry support for planned AJEs (e.g., accrual schedules, depreciation runs).
- System reports: interface logs, exception/error logs, open items aging.

Prerequisites:
- Subledgers closed and interfaced to GL (or confirmed schedule and cutoffs).
- Period status configured (GL and subledgers) per close calendar.
- Depreciation/cost runs completed (FA, inventory close/costing).
- Bank statements imported and significant cash postings completed.
- Access and approvals aligned with segregation of duties (SoD).

Dependencies on other processes:
- 9.3.2.1 Record journal entries (including automated postings).
- 9.3.2.2 Maintain general ledger (COA, period management).
- 9.3.2.5 Perform account reconciliations (supports tie-outs).
- 9.3.2.6 Manage fixed assets accounting (depreciation, disposals).
- 9.3.2.7 Close period (calendar, status management).
- 9.3.3 Prepare financial statements (consumes the ATB).

## Process Steps
1) Plan and initialize
- Review close calendar, dependencies, and period status.
- Confirm subledgers’ closure/feeds status (AP, AR, FA, Inventory, Payroll, Projects).
- Confirm FX rates published and interface jobs completed.

2) Generate Unadjusted Trial Balance (UTB)
- Extract period-end GL balances by entity and currency from ERP.
- Ensure all posting accounts are included; exclude statistical/non-posting accounts if applicable.
- Validate completeness: total accounts, zero-balance accounts (optional), and opening balance roll-forwards.

3) Integrity checks on UTB
- Confirm debits = credits. If not:
  - Identify unposted/unbalanced journals; reprocess or reverse as needed.
  - Review failed interfaces and suspense/clearing accounts.
  - Check period mispostings (next period or wrong entity).
  - Investigate multi-currency rounding residuals and remeasurement journals.
- Run data quality checks:
  - No accounts with invalid signs (e.g., negative AR).
  - No orphan accounts (inactive or unmapped to reporting).
  - Trial balance total equals movement roll-forward.

4) Tie-out control accounts
- Bank/cash: confirm to bank reconciliation balance.
- AR/AP: reconcile to subledger trial balances/aging reports.
- Inventory: reconcile to inventory subledger/valuation; confirm cost close.
- Fixed assets: reconcile to FA subledger net book value and period activity.
- Payroll-related liabilities: tie to payroll registers and tax filings.
- Document reconciling items with aging and resolution plan.

5) Analytical review
- Compare UTB to prior month/quarter, same period prior year, and forecast/budget.
- Identify unusual balances, large swings, new accounts, and stale balances.
- Flag potential adjustments, reclassifications, or error corrections.

6) Prepare adjusting entries (AJEs)
- Accruals/deferrals: expenses/revenues, prepaids amortization, unearned revenue.
- Depreciation/amortization (if not auto-posted).
- Provisions: bad debt, warranty, legal, bonuses; based on documented estimates.
- Reclassifications: correct account, department, cost center, or project coding.
- FX remeasurement (entity-level) to functional currency if required.
- Intercompany true-ups at entity level (eliminations handled at consolidation).
- Prepare JE support: calculations, approvals per control matrix, materiality checks.

7) Post and approve AJEs
- Enter AJEs in ERP with proper descriptions, dates, and attachments.
- Obtain required approvals; ensure SoD compliance (preparer vs approver).
- Confirm posting to correct period/entity; avoid backdating unless approved policy.

8) Generate Adjusted Trial Balance (ATB)
- Re-run TB after all AJEs posted.
- Confirm debits = credits, no suspense balances beyond agreed thresholds.
- Re-perform key tie-outs impacted by AJEs.

9) Final review and sign-off
- Controller/Senior Accountant reviews ATB, variance analysis, and tie-out evidences.
- Resolve open reconciling items or document with action plans and timelines.
- Sign-off in close management tool; note any post-close adjustment windows.

10) Publish and close
- Export ATB to:
  - Financial reporting packages and consolidation system (with mapping).
  - Analytics/BI tools for management reporting.
- Lock/freeze period in ERP per policy to prevent unauthorized postings.
- Archive ATB, JE logs, tie-outs, approvals, and checklists in the DMS with naming conventions and retention.

11) Post-close monitoring (optional)
- Track late entries and assess need for post-close adjustments.
- Update lessons learned and process improvements in the close playbook.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Unadjusted Trial Balance (UTB) and Adjusted Trial Balance (ATB) by entity/currency.
- AJE listing with documentation and approvals.
- Tie-out packages for control accounts and reconciliations.
- Variance analysis summaries and investigation notes.
- Close checklist with preparer and reviewer sign-offs.
- Exported TB files for consolidation/reporting (e.g., CSV/Excel) with mapping metadata.
- Audit-ready archive of evidence and audit trail.

Success criteria:
- ATB balances (total debits = total credits) with no unexplained differences.
- All material control accounts reconciled and tied to subledgers/banks.
- Adjustments supported, approved, and posted to the correct period.
- Published by close deadline (e.g., T+3/T+5) with zero material post-close corrections.
- Clean audit trail; no SoD or access control exceptions.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- GL Accountant (Preparer)
  - Generate UTB/ATB, perform checks, prepare AJEs, compile tie-outs, maintain documentation.
- Senior Accountant
  - Lead tie-outs, perform variance analytics, coach preparers, handle complex AJEs.
- Accounting Manager/Controller (Reviewer/Approver)
  - Review and approve AJEs, validate ATB completeness/accuracy, sign-off, ensure deadlines.
- Subledger Owners (AP/AR/FA/Inventory/Payroll)
  - Close subledgers, resolve interface issues, provide subledger trial balances and reconciliations.
- FP&A
  - Provide forecast/budget; partner on accruals and analytical review.
- Consolidation/Reporting Team
  - Confirm mapping to reporting structures; ingest ATB to consolidation.
- IT/ERP Support
  - Ensure system availability, interface processing, user access, and report configurations.
- Internal/External Auditors (periodic)
  - Review evidence, sample AJEs, test controls and tie-outs.

## Best Practices
- Use a standardized close checklist with ownership, due dates, and dependencies.
- Enforce SoD: JE preparers cannot approve; access rights aligned with roles.
- Automate subledger-to-GL reconciliations and TB generation where possible.
- Maintain a robust COA with clear posting rules and reporting mappings.
- Implement threshold-based materiality and review scope to prioritize efforts.
- Require descriptions and attachments for all AJEs; use JE templates with validations.
- Lock periods progressively (subledgers first, then GL) to reduce rework.
- Perform rolling reviews mid-month to pre-validate balances and reduce month-end spikes.
- Document recurring AJEs in schedules with version control and owner sign-offs.
- Leverage analytics (variance thresholds, trend, and ratio analysis) to detect anomalies early.
- Manage multi-currency explicitly: define remeasurement and translation policies and rate sources.
- Keep suspense/clearing accounts on tight SLAs with aging and escalation.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Out-of-balance TB:
  - Cause: unposted/unbalanced JE, failed interfaces, period mispostings.
  - Solution: run ERP integrity reports, reconcile interface logs, reopen/post with approvals, enforce JE balancing rules.
- Timing/cutoff issues:
  - Cause: late invoices, revenue recognition timing.
  - Solution: standardized cutoff procedures, accrual checklist, late entry policy.
- Subledger mismatches:
  - Cause: interface timing, mapping errors.
  - Solution: daily interface monitoring, reconciliation automation, mapping validation.
- Multi-currency rounding/residuals:
  - Cause: rate precision or posting order.
  - Solution: standard rate precision, end-of-period remeasurement JE, review FX differences accounts.
- Misclassifications:
  - Cause: incorrect account/cost center.
  - Solution: account validation rules, reclass JEs, training and COA guidance.
- Manual spreadsheet risks:
  - Cause: offline calculations and copy/paste errors.
  - Solution: controlled templates with cell protections, version control, or systemize calculations.
- Excessive post-close adjustments:
  - Cause: weak review during close.
  - Solution: earlier analytics, stronger review checkpoints, materiality-based focus.
- Access/SoD breaches:
  - Cause: inadequate role design.
  - Solution: periodic access reviews, role-based provisioning, workflow approvals.

## Performance Metrics (KPIs)
- Close timeliness: days to ATB publication (e.g., T+3/T+5).
- First-pass yield: % of periods with zero material post-close adjustments.
- Out-of-balance incidents: count and resolution time.
- Reconciliation completeness: % of key control accounts reconciled by deadline.
- AJE volume and mix: number/value of AJEs; % recurring vs one-time; % reclass vs accrual.
- Automation rate: % of balances sourced from automated processes vs manual.
- Variance resolution: % of flagged variances investigated and closed by deadline.
- Suspense/clearing aging: average age and balance vs thresholds.
- Audit findings: number/severity related to TB preparation and JE controls.

## Technology and Tools
- ERP/GL systems: SAP S/4HANA (FI), Oracle Cloud ERP, Microsoft Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Workday Financials.
- Subledgers: AP/AR, FA, Inventory, Projects, Payroll modules integrated to GL.
- Close management and reconciliation: BlackLine, FloQast, Trintech Cadency, OneStream Task Manager.
- Consolidation/reporting: SAP Group Reporting, Oracle FCCS, OneStream, Tagetik, Power BI/Tableau.
- Data integration/ETL and integrity: native ERP connectors, APIs, interface monitors.
- Spreadsheets with controls: Excel/Google Sheets with protected templates and audit trails (or controlled via SharePoint/Drive/Box).
- RPA/Scripting: to automate report extraction, tie-outs, and file preparation.
- Document management: SharePoint, Box, OpenText for evidence, approvals, and retention.

This process, executed with discipline and supported by robust controls and automation, ensures a reliable foundation for financial reporting and efficient period close.

Process Details:
## Overview
Establish fixed-asset policies and procedures defines the principles, rules, and controls governing how an organization identifies, acquires, classifies, measures, depreciates, revalues, impairs, safeguards, disposes of, and reports property, plant, and equipment (PPE) and related long-lived assets. This process creates a consistent, compliant framework that ensures:
- Accurate financial reporting under applicable standards (e.g., IFRS IAS 16/IAS 36/IAS 23/IFRS 13; US GAAP ASC 360/ASC 410/ASC 835; local GAAP/tax).
- Strong internal controls over financial reporting (e.g., SOX readiness).
- Operational stewardship and asset lifecycle governance across Procurement, Projects/CAPEX, Operations, and Accounting.
- Efficient close processes and audit readiness.

It sets the authoritative policy, the standard operating procedures (SOPs), and the system configurations in the fixed-asset subledger/ERP to implement those rules. It also defines change governance, roles, and training to sustain compliance across geographies and business units.

Scope typically includes:
- Asset capitalization criteria and thresholds.
- Asset classes, useful lives, componentization, residual values, and depreciation methods.
- Cost capitalization rules (direct, indirect, interest, commissioning).
- Revaluation policies (IFRS) and impairment triggers/measurement.
- Maintenance vs. improvement distinctions; repairs policy.
- Asset identification/tagging, asset master data governance, physical verification.
- Transfers, reclassifications, partial retirements, disposals, gains/losses.
- Construction-in-progress (CIP)/assets under construction (AUC) governance.
- Book vs. tax depreciation differences and reporting.
- Interfaces to lease accounting for right-of-use assets (policy alignment).
- Asset retirement obligations (ARO)/decommissioning provisions.
- Governance, approvals, documentation, and audit evidence.

## Key Activities
- Regulatory and standards assessment: Identify applicable accounting frameworks and local statutory/tax requirements.
- Policy design: Define capitalization thresholds, asset classes, useful lives, depreciation methods, cost capitalization rules, revaluation/impairment, disposals, ARO, and controls.
- Procedures and workflows: Draft SOPs for day-to-day execution (e.g., asset creation, transfers, physical inventory).
- System enablement: Configure ERP fixed-asset subledger (e.g., SAP FI-AA, Oracle Assets) and integrate with P2P, Projects, EAM/CMMS.
- Master data governance: Define asset master fields, validation, and maintenance processes; asset tagging standards.
- Control design: Segregation of duties, approvals, reconciliations, physical verification cadence, exception handling.
- Stakeholder review and approval: Controller/CFO sign-off; Legal/Tax/Operations concurrence; Audit review.
- Training and communication: Rollout materials, sessions, and job aids to impacted teams.
- Implementation and pilot: Test policies in a controlled environment, then deploy.
- Monitoring and continuous improvement: KPIs, compliance monitoring, periodic policy refresh.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Current accounting standards, corporate accounting manual, and audit findings.
- Local statutory and tax rules (e.g., depreciation methods/lives).
- Business strategy and CAPEX plans; asset portfolio profile by asset class.
- Existing FA policy, SOPs, and ERP configuration.
- Materiality assessments and risk appetite.
- Operational maintenance strategies (to align repairs vs. improvements).
- Stakeholder requirements (Finance, Tax, Operations, Projects, Procurement, Legal, EHS).

Prerequisites:
- Executive sponsorship (Controller/CFO) and established governance body.
- Access to subject matter experts (FA accounting, tax, operations, systems).
- An agreed document management standard (version control, approvals, retention).
- Identified change management and training resources.

Dependencies on other processes:
- Capital planning and budgeting (for thresholds and CIP governance).
- Procure-to-Pay and Project Accounting (for capitalization workflow and cost capture).
- Lease accounting process (align treatment of ROU assets and leasehold improvements).
- Impairment assessment and close processes (for revaluation/impairment cadence).
- Physical inventory/asset verification process in Operations/EAM.
- Environmental/EHS processes for ARO estimates.

## Process Steps
1) Initiate and plan
- Appoint policy owner (Fixed Asset Manager/Corporate Accounting).
- Define scope (entities, GAAP basis, asset classes), timeline, and deliverables.
- Form cross-functional working group (Accounting, Tax, Operations, Procurement, Projects, IT/ERP, Legal, EHS, Internal Audit).

2) Assess requirements and current state
- Map applicable accounting and tax requirements by jurisdiction.
- Inventory existing policies, SOPs, system settings, and control gaps.
- Analyze asset portfolio (classes, lives, historical depreciation issues, CIP aging).
- Review audit findings and close cycle pain points.

3) Design policy framework
- Capitalization criteria and thresholds:
  - Define recognition criteria and minimum capitalization thresholds by asset class and currency.
  - Clarify low-value pooling/expense policies and materiality limits.
- Cost capitalization rules:
  - Determine which costs are capitalizable (purchase price, freight, installation, testing) vs. expensed (routine maintenance).
  - Define treatment of internal labor/overheads; interest capitalization (IAS 23/ASC 835) rules and rates.
  - Define treatment for software, development, and cloud implementations (aligned with separate software policy).
- Asset classes and componentization:
  - Establish asset classes and sub-classes with default useful lives, residual value assumptions, and depreciation methods.
  - Define componentization rules for significant parts with different lives (e.g., building components).
  - Clarify standby equipment/spare parts policy (inventory vs. PPE).
- Depreciation policy:
  - Methods (straight-line default; units-of-production for specific assets; reducing balance where appropriate).
  - Conventions (prorata by month, mid-month/half-year conventions).
  - In-service date definition; start/stop rules; handling idle assets.
- Revaluation and impairment:
  - IFRS revaluation model vs. cost model selection by asset class and geography.
  - Frequency and triggers for fair value remeasurements; valuation methodologies; use of external valuers.
  - Impairment indicators, testing cadence, and measurement approach (cash-generating units).
- Disposals, retirements, and transfers:
  - Approval thresholds and required documentation.
  - Partial retirements and component swaps; gain/loss recognition.
  - Intercompany transfers, reclassifications (CIP to PPE), and trade-ins.
- CIP/AUC governance:
  - Criteria to place in service; cutover rules for capitalization from projects.
  - Monthly CIP review and aging thresholds; actions for stale items.
- ARO/decommissioning:
  - Identification criteria; estimation methods; discount rates; unwinding accretion.
- Tax alignment:
  - Book vs. tax depreciation differences; tracking requirements for tax fixed asset ledgers (e.g., MACRS).
- Asset safeguarding and verification:
  - Asset tagging standards (barcode/RFID), physical count cadence, reconciliation process, threshold for investigation of variances.
- Controls and documentation:
  - Segregation of duties; approval matrices; reconciliations; change control for policy and system configuration.
  - Evidence requirements and retention periods.

4) Draft policy and procedures
- Write the policy document (purpose, scope, definitions, principles, roles, controls).
- Draft SOPs and work instructions per process area (asset creation, transfers, disposals, physical verification, month-end depreciation, revaluation).
- Create a RACI and approval matrices.

5) Validate with stakeholders and legal/compliance
- Review with Tax for local requirements and deferred tax implications.
- Review with Legal and EHS for ARO/legal obligations.
- Validate operational practicality with Operations/EAM and Procurement.
- Internal Audit assessment of control design.

6) Configure systems and controls
- Update ERP FA subledger: asset classes, depreciation keys, useful life tables, conventions, books (corporate/statutory/tax), ARO parameters, revaluation settings.
- Implement master data governance rules (required fields, validation, workflows).
- Integrate with P2P and Projects (auto-creation from receipts/WBS; capitalization workflows).
- Set up reports, reconciliations, and close calendars.

7) Pilot and test
- Execute test scenarios end-to-end (capitalization, componentization, depreciation runs, transfers, disposals, revaluation, impairment, ARO).
- Validate outputs (GL tie-outs, tax books, disclosures) and control evidence.
- Remediate issues and finalize configurations.

8) Approve, publish, and train
- Obtain formal approval (Controller/CFO, Audit Committee if required).
- Publish in policy repository; communicate effective date.
- Deliver role-based training and job aids; update onboarding materials.

9) Implement and monitor
- Go-live; ensure cutover for in-flight assets and CIP.
- Monitor KPIs and exceptions; run physical verification as per cadence.
- Conduct post-implementation review at 60–90 days.

10) Maintain and improve
- Annual or trigger-based review (standard changes, business model changes, audit findings).
- Controlled change management for policy and system updates; versioning and communication.

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs:
- Approved Fixed Asset Accounting Policy and related SOPs.
- Configured ERP FA subledger and integrated workflows.
- RACI matrix, approval matrices, and control narratives.
- Training materials and completion records.
- Governance model and review calendar.

Deliverables produced:
- Policy document (version-controlled).
- Useful life and depreciation method schedule by asset class and location.
- Capitalization threshold schedule.
- Asset class and master data dictionary.
- Test scripts and results; sign-off documentation.

Success criteria:
- External and internal audit acceptance with no significant findings.
- Accurate, timely depreciation and asset accounting with minimal manual adjustments.
- Compliance with applicable GAAP/IFRS and local tax; complete and accurate disclosures.
- Reduction in misclassification and CIP aging issues; low exception rate in physical verification.
- Consistent application across entities/geographies.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- CFO/Controller: Sponsor; approve policy; ensure compliance and resourcing.
- Corporate Accounting/Fixed Asset Manager (Process Owner): Lead design, maintain policy, oversee system configuration, monitor KPIs, manage changes.
- Fixed Asset Accountants: Execute SOPs; maintain asset master data; perform reconciliations and depreciation; handle transfers/disposals.
- Tax: Advise on tax depreciation, books, and reporting; ensure alignment with tax law; manage deferred taxes.
- Operations/Plant Management: Safeguard assets; report asset movements; support physical verification; validate in-service dates.
- Procurement: Ensure correct cost capture; tag assets on receipt; route asset-related POs per policy.
- Project Accounting/PMO: Govern CIP; ensure timely capitalization; provide WBS settlement data.
- IT/ERP: Configure and maintain FA module; enable integrations; enforce master data rules.
- Legal/EHS: Identify legal obligations and ARO; advise on contractual terms affecting asset accounting.
- Internal Audit: Assess control design and effectiveness; advise on remediation.
- External Valuers (as needed): Provide fair value assessments for revaluations or impairments.

## Best Practices
- Align with authoritative literature (IAS 16/IAS 36/IAS 23/IFRS 13; ASC 360/ASC 410/ASC 835) and document any policy elections.
- Risk-based capitalization thresholds that balance materiality and operational effort.
- Componentization of significant parts with different useful lives for material assets.
- Standardize asset classes and useful lives; maintain a central schedule with local overlays.
- Clear distinction between repairs/maintenance (expense) and improvements (capitalization) with decision trees/examples.
- Strong CIP governance: monthly aging reviews; strict in-service criteria; prompt closeout of projects.
- Enforce master data governance and asset tagging at receipt/commissioning.
- Automate integrations between P2P, Projects, EAM/CMMS, and FA subledger to minimize manual entries.
- Periodic physical verification with reconciliation and root-cause analysis of variances.
- Define and monitor impairment indicators; integrate with FP&A and Operations for trigger identification.
- Establish revaluation policy only where benefits outweigh costs; use qualified valuers and robust documentation.
- Formal change control and annual policy review cadence; robust training and certification for key users.

## Common Challenges
- Fragmented practices across regions/business units
  - Solution: Central policy with controlled local addenda; governance council; common ERP configurations.
- Misclassification of costs (repairs vs. capital)
  - Solution: Decision matrices, examples, and mandatory review/approval for borderline cases; targeted training.
- Inconsistent useful lives and depreciation methods
  - Solution: Centralized useful life schedule with periodic benchmarking; enforce via ERP keys.
- CIP backlogs and delayed capitalization
  - Solution: Monthly CIP aging KPIs; PMO accountability; automated in-service workflows; thresholds for escalation.
- Poor asset master data quality
  - Solution: Master data governance, required fields, validation rules, and periodic data quality audits.
- Weak disposal controls leading to ghost assets or unrecorded retirements
  - Solution: Disposal approval workflows; asset movement logs; physical verification tie-outs.
- Revaluation and impairment complexity (IFRS)
  - Solution: Clear triggers, valuation methodologies, external valuer panel, and strong documentation.
- Book vs. tax differences management
  - Solution: Separate tax books; automated book/tax tracking; coordinated year-end processes.
- ARO estimation and updates
  - Solution: Cross-functional process with EHS/Legal; standardized models; periodic remeasurement.
- System limitations or misconfigurations
  - Solution: Fit-for-purpose FA module; regression-tested changes; access controls; continuous improvement backlog.

## Performance Metrics
- Policy coverage and adoption:
  - % of entities/business units certified compliant with policy.
  - Number of approved local deviations/addenda.
- Data and process quality:
  - % assets with complete/valid master data fields.
  - Physical verification variance rate (% count variances by value and unit).
  - Exception rate in capitalization (repairs reclassified post-review).
- Timeliness and efficiency:
  - On-time monthly depreciation run (% months on schedule).
  - Average cycle time to capitalize assets from in-service date.
  - CIP aging (value and % >90 days past in-service readiness).
- Accuracy and compliance:
  - Number of audit findings related to fixed assets (internal/external).
  - Manual journal adjustments to FA per period (count/value).
  - Revaluation/impairment documentation completeness (sample pass rate).
- Financial impact indicators:
  - Write-offs due to policy noncompliance (value).
  - Book-to-tax depreciation reconciliation timeliness and variance explanations.
- Training and awareness:
  - Training completion rate for impacted roles.
  - Policy knowledge check pass rates.

Targets should be set based on baseline performance and materiality thresholds.

- ERP fixed-asset subledger:
  - SAP FI-AA, Oracle Fusion Assets, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Fixed Assets, NetSuite Fixed Assets.

Process Details:
## Overview
Maintain fixed-asset master data files is the foundational process for creating, updating, validating, and governing the master records that describe an organization’s fixed assets throughout their lifecycle. The fixed-asset master holds the canonical data used by subledger accounting, depreciation calculation, tax books, physical asset tracking, and financial reporting.

Purpose:
- Ensure all capital assets are accurately identified, classified, and linked to accounting and operational structures.
- Enable compliant and automated depreciation, impairment, and reporting across statutory and tax books.
- Provide traceability from procurement and project spend to capitalized assets, and from assets to responsible owners and locations.
- Support physical inventory, asset transfers, disposals, and audits with high-quality master data.

Role in the organization:
- Serves as the single source of truth for fixed-asset information used by Finance, Tax, Operational/Facilities teams, and Audit.
- Drives the accuracy of depreciation postings, asset balances, and disclosures (e.g., PPE roll-forward).
- Supports regulatory compliance (IFRS/US GAAP/local GAAP, SOX, tax regulations) and internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR).

## Key Activities
- Define and maintain asset master data standards, templates, and validation rules.
- Create new asset master records (including AUC to asset transfers).
- Update master data (e.g., location, custodian, useful life, depreciation method) with approvals.
- Govern asset classification and componentization (asset class, group, book assignments).
- Maintain depreciation parameters for all applicable books (corporate, local GAAP, tax).
- Link assets to source transactions (PO, invoice, WBS/Project, vendor).
- Assign and track asset tags (barcode/RFID) and physical attributes.
- Perform periodic data quality checks, reconciliations, and audits.
- Execute and govern mass changes (e.g., reorg, cost center reassignments).
- Manage data retention, archival, and audit trails.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Approved capitalization request or trigger (e.g., invoice > capitalization threshold, AUC ready-to-capitalize, acceptance certificate).
- Source documents: PO, GRN/receiving, vendor invoice, commissioning/acceptance docs, project/WBS details.
- Organizational reference data: chart of accounts, asset classes and account determination, depreciation keys and useful lives, cost centers, location hierarchy, legal entity/books, currency.
- Technical/spec data: serial/model number, manufacturer, warranty details, installation/commissioning info.
- Policy references: capitalization policy, componentization rules, useful life tables, revaluation/impairment policy, tax depreciation rules.

Prerequisites:
- Asset class dictionary and default templates configured in the FA subledger.
- Depreciation areas/books and methods configured and approved.
- Valid master data for cost centers, locations, legal entities, and account mappings.
- Access controls, workflow/approval paths, and maker-checker controls established.

Dependencies on other processes:
- Procure to Pay (for acquisition data).
- Project accounting/CapEx management (AUC and capitalization events).
- Perform asset transactions (transfers, impairments, revaluations, disposals).
- Period-end close (depreciation run, reconciliations).
- Conduct physical inventory of fixed assets.
- Master data governance for org structures (cost centers, locations).

## Process Steps
1) Intake and Triage
- Receive a create/update request via workflow or auto-trigger (e.g., invoice flagged as capital).
- Validate completeness: required docs, approvals, and policy compliance.
- Classify request type: new asset, AUC to asset, update, reclass, mass change.

2) Determine Asset Structure and Classification
- Identify asset class, sub-class, and grouping (e.g., machinery, IT equipment).
- Determine if componentization is required (major components with different useful lives).
- Determine asset ownership (legal entity), cost center, and responsible person.

3) Assign Accounting Attributes
- Select depreciation method/key, useful life, convention, and depreciation start date (in-service date).
- Assign depreciation areas/books (corporate IFRS/US GAAP and tax/local GAAP), including book-specific methods/lives.
- Confirm account determination (asset, accumulated depreciation, depreciation expense accounts).
- Set salvage/residual value if applicable; set revaluation/impairment flags per policy.

4) Link Source Transactions
- Link to PO, GRN, vendor invoice, and project/WBS for cost traceability.
- For AUC: verify capitalization criteria, final cost, and settlement rules.

5) Enter Technical and Operational Attributes
- Record asset description, model, serial number, manufacturer, warranty dates.
- Record asset location (site, building, room), installation details, and utilization metrics (if applicable).
- Assign asset tag ID; trigger physical tagging workflow (barcode/RFID).

6) Data Entry and Validation in FA Subledger
- Create the asset master using a standard template for the asset class.
- Populate mandatory fields; use dropdowns/lookups to enforce standards.
- System runs validations: mandatory fields present, life/method allowed for class, accounting mappings valid, duplicate checks (serial, PO/invoice).

7) Approval (Maker-Checker)
- Submit for approval per thresholds (finance supervisor/asset accounting manager; tax review for book settings where required).
- Resolve exceptions; update request if changes required.

8) Activate Asset Master
- On approval, set status Active; for AUC, execute settlement/capitalization to the new asset.
- Effective-date any changes to avoid retroactive discrepancies unless approved.

9) Communicate and Tag
- Notify requestor, asset custodian, Facilities/IT, and AP/Procurement as needed.
- Issue or confirm physical tag attachment; update system with tag status and date.

10) Integration and Reporting
- Ensure integration to GL, EAM/CMMS, and inventory/asset tracking tools.
- Generate daily/weekly extracts for downstream systems and analytics.

11) Ongoing Maintenance
- Process updates: location transfers, custodian changes, reclassifications, useful life changes, impairment indicators, status updates (active, held-for-sale, retired).
- Each update follows intake-validation-approval-activation with audit trails.

12) Periodic Controls and Housekeeping
- Run data quality checks (missing/invalid fields, duplicates, inactive org links).
- Reconcile subledger to GL; address exceptions.
- Support physical inventory reconciliation; update master to reflect findings.
- Execute mass changes with controlled tooling and approvals.
- Archive/retire master records per retention policy post-disposal.

Exception Handling
- Incomplete requests: reject with reasons and checklist.
- Conflicting accounting settings: escalate to Asset Accounting Manager/Policy.
- Retroactive change requests affecting closed periods: finance controller approval and corrective postings.
- System validation failures: route to Master Data Analyst for remediation.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Approved and activated fixed-asset master records with complete attributes.
- Updated change log/audit trail with timestamps, user IDs, and approvals.
- Assigned asset tag IDs and tagging confirmation.
- Integration updates to GL, EAM/CMMS, tax books, and reporting layers.
- Periodic data quality and exception reports; reconciliation sign-offs.

Success criteria:
- Accurate depreciation postings with zero master-data-related errors.
- 100% mandatory fields populated; approvals captured.
- SLA adherence for create/update cycle times.
- Clean subledger-to-GL reconciliation; no material audit findings.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Fixed Asset Accountant: Perform data entry, validation, and master maintenance; ensure accounting compliance; run data quality checks.
- Asset Accounting Manager: Approve creations/changes; oversee policy adherence; resolve exceptions; own KPIs.
- Master Data Analyst/MDG Specialist: Configure templates, validation rules; manage mass updates; maintain reference data.
- Procurement/AP: Provide source documents and triggers; ensure PO/invoice linkages and capitalization indicators.
- Project Accountant: Provide AUC settlement details; confirm readiness-to-capitalize and componentization.
- Facilities/IT/Operations (Asset Custodian): Provide technical/spec/location info; ensure physical tagging and move notifications.
- Tax Accountant: Review and approve tax book settings and useful lives; ensure compliance with tax rules.
- Internal Audit/Compliance: Periodic control testing; review audit trails; SOX/ICFR compliance.
- System Administrator (ERP/FA Subledger): Maintain system configurations, roles, and access controls; support integrations.
- Data Owner/Steward (Finance): Define data standards; govern data quality and lifecycle; chair data governance meetings.

## Best Practices
- Standardized templates per asset class with default depreciation settings and account mappings.
- Maker-checker workflow with risk-based approval thresholds.
- Mandatory effective dating; avoid back-dated changes without controller approval.
- Strong validation rules and dropdowns to prevent free-text inconsistencies.
- Componentization for complex assets to reflect different useful lives and maintenance.
- Automated creation from POs above capitalization thresholds with pre-populated fields.
- Tight integration with AUC/project systems for seamless capitalization.
- Physical tagging at or before in-service date; reconcile tag status monthly.
- Periodic (quarterly) data quality scorecards and targeted cleansing.
- Maintain separate books for corporate and tax; synchronize where policy allows; document differences.
- Robust audit trail and attachment of source documents to the asset master.
- Role-based access control and SoD to prevent unauthorized changes.
- Change freeze windows around period-end close; urgent changes via controlled break-glass process.
- Training and reference guides for requestors and custodians to improve data completeness.

## Common Challenges
- Incomplete or inaccurate source data leading to misclassification or wrong depreciation settings.
  - Mitigation: Intake checklist, required attachments, auto-validation against templates.
- Duplicate assets due to multiple requests or split invoices.
  - Mitigation: Duplicate checks on serial/PO/invoice; consolidation rules.
- Out-of-date location/custodian data after moves.
  - Mitigation: Integration with Facilities/IT move tickets; periodic custodian attestation.
- Misaligned corporate and tax books causing reconciliation issues.
  - Mitigation: Tax review workflow; controlled divergence with documented rationale.
- AUC lingering due to delays in capitalization.
  - Mitigation: Automated AUC aging report with escalation; project closeout checklist.
- Retroactive changes impacting closed periods and depreciation.
  - Mitigation: Require controller approval and automated catch-up postings.
- Large-scale org changes (reorgs, M&A) causing mass update risk.

Process Details:
## Overview
Process [9.3.3.3] Process and record fixed-asset additions and retires governs how an organization recognizes, validates, records, and reports new fixed assets and the retirement or disposal of existing ones. It ensures that asset acquisitions are capitalized correctly, depreciation begins and ends at the right time, and disposals (sales, scrapping, donations, trade-ins, intercompany transfers) are recorded accurately with appropriate gain/loss recognition. The process underpins financial statement accuracy (balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement), supports auditability, compliance with GAAP/IFRS/local statutory and tax rules, and provides complete and current asset registers for operational use (maintenance, insurance, risk, and capacity planning).

This process sits within Perform fixed-asset accounting and is tightly integrated with Procurement-to-Pay, Capital Projects/Construction in Progress (CIP), Accounts Payable, General Ledger, and Record-to-Report close activities.

## Key Activities
- Intake and validation of asset additions
  - Capture acquisition sources: PO/invoice, internally constructed assets (CIP), business combinations, donations, finance leases/ROU, trade-ins.
  - Validate against capitalization policy and thresholds; expense non-qualifying costs.
  - Componentization and cost allocation (equipment, installation, freight, taxes, ARO).
  - Create/maintain asset master data (class, location, custodian, cost center, useful life, depreciation method).
  - Assign asset IDs and physical tags; attach supporting documentation.
  - Place assets in service and start depreciation per convention.

- Processing CIP to asset capitalization
  - Accumulate costs, review readiness for intended use, approve capitalization, settle CIP into asset records.

- Processing asset retirements/disposals
  - Initiate disposal requests (sale, scrap, donation, theft/loss, abandonment, trade-in, intercompany transfer).
  - Approvals, compliance checks (IT data sanitization, environmental/HAZMAT, export controls).
  - Update depreciation to disposal date.
  - Record proceeds and taxes, derecognize asset and accumulated depreciation, compute gain/loss.
  - Partial disposals and component retirements.

- Intercompany and intra-entity transfers
  - Retire from sending entity and add in receiving entity at appropriate basis; ensure tax/transfer pricing compliance.

- Controls, reconciliations, and reporting
  - Maintain audit trail, support SOX/ICFR controls.
  - Reconcile fixed asset subledger to GL; prepare rollforwards and disclosure support.
  - Periodic physical verification and tag audits.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs
  - Approved capitalization policy and accounting manual (thresholds, useful lives, depreciation methods/conventions, componentization).
  - Source documents: approved PO, vendor invoice, goods receipt, AFE/project authorization, project cost reports, commissioning certificates, bill of sale, sales invoice, payment receipt, disposal request form, approvals, quotes/appraisals for fair value, tax documentation, environmental/data destruction certificates.
  - Master data: asset classes, depreciation keys, useful life tables, locations, cost centers, custodians, GL accounts, tax codes, exchange rates.
  - Prior period reconciliations and open accounting periods.

- Prerequisites
  - Fixed asset module configured with corporate/statutory/tax books.
  - Segregation of duties and approval workflows established.
  - Integration with AP, Procurement, Projects/CIP, and GL is operational.
  - Asset tagging capability and inventory procedures defined.
  - Training and access for process participants; documented roles and authorities.

- Dependencies on other processes
  - Procure-to-Pay (invoice matching and posting).
  - Project accounting/CIP management for internally constructed assets.
  - Lease accounting for ROU assets if in scope.
  - General accounting and period close for posting windows and reconciliations.
  - Tax management (indirect and fixed asset tax books).
  - IT asset management/EAM for physical control and maintenance linkage.

## Process Steps
A. Additions (Purchased, Constructed, or Otherwise Acquired)
1) Trigger and intake
   - Event: vendor invoice matched to PO/receipt; project milestone reached; business combination close; donation; trade-in; lease commencement; ARO recognized.
   - Create asset candidate in FA module via integration or manual request.

2) Validate capitalization eligibility
   - Review against policy: threshold, asset type, useful life > 1 year, directly attributable costs (purchase price net of discounts, freight, installation, testing, professional fees, non-refundable taxes, capitalized interest, ARO).
   - Expense non-qualifying costs (training, initial operating losses, general admin).

3) Create/complete asset master
   - Assign asset number/ID, class/group, book(s), location, custodian, project/AFE, cost center, and parent/child component structure if applicable.
   - Set depreciation method and useful life per asset class policy; set convention (e.g., half-month, mid-quarter).
   - Determine in-service date (ready for intended use); attach documentation.

4) Allocate and post costs
   - Aggregate costs: base price, freight, installation, taxes, ARO asset, less rebates.
   - Split costs across components where required (e.g., equipment vs. major parts).
   - Post capitalization entry:
     - DR Fixed Asset (by component)
     - CR GR/IR or Accounts Payable (if posting from invoice)
     - For CIP: DR Fixed Asset, CR CIP
     - For ARO: DR Fixed Asset, CR ARO Liability

5) Tag and record physical details
   - Print/affix physical tag/barcode/RFID; update serial numbers and physical attributes.
   - Notify maintenance/EAM and insurance; update asset register.

6) Start depreciation
   - Confirm in-service date and convention; depreciation begins as per policy.
   - Validate depreciation preview and post monthly depreciation via depreciation process.

7) Special cases
   - Self-constructed assets: review commissioning documentation; settle CIP to asset upon readiness.
   - Business combinations: record at fair value; align lives/methods post-PPA.
   - Foreign currency: translate at acquisition date rate; track in local/functional currency.
   - Leasehold improvements: set useful life as shorter of lease term or economic life.

B. Retirements/Disposals
1) Initiate request
   - Custodian submits disposal request specifying reason (sale, scrap, donation, theft/loss, trade-in, intercompany transfer) with supporting documents (approval, appraisals, quotes, buyer details).

2) Approvals and compliance checks
   - Obtain approvals per authority matrix; ensure data sanitization (IT assets), environmental compliance, export controls, and insurance notifications.

3) Update depreciation and net book value
   - Run catch-up depreciation to disposal date if required by convention.
   - Confirm cost and accumulated depreciation; compute net book value (NBV).

4) Determine proceeds and taxes
   - Capture sales proceeds, trade-in credits, or zero for scrap/donation.
   - Determine indirect taxes (VAT/GST/sales tax), withholding, and fees.

5) Post disposal entries
   - Sale:
     - DR Cash/AR (gross proceeds)
     - DR Accumulated Depreciation
     - CR Fixed Asset (cost)
     - CR Output Tax Payable (if applicable)
     - DR/CR Gain or Loss on Disposal (plug to balance)
   - Scrap/Write-off:
     - DR Accumulated Depreciation
     - DR Loss on Disposal (NBV)
     - CR Fixed Asset (cost)
   - Donation:
     - Same as scrap; additionally record non-cash contribution disclosures if required.
   - Trade-in:
     - Record disposal as above; apply trade-in credit to new asset acquisition per policy.

6) Partial disposals/component retirements
   - Identify component’s cost and accumulated depreciation; adjust remaining asset accordingly.
   - Post partial retirement and update lives for remaining components.

7) Intercompany/intra-entity transfers
   - Retire from sending entity (at NBV; no gain/loss if policy prohibits) and add to receiving entity at transfer price per policy/transfer pricing; align useful life and depreciation.

8) Close and update registers
   - Remove/retire asset in register; remove physical tag; update EAM/CMMS and insurance.
   - Archive documents; mark for next physical inventory exclusions.

C. Period-end activities (related)
- Review and clear “asset clearing”/suspense accounts.
- CIP aging review; capitalize eligible items; investigate aged CIP.
- Prepare fixed asset rollforward and subledger-to-GL reconciliation.
- Review disposals and gains/losses for reasonableness and disclosure.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Updated fixed asset master records and register with complete metadata and attachments.
- Posted journal entries for capitalizations, transfers, and disposals across all relevant books (corporate/statutory/tax).
- Depreciation schedules reflecting in-service dates and conventions.
- Disposal documentation, gain/loss calculations, and tax records.
- Fixed asset rollforwards, subledger-to-GL reconciliation, and audit trail.
- Physical tags issued/retired; updated insurance and maintenance records.

- Success criteria
  - 100% of qualifying costs capitalized correctly within SLA from trigger event.
  - Depreciation starts/stops on time with zero material errors.
  - All disposals recorded in the correct period with documented approvals and accurate gain/loss.
  - Subledger reconciles to GL with no unexplained variances.
  - No aged items in asset clearing/CIP beyond thresholds without documented rationale.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Asset Accountant
  - Create/validate asset records; post capitalization, depreciation, and disposal entries; maintain asset register; reconcile subledger to GL.
- Accounts Payable Specialist
  - Process invoices; ensure correct coding to asset/CIP; resolve PO/receipt mismatches.
- Project/Capital Accountant
  - Track CIP; assess readiness; settle projects to assets; componentize assets.
- Fixed Asset Manager/Controller
  - Own policy; approve unusual transactions; oversee controls and close; review KPIs.
- Asset Custodian/Department Manager
  - Initiate additions/disposals; confirm physical existence and in-service status; safeguard assets.
- Procurement
  - Ensure PO data integrity; capture asset indicators in POs; coordinate delivery documentation.
- Tax Specialist
  - Maintain tax books; advise on indirect tax on disposals; manage bonus/accelerated depreciation rules.
- IT/Facilities/Maintenance
  - Tag assets; confirm commissioning; perform decommissioning and data sanitization.
- Internal Audit/Compliance
  - Test controls; review documentation and adherence to policy.
- Treasury/AR
  - Manage cash receipts for asset sales; customer setup when selling to third parties.

## Best Practices
- Maintain a clear, approved capitalization policy with examples and decision trees.
- Use standardized asset classes with preset useful lives, methods, and accounting rules.
- Automate asset creation from AP/PO and projects to reduce manual entry and errors.
- Implement componentization for complex assets; avoid over-aggregation.
- Run multiple books (corporate/statutory/tax) with automated book-specific rules.
- Enforce in-service date controls; require commissioning documentation to start depreciation.
- Regularly review CIP aging; set thresholds (e.g., investigation >90 days).
- Physically tag assets on receipt and perform periodic cycle counts/spot checks.
- Use barcode/RFID and EAM integration to reconcile physical and financial records.
- Establish robust disposal workflow with approvals and compliance checklists.
- Monitor and clear asset clearing/suspense accounts during month-end.
- Maintain complete document packages linked to asset records for audit readiness.
- Address ARO and dismantling costs at inception; integrate with environmental teams.
- Provide training and RACI clarity; enforce segregation of duties.

## Common Challenges
- Misclassification of expenses vs. capitalizable costs
  - Solution: decision matrix, AP coding validations, periodic review by Asset Accounting.
- Delayed capitalization or incorrect in-service dates
  - Solution: commissioning checklists, automated alerts for long-dated CIP, mandatory fields.
- Incorrect useful lives or methods
  - Solution: controlled master data, limited override rights, periodic benchmarking.
- Orphan costs in clearing/CIP
  - Solution: GL controls, ownership assignment, monthly exception reporting.
- Partial disposals and component tracking complexity
  - Solution: componentized structure, clear guidance, system capability for partial retirements.
- Intercompany transfers mishandled (gains/losses, tax)
  - Solution: standardized intercompany procedures and pricing policies; automated transfer functionality.
- Foreign currency acquisition/disposal impacts
  - Solution: system-driven FX handling; disclosures and remeasurement policies.
- Compliance gaps (data destruction, environmental, export controls)
  - Solution: disposal checklist; hold posting until certifications received.
- Differences between corporate, statutory, and tax rules
  - Solution: multi-book configuration; reconciliations and exception logs.

## Performance Metrics
- Cycle time to capitalize (trigger to in-service posting), target: X business days.
- Percentage of assets tagged within Y days of receipt/in-service.
- CIP aging: percent and value >90 days without action.
- Number and value of post-close adjustments to fixed assets.
- Depreciation accuracy: error rate and dollar impact per period.
- Disposal processing time (request to posting) and documentation completeness.
- Subledger-to-GL reconciliation variance (count and value) at month-end.
- Percentage of orphan/clearing account items resolved within SLA.
- Audit findings related to fixed assets (count, severity).
- Ratio of capitalized cost to total project cost by class (benchmarking).

## Technology and Tools
- ERP fixed asset modules: SAP FI-AA, Oracle Fusion/Cloud Fixed Assets, Microsoft Dynamics 365, NetSuite Fixed Assets, Workday, Sage Intacct.
- Project accounting/CIP: Oracle Projects, SAP PS, Primavera, MS Project integrations.
- AP automation and P2P: Coupa, SAP Ariba, Basware; three-way match integration to asset creation.
- EAM/CMMS and ITAM: SAP PM, IBM Maximo, Infor EAM, ServiceNow for physical lifecycle linkage.
- Barcode/RFID tagging and mobile inventory apps.
- Tax engines: Vertex, Avalara for indirect taxes; fixed asset tax books within ERP.
- Document management and workflow: OpenText, SharePoint, DocuSign for approvals and attachments.
- RPA/Integration: bots to create assets from invoices, settle CIP, and post disposals; iPaaS for data sync.
- BI/Analytics: Power BI, Tableau, ERP analytics for rollforwards, aging, KPIs.
- Controls/Compliance: GRC tools for SOX testing, access controls, and change management.

Process Details:
## Overview
Develop capital investment policies and procedures defines the governance, rules, standards, and workflows that determine how an organization evaluates, approves, funds, monitors, capitalizes, and reviews capital projects (fixed-asset and capitalizable intangible projects). This process establishes a consistent, compliant, and transparent framework for capital allocation aligned to corporate strategy, risk appetite, and financial reporting requirements (IFRS/US GAAP). It underpins the integrity of the broader capital planning and project approval process, enabling disciplined decision-making, comparability across proposals, and effective post-investment accountability.

Primary objectives:
- Align capital allocation to strategic priorities and portfolio constraints.
- Ensure financial rigor (e.g., NPV/IRR, hurdle rates, risk adjustments) and compliance with accounting, tax, and regulatory standards.
- Define clear decision rights, stage-gates, documentation, and evidence required at each phase.
- Standardize capitalization criteria, depreciation, interest capitalization, commissioning, and asset settlement.
- Reduce cycle time and variability in approvals while maintaining robust controls and auditability.
- Support benefits realization tracking and continuous improvement via post-investment reviews.

Scope:
- All capital projects (tangible and qualifying intangible) including construction, facilities, manufacturing, utilities, IT infrastructure, internal-use software development, and select digital transformation initiatives meeting capitalization criteria.
- Excludes routine operating expenses and non-capitalizable SaaS subscriptions and similar arrangements unless specific components meet capitalization criteria.

## Key Activities
- Define policy scope, applicability, and governance model.
- Establish capital definitions and classification rules (CAPEX vs OPEX; tangible vs intangible).
- Set financial evaluation standards (valuation methods, discount rates, hurdle rates).
- Specify stage-gate model, approval thresholds, and Delegation of Authority (DoA).
- Define documentation templates and evidentiary requirements (business case, AFE).
- Determine capitalization criteria, componentization, useful life, and depreciation methods.
- Define interest capitalization and overhead capitalization rules.
- Set change control, reforecasting, and variance management guidelines.
- Define commissioning, asset tagging, project-to-asset settlement, and in-service recognition.
- Establish impairment indicators and write-off procedures.
- Define post-investment review and benefits realization process.
- Integrate controls, segregation of duties, and audit requirements.
- Configure enabling systems and data standards in ERP/PPM/EAM.
- Train stakeholders and implement policy governance (versioning, review cadence).

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Corporate strategy and long-range plan; risk appetite statement.
- Existing financial policies (DoA, procurement, travel/expense, accounting manual).
- Applicable accounting and tax frameworks:
  - IFRS (IAS 16 Property, Plant and Equipment; IAS 23 Borrowing Costs; IAS 36 Impairment; IAS 38 Intangible Assets).
  - US GAAP (ASC 360 Property, Plant, and Equipment; ASC 835-20 Interest; ASC 350-40 Internal-Use Software; other relevant guidance).
  - Local tax depreciation rules and incentives.
- Treasury-provided cost of capital (WACC), capital structure, and currency assumptions.
- Historical project performance data and benchmarks.
- Risk management policies (ERM), ESG commitments, and regulatory/permit requirements.
- Current state process maps, templates, and system configurations.

Prerequisites:
- Approved CAPEX budget envelope and portfolio targets from FP&A.
- Defined chart of accounts, asset classes, useful life policy baseline.
- Access to ERP/PPM/EAM and document management platforms.
- Named governance bodies (e.g., Capital Review Board/Investment Committee).

Dependencies on other processes:
- 9.4.1 Perform capital planning and project approval (this policy governs that process).
- Manage FP&A (strategic planning, budgeting, performance management).
- General accounting and reporting (asset accounting, depreciation, close).
- Procurement and vendor management (sourcing, contract terms impacting capitalization).
- Risk and compliance (SOX/ICFR, internal audit).
- Project management (stage-gate execution, scheduling, cost control).

## Process Steps
1. Initiate policy development program
   - Appoint policy owner (Controller/Chief Accounting Officer) and sponsor (CFO).
   - Establish cross-functional working group (Accounting, FP&A, Treasury, Tax, PMO, Procurement, Legal, EHS/ESG, IT, Operations, Internal Audit).
   - Define objectives, scope, timeline, and change management plan.

2. Assess current state and requirements
   - Map current capital processes, approvals, system workflows, and controls.
   - Identify pain points (cycle time, misclassification, audit findings).
   - Gather regulatory, accounting, tax, ESG, and industry requirements relevant to capital projects.

3. Define governance and decision rights
   - Create RACI for investment lifecycle.
   - Establish Capital Review Board (CRB)/Investment Committee composition and quorum.
   - Codify Delegation of Authority: monetary thresholds, project risk tiers, emergency approvals, and exceptions handling.
   - Define conflict-of-interest and independence requirements for reviewers.

4. Establish capital definitions and classification rules
   - Define what qualifies as CAPEX vs OPEX, including:
     - Tangible assets (PPE).
     - Intangible assets (internal-use software, licenses) with criteria under IAS 38/ASC 350-40.
     - Cloud/SaaS implementation: expense vs capitalizable configuration/customization (jurisdiction-specific guidance).
   - Specify minimum capitalization thresholds, unit of account, and componentization rules.
   - Set rules for asset betterments vs repairs and maintenance.

5. Set financial evaluation standards
   - Standardize valuation methods: NPV, IRR, payback, MIRR, and strategic/real-options where relevant.
   - Define discount rate methodology (WACC, risk-adjusted/hurdle rates by category and geography).
   - Require scenario and sensitivity analyses (cost, schedule, demand, FX, carbon price).
   - Define inflation/FX, tax, and residual value assumptions and sources.
   - Establish non-financial criteria scoring (safety, compliance, ESG, capacity, strategic fit).

6. Define stage-gate model and documentation
   - Gate 0: Concept/Intake; Gate 1: Feasibility; Gate 2: Definition/AFE; Gate 3: Execution; Gate 4: Commissioning/Handover; Gate 5: Post-Investment Review.
   - For each gate, specify entry/exit criteria, required documents (business case, AFE, feasibility studies, risk register, permits, environmental impact assessments), and approvals.
   - Provide standardized templates and guidance.

7. Approval workflow and controls
   - Design end-to-end workflow in systems (PPM/ERP) with e-signatures and audit trails.
   - Enforce SoD: project sponsor vs financial approver vs procurement.
   - Set SLA targets for review and escalation paths for delays.

8. Accounting and capitalization policies
   - Capitalization start/stop rules; determining asset ready-for-use/placed-in-service date.
   - Borrowing cost capitalization (IAS 23/ASC 835-20).
   - Overhead capitalization methodology and rate approvals.
   - Useful lives, depreciation methods, salvage values, and review cadence.
   - Asset tagging, commissioning documentation, and project-to-asset settlement procedures.
   - Work-in-progress (CIP) management and WIP aging thresholds.

9. Change control and reforecasting
   - Define what constitutes a change (scope/cost/schedule), thresholds, approval routes.
   - Require updated business case and benefits adjustments for major changes.
   - Establish monthly/quarterly reforecast cadence and reporting.

10. Compliance, impairment, and write-offs
   - Impairment indicators and testing triggers (IAS 36/ASC 360) during project and post-capitalization.
   - Abandonment/write-off procedures and approvals.
   - Environmental and permitting compliance checkpoints.

11. Benefits realization and post-investment review (PIR)
   - Define benefits owners, baseline, measurement methods, and timing.
   - Require PIR within set period after in-service (e.g., 6–18 months) and at steady state.
   - Capture lessons learned and feed continuous improvement.

12. Data, systems, and integration design
   - Define master data standards (project IDs, asset classes, locations, components).
   - Configure ERP/PPM/EAM for gating, approvals, asset settlement, depreciation.
   - Integrate with procurement, contract lifecycle, and document management.

13. Draft policy and procedures documentation
   - Produce policy document, procedures manual, job aids, and quick-reference guides.
   - Include glossary, examples, and decision trees for classification.

14. Review, approval, and publication
   - Stakeholder review; legal and audit validation.
   - Approval by CFO and CRB; publish to policy portal.
   - Establish version control and effective date.

15. Training and rollout
   - Role-based training for sponsors, project managers, accountants, approvers.
   - Track acknowledgements and competency assessments.
   - Provide helpdesk/SME support model.

16. Monitor, audit, and improve
   - Define KPIs and dashboards; track compliance and exceptions.
   - Conduct internal audits and remediation plans.
   - Annual policy review; ad hoc updates for regulatory or strategic changes.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Capital Investment Policy document (approved and published).
- Procedures manual with step-by-step processes and controls.
- Delegation of Authority and approval matrix.
- Stage-gate framework and standardized templates (business case, AFE, PIR, change request).
- Accounting policy addendum (capitalization, depreciation, impairment, interest).
- System configurations and workflow designs (ERP/PPM/EAM).
- Training materials, FAQs, and quick-reference guides.
- RACI/role definitions and governance charter for CRB.
- Compliance checklist and internal control catalogue.

Success criteria:
- Policy adoption across all business units; high training completion and acknowledgement.
- Measurable reduction in approval cycle times with maintained control effectiveness.
- High compliance rate and clean audit results (no material findings).
- Improved forecast accuracy and benefits realization against business cases.
- Reduction in capex misclassification and WIP aging issues.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- CFO (Sponsor): Approves policy, sets capital allocation strategy and hurdle rates.
- Controller/Chief Accounting Officer (Owner): Authors policy; ensures accounting compliance; oversees capitalization, depreciation, impairment guidance.
- Head of FP&A: Aligns with budgeting/portfolio; defines evaluation assumptions; runs portfolio analytics.
- Treasury: Provides WACC/discount rates; funding strategy; FX and interest assumptions.
- Tax: Reviews tax depreciation and incentives; ensures tax reporting alignment.
- PMO Director: Implements stage-gate; ensures project governance and documentation compliance.
- Capital Review Board/Investment Committee: Reviews and approves projects per thresholds; ensures strategic fit and risk oversight.
- Business Unit Sponsors: Own business cases, benefits, and project delivery accountability.
- Procurement: Ensures sourcing/contract terms support capitalization; integrates with approval gates.
- Legal/Compliance/EHS-ESG: Reviews regulatory, contractual, environmental, and ESG compliance.
- IT/Enterprise Architecture: Applies software capitalization rules; validates IT project lifecycle controls.
- Fixed Asset Accounting Team: Manages CIP, settlement, asset master data, depreciation setup.
- Internal Audit: Tests control design and operating effectiveness; advises on remediation.
- Policy Administration/Training: Manages publication, versioning, and training program.

## Best Practices
- Use a formal stage-gate model with clearly defined entry/exit criteria and templates.
- Standardize valuation with consistent assumptions; publish hurdle rates and discount rate policy.
- Require sensitivity and scenario analysis, including downside cases and carbon pricing where relevant.
- Separate strategic justification from financial metrics to avoid bias; include independent review by Finance.
- Define clear CAPEX/OPEX decision trees and examples; minimize exceptions and document all.
- Maintain a portfolio view to optimize capital rationing and risk diversification.
- Enforce change control and periodic reforecasting; tie funding releases to gate approvals.
- Integrate policy into ERP/PPM workflows with e-signatures and audit trails; no “shadow” approvals.
- Establish robust master data and asset componentization to enable accurate depreciation and maintenance.
- Mandate post-investment reviews and capture lessons learned; feed back into assumptions libraries.
- Refresh policy at least annually or when standards change (IFRS/US GAAP, tax laws).
- Provide role-based training and certification; keep a searchable policy portal.

## Common Challenges
- CAPEX vs OPEX misclassification, especially for IT/cloud projects.
  - Solution: Decision trees, examples, mandatory Finance review for borderline cases.
- Optimism bias in business cases; underestimated risk.
  - Solution: Independent challenge by FP&A; standard risk adjustments; required sensitivity analysis.
- Protracted approval cycle times.
  - Solution: Clear thresholds, SLAs, pre-reads, and digital workflows with escalation.
- Scope creep and uncontrolled changes.
  - Solution: Formal change control with thresholds and updated business case requirements.
- WIP aging and delays in capitalization.
  - Solution: Monthly CIP reviews; commissioning checklists; automate project-to-asset settlement.
- Inconsistent discount rates and assumptions across BUs.
  - Solution: Central publishing of rates and assumptions; enforce use via templates/system.
- Weak benefits realization discipline.
  - Solution: Assign benefits owners; set PIR schedule; track benefits KPIs in dashboards.
- Audit findings due to weak controls or documentation.
  - Solution: SoD, mandatory artifacts per gate, system-enforced approvals, periodic internal audits.

## Performance Metrics
- Policy compliance rate (% projects meeting documentation and gate requirements).
- Approval cycle time (submission to decision) by threshold tier.
- Exception rate (% approvals via exception) and average time to resolve exceptions.
- Forecast accuracy (variance of actual vs approved budget at completion).
- Benefits realization rate (% of planned benefits achieved at PIR).
- Misclassification error rate (CAPEX/OPEX reclassifications).
- WIP aging distribution and average days to capitalize after ready-for-use.
- Audit outcomes (number/severity of control deficiencies).
- Change order frequency and cost impact as % of project value.
- Training coverage and assessment scores for key roles.
- Post-investment review completion rate within required timeframe.

## Technology and Tools
- ERP and Fixed Asset Accounting: SAP S/4HANA (FI-AA), Oracle Cloud ERP, Microsoft Dynamics 365.
- Project and Portfolio Management: SAP PS/PPM, Oracle Project Portfolio Management, Planview, Clarity, Microsoft Project Online.
- Enterprise Asset Management/CMMS: IBM Maximo, SAP EAM, Infor EAM.
- Corporate Performance Management/Planning: Anaplan, Workday Adaptive Planning, Oracle EPM Cloud.
- Workflow and Policy Management: ServiceNow, Nintex/K2, Microsoft Power Automate, ConvergePoint, PowerDMS.
- Document Management and e-Signature: SharePoint/Teams, OpenText, DocuSign, Adobe Sign.
- Analytics and Reporting: Power BI, Tableau, Qlik; dashboards for KPIs and PIRs.
- Valuation/risk tools: Standardized Excel models with governance; @Risk, Palisade for Monte Carlo where appropriate.
- Procurement/CLM: SAP Ariba, Coupa, Ivalua, DocuSign CLM; integration to ensure contract terms align with capitalization.
- Asset tagging and commissioning: Mobile apps, RFID/barcode solutions integrated with EAM.
- GRC/Internal Controls: AuditBoard, SAP GRC, Oracle Risk Management Cloud for ICFR/SOX compliance.
