Process Details:
# [9.6.2.2] Capture and report relevant tax data

## Overview
This process captures, validates, classifies, and reports all tax-relevant information associated with employee expense reimbursements. It ensures that indirect taxes (e.g., VAT/GST), use tax/self-assessed tax, and taxable benefits/benefit-in-kind (BIK)/fringe benefit tax (FBT) exposures are correctly identified and recorded. It also creates the datasets and journal entries required for indirect tax filings, payroll tax reporting (for imputed income), and financial statement accuracy.

Purpose and role:
- Enable legal and compliant recovery of eligible input taxes (VAT/GST) on employee-incurred expenses.
- Prevent tax leakage by correctly flagging non-recoverable tax and applying use tax/reverse charge where necessary.
- Identify and report taxable benefits to payroll or statutory authorities (e.g., UK P11D, AU FBT, local BIK regimes).
- Support accurate general ledger postings and audit-ready documentation for tax authorities.
- Provide timely, complete tax data to the Indirect Tax and Payroll Tax functions for statutory filings.

Scope includes expenses paid via corporate cards and out-of-pocket reimbursements, across all relevant jurisdictions where the organization has tax obligations.

## Key Activities
- Configure tax master data and rules:
  - Tax codes, rates, jurisdictions, place-of-supply rules, recovery restrictions, FBT/BIK categories, per-diem thresholds.
- Capture tax data at source:
  - Extract receipt/invoice details via OCR/IDP; ingest corporate card Level 2/3 data; enrich with merchant tax info.
- Validate tax document compliance:
  - Check invoice requirements (supplier legal name, tax ID, invoice number/date, VAT/GST rate/amount, buyer details where required).
- Determine tax treatment:
  - Map expense line to tax code and jurisdiction; determine recoverability (full/partial/blocked); apply use tax or reverse charge as needed.
- Identify taxable benefits:
  - Flag personal or mixed-use items; compute imputed income/BIK; route to payroll for withholding/reporting.
- Currency and jurisdiction processing:
  - Convert currencies at applicable tax dates; assign local reporting currency; map to correct tax registration.
- Post accounting:
  - Record input tax receivable, non-deductible tax to expense, use tax payable/accruals; credit employee/corporate card clearing.
- Aggregate and report:
  - Build VAT/GST return datasets by registration; compile FBT/BIK registers; produce exception and audit logs; interface to tax return systems.
- Exception handling and remediation:
  - Resolve missing or non-compliant invoices; request resubmission; reclassify as non-recoverable if unresolved.
- Record retention:
  - Store digitized receipts with metadata; maintain audit trail and evidence for statutory retention periods.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs:
  - Approved expense reports and line-item details.
  - Digitized receipts/invoices (PDF, image) and/or e-receipts; corporate card transaction data.
  - Employee master data (home/work location, entity, cost center); project/cost object info.
  - Tax master data (tax codes, rates, jurisdictions), exchange rates, fiscal calendars.
  - Expense policy mapping (categories to tax codes, BIK/FBT rules).
- Prerequisites:
  - Expense report verification completed (authenticity, business purpose, policy compliance).
  - Configured T&E system with tax rules or connected tax engine.
  - Data privacy controls for handling employee tax-related data.
- Dependencies on other processes:
  - [9.6.2.1] Receive and verify expense reports.
  - Indirect tax management and filings (e.g., VAT/GST return preparation).
  - Payroll processing for taxable benefits/imputed income.
  - Master data management (tax codes, chart of accounts, legal entities, registrations).
  - Corporate card program management and data feed integrity.

## Process Steps
1. Trigger and data ingestion
   - Receive an expense report that has passed basic verification/approval.
   - Ingest line items, receipts, corporate card data into the T&E/tax determination engine.

2. Extract and normalize tax-relevant data
   - Use OCR/IDP to capture supplier name, tax ID (e.g., VAT/GST), invoice number/date, line net/tax/total, tax rate, merchant address/ISO country.
   - Normalize merchant category code (MCC), expense category, location, and currency.

3. Determine tax jurisdiction and place of supply
   - Resolve jurisdiction based on merchant location, employee/entity registration, and place-of-supply rules (e.g., services vs goods, event location).
   - Assign the correct legal entity and tax registration number (per country/state/province where applicable).

4. Validate invoice compliance for tax recovery
   - Check mandatory fields per jurisdiction (e.g., buyer name/address/tax ID thresholds).
   - Validate that VAT/GST rate aligns with category and timing; confirm invoice authenticity where feasible.
   - Decision:
     - If compliant: mark reclaimable (subject to recovery rules).
     - If non-compliant: route to exception queue to request corrected invoice; provisionally classify tax as non-recoverable.

5. Determine tax treatment and recoverability
   - Map expense category to tax code and recovery percentage (e.g., 100% for hotel lodging in some countries, 0% for entertainment where blocked).
   - Apply partial recovery rules (e.g., apportionment for mixed use; local restrictions like 50% meals in some jurisdictions).
   - Identify non-recoverable local consumption taxes (e.g., Canadian PST/QST in certain cases).

6. Apply use tax/reverse charge/self-assessment where applicable
   - For US out-of-state or untaxed purchases: compute use tax payable by jurisdiction.
   - For EU/UK cross-border services: apply reverse charge; record both input and output tax if required.
   - For missing VAT where seller should have charged tax: accrue self-assessed tax per local rules.

7. Identify taxable benefits/BIK/FBT
   - Flag expenses that create imputed income (e.g., commuting, personal elements, gifts exceeding thresholds, certain per-diems).
   - Compute taxable value per jurisdictional rules (e.g., UK P11D categories, AU FBT gross-up).
   - Create payroll interface records with employee ID, taxable amount, tax period, and category.

8. Currency conversion and dating
   - Convert foreign currency amounts to local reporting currency using tax-authority-approved exchange rate at tax point (invoice date or receipt date per local rules).
   - Ensure date alignment for tax period inclusion.

9. Post accounting entries
   - Debit expense net of recoverable tax; debit input VAT/GST receivable for recoverable amounts.
   - Debit expense for non-deductible tax; credit employee payable or corporate card clearing.
   - Credit tax payable accounts for use tax/reverse charge; book offsetting input tax where allowed.

10. Compile reporting datasets
   - Aggregate VAT/GST by return boxes and registrations; produce control reports (e.g., reconciliations to GL).
   - Build BIK/FBT registers per employee and category for payroll and statutory submissions.
   - Generate exception reports (non-compliant invoices, manual overrides, outliers).

11. Review, approvals, and corrections
   - Tax analyst reviews exceptions and high-risk items; approve overrides or request corrections.
   - Reprocess corrected items; update postings if reclassification occurs.

12. Period-end activities
   - Reconcile VAT/GST subledger to GL; resolve variances.
   - Provide VAT/GST return files (e.g., VAT return, BAS, SAF-T/JPK/MTD datasets) to Indirect Tax.
   - Provide BIK/FBT datasets to Payroll for inclusion in pay run/statutory returns.
   - Archive documents with metadata; ensure retention per jurisdiction.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Tax data outputs:
  - Line-level tax determination results (jurisdiction, tax code, rate, recoverable/non-recoverable split).
  - VAT/GST reclaim datasets by registration and return box.
  - Use tax/reverse charge accrual records.
  - BIK/FBT/imputed income files for payroll.
- Accounting deliverables:
  - Journal entries for input tax receivable, non-deductible tax, use tax liabilities, employee payables.
  - Reconciliations of tax subledger to GL.
- Compliance and audit artifacts:
  - Digitized, validated invoices/receipts with metadata.
  - Exception logs, approvals, and overrides.
- Success criteria:
  - Accurate and timely tax data supporting on-time filings.
  - Maximized eligible VAT/GST recovery; minimal disallowed claims.
  - Correct and timely payroll tax reporting for BIK/FBT.
  - Clean reconciliations and minimal audit findings.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Employee submitter:
  - Provide complete, legible receipts and accurate classifications; correct submissions when requested.
- Line manager/approver:
  - Validate business purpose and policy adherence; escalate anomalies.
- AP/Expense processor:
  - Monitor workflow, handle routine exceptions, ensure timely processing and postings.
- Indirect tax analyst/specialist:
  - Maintain tax rules and codes; review exceptions; approve recovery and self-assessment treatments; prepare/own VAT/GST returns.
- Payroll tax specialist:
  - Receive and process BIK/FBT datasets; ensure correct withholding/reporting; handle year-end statements (e.g., P11D).
- T&E system administrator:
  - Configure categories, validation rules, OCR/IDP integrations; maintain master data mappings.
- IT/ERP support:
  - Maintain interfaces between T&E, tax engine, ERP, payroll; ensure data integrity and security.
- Internal audit/compliance:
  - Perform periodic reviews; test controls; recommend improvements.
- External tax advisor (as needed):
  - Advise on complex or new jurisdictions; review treatments and documentation requirements.

## Best Practices
- Capture at source:
  - Enforce mandatory receipt fields and real-time validation; encourage mobile capture immediately after purchase.
- Automate tax determination:
  - Use a certified tax engine for multi-jurisdictional rules; integrate with T&E for real-time coding.
- Strengthen document quality:
  - Provide supplier guidance for compliant invoices; use e-receipts where available; leverage OCR with validation confidence thresholds.
- Standardize categories and mappings:
  - Maintain a simplified expense taxonomy mapped to tax codes and recovery rules; review quarterly.
- Apply risk-based controls:
  - Auto-approve low-risk items; route high-risk patterns (e.g., entertainment, foreign invoices) to tax review.
- Manage cross-border complexity:
  - Embed place-of-supply logic; automate reverse charge and use tax; maintain entity registration master.
- Tight payroll integration:
  - Define clear rules for taxable benefits; automate imputed income feed with audit trail.
- Monitor and improve:
  - Track reclaim rates, exception rates, and audit outcomes; perform root-cause analysis; enhance guidance/training.
- Compliance and retention:
  - Align retention with the strictest applicable jurisdiction; maintain immutable audit logs.
- Change governance:
  - Review tax rate/rule changes promptly; regression-test configurations before go-live.

## Common Challenges
- Non-compliant invoices limit VAT/GST recovery:
  - Solution: Educate employees and preferred suppliers; pre-check supplier data; use automated invoice compliance checks; obtain corrected invoices.
- Misclassification of expenses:
  - Solution: Simplify categories; default tax codes based on MCC and location; use machine learning suggestions with human-in-the-loop.
- Missing or incorrect tax rates:
  - Solution: Centralize tax rate management; implement effective-dated tax tables and automated updates.
- Cross-border and place-of-supply errors:
  - Solution: Implement jurisdiction resolution logic; maintain entity registrations; include event location fields in expense reports.
- Use tax and reverse charge omissions:
  - Solution: Automate detection and accruals; reconcile expected vs booked use tax; review out-of-state/foreign merchant activity.
- BIK/FBT underreporting:
  - Solution: Embed rules and thresholds; mandatory flags for personal elements; periodic sampling and payroll reconciliation.
- Multi-currency inaccuracies:
  - Solution: Use tax-authority-approved FX sources; lock tax point date for conversion; reconcile FX impacts.
- Data integration gaps:
  - Solution: Strengthen interfaces; implement completeness controls; alert on failed transmissions.
- Timeliness issues:
  - Solution: SLA-driven workflows; auto-reminders to employees; escalation for aging exceptions.

## Performance Metrics
- VAT/GST reclaim rate:
  - Reclaimed amount as % of eligible potential.
- Exception rate:
  - % of expense lines routed to exception queue; breakdown by root cause (missing invoice, non-compliant, miscode).
- On-time compliance:
  - % of periods with on-time provision of VAT/GST datasets and BIK/FBT feeds; days before filing deadline.
- Accuracy rate:
  - Post-filing adjustments as % of total tax; audit finding count/severity.
- Document compliance:
  - % of receipts meeting jurisdictional requirements; OCR extraction confidence rate.
- Use tax coverage:
  - % of eligible transactions with correct use tax accrual; variance between expected vs booked use tax.
- Cycle time:
  - Median time from expense approval to tax determination posting.
- Recovery leakage:
  - Non-recoverable tax due to documentation gaps as % of total tax on T&E.
- Payroll integration quality:
  - % of BIK/FBT records processed in correct pay period; exceptions per 1,000 employees.

## Technology and Tools
- T&E platforms:
  - SAP Concur, Oracle Expenses, Workday Expenses, Coupa Expenses, Navan, etc., with tax rule configuration.
- Indirect tax engines:
  - Vertex, Avalara, Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE, SAP DRC/S/4HANA tax service for automated determination and reporting.
- OCR/IDP and data capture:
  - Abbyy, Kofax, Azure Form Recognizer, Amazon Textract; mobile apps for receipt capture and e-receipts.
- ERP and finance systems:
  - SAP S/4HANA, Oracle Cloud ERP, Microsoft Dynamics; GL and subledger integration.
- Payroll systems:
  - Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM; interfaces for BIK/FBT and imputed income.
- BI and data warehouse:
  - Power BI, Tableau, Snowflake/BigQuery for monitoring KPIs and exception analytics.
- Compliance reporting:
  - VAT/GST return tools, MTD bridging (UK), SAF-T/JPK generators, AU BAS preparation modules.
- RPA and workflow:
  - UiPath, Automation Anywhere for exception handling, reminders, and data reconciliations.
- Master data and governance:
  - MDM tools for maintaining tax codes, jurisdictions, and entity registrations; policy rule repositories.

Note: Tax laws vary by jurisdiction. Align configurations and decisions with current local regulations and involve qualified tax advisors for complex or changing scenarios.

Process Details:
# [9.6.2.4] Process Reimbursements and Advances

## Overview
This process covers the execution of payments to employees for approved expense reimbursements and the issuance and settlement of cash advances. It translates approved expense and advance requests into accurate, timely payments, posts accounting entries, reconciles cash movements, manages exceptions, and ensures compliance with corporate policies, tax, and regulatory requirements. The process supports employee experience, cash management, and accurate financial reporting across legal entities and geographies.

Key objectives:
- Pay employees accurately and on time for approved business expenses.
- Issue and track advances, and settle them against submitted expense reports.
- Maintain strong internal controls to prevent duplicate or fraudulent payments.
- Record and reconcile financial transactions to the general ledger.
- Comply with local tax rules, data privacy, and audit requirements.

## Key Activities
- Intake of approved reimbursement and advance requests from the expense management system.
- Pre-payment validations (master data, banking info, employment status, duplicates, holds).
- Payment run preparation, approval, and execution (ACH/SEPA, wire, check, payroll off-cycle).
- Remittance communication to employees.
- Accounting postings and clearing (liabilities, advances, bank clearing).
- Bank reconciliation and exception handling (returns, rejects, stale checks).
- Advance settlement and recovery (offsets to expense reports or payroll deductions).
- Tax, compliance, and reporting (e.g., VAT/GST reclaim, taxable benefits where applicable).
- Period close activities (cut-off, open item review, accruals as needed).
- Record retention and audit support.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Approved expense reports and approved advance requests (from Approve reimbursements and advances [10882]).
- Employee/vendor master data with valid payment method, bank account/IBAN, currency, tax attributes, cost objects.
- Payment calendar, cut-off timelines, and pay group definitions by entity/currency.
- Bank master and connectivity details, approved payment formats (e.g., NACHA, ISO 20022 pain.001).
- Exchange rates for cross-currency transactions.
- Policy configuration (per diems, caps) and tax configuration (VAT/GST codes, accountable plan rules).
- Outstanding advances ledger per employee.

Prerequisites:
- Segregation of duties configured (request/approve vs. pay).
- Bank account validation process in place (e.g., prenotes, micro-deposits, third-party verification).
- Authorized signatory matrix and payment approval thresholds.
- Data privacy controls for PII (encryption at rest/in transit).
- Exception management workflows for returned or rejected payments.

Dependencies on other processes:
- [9.6.2.3] Approve reimbursements and advances (upstream approval).
- Master data management for employees and banking details.
- Treasury/cash management for funding and bank connectivity.
- General accounting for GL structure and period close.
- Payroll (for taxable benefit reporting or recovery via payroll).
- Tax management for VAT/GST reclaim and fringe benefit rules.

## Process Steps
1. Intake and queue
   - Receive approved reimbursement and advance items from the expense system into AP/T&E payables.
   - Stamp each item with due date, pay group, legal entity, currency, and payment method according to employee master data and policy.

2. Pre-payment validation
   - Validate employee/vendor master status (active, not on payment hold; employment status checked).
   - Verify banking details (format, checksum/IBAN, prenote status, account ownership if mandated).
   - Check for duplicates (same employee, amount, currency, date range, report ID) and policy violations escalated from prior steps.
   - Confirm funds availability with Treasury for the pay run.
   - Validate tax flags (e.g., potential taxable reimbursements) and cost object coding completeness.

3. Payment run configuration
   - Select items due within the calendar window by legal entity, currency, and method.
   - Separate runs if needed: reimbursement vs. advances, domestic vs. cross-border, high-value wires vs. bulk ACH/SEPA.
   - Generate preliminary payment proposal and exception list.

4. Review and approval (maker-checker)
   - AP/T&E processor reviews proposal, resolves exceptions, and prepares supporting documentation.
   - Authorized approver(s) validate totals, spot-check samples, and approve the payment run per threshold matrix.

5. Execute payments
   - Generate bank payment files (e.g., NACHA, ISO 20022 pain.001) or checks; transmit via secure channel (host-to-host, SWIFT, bank portal).
   - For off-cycle payroll method, transmit net payment details to payroll with appropriate earning code.
   - Issue remittance advices to employees with itemized details and expected settlement date.
   - Produce positive pay and check printing files where applicable.

6. Accounting postings
   - Reimbursements: Debit expense accounts/clearing, credit employee payables at approval; on payment, debit employee payables, credit bank clearing/cash.
   - Advances: Debit employee advances/receivables, credit bank clearing/cash at issuance; upon settlement, credit employee advances and debit expenses (or clear against payable).
   - Apply FX remeasurement/realization where currency differences occur.
   - Post bank fees to appropriate GL accounts.

7. Bank reconciliation and status updates
   - Ingest bank confirmations/advices (e.g., camt.054/BAI2), auto-match to payments, and update status to Paid.
   - Investigate and resolve exceptions: rejected/returned transactions, short payments, fees deducted by bank.
   - Void and reissue stale or lost checks; update positive pay.

8. Advance settlement and recovery
   - Auto-apply outstanding advances to submitted expense reports; calculate residuals.
   - If advances remain unliquidated past due date, initiate reminders and recovery via payroll deduction or employee receivables process.
   - Handle cross-currency settlements with transparent FX calculations and communication to the employee.

9. Tax and compliance processing
   - Flag reimbursements that are potentially taxable benefits based on local rules; transmit to payroll for reporting and withholding where required.
   - Prepare VAT/GST reclaim data extracts with appropriate tax codes and receipt evidence.
   - Maintain audit trail of payment approvals, exceptions, and overrides.

10. Period close activities
   - Ensure cut-off compliance: include approved items in the designated payment cycle; accrue material approved-but-unpaid items if policy requires.
   - Review and clear open items (employee advances aging, stale checks).
   - Reconcile related balance sheet accounts (employee payables, advances, bank clearing).

11. Records retention and continuous improvement
   - Archive payment files, approvals, remittances, and reconciliation evidence per retention policy.
   - Analyze KPIs, identify root causes for exceptions, and implement corrective actions.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Paid reimbursements and issued advances with remittance advice to employees.
- Updated financial records: cleared payables, updated advances ledger, bank and FX postings.
- Exception and resolution logs (returns, reissues, deductions).
- Compliance and tax reports (VAT/GST reclaim files, taxable benefit feeds to payroll).
- Reconciliations and period close documentation.

Success criteria:
- Payments are accurate, timely, compliant, and fully reconciled.
- No duplicate or fraudulent payments.
- Advances are settled within policy timelines.
- Clean audit trail with minimal control exceptions.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Employee/Payee: Submits expense reports; provides accurate bank details; settles advances on time; responds to queries.
- Manager/Approver (upstream dependency): Approves expenses/advances per policy before payment.
- AP/T&E Processor: Performs validations; prepares payment proposals; resolves exceptions; posts accounting entries.
- Payment Run Approver/Authorized Signatory: Approves payment batches according to threshold matrix.
- Treasury/Cash Management: Ensures funding; manages bank connectivity; oversees payment formats and banking relationships.
- Payroll: Processes off-cycle reimbursements or taxable benefits; executes deductions for unliquidated advances where applicable.
- Tax: Configures tax rules; supports VAT/GST reclaim and taxable benefit determinations.
- IT/Systems Admin: Maintains integrations, security, and payment file configurations; supports automation and controls.
- Compliance/Internal Audit: Monitors adherence to policy, SoD, and regulatory requirements; performs periodic audits.
- HR: Provides employment status updates impacting payment eligibility; coordinates terminations.

## Best Practices
- Centralize payment runs with a standardized global calendar and pay groups by entity/currency.
- Enforce strong SoD and maker-checker controls for payment proposals and execution.
- Validate banking details using automated account verification services and change control (four-eyes review).
- Use secure, automated bank connectivity (ISO 20022, host-to-host) and avoid manual uploads where possible.
- Pay via electronic methods (ACH/SEPA) by default; minimize checks to reduce fraud and cost.
- Automate duplicate detection and anomaly scoring on reimbursement items before payment.
- Integrate advances tightly with expense systems to auto-apply and age outstanding balances.
- Configure clear SLAs and communication templates for rejects, returns, and advance reminders.
- Leverage corporate cards and central bill programs to reduce out-of-pocket reimbursements.
- Maintain clear tax logic and evidence for VAT/GST reclaim; route potential taxable items to payroll.
- Protect PII with encryption, role-based access, and strict retention schedules.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Incorrect or changed bank details leading to returns
  - Solution: Bank account verification, mandatory re-authentication for changes, out-of-band confirmations.
- Duplicate payments
  - Solution: System-level duplicate checks on key attributes; reference ID matching; payment hold on suspected duplicates.
- Cross-border/FX issues (fees, short payments)
  - Solution: Transparent fee options (OUR/SHA/BEN), pay in local currency where possible, communicate FX rates, gross-up if policy allows.
- Unliquidated advances
  - Solution: Automated aging dashboards, reminders, escalation, and payroll deduction workflows per policy.
- Stale or lost checks
  - Solution: Positive pay, check aging monitoring, timely void/reissue, migrate to electronic payments.
- Terminated employees with pending reimbursements/advances
  - Solution: HR-AP integration to block advances, reroute payments, and enforce settlement before final payroll.
- Tax compliance ambiguities
  - Solution: Centralized tax governance, documented rules per country, periodic reviews with Tax and Payroll.

## Performance Metrics
- Cycle time: Approval-to-payment time (median, 90th percentile) vs. SLA.
- On-time payment rate: % of reimbursements paid by due date.
- Exception rate: % payments rejected/returned by bank.
- Duplicate payment rate: Duplicates detected per 1,000 transactions (target: near zero).
- Advance aging: % of advances outstanding >30/60/90 days; average days to settlement.
- Cost per transaction: Total processing cost per reimbursement/advance payment.
- Electronic payment adoption: % of payments via ACH/SEPA/wire vs. checks.
- Policy compliance rate: % reimbursements with zero violations; audit pass rate.
- VAT/GST reclaim effectiveness: % eligible tax successfully reclaimed.
- Reconciliation timeliness: Days to clear bank transactions and related open items.

## Technology and Tools
- ERP/AP and T&E systems: SAP S/4HANA, Oracle Fusion, Workday Expenses, Coupa, SAP Concur, NetSuite, Dynamics 365.
- Payment factory/connectivity: Bank host-to-host, SWIFT, ISO 20022 payment engines, payment hubs (e.g., Kyriba, Coupa Pay).
- Bank account verification and fraud controls: IBAN/BBAN validation, micro-deposit services, vendor bank change controls.
- OCR/IDP and audit tools: Automated receipt capture, policy audit engines, anomaly detection.
- Tax engines: Vertex, Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE, Avalara for VAT/GST and tax determinations.
- Reconciliation tools: Bank statement ingestion and auto-match (e.g., BlackLine, Trintech, ERP-native).
- Workflow and RPA: Orchestrate approvals, exception handling, and routine reconciliations.
- Security and compliance: Role-based access control, encryption, logging, and retention solutions.

Process Details:
## Overview
Manage personnel accounts is the end-to-end process for creating, maintaining, and reconciling financial sub-ledger accounts for individuals connected with the business—primarily employees, but also contractors, interns, board members, and other natural persons who incur expenses on behalf of the organization. Within the expense reimbursements domain, this process ensures that every financial interaction with an individual (e.g., travel advances, out-of-pocket reimbursements, corporate card settlements, recoveries of overpayments) is recorded accurately, safeguarded by appropriate controls, and settled timely.

Purpose:
- Provide a controlled, auditable mechanism to pay, recover, and track amounts to and from individuals.
- Maintain high-quality master data (e.g., banking, tax, cost allocations) to enable straight-through processing.
- Ensure compliance with accounting standards, tax regulations, data privacy, and internal controls.
- Support period-end close with reconciled sub-ledger balances and complete documentation.

Role in the organization:
- Bridges HR, Accounts Payable, Expense Management, Payroll, Treasury, and Corporate Card Administration.
- Directly impacts employee experience (timely reimbursements) and financial integrity (accurate liabilities/receivables).
- Provides data for management reporting, audits, tax reporting, and working capital management.

## Key Activities
- Master data administration for personnel accounts (create, update, inactivate; prevent duplicates; maintain audit trail).
- Payment method and banking data management with verification and approvals.
- Tax setup for taxable benefits and local withholding/compliance flags (where applicable).
- Default coding and policy attributes management (cost center, project, location, approval hierarchies).
- Advance management (cash/travel advances: request, approve, disburse, track, clear).
- Corporate card profile mapping and clearing rules (individual vs. central liability) where relevant.
- Transaction posting and clearing (expense reports, advance liquidations, overpayment recoveries).
- Payment release and holds (inclusion in payment runs, blocks for investigation).
- Account reconciliation and aging (identify overdue advances, unmatched card charges, stale balances).
- Employee statements and dunning (communications, repayment plans, payroll deductions if applicable).
- Exception handling (returned payments, over/underpayments, fraud indicators, name mismatches).
- Period-end activities (accruals, reclasses, sub-ledger to GL reconciliation, close certification).
- Offboarding and dormancy management (freeze, settle balances, deactivate; data retention).

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Verified identity and HR master data for the individual (legal name, employee ID, employment status, cost center).
- Completed and approved request for account creation/update (ticket/workflow with maker–checker).
- Banking details and consent; tax forms or compliance data (as applicable by jurisdiction).
- Expense policy, approval matrix, and coding defaults.
- Chart of accounts, vendor/customer group configuration, payment methods, and withholding settings.
- Corporate card details/feeds and liability model (if applicable).
- Existing balances and history (for updates/transfers).

Prerequisites:
- Segregation of duties established (creator vs. approver vs. payer).
- Data privacy/security controls in place (role-based access, encryption, retention).
- Configured ERP/expense tool integration (master data, postings, payments).
- Defined SLAs and control checkpoints (e.g., bank verification, change approvals).

Dependencies on other processes:
- HR onboarding/offboarding and position changes.
- Expense report processing and approvals.
- Cash disbursements and payment execution.
- Corporate card program administration and feeds.
- Payroll (for taxable benefits or deductions/recoupments).
- General ledger close and account reconciliation.

## Process Steps
1) Intake and verification
- Receive request to create or update a personnel account (e.g., new hire, banking change, role/location change).
- Validate requester authorization; confirm employment/engagement status from HRIS.
- Collect mandatory data: legal name, address, bank details (IBAN/ACH routing), tax IDs/forms where required, email, default cost center/project, payment currency, preferred payment method.
- Screen for duplicates (exact and fuzzy matching on name, ID, bank account, email). If potential duplicate:
  - Decision: If duplicate confirmed, update existing account; else proceed with new account.
- Verify banking details (e.g., micro-deposit validation, third-party verification, or bank letter) per policy.
- Log a master data change ticket with traceable reference.

2) Account setup/update in ERP and expense system
- Create/maintain Business Partner/vendor/employee sub-ledger record in ERP for relevant company codes.
  - Set: payment terms/methods, bank, tax withholding flags, currency, tolerance keys and payment blocks (default).
  - Assign coding defaults (cost center, legal entity, location, project if applicable).
  - Assign vendor group/supplier type as “personnel” to drive controls and reporting.
- Link to expense management profile and HR master (single source of truth for identity).
- Map corporate card profile and clearing rules if applicable (individual liability vs. central bill; default clearing account).
- Route the record for maker–checker approval; apply payment block until approved.
- Notify the individual of account setup and any steps required (e.g., confirm micro-deposit).

3) Advance management (if used)
- Receive and validate advance request (purpose, dates, estimate, policy compliance).
- Obtain approval per policy thresholds.
- Post advance as a receivable against the personnel account; initiate payment via standard payment run.
- Configure clearing rules to auto-liquidate the advance upon related expense report submission.
- Monitor open advances with due dates; trigger reminders/Dunning for overdue items.

4) Transaction posting and clearing
- Expense system posts approved expense reports to ERP: debit expense accounts, credit personnel account (for reimbursements), and clear advances where relevant.
- Corporate card clearing:
  - Import card feed; match to submitted expenses.
  - Post matched amounts; unresolved or personal charges remain as receivable from the individual until cleared.
- Handle exceptions:
  - Returned/rejected payments: place payment block; correct data; re-run.
  - Overpayments: record receivable and set recovery path (refund, payroll deduction where permitted, or offset against future reimbursements).

5) Payment processing
- Include eligible, approved balances in scheduled payment runs (ACH/SEPA/wire/check per region).
- Apply payment blocks for high-risk or incomplete records (e.g., bank unverified, policy hold).
- Generate remittance advice to employee with line-item details.
- Update payment status back to expense system and notify employee.

6) Reconciliation and monitoring
- Perform monthly sub-ledger to GL reconciliation for personnel accounts; substantiate balances.
- Review aging of receivables (advances, personal charges, overpayments); escalate overdue cases.
- Investigate unmatched corporate card transactions and stale items.
- Produce and distribute statements of account to individuals as needed.

7) Period-end close
- Accrue for approved but unpaid reimbursements and significant unsubmitted expenses per policy.
- Reconcile corporate card clearing accounts and suspense accounts.
- Certify account ownership and controls (close checklist) and archive evidence.

8) Offboarding and dormancy
- Receive termination/transfer notice from HR; immediately:
  - Freeze account for new spend; block payments except for final approved reimbursements.
  - Collect/disable corporate card; confirm final expense submission timeline.
- Reconcile and settle outstanding balances:
  - Clear advances; recover remaining receivables via payroll deduction or invoice as permitted.
- Mark account as inactive once settled; retain data per retention policy.

9) Audit, controls, and continuous improvement
- Maintain audit trails for all master data changes and approvals.
- Periodically test SOX/ICFR controls; remediate deficiencies.
- Analyze KPIs; address root causes (training, policy tweaks, automation).

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Active, accurate personnel accounts with verified banking and tax settings.
- Posted and cleared transactions for advances, reimbursements, and recoveries.
- Payment files and remittance advices; returned payment logs.
- Monthly reconciliations, aging reports, statements of account, and dunning notices.
- Close documentation (accruals, reconciliations, certifications).
- Audit-ready master data change logs and control evidence.

Success criteria:
- Accurate master data with minimal defects and no unauthorized changes.
- Timely reimbursements within SLAs; minimal returned payments.
- Clean reconciliations with aging within policy thresholds.
- Complete, compliant documentation and positive audit outcomes.
- High employee satisfaction with reimbursement timeliness and clarity.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Personnel Accounts/Accounts Payable Specialist
  - Create/update personnel master records; validate banking; process holds/unblocks.
  - Post advances, clear transactions, run payment proposals, manage exceptions.
  - Perform reconciliations and aging reviews.
- Expense Management Administrator
  - Maintain expense system profiles, policy rules, workflows, and integrations.
  - Manage corporate card feed mappings and clearing configurations.
- HR Partner
  - Provide timely onboarding/offboarding data; maintain identity and employment status.
- Treasury/Payments
  - Configure payment methods, bank connectivity; manage payment runs; monitor rejects.
- Payroll
  - Process taxable benefits flags and execute deductions/recoupments as authorized.
- Corporate Card Program Administrator
  - Manage card issuance/closure, liability model, delinquency, and feed integrity.
- Employee
  - Provide accurate information; submit expenses timely; clear advances/personal charges.
- Manager/Approver
  - Approve expense reports and advances; ensure policy compliance.
- Tax/Compliance
  - Define tax treatment; review controls and compliance with local regulations.
- IT/Master Data Governance
  - Maintain ERP/MDG configurations; duplicate detection; role-based access.
- Internal Controls/Audit
  - Define, test, and monitor SOX/ICFR controls; review audit trails and reconciliations.

Note: Enforce segregation of duties between master data maintenance, transaction processing, and payment release.

## Best Practices
- Centralize personnel account master data via governed workflows with maker–checker approvals.
- Verify bank accounts using independent verification (micro-deposits/API) before lifting payment blocks.
- Use a single Business Partner/unique ID across HR, expense, and ERP to prevent duplicates.
- Implement automated duplicate detection and periodic de-duplication reviews.
- Enforce default payment blocks on new/changed records until approved and verified.
- Integrate expense system and corporate card feeds for auto-matching and auto-clearing.
- Maintain strict role-based access; mask/baseline PII; encrypt bank data at rest and in transit.
- Run monthly sub-ledger to GL reconciliations with aging dashboards and owner sign-offs.
- Set and enforce advance clearing deadlines; auto-dun and enable payroll deductions where legal.
- Standardize global templates but localize for tax, currency, and banking requirements.
- Maintain comprehensive audit trails for master data and payment changes; enable change logs.
- Provide employee self-service for data updates with built-in validations and approvals.
- Use exception queues and RPA to auto-handle common changes (address, bank updates) with risk scoring.
- Establish offboarding checklists tied to HR events to freeze accounts and settle balances fast.
- Review metrics and perform root-cause analysis; publish performance and compliance scorecards.

## Common Challenges
- Duplicate or inaccurate personnel accounts
  - Solution: Unique identifiers, fuzzy-match detection, MDG workflows, periodic data cleansing.
- Returned or misdirected payments due to bad banking data
  - Solution: Bank verification before release, validation rules, address/bank change controls, payment blocks.
- Unreconciled or aged advances and personal charges
  - Solution: Automated reminders/dunning, strict clearing deadlines, payroll deductions/repayment plans, manager escalation.
- Delayed offboarding notifications causing leakage
  - Solution: Real-time HR-ERP integration; automated account freeze on termination events.
- Corporate card feed mismatches or delays
  - Solution: Daily feed monitoring, fallback files, exception queues, reconciliation between issuer and ERP.
- Tax and compliance gaps (e.g., taxable benefits not flagged)
  - Solution: Tax governance, periodic reviews, integration with tax engine, training and automated classification rules.
- Segregation of duties breaches
  - Solution: Role design, access recertification, compensating controls, audit logs and alerts.
- Employee dissatisfaction due to slow reimbursements
  - Solution: SLA commitments, automation, clear communication, self-service status tracking.
- Global complexity (multi-currency, banking formats, local regulations)
  - Solution: Localized configurations, multi-entity templates, payment format libraries, regional support.

## Performance Metrics
- Master data accuracy rate (% records without defects over period).
- Cycle time to create/update personnel account (request to approval).
- Percent of bank details verified before first payment.
- Payment return rate (% of payments rejected/returned).
- Reimbursement timeliness (% processed within SLA, e.g., 5 business days after approval).
- Open advance aging (median days outstanding; % > 30/60/90 days).
- Corporate card clearing rate (% of card transactions matched and cleared within X days).
- Sub-ledger to GL reconciliation timeliness (% completed by close +X days).
- Overpayment incidence rate and recovery rate.
- Duplicate account rate (per 1,000 active personnel accounts).
- Offboarding settlement time (termination to account closure).
- Control effectiveness (SOX/ICFR exceptions; access violations).
- Employee satisfaction (CSAT/NPS for reimbursements and payments).

## Technology and Tools
- ERP and finance systems: SAP S/4HANA (Business Partner, FI-AP), Oracle ERP Cloud, Workday Financials, Microsoft Dynamics.
- Expense management: SAP Concur, Coupa Expenses, Navan/TripActions, Emburse, Zoho Expense.

Process Details:
# [9.6.3.2] Process Corporate Credit Card Requests

Level: 4  
Description: Handling applications and approvals for corporate credit cards used for business expenses (e.g., T&E, purchasing cards, virtual cards).

## Overview
This process governs how employees, contractors, and designated business entities request, are evaluated for, and receive corporate credit cards for sanctioned business expenses. It ensures issued cards meet policy, risk, and regulatory requirements; are configured with appropriate limits and controls; and are correctly integrated with expense, ERP, and card program systems.

Purpose:
- Provide timely access to appropriate corporate payment instruments for business needs.
- Enforce policy-driven eligibility, spending controls, and approvals to reduce fraud and misuse.
- Ensure accurate financial integration (GL mapping, cost center assignment) and auditability.
- Standardize onboarding and cardholder accountability through training and attestation.

Role in the organization:
- Supports spend efficiency, traveler productivity, and supplier enablement.
- Reduces out-of-pocket reimbursements and improves visibility of spend.
- Aligns with AP, expense management, and compliance monitoring to maintain control environment (SOX, internal audit).

Scope:
- In-scope: New card requests (T&E, P-Card, ghost/virtual cards), upgrades/downgrades of limits, reinstatements after suspension.
- Out-of-scope (covered by related processes): Card monitoring and compliance, statement reconciliation and payment, dispute management, card termination/offboarding, card master data maintenance.

## Key Activities
- Intake and triage of card requests via standardized portal/form.
- Eligibility and policy validation (role, tenure, need, geography).
- Approval workflow orchestration (manager, cost center/budget owner, Finance, Risk/Compliance as needed).
- Submission to card issuer/program portal and KYC/CIP coordination as applicable.
- Card configuration (credit limits, MCC blocks, cash advance settings, billing type, cycle).
- Cardholder onboarding: policy training, agreement/attestation, activation.
- Systems setup: card-to-user mapping in expense tool, GL and cost center defaults, data feed enablement.
- Communications and documentation retention for audit.
- Handover to monitoring and periodic recertification processes.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Completed card request form (request type, business justification, anticipated spend, travel frequency, required limit, card type).
- Requester identity and HR metadata (employee ID, role, location, employment type, manager).
- Cost center and project codes; default approver chain.
- Evidence of manager pre-approval (if not orchestrated by workflow).
- Policy acknowledgments and completed training (or commitment to complete before activation).
- For certain models: personal credit check consent (individual liability programs), copy of government ID if required by issuer.
- For virtual/ghost cards: supplier details, duration, ceiling, MCC, and intended use.

Prerequisites:
- Corporate card policy, eligibility criteria, and limit tiers defined and published ([9.6.3.1] Manage corporate card program and policy).
- Issuer(s) onboarded, master agreements in place, KYC completed at entity level.
- Expense management system configured to ingest card transactions and map to GL.
- Segregation of duties defined (request vs. approve vs. administer).
- Data privacy and information security controls defined (minimize/steward PII, secure storage).

Dependencies on other processes:
- [9.6.3.1] Define and maintain policy, card types, and controls.
- [9.6.3.4] Maintain card master data (ongoing updates post-issuance).
- [9.6.3.5] Reconcile and pay corporate card statements (post-issuance).
- [9.6.3.6] Monitor card usage and compliance; periodic recertification.
- Workforce onboarding/offboarding processes for identity and status updates.
- Budgeting and cost center governance for approval routing.

## Process Steps
1. Initiation and Intake
   - Requester completes online corporate card request in the service portal (e.g., ServiceNow) selecting card type (T&E, P-Card, virtual).
   - Provide business justification, expected spend profile, travel needs, desired limit tier, and cost center.
   - The portal pulls HR profile data and routes based on location and role.
   - Auto-validation checks for duplicates, active cards, and eligibility by role and employment type.

2. Pre-Screening (Program Administrator)
   - Verify completeness and eligibility (tenure, role-based need, geography constraints).
   - Check if training and policy attestation are current; if not, queue prerequisites.
   - Confirm alignment to approved limit tiers and MCC control templates.
   - Determine liability model (corporate vs. individual) and any credit check requirements.

3. Approval Workflow
   - Manager approval for business need.
   - Cost center/budget owner approval for funding responsibility.
   - Finance approval for requested limit and billing type (central vs. individual).
   - Risk/Compliance approval for exceptions (high limits, cash advance privilege, restricted MCCs, high-risk geographies).
   - Automated reminders and escalation for SLA adherence.

4. Issuer Submission and Due Diligence
   - Program Administrator initiates card creation in issuer portal (e.g., AmEx @Work, Visa IntelliLink, Mastercard Smart Data).
   - Provide required cardholder details; use tokenization where possible to avoid storing PANs internally.
   - For individual liability programs, capture cardholder consent for credit check as required by issuer/jurisdiction.
   - For virtual/ghost cards, define ceiling, time window, and merchant restrictions.
   - Track issuer approval; resolve any data issues.

5. Card Configuration
   - Apply approved credit limit and cash advance setting (if allowed).
   - Assign MCC blocks aligned with card type and policy.
   - Set billing cycle, statement delivery, and charge allocation (central/individual).
   - Assign cost center defaults and GL mapping templates.
   - Configure regional usage and currency restrictions if applicable.

6. Compliance Prerequisites and Agreements
   - Enroll cardholder in mandatory training (policy, do’s/don’ts, expense submission).
   - Obtain electronic signatures for Cardholder Agreement and Policy Acknowledgment (e.g., DocuSign).
   - Store executed documents and training completion evidences in the document repository with retention tags.

7. Issuance and Activation
   - Physical card: arrange shipping to office or cardholder address; track delivery.
   - Virtual card: provision and communicate secure retrieval or wallet tokenization steps.
   - Provide activation instructions and two-factor verification setup.
   - Confirm activation in issuer and internal systems.

8. Systems Setup and Integration
   - Link card account to cardholder profile in expense system (e.g., SAP Concur, Oracle Expenses, Workday, Coupa).
   - Enable transaction feed from issuer (file SFTP or API); test postings and GL mapping.
   - Verify default approver chain and cost center assignment.
   - For P-Cards, configure commodity code approvals and receipt/PO exceptions if applicable.

9. Communication and Onboarding
   - Send welcome package: policy highlights, spend categories allowed, limits, travel support, dispute instructions, expense submission timing, and compliance contact.
   - Provide quick reference guides and links to training resources and FAQs.

10. Recordkeeping and Handover
    - Capture and archive request, approvals, agreements, training proof, and configuration snapshot.
    - Update card inventory and ownership registry.
    - Add cardholder to monitoring and periodic recertification schedule.
    - Close the request with status and SLA metrics logged.

11. Exceptions and Expedited Requests (as-needed path)
    - For urgent travel or critical supplier needs, use expedited workflow with temporary limits or virtual card issuance, ensuring post-facto approval and tighter monitoring.
    - Document exception rationale and approvals.

Control points:
- Eligibility, approval, and configuration require evidence and are non-bypassable in the workflow.
- Segregation of duties enforced (requester cannot approve or administer their own card).
- System checks for duplicate or active cards before proceeding.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Activated corporate card (physical or virtual) with approved configuration.
- Completed and stored Cardholder Agreement and Policy Acknowledgment.
- User-to-card mapping in expense/ERP systems; GL defaults configured.
- Transaction feed enabled and validated.
- Welcome/onboarding communications delivered.
- Audit trail of request, approvals, and configuration.
Success criteria:
- Card issued within SLA with zero critical defects (wrong limit/MCC, wrong owner).
- 100% completion of training and attestation before activation.
- Transaction feed posts correctly on first pass.
- No policy exceptions outside approved thresholds.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Requester/Cardholder: Initiates request, provides justification, completes training, acknowledges policy, uses card per policy.
- Line Manager: Validates business need, approves request, ensures ongoing oversight.
- Cost Center/Budget Owner: Confirms funding source and budget availability.
- Finance/AP Card Program Administrator: Operates workflow, validates eligibility, configures card, liaises with issuer, sets up integrations, maintains records.
- Risk/Compliance/Internal Audit: Reviews high-risk requests/exceptions, defines control frameworks, audits evidence.
- HR/Identity Management: Supplies authoritative employment and manager data; flags status changes.
- IT/Application Support: Maintains workflow portal, integrations (issuer feeds, ERP/expense), SSO, and data security.
- Card Issuer/Bank: Performs KYC/CIP as required, provisions card, provides data feeds and controls.
- Travel/Procurement (as applicable): Aligns card type with travel program or P-Card commodity policies.

## Best Practices
- Standardize request forms with dynamic fields and validation; integrate with HRIS to auto-populate data.
- Use predefined limit tiers and MCC control templates by role and card type.
- Prefer virtual cards for one-time or supplier-specific transactions to minimize risk.
- Enforce mandatory training and electronic policy attestation before activation.
- Implement segregation of duties and automated approval workflows with SLAs and escalations.
- Minimize PII storage; use tokenization for PAN where possible; restrict access on a need-to-know basis.
- Integrate issuer data feeds via API for near real-time monitoring; validate GL mapping in a test queue before go-live.
- Maintain a central card inventory with ownership, limits, and review dates; conduct periodic recertifications.
- Define an expedite path with clear guardrails (temporary lower limits, tighter MCCs, short validity).
- Align with global and local regulations (e.g., GDPR, OFAC screening by issuer, local labor/work council requirements).

## Common Challenges
- Incomplete or inaccurate requests: Mitigate with guided forms, required fields, and eligibility checks.
- Approval bottlenecks: Set SLA-based reminders, delegate approvers, and escalation rules; provide mobile approvals.
- Wrong limits/MCC settings: Use templates and dual-review for configuration changes; maintain change logs.
- Duplicate cards or orphaned accounts: Enforce duplicate checks and integrate with HR offboarding for automatic suspension.
- Issuer delays or KYC hurdles: Maintain standing corporate profiles with issuers; pre-validate data; establish bank SLAs.
- Integration or feed failures: Monitor with automated alerts, retry logic, and fallback SFTP feeds; maintain a reconciliation queue.
- Policy non-compliance post-issuance: Hand off to monitoring; educate cardholders; use transaction controls and progressive discipline.
- Global variations (tax, privacy, labor rules): Localize policies and workflows; maintain a solution design per region.

## Performance Metrics
- Cycle time: Request submission to activation (median and 90th percentile).
- First-pass yield: % of requests processed without rework.
- SLA attainment: % requests completed within target time by card type.
- Approval lead time: Average time at each approval step; bottleneck analysis.
- Training and attestation compliance: % completed before activation.
- Configuration accuracy: % cards with correct limits/MCC/GL mapping on first issuance.
- Exception rate: % of requests requiring policy exceptions; trend over time.
- Integration uptime: % availability of issuer feeds; number of failed postings per period.
- Duplicate/Orphan rate: # of duplicate or unassigned cards detected per quarter.
- Recertification adherence: % of cards reviewed on schedule.
- Customer satisfaction (CSAT): Cardholder survey score post-onboarding.

Target examples:
- Cycle time: Standard 5 business days; expedited 1 business day.
- First-pass yield: >95%.
- Configuration accuracy: >99.5%.

## Technology and Tools
- Request and Workflow: ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, Microsoft Power Platform, Pega.
- Expense Management: SAP Concur, Oracle Expense Cloud, Workday Expenses, Coupa, Emburse (Certify/Chrome River), Navan.
- ERP/GL: SAP S/4HANA, Oracle Cloud ERP, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics 365.
- Issuer/Program Portals and Data: American Express @Work, Visa IntelliLink, Mastercard Smart Data; issuer APIs/SFTP feeds.
- Integration/Middleware: Mulesoft, Boomi, Azure Integration Services, Kafka for eventing.
- Identity/Access and SSO: Okta, Azure AD; HRIS (Workday, SAP SuccessFactors) as source of truth.
- E-signature and Content Management: DocuSign, Adobe Acrobat Sign; SharePoint, OpenText for retention.
- Data Security: Tokenization/vaulting for PAN, DLP tools, role-based access controls; encryption at rest and in transit.
- Monitoring/Analytics: BI dashboards (Power BI, Tableau), log monitoring (Splunk), workflow analytics for SLA tracking.

Process Details:
## Overview
Process: [9.7.1.7] Develop and confirm internal controls for treasury

Purpose: Establish, implement, and maintain a robust internal control framework over corporate treasury activities related to investments in bonds, currencies (FX), and financial derivatives. The process ensures compliance with policies and regulations, safeguards assets, maintains reliable financial reporting and valuations, mitigates market/liquidity/counterparty/operational risks, and enables efficient, well-governed treasury operations.

Role in the organization: This process operationalizes treasury policies by translating risk appetite and governance requirements into practical, testable controls embedded in daily front-, middle-, and back-office workflows. It supports audit readiness (e.g., SOX 404), accurate accounting (e.g., IFRS 9/ASC 815), regulatory obligations (e.g., EMIR/Dodd-Frank reporting where applicable), and decision-making through reliable data. It is a foundational element of the “three lines of defense” model and underpins confidence from management, the board, lenders, and rating agencies.

Scope:
- Instruments: FX spot/forwards/swaps/options, interest rate swaps and futures, bonds and money market instruments, commodity hedges where in scope.
- Activities: Deal origination, approval and limit checks, trade capture, valuation and market data, confirmation and settlement, collateral/margining, accounting/hedge documentation, reporting, and system access/change management.
- Control lifecycle: Risk assessment, design, documentation, implementation, testing/attestation, remediation, and continuous improvement.

## Key Activities
- Risk and control assessment (RCSA): Identify inherent risks across treasury processes and define control objectives aligned to COSO/ISO 31000.
- Control design and selection: Define preventive/detective/corrective controls; determine manual vs automated; establish frequency, evidence, tolerances, and ownership.
- Segregation of duties (SoD) and authority: Design SoD across front-, middle-, back-office; embed maker-checker and dual-approval controls; enforce trading and payment authority matrices.
- Limit/constraint framework: Set and implement counterparty credit limits, instrument limits, tenor limits, stop-loss/VaR limits, and liquidity/FX exposure thresholds with automated pre-trade checks.
- Market data and valuation controls: Define sources, curve-building rules, independent price verification (IPV), model validation, and tolerance-based exception handling.
- Trade lifecycle controls: Capture, confirmation matching, settlement, reconciliations, collateral/margining, dispute management, and custodial safekeeping.
- Hedge accounting controls: Documentation at inception, designation/effectiveness testing, rebalancing/de-designation, and disclosures.
- Access and change management: Role-based access, periodic recertification, privileged access monitoring, system change controls, and release governance.
- Documentation and evidence management: Control narratives, RCMs (risk-control matrices), SOPs, evidence repositories, data retention schedules.
- Testing and assurance: Control operating effectiveness testing (SOX/SOC), KRIs, control attestations, remediation tracking, and audit coordination.
- Training and communication: Role-specific training on policies, systems, and control execution; periodic refreshers and certifications.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Treasury policy, risk appetite statement, and approved instruments list
- Authority matrices and deal approval limits; list of approved counterparties and ISDA/CSA terms
- Process maps, system architecture, and data flows for treasury, TMS/ETRM, bank connectivity, and ERP
- Regulatory requirements (e.g., EMIR/DFA reporting, UMR for margin, sanctions/AML screening requirements)
- Accounting policies (IFRS 9/ASC 815 for hedge accounting; IFRS 13/ASC 820 for fair value)
- Historical incidents/audit findings and current KRIs/KPIs
- Existing controls inventory and SoD matrix

Prerequisites:
- Governance body established (Treasury/Risk Committee) with clear escalation pathways
- Sponsorship from CFO/Treasurer; defined roles across three lines of defense
- Core systems in place (TMS, market data feeds, confirmation/settlement channels)
- Legal agreements executed with counterparties (ISDA, CSA, clearing agreements, custodial agreements)

Dependencies on other processes:
- [9.7.1] Manage treasury policies and procedures (upstream)
- Counterparty onboarding and credit risk management
- Liquidity management and cash forecasting
- General accounting and financial reporting
- IT change management and cybersecurity
- Compliance and regulatory reporting
- Business continuity and disaster recovery management

## Process Steps
1. Initiate and scope
   - Confirm instrument coverage, entities, geographies, and regulatory landscape.
   - Define control objectives per process area (e.g., authorization, completeness, accuracy, valuation, existence).

2. Perform risk assessment (RCSA)
   - Identify risks: market, counterparty, liquidity, operational, model, legal, compliance, data, cyber.
   - Assess inherent risk and determine risk responses; rank by impact/likelihood.

3. Design control framework
   - Map risks to control objectives and specific controls.
   - Specify control type (preventive/detective/corrective), frequency, owners, evidence, thresholds, and escalation criteria.
   - Define SoD and maker-checker points across trade lifecycle.
   - Draft a detailed RCM with links to SOPs and system configurations.

4. Align with policy and authority
   - Ensure controls enforce policy (approved instruments, limits, hedging rationale) and authority matrices (deal size, tenor, payments).
   - Configure pre-trade limit checks and approval workflows in TMS/OMS.

5. Define valuation and market data controls
   - Establish golden sources, hierarchy/fallbacks, and curve-building methodologies.
   - Implement IPV with defined tolerances and independent ownership.
   - Document model governance (validation, backtesting, change approvals).

6. Establish trade lifecycle controls
   - Trade capture: same-day capture with time stamps; independent middle-office verification.
   - Confirmations: STP via SWIFT/MarkitSERV; timely matching; exception queues.
   - Settlement: payment factory with dual approvals; CLS/netting where applicable; sanction screening.
   - Collateral/margin: margin call calculations, dispute logs, segregation, and reconciliations.
   - Custody and safekeeping: reconcile positions/cash with custodians/banks daily.

7. Implement access and change controls
   - Role-based access in TMS, bank portals, market data systems; quarterly access recertification.
   - Segregate production vs UAT; require change tickets, testing evidence, and approvals for releases.

8. Document procedures and evidence requirements
   - Author SOPs, desk procedures, and control narratives with step-by-step instructions.
   - Define evidence artifacts, storage locations, retention periods, and naming conventions.

9. Pilot and deploy
   - Run pilots in UAT; conduct dry-runs of control execution and evidence capture.
   - Validate integrations (TMS-ERP, TMS-bank, market data) and exception handling workflows.

10. Train and communicate
    - Deliver role-based training; certify understanding of responsibilities and SoD.
    - Publish quick-reference guides and escalation matrices.

11. Operate, monitor, and test
    - Execute controls per defined cadence; log exceptions and breaches.
    - Perform periodic control effectiveness testing (self-assessments, SOX testing).
    - Track KRIs/KPIs; report to Treasury/Risk Committee.

12. Remediate and improve
    - Investigate root causes; implement corrective actions and compensating controls as needed.
    - Update RCMs/SOPs following changes or regulatory updates.
    - Conduct annual comprehensive review and re-approval by governance bodies.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Approved treasury control framework and RCMs
- SOPs, control narratives, SoD matrices, and authority matrices
- Configured system controls (limit checks, workflows, access controls)
- Testing plans, test results, and control attestations (e.g., SOX 302/404)
- Exception and breach logs with remediation actions
- IPV reports, valuation control memos, model validation reports
- Audit-ready evidence repository and audit response packages
- Periodic management reporting (KRI/KPI dashboards)
Success criteria:
- Controls designed to address all key risks and operating effectively with timely, complete evidence
- Minimal significant deficiencies/material weaknesses; prompt remediation of findings
- Compliance with relevant accounting/regulatory requirements and internal policies
- Reduction in operational incidents, settlement fails, and limit breaches over time

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Treasurer/CFO sponsor: Approve framework, risk appetite, and major changes; receive escalations.
- Treasury Front Office (Dealers/Traders): Execute trades within limits; initiate hedge documentation; no access to confirmations/settlements.
- Treasury Middle Office/Risk: Own RCSA; design/monitor controls; run limit checks; IPV; KRI reporting.
- Treasury Back Office/Settlements: Confirm trades, process settlements, manage collateral, perform reconciliations.
- Treasury Operations Manager: Day-to-day control execution oversight; exception management; training coordination.
- Accounting/Reporting: Hedge accounting documentation, effectiveness testing, journal review, disclosure support.
- IT/TMS Administrators: Access provisioning, system configurations, change management, interface monitoring.
- Market Data Admin/Model Risk: Source management, curve governance, model validation.
- Legal/Compliance: Contracting (ISDA/CSA), regulatory reporting oversight, sanctions/AML controls.
- Internal Audit: Independent assurance, advisory on control improvements.
- Risk Committee/Board Audit Committee: Oversight, review of KRI/KPI, approval of key policies and remediation plans.

## Best Practices
- Anchor on COSO internal control framework and ISO 31000 risk management principles.
- Enforce strong SoD: front office cannot confirm/settle; back office cannot trade; middle office independent from both.
- Automate wherever possible: pre-trade limit checks, confirmations (SWIFT/MarkitSERV), reconciliations, and alerts.
- Establish a clear limit governance: approved counterparty lists, credit limits with real-time consumption, breach escalation.
- Implement robust market data governance: golden source, secondary source, IPV thresholds, and audit trails.
- Maintain end-to-end STP with exception-based workflows and dashboards.
- Align hedge accounting controls with IFRS 9/ASC 815: contemporaneous documentation, methodical effectiveness testing.
- Periodic access recertification and privileged access monitoring across all treasury and bank systems.
- Use standard evidence packages with consistent naming, timestamps, and sign-offs to streamline audits.
- Conduct scenario and stress testing for market/liquidity risks; link results to control enhancements.
- Apply third-party risk management to banks, custodians, and vendors (SOC 1/2 reviews, SLAs).
- Integrate BCP/DR testing for critical treasury processes and connectivity.

## Common Challenges
- Limited resources causing SoD conflicts in small teams
  - Solutions: Compensating controls (increased supervisory review, random spot checks), rotation, and periodic independent oversight by internal audit.
- Overreliance on manual spreadsheets
  - Solutions: Implement TMS modules, RPA for routine checks, spreadsheet governance (protected cells, version control).
- Inadequate market data and valuation controls
  - Solutions: Define data hierarchies, IPV routines, and independent ownership; periodic model validation.
- Complex derivatives and hedge accounting errors
  - Solutions: Pre-trade reviews by accounting, standardized documentation templates, automated effectiveness testing.
- Weak limit discipline and delayed escalations
  - Solutions: Real-time alerts, hard stops in systems, formal breach logs with root-cause analysis.
- Integration and interface failures causing data breaks
  - Solutions: Interface monitoring, automated reconciliations, failover procedures, and incident playbooks.
- Regulatory change fatigue
  - Solutions: Compliance horizon scanning, change control boards, and training refreshers.

## Performance Metrics
- Control effectiveness rate: percent of key controls passing tests
- Exception rate and aging: open control exceptions and average days to closure
- Limit breaches: count, severity, and time to escalate/resolve
- Confirmation timeliness: percent matched within T+1 (or instrument standard)
- Settlement fail rate: percent and value of fails; average days outstanding
- Reconciliation breaks: count/value and aging of cash/position breaks
- IPV results: percent within tolerance; average valuation variance
