Process Details:
## Overview
Manage and reconcile cash positions ensures the organization has an accurate, timely view of available cash across all bank accounts and entities, and that differences between bank-reported balances and book balances are identified, investigated, and resolved. The process enables optimal utilization of funds (e.g., concentrating idle cash, repaying short-term debt, investing surpluses) while maintaining control, auditability, and compliance with internal policies and external regulations.

This Level 4 process sits within Manage cash and Treasury operations and typically runs daily and intraday. It connects operational cash movements (AP, AR, payroll, tax, merchant settlements) to treasury decisions (funding, investment, FX) and accounting integrity (bank-to-GL reconciliation).

Primary objectives:
- Provide a reliable cash position by bank, account, legal entity, and currency.
- Reconcile bank vs. book balances; resolve timing and data discrepancies promptly.
- Trigger liquidity actions to meet obligations and minimize cost of carry.
- Maintain a complete audit trail and controls (segregation of duties, approvals).
- Feed accurate cash data into cash forecasting and financial reporting.

## Key Activities
- Collect bank balance and transaction data (intraday and prior-day statements).
- Aggregate expected cash flows (AP runs, AR receipts, payroll, tax, merchant/card settlements).
- Build and publish the daily cash position by currency, legal entity, and account.
- Reconcile bank balances and transactions with ERP/GL cash accounts.
- Investigate and clear variances (timing differences, missing postings, duplicates, fees).
- Execute cash concentration, intercompany funding, and short-term investments/borrowings.
- Perform FX conversions to fund accounts in required currencies as needed.
- Post and approve journal entries for bank charges, interest, returned items, and corrections.
- Update cash forecasts with actuals and new insights from variances.
- Produce daily and period-end reconciliation reports with sign-offs and aging of open items.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Bank statements and intraday reports (e.g., ISO 20022 camt.052/053/054, SWIFT MT940/942, BAI2).
- ERP/GL cash account balances and prior-day closing balances.
- Expected cash flow files/schedules: AP payment proposals, AR remittance/lockbox, payroll run dates/amounts, tax payments, merchant card settlement cycles, treasury deal settlements.
- Outstanding items lists: uncleared checks, returned/NSF items, bank fee advices.
- FX rates and holiday calendars by currency/country.
- Bank account master data: accounts, signatories, limits, cut-off times, currencies, pooling structures.
- Treasury policies: approval limits, variance thresholds, investment and borrowing policies, FX policy.

Prerequisites:
- Bank connectivity established (host-to-host, SWIFT, APIs) and automated file imports.
- Configured TMS/ERP cash management modules and reconciliation rules.
- Segregation of duties in place (preparation vs. approval vs. execution).
- Defined daily schedule and cut-offs aligned to bank and market deadlines.
- Access controls and multi-factor authentication for bank and TMS portals.

Dependencies on other processes:
- Accounts receivable cash application and lockbox processing.
- Accounts payable disbursements and payment runs.
- Payroll processing.
- Short-term investing/borrowing and FX dealing.
- General accounting and period close; bank account management.
- Cash flow forecasting.

## Process Steps
1) Plan daily cycle and cut-offs
- Treasury sets daily calendar with time zones and bank market cut-offs (e.g., 9:30 intraday snapshot, 11:00 domestic transfers, 14:00 cross-border).
- Confirm any exceptional events (bank holidays, large one-off payments).

2) Collect bank data
- Automatically retrieve prior-day (camt.053/MT940/BAI2) and intraday (camt.052/MT942) statements for all accounts.
- Validate file completeness (all expected accounts/files received), timestamps, and controls (hash/acknowledgment).
- Log missing or late statements; trigger alerts to banks/IT.

3) Ingest expected cash flows
- Pull AP payment proposals and payment status, AR expected receipts/remittances, payroll funding schedules, tax payments, treasury settlements, merchant settlements.
- Normalize data to common templates (value date, amount, currency, status).

4) Build the cash position
- Calculate opening available balance per account/currency from prior-day EOD plus intraday movements.
- Adjust for in-transit items (e.g., uncleared checks, card settlement timing).
- Aggregate to entity and currency levels; compute net funding needs and headroom vs. limits.
- Highlight exceptions (negative balances, limit breaches, unexpected large variances).

5) Reconcile bank vs. book balances and transactions
- Auto-match bank transactions to ERP cash ledgers using rules (amount, date, reference, payer, check number).
- Identify unmatched items and categorize: timing differences, missing postings, duplicates, bank fees/interest, FX spreads, returns/chargebacks.
- Compare bank balance to book balance; calculate variances by account; apply tolerance thresholds.

6) Investigate and resolve variances
- Research unmatched items by collaborating with AP, AR, payroll, and accounting.
- Post missing journal entries (e.g., bank fees, interest, FX differences) with required approvals.
- Correct misapplied cash or duplicate postings; initiate chargeback handling and returned item workflows.
- For timing differences, document and monitor until cleared; update the open items aging.

7) Decide liquidity actions
- Based on the consolidated position, determine:
  - Amounts to concentrate/sweep between accounts and pools.
  - Borrowings/repayments on revolvers or in-house bank positions.
  - Short-term investments (e.g., overnight MMFs, term deposits) for surpluses.
  - FX conversions to fund currency shortfalls or reduce exposures.
- Prepare transfer instructions aligned with cut-offs and approval limits.

8) Approve and execute transfers
- Obtain dual approvals per policy for funding, investments, and FX.
- Execute via TMS payment hub or bank portals using STP; capture confirmations.
- Record deals/transfers in TMS/ERP; interface postings to GL.

9) Communicate and report
- Distribute the daily cash position report to stakeholders (treasury, finance leadership, AP/AR).
- Notify business units of funding decisions and any constraints.
- Update short-term cash forecast with actuals and revised assumptions.

10) End-of-day reconciliation and lock
- Perform a final intraday refresh (if applicable); ensure transfers settled as expected.
- Update reconciliation status; carry forward unresolved items with aging.
- Archive all statements, reports, and approvals; ensure audit trail completeness.

11) Period-end activities
- Perform full bank-to-book reconciliations with CFO/controller sign-off.
- Resolve aged items beyond policy thresholds; escalate persistent issues.
- Review bank fees, interest, and service quality vs. agreements.

Control points:
- Automated file completeness checks; exception alerts.
- Reconciliation tolerances and mandatory root-cause coding.
- Dual approval for transfers/investments/FX; daily segregation of duties review.
- Monthly reconciliation certification and management review.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Daily cash position report by account, currency, and entity.
- Bank-to-book reconciliation status with variance details and aging.
- List of executed transfers, investments, borrowings, and FX deals with confirmations.
- Journal entries for bank fees, interest, FX differences, and corrections.
- Exception and incident logs (missing statements, system outages).
- Updated short-term cash forecast.
- Period-end reconciliation package with sign-offs and supporting documentation.

Success criteria:
- Accurate, timely cash position enabling on-time payments and optimized liquidity.
- Same-day clearance of material variances; no unresolved high-risk items past policy.
- Minimal idle cash and minimized overdraft/interest costs.
- Complete, auditable records and adherence to approvals and policies.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Treasury Analyst
  - Retrieve bank data, prepare cash position, perform first-level reconciliation.
  - Investigate variances; propose journal entries and liquidity actions.
  - Prepare transfer instructions and supporting documentation.

- Cash/Treasury Manager
  - Review and approve cash position, variances, and proposed actions.
  - Approve transfers/investments/FX within limits; escalate as needed.
  - Ensure adherence to policies and cut-offs; communicate with stakeholders.

- AP Manager/Team
  - Provide payment schedules/status; resolve duplicate/missing payments.
  - Support variance investigation related to disbursements.

- AR Manager/Team
  - Provide remittance and lockbox details; accelerate cash application.
  - Resolve unapplied cash and chargebacks.

- Payroll Manager
  - Communicate payroll funding requirements and confirm settlement.

- GL/Accounting
  - Post and approve journal entries; maintain account mappings.
  - Perform month-end reconciliations and certifications.

- Treasury Operations Manager/Controller
  - Oversee process controls, policy compliance, and performance metrics.
  - Review aged items and approve period-end reconciliations.

- IT/Integration Support
  - Maintain bank connectivity and TMS/ERP interfaces; resolve data issues.
  - Monitor automation, security, and disaster recovery.

- Bank Relationship Manager (external)
  - Ensure statement availability, resolve bank-side errors, and optimize services.

## Best Practices
- Centralize bank connectivity using secure, automated channels (SWIFT, APIs) with ISO 20022 formats.
- Use a Treasury Management System with rules-based auto-reconciliation and STP to ERP/GL.
- Establish clear daily schedules and cut-offs across time zones; maintain holiday calendars.
- Implement cash pooling/zero-balancing to minimize idle balances; define target balances.
- Define reconciliation tolerances and root-cause categories; track aging and closures.
- Maintain strict segregation of duties and dual approvals; enforce entitlements reviews.
- Leverage virtual accounts and reference-rich remittances to improve matching rates.
- Monitor intraday liquidity for high-velocity accounts; set alert thresholds.
- Regularly review bank fees and service quality; benchmark and negotiate.
- Keep robust documentation and audit trails; retain artifacts per policy.
- Continuously feed actuals back into forecasting; measure and improve forecast accuracy.
- Test disaster recovery for bank connectivity and TMS at least annually.

## Common Challenges
- Missing or delayed bank statements
  - Mitigation: Redundant channels (primary API, fallback SWIFT/portal), automated alerts, bank SLAs.
- Low auto-match rates in reconciliation
  - Mitigation: Improve data quality (remittance info, virtual accounts), refine matching rules, collaborate with AR/AP.
- Timing differences causing persistent variances
  - Mitigation: Maintain expected clearing calendars; separate timing vs. true discrepancies; implement clearing accounts.
- Unapplied cash and merchant chargebacks
  - Mitigation: Speed AR cash application; integrate lockbox and merchant data; create dedicated exception workflows.
- FX and multi-currency complexities
  - Mitigation: Standardize value dating; pre-fund currency needs; automate FX rate application and deal capture.
- Manual errors and control breaches
  - Mitigation: Automate wherever possible; enforce dual approvals; periodic access reviews; training and SOPs.
- Integration and system outages
  - Mitigation: Data resiliency, retry logic, runbooks, RTO/RPO targets, and IT on-call support.
- Trapped cash in restricted jurisdictions
  - Mitigation: Local pooling, intercompany netting, evaluate permitted instruments; tax/legal consultation.

## Performance Metrics
- Timeliness and accuracy
  - Time to publish daily cash position (e.g., by 10:00 local).
  - Same-day reconciliation rate (% bank transactions matched same day).
  - Balance variance rate (absolute variance as % of ending balance).

- Control effectiveness
  - Number of reconciling items aged > 7/30 days.
  - Transfer error rate and exception count.
  - Policy compliance rate (dual approvals, cut-offs met).

- Liquidity optimization
  - Idle cash vs. target (daily average).
  - Intraday overdraft duration/fees.
  - Cost of carry (net interest expense on cash and short-term debt).
  - Cash concentration rate (% of cash in pools vs. total).

- Process efficiency
  - STP rate from bank statements to reconciliation.
  - Analyst hours per cycle.
  - Forecast accuracy for 1–7 day horizons.

- ERP and Cash Management: SAP S/4HANA, Oracle Cloud ERP, Microsoft Dynamics 365, NetSuite.

- Reconciliation and Close: BlackLine, Trintech Cadency, Oracle ARCS, ERP-native bank recon modules.
- Payment Hubs and Gateways: Bottomline, Serrala, FIS, Finastra, Coupa Pay.
- FX and Money Market Platforms: FXall, 360T, Bloomberg, Refinitiv; MMF portals (e.g., ICD).
- Analytics and Reporting: Power BI, Tableau, embedded TMS dashboards.
- Security and Governance: MFA/SSO, PAM solutions for privileged access, audit trail and e-signature tools.
- Alerting and Automation: RPA (UiPath, Automation Anywhere), workflow engines, integration platforms (MuleSoft, Boomi).

Process Details:
## Overview
Calculate interest and fees for in-house bank (IHB) accounts is the recurring process of determining, booking, communicating, and settling all interest and fee charges related to the internal banking services provided by the corporate in-house bank to group entities. It covers debit and credit interest on internal current accounts and cash pools, overdraft and facility fees, payment and account service fees, FX conversion spreads, and other treasury service charges. The process ensures:

- Accurate accruals and postings in the general ledger and intercompany subledgers
- Arm’s-length transfer pricing and tax compliance
- Transparent cost and value allocation for liquidity services
- Timely settlement and reconciliation with entities and consolidation

This process is a core revenue/expense and cost recovery mechanism for the in-house bank, directly impacting liquidity optimization, P&L, intercompany balances, and statutory and management reporting.

## Key Activities
- Define and maintain rate curves and fee schedules aligned to transfer pricing policy
- Capture and validate value-dated balances by account, currency, and product (e.g., pool participant, header account, intercompany loan)
- Calculate daily interest accruals using approved day-count conventions and compounding rules
- Allocate pool interest for notional and physical cash pools to participants
- Compute non-interest fees (payment processing, account maintenance, overdraft, facility/commitment, service, FX spread)
- Review exceptions and resolve data or method discrepancies
- Post accruals and period-end true-ups to GL and intercompany ledgers
- Generate account statements, fee notes, and IC invoices/settlement instructions
- Perform reconciliations and analytical review against benchmarks and budgets
- Facilitate settlement/netting and manage FX conversions for cross-currency settlements

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Account master data: in-house bank accounts, legal entity, currency, product type, pool membership, value date rules
- Balance data: start/end balances, intra-day and value-dated transactions, cash pool zero-balances, notional pool contributions
- Rate data: internal transfer pricing curves (e.g., SOFR/EURIBOR/SONIA + margin), base/debit/credit rates, floors/caps, tiered schedules
- Fee schedules: payment fees (per transaction/volume tier), account service fees, overdraft/line utilization, commitment fees, FX spreads, maintenance fees
- Conventions: day-count (ACT/360, ACT/365F, 30/360), business day calendars, compounding/averaging rules, rounding and de minimis thresholds
- Policies: transfer pricing policy, arm’s-length documentation, tax/WHT rules, intercompany agreements, negative interest policy
- Market data: benchmarks, FX rates, holiday calendars
- Prior period carry-forwards: unbilled fees, accruals, adjustments

Prerequisites:
- Approved and current rate/fee configurations in TMS/ERP
- Legal intercompany agreements (accounts, facilities, pricing) in place
- Closed cash positioning and pool sweeps for the calculation window
- Data quality checks passed (balances, value dates, currency codes)
- Segregation of duties and defined approval workflows

Dependencies on other processes:
- 9.7.3.1/9.7.3.2 Manage in-house bank master data and cash pooling
- 9.7.1 Manage market data and internal transfer pricing
- 9.7.3.5 Post and reconcile in-house bank transactions
- 9.7.4 Manage intercompany settlements and netting
- 9.6 General accounting and period close
- 9.5 Tax and transfer pricing compliance

## Process Steps
1) Plan and prepare
- Confirm calculation calendar (daily accruals, monthly billing/settlement dates, period close timelines).
- Lock rate curves and fee schedules for the billing period. Capture any mid-period changes with effective dates.
- Communicate any policy changes (e.g., new margins, floors) to stakeholders.

2) Gather and validate data
- Extract value-dated balances per account/currency/day for the period from TMS/ERP; include pool header and participant accounts.
- For physical pools (zero-balancing): confirm target balance and end-of-day sweeps; for notional pools: obtain bank pool interest and participant contributions.
- Validate data: completeness, outliers, negative balances vs. product rules, back-valued transactions. Resolve exceptions with cash ops.

3) Determine calculation method per account/product
- Current/internal accounts: simple daily accrual on EOD or value-dated balances.
- Overdraft lines: apply overdraft rate/margin and line utilization; calculate commitment fee on undrawn portions.
- Physical cash pools: allocate header account lending/borrowing interest to participants based on intraday or EOD balances per policy.
- Notional cash pools: allocate bank-paid or internal pool interest to participants using chosen allocation method (e.g., pro-rata average balances, marginal contribution).
- Intercompany revolving facilities: use floating index + margin with floors/caps and appropriate compounding rules.

4) Retrieve rates and conventions
- Pull base rates (e.g., 1M/3M tenors) or overnight where applicable; interpolate/average if using daily averages.
- Add approved margins by entity/risk class and product (credit interest margin may differ from debit).
- Apply day-count convention and business day adjustments (following, modified following).

5) Calculate interest
- Simple daily accrual (typical for current accounts): interest_d = principal_d × annual_rate_d × (day_count_fraction_d). Accumulate over the period.
- Compounded (if applicable): apply compounding frequency (e.g., daily compounded SOFR) per policy.
- Apply floors/caps and negative rate rules (e.g., floor at 0 for credit interest).
- Round per currency rules; apply de minimis thresholds.

6) Allocate pool interest
- Compute pool interest at header or using bank statement for notional pools.
- Choose allocation basis:
  - Pro-rata by average balance: allocated_i = pool_interest × avg_balance_i / Σ avg_balance
  - Marginal contribution method: allocate based on incremental benefit contribution.
- Document and store allocation factors for audit.

7) Calculate fees
- Payment processing fees: per transaction or volume tier by channel/type (e.g., wires, SEPA, ACH).
- Account service fees: monthly flat or per account.
- Overdraft/line utilization fees: percentage of utilized amount; commitment fees on undrawn lines.
- FX conversion spread: notional × spread; or differential vs. mid-rate.
- Other services: bank guarantee administration, loan admin fees as per schedule.

8) Review and approval
- Run variance analytics vs. prior period and budget; investigate significant swings (rate changes, volume spikes).
- Review exception reports: negative credit interest if disallowed, missing rates, out-of-policy allocations.
- Obtain approvals per threshold (e.g., >10% variance, manual overrides). Maintain audit trail.

9) Post accounting entries
- Accruals (periodic, often daily with month-end true-up):
  - For entities with debit balances (interest expense):
    - Dr Interest expense (P&L) / Fees expense
    - Cr Intercompany payable to IHB
  - For entities with credit balances (interest income):
    - Dr Intercompany receivable from IHB
    - Cr Interest income (P&L)
  - Mirror entries on IHB books (income/expense reversed).
- Record FX remeasurement for foreign currency balances at month-end.
- Post WHT where applicable and recognized.

10) Communicate statements and invoices
- Generate account statements detailing daily balances, interest calculations, fees, and allocation notes.
- Issue IC invoices/credit notes where statutory invoicing is required; include tax information and WHT where applicable.
- Provide transparency on rate sources, conventions, and any adjustments.

11) Settle and net
- Include net interest and fees in intercompany netting cycle or settle via internal payment on agreed dates.
- Convert currency at settlement rate per policy; hedge if material exposures arise.

12) Reconcile and close
- Reconcile GL and IC subledgers to the calculation engine outputs and statements.
- Tie out pool allocations to bank’s notional pool statement (for externally hosted pools).
- Resolve breaks and post adjusting entries; lock period; archive calculation artifacts.

13) Continuous improvement
- Collect metrics and exceptions; refine rate curves, allocation methods, and fee schedules.
- Review transfer pricing compliance annually and adjust margins/structures as needed.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Calculated interest and fee amounts by account/entity/currency and period
- Accounting postings: accruals, true-ups, WHT, FX remeasurements
- Participant statements and IC invoices/credit notes
- Settlement instructions/netting files
- Reconciliations and exception logs
- Management reports: pool yields, NIM, cost recovery rates, variances
- Audit-ready documentation: rate sources, conventions, approvals, allocation methodology

Success criteria:
- 100% of eligible accounts calculated and posted by cutoff
- Variances within defined thresholds; immaterial true-ups at close
- Zero unreconciled differences between GL, subledger, and statements
- Compliance with transfer pricing policy and audit requirements

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Treasury Operations (IHB Operations)
  - Owns end-to-end calculation process, data validation, postings, and statements
  - Manages exceptions and coordinates with entities
- Treasury Front Office / ALM
  - Provides benchmark rate sources, approves internal curves and margins
  - Advises on liquidity pricing and pool structures
- Transfer Pricing/Tax
  - Defines arm’s-length methodologies, WHT applicability, documentation
  - Reviews annual pricing and ensures regulatory compliance
- Intercompany Accounting / GL Accounting
  - Posts accruals/settlements, performs reconciliations, manages IC netting
  - Ensures proper FX and WHT accounting
- Local Entity Finance/Cash Managers
  - Review statements, validate charges, approve settlements, raise disputes
- Risk/Compliance/Internal Audit
  - Reviews controls, segregation of duties, and audit trails
- TMS/ERP Administration / IT
  - Maintains calculation engines, master data, integrations, calendars
  - Ensures performance, access controls, and change management

## Best Practices
- Automate daily accruals with value-dated balances and locked conventions
- Maintain centralized rate and fee repositories with effective dates and approvals
- Use standardized day-count and business day rules by currency; document exceptions
- Separate physical and notional pool allocation methodologies; review annually
- Apply clear negative interest policies and floors/caps; prevent unintended outcomes
- Implement tolerance-based exception reporting and 4-eyes review on overrides
- Align fee schedules to service cost and market benchmarks; review at least annually
- Provide transparent participant statements with methodology disclosures
- Integrate with IC netting and settlement to minimize intercompany float
- Maintain strong SOX/ICFR controls: access, change management, reconciliations, audit trail

## Common Challenges
- Data quality issues (back-valued transactions, missing value dates)
  - Mitigation: enforce cutoff rules, automated data validations, and exception workflows
- Mid-period rate changes or benchmark transitions (e.g., IBOR to RFR)
  - Mitigation: effective-dated rates, compounding support, parallel runs during transitions
- Negative interest environments and floors impacting allocations
  - Mitigation: explicit policies and system configuration for floors/caps
- Complex notional pool allocations and disputes from entities
  - Mitigation: clear documented allocation method, participant transparency, periodic education
- Cross-border tax/WHT and transfer pricing scrutiny
  - Mitigation: robust documentation, periodic benchmarking, and tax advisory review
- FX volatility impacting settlement amounts
  - Mitigation: hedge policies, settlement in functional currency where feasible, timely netting
- System limitations or manual workarounds
  - Mitigation: invest in TMS capabilities, RPA for low-risk tasks, rigorous change control

## Performance Metrics
- Timeliness:
  - Percentage of accounts calculated and posted by T+1 and month-end cutoff
  - Average cycle time from period end to statement issuance
- Accuracy/Quality:
  - Number of exceptions per 100 accounts
  - Accrual-to-actual variance (%) and absolute value
  - Reconciliation breaks count and aging
- Efficiency:
  - Automation rate (% of calculations performed automatically)
  - Manual adjustments per period
- Financial performance:
  - Net interest margin (IHB interest income – expense) vs. target
  - Pool yield vs. benchmark (e.g., O/N RFR)
  - Cost recovery ratio for fees (% of treasury service cost recovered)
- Compliance/Control:
  - Percentage of rates/fees with documented approvals
  - Audit findings related to this process (count, severity)

  - Examples: SAP Treasury and Risk Management (IHC/In-House Cash), SAP S/4HANA Cash Management, Kyriba, FIS Integrity/Quantum, Serrala

Process Details:
## Overview
Manage issuer exposure is the treasury process that controls, measures, and optimizes the organization’s credit exposure to individual issuers (borrowers) across all investment and lending activities. When the organization buys bonds, commercial paper, places bank deposits, enters into repos, or engages in OTC derivatives, it is effectively extending credit to the issuer/counterparty. This process ensures exposures stay within approved risk appetite, concentration limits, regulatory constraints, and liquidity needs while supporting yield objectives.

Role in the organization:
- Protects capital by preventing excessive concentration to any single issuer, corporate group, sector, or country.
- Enables compliant investment execution via pre-trade and post-trade limit controls.
- Provides early warning and remediation plans for deteriorating credits.
- Supplies accurate exposure and provisioning data to finance, risk, ALCO, and regulators.

Scope:
- Instruments: Bonds, notes, commercial paper (CP), certificates of deposit (CDs), time deposits, repos/reverse repos, OTC derivatives (and PFE), money market funds (look-through), structured products (where possible).
- Risk dimensions: Single-name issuer, ultimate parent group, sector/industry, country, rating bucket/score, maturity buckets, secured vs unsecured, collateralized vs uncollateralized.

## Key Activities
- Define and maintain issuer exposure policies and limits (per issuer, group, sector, country, ratings, tenor).
- Onboard and maintain issuer master data and hierarchies (entity, LEI, ultimate parent, affiliations).
- Perform pre-trade eligibility screens and limit checks.
- Aggregate and calculate exposure including netting, collateral, and potential future exposure (PFE) for derivatives.
- Monitor ongoing credit quality (ratings, CDS spreads, financials), watchlists, and triggers.
- Identify, escalate, and remediate limit breaches or deteriorating credits.
- Conduct stress testing and concentration analysis across portfolios.
- Manage exceptions and approvals with documented rationale and time-bounded actions.
- Report exposure, concentration metrics, breaches, and trends to stakeholders (Front Office, Risk, ALCO).
- Feed expected credit loss (ECL/CECL) and impairment processes with accurate exposure and staging data.
- Periodically review and recalibrate limits and assumptions.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Risk appetite statement, treasury investment policy, counterparty/issuer limit framework.
- Issuer master data: legal names, LEIs, ratings, industry codes, domicile, ultimate parent mappings.
- Credit information: external ratings (S&P/Moody’s/Fitch), internal scores, financial statements, CDS/market spreads, ESG where applicable.
- Legal documentation: investment guidelines, ISDA/CSA, repo GMRAs, deposit agreements, netting opinions.
- Transaction and position data: holdings, trade blotter, cash balances, collateral positions, derivatives exposures.
- Regulatory constraints: large exposure rules, concentration limits, sanction lists, eligible instruments.
- Systems access: TMS/OMS, risk engines, market data feeds, limit management tools.

Prerequisites:
- Approved policy and limit structures and governance (including approval authorities and escalation matrix).
- Data governance and MDM for issuers and hierarchies.
- Integrated pre-trade and post-trade limit checking capability.
- Defined methodologies for exposure calculations (EAD, PFE, netting, collateral haircuts).
- Clear documentation standards and audit trail requirements.

Dependencies on other processes:
- Set treasury risk appetite and policy [9.7].
- Manage investment portfolio execution [9.7.4].
- Counterparty/credit approval and internal rating assignment.
- Market data management and pricing services.
- Collateral management and margining.
- Financial close and reporting (ECL/CECL, impairments).
- Regulatory compliance, sanctions screening, and KYC/AML.

## Process Steps
1. Establish and review policy and limits
   - Define/affirm issuer, group, sector, and country limits; rating-based caps; tenor buckets; secured/unsecured distinctions.
   - Obtain approvals from Credit Committee/ALCO; publish in the limit management system.

2. Maintain issuer master and hierarchies
   - Onboard issuers with LEI, legal entity hierarchy, ultimate parent mapping, sector and country.
   - Validate sanctions, eligibility, and KYC where required.

3. Calibrate exposure methodology
   - Document formulas for current exposure, EAD, PFE (derivatives), netting, collateral haircuts, and look-through for funds.
   - Configure in risk engine; back-test and validate.

4. Pre-trade eligibility screen
   - Front Office selects candidate issuer/instrument.
   - System verifies eligibility: policy-compliant instrument, maturity/tenor within buckets, minimum rating/internal score, documentation in place.

5. Pre-trade limit check
   - Aggregate real-time exposure by issuer and group (including pending trades).
   - Compare to available headroom across all applicable limits (name, group, sector, country, tenor).
   - If within limits, proceed; if not, trigger exception workflow.

6. Exception handling (if needed)
   - Route to Credit Risk and delegated approvers for variance approval with specific conditions (size cap, tenor reduction, collateral, time-bounded).
   - Record rationale and expiry; adjust limits or place temporary override in the system.

7. Trade execution and capture
   - Execute the approved transaction.
   - Capture trade in TMS/OMS; ensure straight-through processing (STP) to risk engine and position systems.

8. Post-trade exposure aggregation
   - Recalculate exposure with latest positions, netting agreements, collateral, and PFE updates.
   - Update utilization across all applicable limits; flag breaches immediately.

9. Ongoing surveillance and triggers
   - Monitor ratings changes, outlooks, CDS/credit spreads, price moves, covenant breaches, earnings/news, ESG events.
   - Maintain watchlist; assign surveillance frequency by risk tier.

10. Stress testing and concentration analysis
    - Run periodic issuer/group/sector/country stress tests (spread widening, downgrade waves, default clustering).
    - Assess HHI and top-10 concentration metrics; simulate management actions.

11. Breach and deterioration management
    - For limit breaches or adverse triggers, execute mitigation options: no new purchases, partial sell-down, hedges (CDS), reduce tenor, increase collateral, transfer exposure.
    - Escalate per RACI; document actions and timeline.

12. Provisioning and impairment support
    - Provide accurate exposure and staging inputs to ECL/CECL models.
    - Record impairment recognition decisions and link to exposure records.

13. Reporting and governance
    - Produce daily/weekly dashboards: exposures, utilizations, breaches, watchlists, concentration metrics.
    - Present to ALCO/Credit Committee as scheduled; capture decisions and policy changes.

14. Periodic limit and model review
    - Quarterly/semi-annual limit recalibration based on performance, macro outlook, and stress results.
    - Validate exposure models; remediate findings from Risk/Internal Audit.

15. Recordkeeping and audit
    - Maintain full audit trail: approvals, overrides, data lineage, calculations, reports.
    - Ensure retention and access controls per policy.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Exposure dashboards by issuer, group, sector, country, rating, tenor.
- Limit registers and utilization reports; exception/override logs with expiry and conditions.
- Watchlists and issuer surveillance memos; early warning indicators.
- Stress test results and concentration analyses (HHI, top-10 exposures).
- Action plans and execution evidence for breaches/deteriorations (sell-downs, hedges, collateral changes).
- Inputs to ECL/CECL and impairment accounting; reconciled exposure files for Finance.
- ALCO/Credit Committee packs and minutes.
- Audit-ready documentation and data lineage.

Success criteria:
- No unauthorized limit breaches; all exceptions documented and within delegated authority.
- Concentration metrics within policy thresholds.
- Timely detection and remediation of deteriorating credits.
- Accurate, reconciled exposure figures feeding finance and regulatory reports.
- High STP rate for pre-trade checks and post-trade aggregation.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Treasurer/Head of Treasury: Own policy execution; ensure compliance and resources; chair escalation as needed.
- Front Office (Portfolio/Investment Managers, Dealers): Initiate trades; perform pre-trade checks; adhere to limits; propose exceptions with justification.
- Credit Risk Management: Set/approve limits; maintain internal ratings; monitor credit developments; lead breach remediation plans.
- Risk Analytics/Quant: Maintain exposure/PFE models, stress testing, and back-testing; support methodology updates.
- Middle Office/Treasury Operations: Trade capture quality; exposure aggregation; control monitoring; reporting; breach flagging.
- Collateral Management: Manage CSA/GMRA agreements; margin calls; collateral valuation and haircuts.
- Compliance/Regulatory: Sanctions screening; large exposure and policy compliance reviews.
- Data Management/MDM: Maintain issuer master, hierarchies, LEIs, and data quality controls.
- ALCO/Credit Committee: Approve policies and limits; review reports; decide on escalated cases.
- Internal Audit: Periodic audits of process design, controls, data, and governance.

## Best Practices
- Use a single source of truth for issuer hierarchies and LEIs; map to ultimate parents and groups.
- Integrate pre-trade limit checks into the OMS/TMS for real-time headroom validation and STP.
- Combine external ratings with internal credit scores and market-implied measures (CDS, spreads) for surveillance.
- Implement multi-dimensional limits (issuer, group, sector, country, rating, tenor) with aggregation across legal entities and books.
- Apply look-through for funds and securitizations where data allows; otherwise impose conservative caps.
- Distinguish secured vs unsecured exposures; incorporate collateral and netting benefits rigorously with legal opinions.
- Define automated early warning indicators and watchlist criteria; increase surveillance cadence for higher-risk names.
- Perform regular scenario and reverse stress testing for concentration and downgrade risks.
- Time-bound and conditional exceptions; avoid “evergreen” overrides; auto-expire and review.
- Maintain robust documentation and audit trails for all approvals, calculations, and reports.

## Common Challenges
- Data quality and issuer hierarchy mapping errors leading to under-reported group exposure.
  - Solution: MDM governance, LEI adoption, automated parent mapping with manual overrides and controls.
- Fragmented systems causing delayed or inconsistent exposure aggregation.
  - Solution: Integrate risk engine with TMS/OMS; near-real-time data feeds; reconciliation controls.
- Measuring derivatives PFE consistently across products and CSAs.
  - Solution: Standardized models (e.g., SA-CCR where applicable), validated parameters, and daily back-testing.
- Limited look-through for funds or structured products.
  - Solution: Require transparency from managers; apply conservative exposure caps when data is incomplete.
- Frequent rating downgrades/market volatility triggering repeated breaches.
  - Solution: Dynamic headroom buffers, proactive de-risking triggers, playbooks for rapid actions.
- Governance bottlenecks in exception approvals.
  - Solution: Clear delegation matrices, digital workflows, SLAs, and dashboards for pending approvals.

## Performance Metrics
- Limit management:
  - Number of limit breaches (unauthorized vs authorized), and average time to remediation.
  - Percentage of exposure under temporary exceptions and average duration.
- Concentration:
  - Top-10 issuer exposure as % of portfolio; HHI concentration index.
  - Exposure by sector/country vs policy thresholds.
- Credit quality and surveillance:
  - Weighted average rating/internal score of portfolio; migration/downgrade rates.
  - Watchlist additions/removals; time from trigger to action.
- Process efficiency and control:
  - Pre-trade check STP rate; latency from trade to exposure update.
  - Data reconciliation breaks and resolution time.
- Risk and loss outcomes:
  - ECL/CECL coverage ratio accuracy (back-testing error).
  - Credit loss incidents vs risk appetite; stressed loss vs limits.

Targets should be set by risk appetite and regulatory context.

## Technology and Tools
- Treasury/Investment Systems: TMS/OMS (e.g., SAP TRM, Kyriba, SimCorp Dimension, Charles River) with integrated limit checks.
- Risk Engines: Murex, Calypso/Adenza, Moody’s RiskAuthority/RiskFrontier, QRM, or in-house for exposure/PFE and stress testing.
- Market and Reference Data: Bloomberg/Refinitiv for prices and CDS; rating feeds (S&P/Moody’s/Fitch); GLEIF for LEIs; D&B/FactSet for hierarchies.
- Limit and Workflow Management: Dedicated limit engines, GRC tools (e.g., MetricStream), or custom workflow with role-based approvals.
- Collateral and Agreements: Collateral management systems; document repositories for ISDA/CSA/GMRA and netting opinions.
- BI and Reporting: Power BI/Tableau/Qlik; data warehouse/lakehouse for aggregation and lineage.
- Alerting and Surveillance: Automated alerts on ratings changes, spread moves, news sentiment; watchlist management tools.
- Data Quality and MDM: Tools for entity resolution, hierarchy management, and data validation rules.

This end-to-end process ensures the organization prudently allocates investments and credit, maintains compliance and resilience, and supports strategic liquidity and yield objectives while controlling issuer concentration risk.

# [9.7.4.7] Produce debt and investment accounting transaction reports

## Overview
This process creates and maintains the accounting transaction reports for the organization’s debt and investment portfolios. It compiles all accounting-relevant events (e.g., trades, principal movements, interest accruals, fees, amortization, mark-to-market, FX translation, impairment) into accurate, reconciled, and approved reports for use by Treasury, Accounting/Controllership, FP&A, Risk, Compliance, and Audit.

Purpose:
- Provide timely, audit-ready transaction detail supporting the general ledger (GL), management reporting, regulatory filings, lender reporting, and treasury decision-making.
- Evidence the completeness and accuracy of accounting for loans, debt instruments, securities, and derivatives under applicable accounting policies (e.g., IFRS or US GAAP).
- Enable traceability from front-office activity through sub-ledger and into the GL, with clear reconciliations and exception management.

Role in the organization:
- Integral to period-end close and financial statement integrity.
- Supports liquidity and investment oversight by explaining P&L and balance sheet movements.
- Provides control evidence for SOX and internal audit over treasury accounting and reporting.

## Key Activities
- Gather and integrate transactional data from source systems (TMS/IMS/ERP, bank/custodian, market data).
- Apply accounting policies and mappings (e.g., classification, measurement, hedge accounting designations).
- Calculate accounting impacts (accruals, amortization, EIR, realized/unrealized gains/losses, FX, impairment).
- Generate transaction-level reports and journal-entry listings by instrument, counterparty, account, and period.
- Perform sub-ledger to GL reconciliations, variance analysis, and exception remediation.
- Obtain management review and approvals; distribute reports to stakeholders.
- Archive workpapers and maintain an audit trail; feed continuous improvement.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs:
  - Trade and position data for debt and investments (front-office/trade capture, trade blotters).
  - Master data: instrument terms, counterparties, legal entities, chart of accounts (CoA), product/account mapping rules.
  - Cash movements: bank statements, custodian statements, loan agent notices, confirmations.
  - Market data: prices, yield curves, credit spreads, FX rates; corporate actions.
  - Prior-period balances and amortization schedules (premiums/discounts, deferred financing costs).
  - Hedge documentation and effectiveness results if hedge accounting is applied.
  - Accounting policies (IFRS/US GAAP), materiality thresholds, close calendar.
- Prerequisites:
  - Upstream processes completed: trade capture/validation, position reconciliation, valuation/impairment runs, master data updates.
  - Period status open for reporting; data interfaces completed (no failed jobs).
  - Access rights and segregation of duties configured (maker/checker, approvals).
  - COA mappings validated; latest FX/market data locked for the reporting date.
- Dependencies on other processes:
  - 9.7.4 Manage debt and investment (trade lifecycle, master data, valuations, hedge accounting).
  - 9.7.2 Treasury cash management (bank reconciliations).
  - 9.3 General accounting and reporting (GL posting, period close, consolidations).
  - 9.5 Financial reporting (external/internal reporting requirements).
  - Risk and compliance monitoring for investment limits and covenants.

## Process Steps
1) Plan and schedule
- Confirm reporting calendar (daily, monthly, quarter-end, year-end); identify cutoffs for trades, cash, market data.
- Communicate dependencies and deadlines with front office, valuations, and cash ops.
- Control: publish runbook; assign maker/checker; confirm approvals required.

2) Data extraction and staging
- Pull transactional data from TMS/IMS/ERP and custodians/banks for the reporting window.
- Load market data (closing prices, curves, FX) for the valuation date.
- Stage prior-period amortization balances and schedules.
- Control: completeness checks vs. prior day/period, position counts, and external statements.

3) Data validation and enrichment
- Validate master data (instrument terms, coupon schedules, day count conventions, payment calendars).
- Validate COA mappings and accounting classifications (amortized cost vs FVOCI/FVTPL; ASC 320/321/815/825 analogs).
- Enrich with hedge designations, effectiveness results, and documentation references.
- Flag gaps (e.g., missing ISIN, counterparty LEI) and route exceptions.

4) Compute accounting impacts
- Accruals: interest income/expense, accretion/discount amortization using EIR.
- Amortization: premiums/discounts; deferred financing costs; fees per policy.
- Realized results: sales, maturities, prepayments, early extinguishments, break costs.
- Unrealized results: MTM and OCI/FV changes per classification; hedge ineffectiveness.
- FX: remeasurement/translation for foreign currency instruments.
- Impairment: ECL (IFRS 9) or CECL (US GAAP) where applicable.
- Control: lock valuation inputs; document key assumptions and parameter versions.

5) Generate journal entries and transaction records
- Produce JE lines at instrument, account, and legal-entity level per mapping rules.
- Tag with source identifiers (trade ID, deal number, ledger, cost center, project).
- Separate realized vs unrealized, P&L vs OCI vs balance sheet.

6) Reconcile and analyze
- Sub-ledger to GL reconciliation: by account and instrument; identify and explain differences.
- Cash tie-outs: link interest/principal cash flows to bank/custodian statements.
- Variance analysis: period-over-period movements; threshold-based investigation.
- Control: document reconciling items with owners and target resolution dates.

7) Report production
- Transaction registers: detailed listings by instrument/portfolio with JE lines.
- Accrual and amortization schedules by instrument and account.
- Realized/unrealized gain/loss reports; FX impact reports.
- Debt-specific: interest expense rollforward, principal movement register, deferred financing cost amortization.
- Investment-specific: trade blotter accounting view, income accruals, corporate actions accounting.
- Hedge accounting: effectiveness results, hedge accounting entries, OCI rollforward.
- Sub-ledger to GL reconciliation reports and exception logs.
- Management summaries and drilldown packs (entity/portfolio/counterparty).
- Control: version and timestamp each report; mark as preliminary/final.

8) Review and approval
- Maker checks completeness and ties to control totals; checker performs independent review.
- Resolve exceptions or raise adjusting entries per materiality thresholds.
- Obtain management sign-off (Treasury Accounting Manager/Controller).
- Control: approvals recorded in workflow tool; retain evidence.

9) Distribution and publication
- Distribute per distribution list and schedule; publish to secure repository/BI portal.
- Provide data extracts to downstream consumers (FP&A, regulatory reporting, tax).

10) Archival and audit readiness
- Archive reports, workpapers, reconciliations, and data snapshots in retention system.
- Maintain data lineage and change logs.
- Update process metrics and issues log for continuous improvement.

11) Continuous improvement
- Root-cause analysis of recurring exceptions; update mappings/policies.
- Automate manual steps (RPA/ETL); refine data quality rules.
- Review and update control design, thresholds, and templates.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Outputs:
  - Transaction-level accounting reports for debt and investments (accruals, amortizations, gains/losses, FX, impairment).
  - Journal entry listings and posting files (where applicable).
  - Sub-ledger to GL reconciliation reports with documented breaks.
  - Hedge accounting reports (if applicable) and OCI rollforwards.
  - Exception logs and variance analysis.
- Deliverables:
  - Management summary pack with key movements and explanations.
  - Certified close workpapers with maker/checker approvals.
  - Data extracts for FP&A, regulatory reporting, and audit.
- Success criteria:
  - Reports delivered on time per calendar; reconciled to GL with no unexplained variances.
  - Accuracy and completeness thresholds met; zero material post-close adjustments.
  - Audit-ready documentation with clear lineage and approvals.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Treasury Accounting Analyst (Maker)
  - Run data pulls, compute accounting impacts, prepare reports, compile workpapers.
- Treasury Accounting Supervisor/Manager (Checker/Approver)
  - Review and approve reports, reconciliations, and adjustments; ensure policy compliance.
- Investment Accounting Specialist
  - Oversee investment classification, income recognition, corporate actions, and impairment.
- Debt Accountant
  - Manage debt rollforwards, interest expense, deferred costs, and covenant-related disclosures.
- Valuation/Risk Analyst
  - Provide and validate valuations, market data, and hedge effectiveness results.
- Treasury Operations
  - Ensure completeness of trade capture, confirmations, and cash postings.
- Controllership/GL Accounting
  - Post entries, manage period close, and resolve GL issues.
- Compliance/Internal Audit
  - Review control adherence, perform testing, and provide findings.
- IT/Data Management
  - Maintain systems, integrations, data quality rules, security, and access controls.
- FP&A/Treasury Front Office (Consumers)
  - Consume reports for analysis and decision-making; provide feedback.

## Best Practices
- Establish a standardized close calendar with clear cutoffs, responsibilities, and SLAs.
- Use a golden source for market data; lock valuation inputs for each reporting date.
- Maintain robust COA mapping governance with change control and testing.
- Implement maker-checker approvals and segregation of duties for all critical steps.
- Automate data ingestion, calculations, and reconciliations; minimize spreadsheets.
- Maintain an auditable data lineage from trade to GL; include versioning and timestamps.
- Use threshold-based exception management and root-cause analysis for recurring breaks.
- Support multi-GAAP/Multi-entity reporting with configurable accounting rules.
- Keep comprehensive documentation: policies, runbooks, SOPs, and reconciliation playbooks.
- Periodically benchmark and validate models (EIR, impairment, hedge effectiveness).

## Common Challenges
- Incomplete or late trade/cash data
  - Mitigation: enforce cutoffs, near-real-time interfaces, exception dashboards, escalation paths.
- Mapping errors and master data quality issues
  - Mitigation: centralized master data management, mapping validation tests, maker/checker for changes.
- Valuation inconsistencies (prices, curves, FX)
  - Mitigation: single golden source, input locks, tolerance checks against prior periods.
- Complex instruments and hedge accounting
  - Mitigation: specialized accounting engines, expert review, clear documentation, periodic training.
- Corporate actions processing errors
  - Mitigation: automated event feeds, dual verification, and post-event reconciliations.
- Multi-GAAP/Entity reporting complexity
  - Mitigation: rules-based accounting engines and parallel ledgers.
- Reconciliation breaks and timing differences
  - Mitigation: standardized recon templates, aging of breaks, root-cause tracking and SLAs.
- Manual processes and spreadsheet risk
  - Mitigation: automation (ETL/RPA), access-controlled templates, and audit trails.
- Period-end time pressure
  - Mitigation: pre-close dry runs, flash reporting, prioritization based on materiality.

## Performance Metrics
- Timeliness: percentage of reports delivered by SLA (e.g., T+1 by 9:00 AM local).
- Accuracy: percentage of transactions without post-close adjustments; error rate per 1,000 lines.
- Completeness: sub-ledger to GL reconciliation breaks as a percentage of balance; number of unmatched trades/cash items.
- Exception management: count and aging of open exceptions; average resolution time.
- Automation level: percentage of transactions processed straight-through (no manual touch).
- Cycle time: end-to-end processing time from cutoff to approved reports.
- Audit/control health: number of control failures; audit findings and severity.
- Data quality: failed validation checks per run; mapping changes causing errors.
- Stakeholder satisfaction: survey scores from Controllership, FP&A, and Treasury.

- ERP/GL: SAP S/4HANA, Oracle Cloud ERP, Microsoft Dynamics.
- Hedge/Derivatives Accounting: ChathamDirect, ION Reval, FINCAD.
- Reconciliation and Close: BlackLine, Trintech Cadency, OneStream/Hyperion for consolidation support.
- Data Integration/ETL and EDM: Informatica, Fivetran, Azure Data Factory; GoldenSource/SmartCo for securities master.
- BI/Reporting: Power BI, Tableau, Qlik; secure portals for distribution.

- Document Management and Workflow: ServiceNow/Jira for issues, SharePoint/Documentum for workpapers and approvals.

Process Details:
## Overview
Develop risk management/hedging strategy is the process of defining how the organization will mitigate market risks (e.g., interest rate, foreign exchange, commodity, inflation) that could impact earnings, cash flows, balance sheet values, liquidity, and covenants. It sets the objectives, scope, instruments, hedge ratios, tenors, and governance under which hedges will be executed and maintained. The strategy aligns economic risk reduction with policy, accounting, tax, liquidity, and regulatory constraints and provides the executable mandate for subsequent hedge execution, monitoring, and reporting.

This process sits within treasury operations and interfaces tightly with planning/forecasting, debt and capital structure management, liquidity management, financial reporting, and risk governance. It ensures the organization proactively manages exposures, reduces P&L and cash flow volatility, preserves borrowing capacity, and supports predictable financial outcomes.

## Key Activities
- Define risk appetite and objectives
  - Translate board/CFO risk appetite into target risk metrics (e.g., EaR/CFaR thresholds) and coverage levels by risk type and horizon.
- Exposure identification and aggregation
  - Catalog existing and forecast exposures (balance sheet, cash flows, committed/uncommitted) across currencies, rates, commodities, and geographies; net at the enterprise level.
- Risk measurement and diagnostics
  - Quantify baseline risk using models (e.g., DV01, VaR, EaR/CFaR), scenario and stress tests; identify material risk drivers and basis risks.
- Strategy design
  - Select hedging approaches (natural hedging, static/dynamic hedging, layering/rolling), instruments (forwards, swaps, options, futures), hedge ratios, tenors, and triggers.
- Accounting and tax alignment
  - Determine hedge accounting designations (IFRS 9/ASC 815), documentation, effectiveness methodology, and tax implications.
- Counterparty, liquidity, and collateral considerations
  - Ensure counterparty capacity, CSA requirements, liquidity impact, and regulatory compliance are addressed.
- Governance and approvals
  - Draft the strategy paper, obtain reviews (Risk, Accounting, Legal, Tax) and approvals (Treasurer, ALCO/Risk Committee, CFO/Board as required).
- Implementation planning
  - Develop an execution mandate and calendar, limits and triggers, monitoring and reporting plan, and controls.
- Communication and training
  - Cascade the strategy to Treasury FO/MO/BO, Controllers, Business Units; update procedures and playbooks.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs
  - Risk policy, risk appetite statements, and limit frameworks.
  - Exposure data: FX-denominated revenues/costs, intercompany loans, forecast cash flows, debt portfolio (fixed/floating, currency mix), commodity consumption/production.
  - Market data: yield curves, FX rates and volatilities, commodity curves, correlations, credit spreads, cross-currency basis.
  - Financial plans: budgets, forecasts, capex plans, M&A pipeline, covenant thresholds, rating targets.
  - Legal documentation status: ISDA/CSAs, futures clearing agreements, board resolutions and trading authorities.
  - Accounting/tax guidance: hedge accounting objectives, historical effectiveness results, tax constraints.
- Prerequisites
  - Approved Treasury/Risk Management Policy.
  - Adequate systems and data quality to measure exposures and risk.
  - Segregation of duties and defined governance (FO/MO/BO, ALCO).
  - Counterparty onboarding completed for intended instruments/venues.
- Dependencies on other processes
  - Cash and liquidity management (to assess collateral/liquidity capacity).
  - Debt and capital structure management (to align interest rate/currency mix).
  - Financial planning and analysis (for forecasts and scenarios).
  - General accounting and reporting (for hedge accounting and disclosures).
  - Legal and compliance (for regulatory adherence, e.g., EMIR/Dodd‑Frank).
  - Collateral and counterparty risk management.

## Process Steps
1. Initiate and frame objectives
   - Confirm enterprise risk appetite and priorities (e.g., protect EBITDA in next 12–24 months; maintain interest expense within x%).
   - Define scope by risk type, entities, horizons, and materiality thresholds.

2. Gather and validate exposures
   - Collect actual and forecast positions from ERP/TMS and business units.
   - Net exposures at the enterprise level; identify natural hedges.
   - Assess data quality; reconcile to GL/FP&A; resolve gaps.

3. Measure risk and diagnose drivers
   - Compute baseline metrics (e.g., DV01 of debt; CFaR/EaR by horizon).
   - Run scenarios (parallel shifts, curve twists, FX devaluation, commodity shocks) and stress tests aligned to risk appetite.
   - Identify basis risk (e.g., Brent vs. consumed grade; forecast vs. contracted volumes).

4. Define hedging objectives and target profiles
   - Set hedge coverage bands by horizon (e.g., 0–12 months: 70–90%; 13–24 months: 40–70%; >24 months: 20–50%).
   - Determine desired interest rate/currency mix (e.g., fixed/floating, functional currency exposure).

5. Select strategies and instruments
   - Determine approach: static vs. dynamic, layering vs. opportunistic, collars vs. forwards, IRS vs. options, CCS/NDFs, futures.
   - Choose hedge ratios and tenors to match risk profile, liquidity, and accounting goals.
   - Define triggers for adding/reducing hedges (market levels, time, budget/forecast changes).

6. Evaluate economics, liquidity, and credit
   - Quantify cost of carry, premium spend, expected P&L volatility reduction, and potential mark-to-market impacts.
   - Assess collateral demands under CSAs, liquidity buffers, and counterparty limit usage.
   - Compare alternative strategies (decision matrix) and select preferred mix.

7. Align with accounting and tax
   - Determine hedge accounting designation (cash flow, fair value, net investment) and documentation requirements.
   - Define effectiveness testing methods (quantitative/qualitative), hedge components, and rebalancing rules.
   - Review tax impacts (e.g., deductibility of premiums, jurisdictional considerations).

8. Review legal and regulatory constraints
   - Confirm permitted instruments by jurisdiction/entity, EMIR/Dodd‑Frank classification, clearing/mandatory margining.
   - Verify execution channels and legal docs are in place (ISDA/CSA, clearing agreements).

9. Draft the hedging strategy and mandate
   - Produce a strategy paper including objectives, exposures, metrics, chosen instruments, hedge schedule, limits, triggers, accounting/tax treatment, and controls.
   - Include execution guidance: tenor buckets, minimum trade sizes, approved dealers/venues, pricing benchmarks.

10. Obtain approvals
    - Circulate to Risk, Accounting, Legal, Tax, and Business Unit finance for review.
    - Present to Treasurer and ALCO/Risk Committee; escalate to CFO/Board if policy updates are required.
    - Record approvals and version the strategy.

11. Prepare implementation artifacts
    - Create hedge documentation templates per relationship.
    - Build effectiveness testing plan and monitoring dashboards.
    - Configure limits, alerts, and workflows in TMS/ETRM; update procedures and RACI.

12. Communicate and train
    - Brief Treasury FO/MO/BO, Controllers, BU finance; run playbooks and dry‑runs.
    - Publish the hedge calendar and reporting cadence.

13. Handover to execution and monitoring
    - Issue trade mandates to Front Office with controls; schedule periodic strategy reviews (quarterly/after material events).

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Hedging strategy document, including:
  - Objectives, scope, coverage targets, and risk metrics.
  - Instrument selection, hedge ratios, tenors, layering plan, triggers.
  - Accounting designations and effectiveness methodologies.
  - Counterparty, collateral, and liquidity considerations.
  - Governance, limits, controls, and reporting requirements.
- Execution mandate and hedge calendar.
- Updated Treasury Policy or addendum (if changed).
- Hedge documentation templates and checklists.
- System configurations: limits, reports, alerts in TMS/ETRM.
- Success criteria
  - Achieves targeted reduction in risk metrics (e.g., EaR/CFaR) within risk appetite.
  - Compliance with policy, regulatory, and hedge accounting requirements.
  - Economic efficiency: risk reduction per unit cost meets thresholds.
  - Operational readiness: controls and monitoring in place with no audit issues.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- CFO
  - Sponsors risk appetite and approves major strategies/policy changes.
- Treasurer
  - Owns strategy development; ensures alignment with liquidity and capital structure; presents to ALCO/Board.
- Asset-Liability Committee (ALCO)/Risk Committee
  - Reviews and approves strategy; oversees limits and risk metrics.
- Treasury Front Office
  - Provides market insights; proposes instruments/structures; executes trades per mandate (execution occurs in subsequent process).
- Treasury Middle Office/Risk
  - Measures exposures and risk; runs scenarios; validates models; sets/monitors limits; effectiveness testing framework.
- Treasury Back Office/Operations
  - Ensures settlement and confirmations processes can support chosen instruments; sets up static data and collateral workflows.
- Accounting/Controllers
  - Advises on hedge accounting feasibility, documentation standards, and reporting/disclosures.
- Tax
  - Reviews tax implications and jurisdictional considerations.
- Legal/Compliance
  - Reviews regulatory constraints; ensures legal documentation is in place.
- FP&A/Business Unit Finance
  - Provides forecasts/exposure data; validates business assumptions; aligns with operational plans.
- Internal Audit
  - Reviews governance, controls, and compliance with policy.

## Best Practices
- Govern with a clear, board-approved treasury policy that defines risk appetite, permitted instruments, and limits.
- Hedge the exposure, not the view: avoid speculative positions; anchor to economic exposures and documented objectives.
- Use layering and time buckets to smooth entry points and reduce timing risk; align hedge horizons with exposure life.
- Favor natural hedging (offsets, currency matching of revenues and costs, balance sheet structuring) before derivatives.
- Align economic hedging with hedge accounting objectives to minimize P&L volatility and earnings noise.
- Quantify trade-offs with scenario analysis and stress testing; include tail risk and basis risk assessments.
- Set measurable targets (coverage bands, EaR/CFaR reductions) and define triggers for adding/reducing hedges.
- Diversify instruments and tenors; avoid concentration in single counterparties or maturities.
- Incorporate liquidity and collateral implications (CSA terms, initial/variation margin) into strategy selection.
- Maintain robust documentation and effectiveness testing methodologies; plan for rebalancing and de-designation.
- Centralize exposure aggregation across entities; net positions to hedge at the portfolio level where permitted.
- Establish model risk controls: validate pricing/risk models; backtest effectiveness; independent oversight by Middle Office.
- Plan for benchmark transitions and fallback language (e.g., IBOR to risk-free rates).
- Periodically review strategy performance and update for market/regulatory changes or business events (M&A, new markets).

## Common Challenges
- Inaccurate or late exposure forecasts
  - Solution: institute data governance, rolling forecast updates, variance analysis, and thresholds for hedging forecasted transactions.
- Basis risk between hedge and exposure (e.g., proxy indexes, grade/location differences)
  - Solution: quantify basis risk; choose closer proxies; consider cross-hedges with conservative hedge ratios; disclose residual risk.
- Misalignment with hedge accounting leading to earnings volatility
  - Solution: involve Accounting early; design hedges to qualify; robust documentation; pre-trade effectiveness testing.
- Over-hedging due to demand shortfalls or cancellations
  - Solution: use coverage bands, staged hedging, options for asymmetric protection; implement stop-loss/roll-off rules.
- Counterparty and liquidity constraints, collateral calls
  - Solution: diversify counterparties; set collateral buffers; optimize CSAs; consider cleared/futures when appropriate.
- Operational complexity and control gaps
  - Solution: standardized templates; workflow automation in TMS; clear RACI; periodic internal audits and training.
- Regulatory and legal constraints (e.g., local market restrictions, reporting)
  - Solution: compliance review in design; approved instrument lists by jurisdiction; regulatory reporting readiness.
- Model risk and parameter uncertainty
  - Solution: independent model validation; sensitivity analysis; conservative assumptions; periodic recalibration.

## Performance Metrics
- Risk reduction
  - Change in EaR/CFaR/VaR versus baseline; percent within risk appetite.
  - Interest rate DV01 or FX exposure reduction versus target.
- Coverage and alignment
  - Percent of eligible exposures hedged by horizon versus coverage bands.
  - Degree of mismatch (tenor, notional, currency) between hedge and exposure.
- Economic efficiency
  - Cost of hedging (premiums, carry, basis) per unit of risk reduced.
  - Realized P&L volatility versus planned; slippage versus strategy benchmarks.
- Accounting and compliance
  - Hedge effectiveness results; percentage of hedge relationships qualifying for hedge accounting.
  - Timeliness and accuracy of documentation; audit findings; regulatory reporting on time.
- Liquidity and counterparty
  - Collateral/margin utilization versus limits; liquidity buffer sufficiency.
  - Counterparty limit utilization and concentration metrics.
- Process effectiveness
  - Cycle time from strategy initiation to approval.
  - Number of exceptions/limit breaches; remediation time.

## Technology and Tools
- Treasury Management System (TMS)
  - Examples: SAP TRM, Kyriba, FIS Quantum, ION Reval; supports exposure aggregation, policy limits, workflows, hedge documentation, and accounting integration.
- Risk analytics and pricing
  - Tools for DV01, VaR/EaR/CFaR, scenario/stress testing, option pricing, and XVA; platforms such as Murex, Numerix, internal analytics.
- Market data platforms
  - Bloomberg, Refinitiv for curves, FX, vol surfaces, commodity forward curves.
- ERP/FP&A integration
  - SAP/Oracle and planning tools (Anaplan, Oracle EPM) for forecast and actuals; APIs to TMS for exposure feeds.
- Trading and execution
  - Multi-dealer platforms (360T, FXall), SEFs, exchanges for futures/cleared derivatives; OMS integration.
- Collateral and counterparty management
  - Collateral systems for CSA margining, limit monitoring, and dispute management.
- Document and GRC systems
  - Contract management for ISDAs/CSAs; GRC for policy, approvals, attestations, and audit trails.
- Reporting and BI
  - Dashboards and automated reports via Power BI/Tableau; alerts for limits/triggers.
