Level: 4

Process Details:
## Overview
[10.1.2.5] Manage construction or modification to building covers the end-to-end management of constructing new facilities or renovating/modifying existing ones to meet approved facility plans and user requirements. It transforms design intent into a compliant, safe, functional, and operationally ready built environment.

Purpose:
- Deliver new construction or renovations that meet program requirements, codes, budget, and schedule.
- Minimize disruption to ongoing operations during modifications of occupied buildings.
- Ensure safety, quality, sustainability, and maintainability are built into the asset.

Role in the organization:
- Executes the built-environment component of capital and small-works programs.
- Interfaces with planning, design, procurement, finance, operations, EHS, IT/OT, and asset management to convert capital plans into usable assets.
- Provides auditable records for capitalization, warranties, and ongoing maintenance.

## Key Activities
- Preconstruction and mobilization: finalize IFC (Issued for Construction) documents, procure contractors, permits, site logistics.
- Construction execution: demolition, structural/civil, building envelope, MEPF systems, interiors/fit-out, specialty systems.
- Quality management: inspections, tests, submittals, RFIs, nonconformance management.
- Safety and environmental management: site-specific safety plans, permits (hot work, confined space), environmental controls.
- Cost and schedule control: baseline setup, progress tracking, change control, forecasting.
- Stakeholder and operations coordination: phasing, shutdown planning, communications, access control.
- Commissioning: pre-functional and functional testing, integrated systems testing, performance verification.
- Handover and closeout: punch lists, O&M manuals, as-builts, training, occupancy certification, asset data handoff.
- Warranty and post-occupancy: issue resolution, performance monitoring, lessons learned.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Approved business case, funding approval, and CAPEX allocation.
- Program of requirements (Owner’s Project Requirements - OPR), design basis (BOD), and IFC drawings/specifications.
- Site information: surveys, geotechnical, utilities locates, existing as-builts verification, hazardous materials reports (e.g., asbestos, lead).
- Permits/approvals plan: building permits, environmental approvals, right-of-way, special inspections requirements.
- Contracting strategy and documents: tender results, executed contracts, bonds, insurances (builder’s risk, general liability), procurement plan.
- Baselines: schedule (WBS, milestones), cost (budget/contingency), quality plan, risk register.
- Operational constraints: occupancy status, shutdown windows, security and access protocols, infection control (if healthcare), noise/vibration limits.

Prerequisites:
- Completion of prior planning and design processes (needs assessment, feasibility, concept, design development).
- Selection and onboarding of architect/engineer, general contractor/CM, commissioning agent.
- Digital environment established: Common Data Environment (CDE), PMIS, BIM model coordination.
- Safety and environmental plans approved (e.g., SWPPP, waste management, traffic management plan).
- Stakeholder communication plan and change control governance set.

Dependencies on other processes:
- [10.1.2] Plan facility (needs definition, design development, site selection).
- Procurement and contract management for services, materials, and equipment.
- Finance for funding release, progress payments, capitalization.
- Facilities operations for integration, shutdowns, and transition to operations.
- IT/OT for network, security, building systems integration (BMS, BAS).

## Process Steps
1) Initiation and Gate Approval
- Confirm scope, budget, schedule baselines aligned to OPR/BOD.
- Approve go/no-go at construction start gate; confirm funding and contingencies.
- Assign project governance, escalation path, and decision rights.

2) Preconstruction
- Conduct constructability and maintainability reviews; finalize IFC set.
- Perform model coordination/clash detection (BIM) and update coordinated shop drawings approach.
- Finalize procurement plan; identify long-lead items and pre-order as needed.
- Secure permits and special inspections plan; align with Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ).
- Develop logistics plan: site access, laydown, crane plans, temporary utilities, hoisting.
- Develop safety plan (JHAs, method statements), environmental plan (erosion control, waste).
- Establish QA/QC plan and inspection test plans (ITPs).
- Validate existing conditions (laser scanning, GPR, selective openings); update as-builts if gaps found.
- Plan phasing and shutdowns (MEP isolation, hot work, after-hours work) to minimize business disruption.

3) Contractor Mobilization
- Kickoff meetings: safety, quality, coordination protocols, RFI/submittal workflows, communication cadence.
- Install site controls: fencing, signage, access control, badging, laydown, temporary power/water.
- Baseline schedule load: activities, logic ties, resources; integrate 4D simulations if applicable.
- Establish document control in CDE; standardize file naming, transmittals, revisions.

4) Execution – Enabling and Demolition
- Abatement and removal of hazardous materials per regulations.
- Selective demolition with noise/dust/vibration controls; maintain fire/life-safety systems.
- Protect existing assets, occupants, and egress paths; implement infection control where relevant.

5) Execution – Core and Shell/Structure
- Foundations, structural framing, seismic and wind systems.
- Building envelope: waterproofing, roofing, façade systems; perform mockups and testing (air/water).

6) Execution – MEPF Rough-In and Systems
- Install mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, low-voltage, and controls infrastructure.
- Coordinate with BIM to avoid clashes; verify supports, penetrations, and sleeves.

7) Execution – Interiors and Fit-Out
- Partitions, ceilings, flooring, casework, finishes.
- Specialty spaces (labs, clean rooms, data centers, healthcare suites) with specific standards.

8) Quality Assurance and Control (Continuous)
- Submittals and approvals tracking; maintain logs and turnaround targets.
- Inspections: first-article mockups, hold points, special inspections (structural, welding, fireproofing).
- Nonconformance reports (NCRs), corrective actions, re-inspection.
- Materials testing and verification (concrete breaks, weld tests, envelope tests).

9) Safety, Environmental, and Security (Continuous)
- Daily briefings, toolbox talks, permit-to-work (hot work, confined space, LOTO).
- Incident reporting and corrective actions; leading indicator tracking (observations).
- Environmental compliance: erosion control, stormwater, waste diversion, noise/dust monitoring.
- Security of occupied facilities: access control, background checks, escorting.

10) Cost, Schedule, and Change Control (Continuous)
- Track progress vs baseline (SPI/CPI); weekly look-aheads; Last Planner pull planning.
- Measure quantities installed, earned value calculations.
- Manage changes via formal change control board; evaluate scope, cost, schedule, risk; update logs.
- Process pay applications, lien waivers; update forecast at completion (EAC).

11) Communications and Stakeholder Management (Continuous)
- Issue weekly/monthly status reports, dashboards, risk/issue logs.
- Coordinate with occupants for noisy work, utility shutdowns, deliveries.
- Maintain minutes, decision logs, and action item tracking.

12) Commissioning
- Commissioning plan and schedule integrated early; update with construction progress.
- Pre-functional checklists; equipment start-up and balancing (TAB).
- Functional performance tests; integrated systems testing (life safety, BMS, security).
- Verify energy and performance criteria; track deficiencies to resolution.

13) Substantial Completion and Punch List
- Perform inspections with owner/AE; generate and manage punch lists to zero critical defects.
- Achieve certificate of substantial completion and conditional/unconditional occupancy permits.

14) Handover and Closeout
- Deliver as-builts (models and drawings), O&M manuals, warranties, test reports, attic stock.
- Train operations staff; hand off asset tags and data to CMMS/EAM.
- Complete final inspections, fire marshal sign-offs, code compliance certificates.
- Financial close: final pay apps, retainage release, change order reconciliation, capitalization.

15) Warranty and Post-Occupancy
- Manage warranty issues, seasonal testing, performance tuning.
- Conduct post-occupancy evaluation against OPR; capture lessons learned; update asset register.

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs:
- A constructed or renovated facility/space meeting approved requirements and codes.
- Operationally ready systems with verified performance and occupancy certification.

Deliverables:
- As-built drawings/models, O&M manuals, training records, commissioning reports.
- Warranties, spare parts/attic stock, permits and certificates (CO), testing and inspection records.
- Updated asset registry and CMMS/EAM data (equipment lists, PM plans, asset hierarchies).
- Financial closeout documentation and final cost report, change order log, lessons learned.

Success criteria:
- Safety: zero fatalities, low TRIR/LTIR, no major environmental incidents.
- Schedule: substantial completion by target date; minimal schedule variance.
- Cost: within approved budget and contingency; acceptable CPI.
- Quality: punch list closure within target; minimal rework; inspections pass rate.
- Compliance: all code and permit requirements satisfied; CO issued.
- Performance: systems meet OPR (e.g., energy, air changes, redundancy).
- Stakeholder satisfaction: end-user acceptance and readiness for operations.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Project Sponsor/Owner: approve scope/funding; resolve escalations; accept deliverables.
- Facilities Owner/End-User Rep: validate requirements; participate in inspections, commissioning, training.
- Project Manager (Owner’s side): overall delivery, governance, cost/schedule/risk/change management, reporting.
- Construction Manager/General Contractor: plan and execute work; manage subs; safety, quality, logistics.
- Superintendent: daily field coordination, sequencing, site control, look-ahead planning.
- Architect/Engineer of Record: design conformance, submittal/RFI responses, site observations, code interpretation.
- Commissioning Agent: commissioning plan, testing, deficiency tracking, performance verification.
- EHS Manager: site safety plan, audits, incident management, environmental compliance.
- Quality Manager: QA/QC plan, inspections, ITPs, NCRs, closeout quality verification.
- Cost Engineer/Controller: budget management, forecasting, pay apps, change order evaluation.
- Scheduler/Planner: baseline, updates, look-aheads, critical path management.
- Procurement/Supply Chain: material/equipment purchasing, expediting, long-lead tracking.
- Document Control: CDE/PMIS administration, transmittals, version control, closeout docs.
- IT/OT Lead: network, security systems, BAS integration, commissioning oversight for tech.
- Facilities Operations/Maintenance: maintainability input, shutdown coordination, operations training, CMMS data.
- External Inspectors/AHJ: code inspections, approvals, certificates.
- Security/Access Control: site access, badging, protection of occupied areas.
- Legal/Contracts: contract administration, claims, lien waivers, compliance.

## Best Practices
- Front-load planning: robust preconstruction, constructability, and maintainability reviews.
- Early involvement of operations/maintenance and commissioning agent; develop OPR and commissioning plan early.
- Use BIM for 3D coordination, 4D scheduling, and 5D cost; perform clash detection before field work.
- Validate existing conditions with laser scanning/GPR; reconcile discrepancies before committing to fabrication.
- Lean construction: Last Planner System, daily huddles, visual management, just-in-time deliveries.
- Prefabrication/modularization for MEP racks, bathrooms, headwalls to reduce risk and schedule.
- Detailed phasing and shutdown plans for occupied buildings; work off-hours where needed.
- Rigorous change control with impact analysis and tiered approval thresholds.
- Quality at the source: first-article mockups, sample rooms, and hold points to set expectations.
- Safety culture: active observations, leading indicators, near-miss learning; embed permit-to-work.
- Proactive supply chain management: identify long-leads, secure alternates, track logistics.
- Sustainability: waste diversion goals, low-VOC materials, envelope commissioning, energy targets, certification readiness (LEED/WELL as applicable).
- Digital delivery: single source of truth CDE, standardized naming, mobile field tools, e-signatures.
- Clear definition of done: acceptance criteria per system/area; use checklists; don’t defer to closeout.

## Common Challenges
- Unforeseen existing conditions (hidden utilities, structural surprises)
  - Solutions: thorough surveys, exploratory openings, contingency, flexible design details, design-build collaboration.
- Permitting and AHJ delays
  - Solutions: early engagement, pre-application meetings, complete submittals, track with SLAs, allow float for reviews.
- Scope creep and unclear requirements
  - Solutions: freeze points, change control board, clear OPR, decision logs, user representative governance.
- Supply chain disruptions and long-lead items
  - Solutions: early procurement, alternates pre-approved, vendor diversification, schedule resequencing.
- Working in occupied buildings (noise, dust, security, life safety)
  - Solutions: phased work, temporary partitions/negative air, off-hours, security escorts, maintain egress and fire watch.
- Safety incidents and compliance risks
  - Solutions: robust safety plan, daily JHAs, competency verification, enforce stop-work authority.
- Quality defects and rework
  - Solutions: mockups, first-work inspections, QC checklists, supervise critical path trades, root-cause corrective actions.
- Coordination clashes between trades
  - Solutions: BIM coordination with weekly model updates, field verification, superintendent-led coordination meetings.
- Budget overrun and schedule slippage
  - Solutions: earned value tracking, trend logs, risk registers, recovery plans, value engineering workshops aligned to OPR.
- Late commissioning and operational readiness
  - Solutions: commissioning integrated schedule, early TAB, dry runs, operator involvement, phased turnover.

## Performance Metrics
Safety and environmental:
- Total Recordable Incident Rate (TRIR), Lost Time Incident Rate (LTIR)
- Leading indicators: safety observations per 1000 work hours, JHA compliance rate
- Environmental incidents, waste diversion rate (%), dust/noise exceedances

## Technology and Tools

- Document control: standard metadata, versioning, transmittals, submittals, RFIs

Commissioning and operations:

Process Details:
# [10.1.3.1] Acquire Workspace and Facilities

## Overview
Acquire Workspace and Facilities is the end-to-end process of sourcing, securing, fitting out, equipping, and readying office or operational workspace to meet defined business needs. It spans real estate search and transaction (lease or purchase), design and fit-out, procurement of furniture, fixtures and equipment (FF&E), IT/OT infrastructure, environment-health-safety (EHS) compliance, service contracts, commissioning, and handover for occupancy.

Purpose:
- Ensure the organization has the right workspace, in the right location, at the right time and cost, aligned to business requirements (capacity, functionality, security, compliance, brand).
- Provide a safe, compliant, efficient environment that enables productivity and supports culture and employee experience.
- Optimize total cost of ownership (TCO) and flexibility via robust planning, competitive sourcing, and effective vendor and risk management.

Role in the organization:
- Enables growth, consolidation, or relocation strategies.
- Supports workforce strategy (hybrid/remote, collaboration spaces, accessibility).
- Integrates with finance (capital/lease accounting), legal (contracts), HR (headcount planning), IT (network/security), and operations (facilities management).

## Key Activities
- Requirements definition: capacity, location, budget, timelines, functional/technical needs, sustainability and security requirements.
- Market search and site shortlisting: broker engagement, market intelligence, site visits, preliminary feasibility.
- Due diligence: technical, legal, financial, environmental, and compliance assessments.
- Transaction management: RFP/RFQ, proposal evaluation, lease/purchase negotiation, approvals, execution.
- Design and fit-out: space planning, architectural/MEP design, permits, construction, quality control.
- Procurement and installation: FF&E, AV, IT/OT, security systems, signage, utilities, supplies.
- EHS and compliance: building codes, fire/life safety, accessibility, environmental standards.
- Service enablement: cleaning, waste, HVAC maintenance, security, reception, mail, cafeteria/coffee.
- Commissioning and testing: building systems, IT networks, life safety, readiness checks.
- Transition and move-in: move planning, change management, communications, day-1 support.
- Handover and documentation: as-builts, O&M manuals, asset registry, warranties, lease abstracts.
- Post-occupancy evaluation: user satisfaction, utilization, corrective actions.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Business case and demand signal (headcount forecast, team locations, growth/consolidation plan).
- Functional requirements (space types, meeting rooms, labs, secure areas, accessibility).
- Budget and funding model (CapEx/OpEx, TCO target, contingency).
- Location strategy and key constraints (commute radius, regulatory, tax incentives).
- Timeline and critical dates (current lease expiry, project milestones, move window).
- Corporate standards (branding, space density, sustainability, IT/security baselines).
- Risk and compliance requirements (HSE, data privacy for CCTV/access, industry standards).

Prerequisites:
- Executive sponsor and governance structure (steering committee).
- Approved business case and sourcing strategy (lease vs. buy vs. serviced/flexible workspace).
- Procurement policy alignment and vendor prequalification list.
- Access to internal SMEs (IT, EHS, Legal, Finance, Security, Facilities).

Dependencies on other processes:
- Strategic workforce and real estate planning (defines demand, location strategy).
- Budgeting and capital planning (fund allocation).
- Vendor management and procurement (RFX, contracting).
- Information security architectures (network/security requirements).
- Facility operations readiness (FM team onboarding for steady state).
- Change management and internal communications.

## Process Steps
1) Initiation and Governance
- Appoint project sponsor, project manager, and cross-functional team.
- Establish scope, objectives, success criteria, and stage-gate plan.
- Create risk register and communications plan.

2) Requirements and Business Case
- Confirm headcount and usage profiles (assigned vs. flexible seating).
- Define functional needs (e.g., labs, training rooms), adjacencies, and service levels.
- Draft budget (fit-out, FF&E, IT, soft costs, contingency) and TCO over lease term.
- Approve business case and funding.

3) Market Scan and Shortlist
- Engage broker/CRE advisor; issue requirements brief.
- Identify long-list of properties (including flexible workspace options).
- Conduct site visits; assess commute/amenities, utilities capacity, building performance.
- Shortlist 3–5 options based on weighted criteria (cost, timing, fit, risk).

4) Due Diligence
- Technical: base building drawings, structural and MEP capacity, IT risers, power density.
- Legal: title/encumbrances, landlord obligations, compliance records.
- Environmental: Phase I (and II if needed), hazardous materials, sustainability attributes.
- Regulatory: zoning, permits needed, accessibility, fire code, life safety systems.
- Financial: comparative lease analysis, incentives, escalation, operating expenses.
- Document findings and update risk/cost models.

5) Transaction and Approvals
- Issue RFP/RFQ to shortlisted landlords or serviced office providers.
- Evaluate proposals; negotiate key terms (rent, TI allowance, free rent, exit/expansion rights).
- Coordinate internal reviews (Legal, Finance, Risk, Tax, Insurance).
- Finalize and execute LOI and lease/purchase agreement; abstract critical dates/clauses.
- Obtain insurance certificates, bank guarantees/LCs if required.

6) Design and Permitting
- Appoint design team (architect, MEP, AV/IT, acoustics), cost consultant, and code consultant.
- Develop concept, schematic, and detailed design aligned to standards and budget.
- Space planning: test fits, occupancy strategy (hoteling ratios), accessibility.
- Sustainability and wellness targets (LEED/WELL/energy intensity).
- Submit permit applications; respond to AHJ comments; secure approvals.

7) Construction and Fit-Out
- Select general contractor via competitive bid; define QA/QC and safety plan.
- Conduct pre-construction kickoff; lock baseline schedule and change control.
- Execute construction; hold regular site meetings and inspections.
- Manage change orders; track schedule, cost, quality, and HSE performance.
- Coordinate landlord works, utilities upgrades, and base building interfaces.

8) Procurement and Installation (FF&E, IT, Security)
- Finalize specifications and POs for furniture, fixtures, signage, window treatments.
- Order IT: cabling, switches, Wi-Fi, endpoints, AV, conferencing, servers if needed.
- Security: access control, CCTV, intrusion, visitor management.
- Coordinate deliveries, staging, and installation with construction sequence.
- Tag assets; record in asset register/CMDB with warranty and maintenance data.

9) Service Enablement and Contracts
- Select and contract soft and hard services: cleaning, waste, pest, landscaping, mail, reception, maintenance (HVAC, lifts), coffee/water, vending.
- Define SLAs/KPIs and onboarding plans; schedule preventive maintenance.
- Set up utilities and services accounts; commission BMS integrations as applicable.

10) Commissioning and Readiness
- Commission MEP, life safety, IT, AV; conduct integrated systems testing.
- Perform inspections: building, fire, elevator, health department (where applicable).
- Obtain occupancy permits/certifications.
- Punch list walkthroughs; remediate defects; practical completion signoff.
- Prepare Day-1 readiness checklist and incident response plans.

11) Transition and Move-In
- Execute change management plan: comms, training on new ways of working, etiquette.
- Plan moves (phased if needed); engage move vendor; pack/label and transport.
- Set up reception, access badges, lockers, seating/booking systems.
- Provide floor wardens, IT walk-the-floor support, and HSE induction on Day-1/week-1.

12) Handover and Closeout
- Deliver handover package: as-builts, O&M manuals, warranties, test certificates, permits, lease abstract, asset register, vendor contacts, maintenance schedules.
- Financial close: finalize accounts, reconcile allowances, release retainage.
- Post-occupancy evaluation (30–90 days): satisfaction survey, utilization analytics, defect closure.
- Transition to steady-state FM; update IWMS/lease systems with critical dates and obligations.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Executed lease/purchase agreements and lease abstracts with critical dates.
- Approved designs, permits, and inspection certificates; occupancy permit.
- Completed fit-out and installed FF&E, IT/AV, and security systems.
- Commissioning reports, test results, and punch list closure records.
- Service contracts with SLAs; utilities set up.
- Asset registry/CMDB entries and barcodes/RFID tags.
- As-built drawings, O&M manuals, warranties, and maintenance plans.
- Move plans, seating charts, access credentials issued.
- Post-occupancy evaluation report with action plan.

Success criteria:
- Space delivered on time, within budget, and meeting functional and compliance requirements.
- Zero critical safety incidents; all permits/certifications in place.
- User satisfaction ≥ target (e.g., ≥80% favorable).
- Space utilization aligns with design assumptions within 90 days.
- Defects resolved within agreed timeframe; service SLAs achieved in first 60 days.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Executive Sponsor: Approves business case, resolves escalations.
- Corporate Real Estate/Facilities Lead: Owns site selection, transaction strategy, and delivery oversight.
- Project Manager: Leads day-to-day delivery, schedule/cost/risk management, stakeholder coordination.
- Procurement: Manages RFX, vendor selection, contracts, and compliance with sourcing policy.
- Legal Counsel: Negotiates and reviews lease/purchase and vendor contracts; ensures regulatory compliance.
- Finance/Accounting: Budgeting, approvals; lease accounting (ASC 842/IFRS 16) setup; TCO analysis.
- IT/Network/Security: Designs and deploys IT/AV, access control, cybersecurity controls; Day-1 support.
- EHS/Compliance: Ensures adherence to HSE standards; conducts audits and safety oversight.
- Design Team (Architect/MEP/Acoustics): Delivers drawings/specs, permitting support, CA services.
- General Contractor and Subcontractors: Executes construction and fit-out per contract and safety plan.
- Facilities Operations Manager: Prepares for steady-state operations; service vendor onboarding.
- HR/Change Management/Communications: Manages change, communications, training, and move logistics.
- Reception/Admin Services Lead: Defines front-of-house services; hires/trains staff if insourced.
- Security Manager: Physical security plan, policies, and systems commissioning.
- Landlord/Broker: Provides property information, executes landlord works, supports transaction.

## Best Practices
- Use a stage-gate model with clear approval points (site shortlisting, LOI, lease, design, construction).
- Align early with all stakeholders; capture must-haves vs. nice-to-haves; prevent scope creep.
- Perform TCO and scenario analysis (lease term options, expansion/contraction rights, fit-out reuse).
- Prequalify vendors; run competitive sourcing; include performance and safety history in evaluations.
- Standardize design kits and FF&E/IT catalogs to reduce cost, lead time, and complexity.
- Incorporate sustainability and wellness (energy targets, indoor air quality, daylighting, materials).
- Build realistic schedules with permitting and lead-time buffers; place long-lead orders early.
- Maintain rigorous change control and transparent contingency management.
- Commission third-party testing for critical systems; conduct mock-ups and pilot rooms.
- Tag assets at receipt; capture warranty and maintenance data; integrate with CMMS/IWMS.
- Establish critical date tracking for lease obligations and options.
- Plan for flexible/hybrid work: booking systems, sensors for utilization insights, adaptable furniture.
- Execute a formal change management plan and Day-1/Week-1 hypercare.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Underestimated lead times for permits or long-lead items: Track permitting milestones; engage code consultants; pre-order critical items; keep alternates pre-approved.
- Scope creep and design changes: Use strict change control; freeze design; maintain options log with cost/schedule impacts.
- Budget overruns: Include 10–15% contingency; value-engineering workshops; standardize specifications; negotiate landlord contributions.
- Hidden site conditions/unexpected base building issues: Conduct thorough due diligence; include allowances; maintain escalation path with landlord.
- Vendor performance variability: Prequalify; use performance-based contracts and SLAs; hold regular performance reviews; enforce QA/QC.
- IT/AV integration delays: Lock technical requirements early; perform lab tests; staged network rollout; involve InfoSec early.
- Compliance gaps discovered late: EHS and code reviews at 30/60/90% design; third-party audits; mock inspections.
- Day-1 operational hiccups: Detailed readiness checklists, staff training, and hypercare with SWAT support team.
- Mismatch between designed and actual utilization: Use sensors and booking analytics; adjust layouts; implement workplace policies and coaching.
- International regulatory and cultural differences: Use local experts; adapt standards; verify local labor and import regulations.

## Performance Metrics
- Schedule: Time from approval to occupancy; schedule variance (%).
- Cost: Fit-out cost per square foot/meter; cost per workstation; budget variance (%); landlord contribution realized.
- Quality: Punch list items per 1,000 sq ft; defects resolved within SLA; rework rate.
- Safety: Recordable incident rate; lost-time incidents; safety audit scores.
- Compliance: On-time permit approvals; number of nonconformities at inspection.
- Utilization and Experience: Space utilization (%), peak vs. average; meeting room no-show rate; occupant satisfaction/NPS.
- Procurement and Vendor: Competitive bid coverage (% spend competitively sourced); on-time, in-full delivery; supplier performance score.
- Sustainability: Energy intensity (EUI), waste diverted during construction, materials VOC compliance, anticipated operational carbon.
- Operations readiness: % assets tagged and in CMMS; service contracts live at Day-1; helpdesk tickets during hypercare and time-to-resolve.

## Technology and Tools
- IWMS/CAFM: Portfolio planning, space planning, lease administration, move management, asset tracking.
- CMMS: Maintenance plans for building systems and assets post-handover.
- Lease accounting/compliance tools: ASC 842/IFRS 16 calculations, critical date management.
- Project and portfolio management: Scheduling, risk, cost, document control; collaboration platforms.
- eSourcing/eProcurement: RFX, vendor onboarding, PO management, contract lifecycle management.
- CAD/BIM and space planning: AutoCAD/Revit-compatible tools; clash detection; as-built management; digital twins where available.
- EHS and quality management: Incident tracking, audits, permits-to-work.
- Security systems: Access control, CCTV, visitor management, identity integration.
- IT/AV infrastructure: Network monitoring, asset discovery, ITSM/CMDB for end-user devices and infrastructure.
- BMS/IoT and utilization analytics: Environmental monitoring, energy management, occupancy sensors, room/desk booking.
- Digital signature and document repositories: Secure contract execution and centralized document control.
- GIS/location analytics: Commute analysis, amenity mapping, catchment analysis.

Process Details:
## Overview
[10.1.3.2] Change fit/form/function of workspace and facilities is the end-to-end process of modifying an existing workspace to meet evolving business needs. It covers minor reconfigurations (e.g., moving desks), adjustments to form and aesthetics (e.g., finishes, lighting, acoustics), and changes to function and use (e.g., converting offices to collaboration zones, labs, or training rooms). The process ensures modifications are safe, compliant, cost-effective, and delivered with minimal operational disruption, while maintaining accurate records of assets, drawings, and occupancy.

Purpose:
- Enable the organization to respond rapidly to growth, downsizing, reorganization, new work models (hybrid, ABW), technology changes, and regulatory requirements.
- Preserve employee experience, productivity, safety, and brand consistency.
- Protect asset value and lifecycle by ensuring changes follow standards and are correctly documented.

Role in the organization:
- Acts as the execution arm of space strategy, turning business requirements into practical, built environments.
- Integrates facilities, IT, EHS, security, finance, and procurement in a controlled change workflow.
- Feeds accurate data into real estate and asset portfolios (space plans, BIM/CAD, inventories) to inform future planning.

## Key Activities
- Intake and triage of change requests, including categorization (minor/standard, major, emergency).
- Requirements gathering and validation (headcount, adjacency, technology, special use conditions).
- Feasibility assessment (space, structural, MEP, IT, code compliance).
- Concept and detailed design, including test-fits and finish schedules.
- Costing and budgeting (CapEx/OpEx), option analysis, and business case.
- Stakeholder review and approvals (including landlord/building management where applicable).
- Scheduling and phasing to minimize business disruption.
- Permitting and compliance planning (building codes, fire/life safety, accessibility, EHS).
- Procurement and contractor selection (furniture, trades, technology).
- Site readiness, method statements, and safety planning (LOTO, RAMS/JHA, Permit-to-Work).
- Execution and move management (including IT cutover and user coordination).
- Commissioning, inspections, and quality assurance.
- Handover, training, and user acceptance.
- Documentation updates (as-built drawings, asset registry, occupancy).
- Post-implementation review and benefits validation.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Formal change request with business justification and timeline.
- Current floor plans, BIM/CAD models, and as-built documentation.
- Occupancy and headcount forecasts, adjacency requirements.
- IT/AV requirements (network density, power, Wi-Fi, conferencing).
- EHS requirements (ergonomics, hazardous materials, ventilation).
- Brand and design standards, furniture and finish standards.
- Budget availability and financial constraints.
- Landlord/building rules and lease clauses (alterations, hours, approvals).
- Historical maintenance records and outstanding defects.

Prerequisites:
- Defined workspace standards and design guidelines.
- Approved category and authority matrix for change approvals.
- Active vendor/contractor panels and procurement channels.
- Established permit-to-work and safety management system.
- Access to space/asset systems (IWMS/CAFM, CMMS, ITSM).
- Change freeze calendars (e.g., peak periods) and communication channels.

Dependencies on other processes:
- 10.1.1 Plan and acquire assets: strategic space planning and standards.
- 10.1.2 Acquire assets: procurement of furniture, fixtures, equipment (FF&E).
- 10.1.3.1 Provide workspace and facilities: baseline setup and asset provisioning.
- IT change and release management for network/AV/endpoint changes.
- EHS management and incident reporting.
- Finance (budgeting, CapEx/OpEx approvals) and procurement (contracts).
- Security and access control updates; landlord coordination.
- Records management for drawings and asset registers.
- Business continuity planning for downtime and relocations.

## Process Steps
1. Initiate and Triage
   - Submit request via IWMS/ITSM form with scope, urgency, drivers, and constraints.
   - Categorize as:
     - Standard/minor (e.g., desk moves, small furniture reconfigurations).
     - Major (e.g., construction, new functions, MEP changes).
     - Emergency (safety or critical operations).
   - Assign a project manager (PM) and facilities lead; open a work order/project.

2. Gather Requirements
   - Conduct stakeholder interviews and workplace observations.
   - Capture headcount, role types, work modes, adjacency, accessibility, and storage needs.
   - Define technical needs: power, data, AV, HVAC, acoustics, lighting, security.
   - Document EHS requirements (ergonomics, safe egress, hazardous substances).
   - Confirm business constraints (timeline, budget, change freeze windows).

3. Assess Feasibility
   - Review structural and MEP limits; evaluate base-building systems capacity.
   - Conduct site survey and verify against existing as-builts.
   - Identify code and compliance impacts (fire codes, OSHA, ADA, local building code, accessibility).
   - Identify risks and draft initial risk register; define mitigation options.

4. Concept Design and Options
   - Produce 1–3 test-fit layouts and concept boards aligned to standards.
   - Include modular/flexible options (demountable partitions, reconfigurable furniture).
   - Provide rough order of magnitude (ROM) costs and high-level schedule.
   - Run cross-functional review (Facilities, IT, EHS, Security, Business Sponsor).

5. Select Option and Approvals
   - Choose preferred option based on criteria (cost, timeline, capacity, compliance).
   - Prepare business case with TCO, benefits, and downtime impact.
   - Obtain approvals per authority matrix (Sponsor, Finance, Real Estate, Landlord, CAB if IT).
   - Record decisions and stage gate approval.

6. Detailed Design and Planning
   - Develop detailed drawings (CAD/BIM), finish schedules, power/data points, furniture specifications.
   - Create method statements, construction phasing, and move plans.
   - Identify long-lead items; lock procurement strategy and delivery dates.
   - Plan EHS controls: RAMS/JHA, Permit-to-Work, LOTO, hot work permits, dust/noise controls.
   - Plan IT/AV cutover and endpoint deployment.
   - Update communication plan (stakeholders, blackout periods, signage).

7. Permits and Procurement
   - Submit permit applications (building permits, fire/life safety, landlord approvals).
   - Source contractors/vendors, issue POs/contracts, ensure insurance and compliance documents are in place.
   - Schedule materials logistics (dock access, storage, waste disposal).

8. Site Preparation
   - Pre-start meeting and site induction for all workers.
   - Implement isolations, protection of existing finishes, and safety barriers.
   - Confirm permit-to-work is active and inspections scheduled.

9. Execute Works and Move Activities
   - Perform construction/reconfiguration per plan; daily coordination huddles.
   - Deliver and install furniture, fixtures, signage; manage cable/electrical works.
   - IT tasks: install racks/APs/switches as needed, patching, device deployments, AV commissioning.
   - Conduct interim inspections; update risk controls as conditions change.
   - Manage move events (swing space, phased moves, after-hours work) to minimize downtime.

10. Commissioning and Quality Assurance
    - Test MEP systems, lighting levels, life safety devices; reinstate fire systems.
    - Verify IT/AV performance (coverage, bandwidth, conferencing).
    - Ergonomic checks and accessibility validation.
    - Punch list creation and resolution; building and landlord inspections as required.

11. Handover and User Readiness
    - Conduct user walkthroughs and training (new equipment, booking systems, etiquette).
    - Update wayfinding and digital signage; distribute user guides/FAQs.
    - Formal acceptance sign-off from sponsor; transition to operations.

12. Documentation and Close-Out
    - Update as-built drawings, BIM models, and IWMS space records.
    - Update asset registry with new/relocated items (tagging, barcoding).
    - Update maintenance plans and warranties in CMMS.
    - Close permits; capture compliance certificates and O&M manuals.
    - Financial close-out: reconcile invoices, finalize CapEx/OpEx.
    - Post-implementation review: measure outcomes vs. objectives, capture lessons learned.

13. Sustain and Monitor
    - Monitor utilization, comfort, and fault reports for 4–12 weeks post-change.
    - Address defects under warranty; adjust layouts if needed.
    - Feed insights to planning standards and future change cycles.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Updated and operational workspace aligned to approved requirements.
- As-built drawings and updated BIM/CAD models.
- Updated space records (IWMS), occupancy and allocations.
- Updated asset inventory (FF&E, IT equipment) with tags and locations.
- Commissioning reports, test results, compliance certificates, permits closed.
- O&M manuals, warranties, and maintenance schedules.
- Training materials, user communications, wayfinding/signage.
- Financial close-out package and benefits realization report.
- Lessons learned and updated standards if applicable.

Success criteria:
- Scope, budget, and schedule adherence within agreed tolerances.
- Zero recordable safety incidents; all work executed under valid permits.
- Code compliance and landlord approvals attained; no audit findings.
- User acceptance ≥ agreed satisfaction threshold (e.g., CSAT ≥ 4.3/5).
- Minimal business disruption (downtime within planned windows).
- Accurate documentation updates within 10 business days of go-live.
- Measurable improvement in utilization, productivity, or experience per business case.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Business Sponsor/Requestor: Initiates request, provides requirements, funding, and acceptance.
- Facilities/Workplace Manager: Owns process, ensures standards and compliance, coordinates stakeholders.
- Project Manager: Plans and orchestrates end-to-end execution, risk, schedule, and budget management.
- Space Planner/Designer: Produces layouts, test-fits, detailed design; ensures adherence to standards.
- EHS Lead: Oversees safety plans, risk assessments, permits, and compliance with OSHA/ISO 45001.
- IT/AV Lead: Specifies and delivers network, Wi-Fi, AV, endpoints; manages cutover and testing.
- Security Lead: Access control, CCTV, intrusion systems, and physical security requirements.
- Finance Partner: Validates budget, tracks CapEx/OpEx, approves expenditures.
- Procurement: Sources vendors, manages contracts, ensures insurance and compliance.
- Landlord/Building Management: Reviews and approves alterations, coordinates base building impacts.
- General Contractor/Trades: Execute construction, installations, and commissioning.
- Move Coordinator: Plans and executes relocations, labeling, and communications.
- Records/Asset Management: Updates drawings, IWMS, asset registers.
- Change/Communications Manager: Stakeholder engagement, messaging, training, and change readiness.
- Quality/Commissioning Agent (optional): Independent verification of performance and compliance.

## Best Practices
- Use a tiered change classification with pre-approved “standard changes” for speed and predictability.
- Apply modular, reconfigurable furniture and demountable partitions to reduce future change costs.
- Design for accessibility, ergonomics, and inclusivity; comply with ADA and universal design principles.
- Engage EHS and landlord early; secure permits well ahead of mobilization.
- Pilot high-impact changes (mock-ups, sample rooms); use user feedback to refine designs.
- Plan phased work and after-hours execution to minimize operational disruption.
- Maintain a robust Permit-to-Work, LOTO, and contractor induction program.
- Incorporate sustainability: reuse/refurbish furniture, low-VOC materials, circular disposal, LEED/WELL alignment.
- Keep a single source of truth for plans and assets (IWMS/BIM) and update within a defined SLA.
- Manage long-lead items proactively; lock finishes and equipment early.
- Establish clear decision gates with documented approvals and change control.
- Use data to inform decisions: utilization sensors, booking data, comfort/IEQ metrics.
- Provide clear wayfinding and change management to support behavior in new layouts (e.g., ABW etiquette).

## Common Challenges
- Scope creep and late changes: Use change control with impact assessments; time-box decisions.
- Permitting and landlord delays: Pre-consult, submit complete packages, track SLAs, maintain buffer in schedule.
- Supply chain constraints: Identify alternates, prequalify suppliers, order long-lead items early.
- Hidden site conditions: Conduct thorough surveys; hold contingency (10–20%); plan investigative demolition.
- Business disruption: Phase work, use swing spaces, schedule after-hours, communicate early and often.
- IT dependencies and cutover risks: Run dress rehearsals; back-out plans; freeze windows; dual-run where possible.
- Safety incidents: Enforce PTW/LOTO, supervisor presence, daily toolbox talks, and audits.
- Non-compliance with codes: Involve code consultants; conduct design reviews and pre-inspections.
- Documentation gaps: Assign a document controller; set SLAs; make updates a prerequisite for financial close.
- User resistance to new ways of working: Change champions, training, clear policy updates, and feedback loops.

## Performance Metrics
- Schedule adherence: % milestones met on time; schedule variance (SV).
- Budget adherence: Cost variance (CV), final cost vs. approved budget.
- Change request cycle time: Avg. days from request to approval; from approval to completion.
- Downtime impact: Hours of business disruption vs. plan; % work executed after-hours.
- Safety: TRIR, number of PTW breaches, near misses reported and resolved.
- Quality: Punch list items per 1,000 sq ft; time to close punch items; rework rate.
- Compliance: % permits approved first pass; audit findings count; code compliance defects.
- User satisfaction: Post-occupancy CSAT, ergonomics comfort scores.
- Utilization and effectiveness: Pre/post occupancy utilization, meeting room availability, density vs. target.
- Data integrity: % assets correctly tagged; timeliness of as-built and IWMS updates.
- Sustainability: % materials reused/recycled; waste diverted from landfill; VOC/IEQ metrics post-change.

## Technology and Tools
- IWMS/CAFM: Space planning, move management, work orders (e.g., Archibus, Planon, Tririga).
- BIM/CAD: Revit, AutoCAD for design, as-builts, clash detection.
- CMMS: Maintenance integration, asset and warranty updates (e.g., Maximo).
- ITSM: Request intake and change coordination (e.g., ServiceNow, Jira Service Management).
- Project and portfolio management: MS Project, Smartsheet, Primavera; risk and issue logs.
- EHS and PTW systems: Digital permit-to-work, incident reporting, LOTO registers.
- Procurement and ERP: SAP/Oracle for sourcing, POs, budget control; contractor prequalification tools.
- Occupancy and analytics: Sensors, booking systems, Wi-Fi analytics, digital twins for scenario planning.
- AV and network management: Monitoring and remote configuration tools for IT/AV.
- Visualization and engagement: VR/AR walkthroughs, 3D renders; communication platforms (email, Teams, Slack).
- Labeling and asset tagging: Barcoding/QR systems and mobile scanners for move accuracy.
- Document management: SharePoint/Confluence for drawings, O&Ms, permits, and version control.

Process Details:
## Overview
Relocate people is the structured process for moving employees or teams from one location to another (e.g., desk-to-desk, floor-to-floor, building-to-building, or city-to-city) to support organizational changes such as headcount growth, reorganizations, restacks, renovations, lease changes, or space optimization. It sits within Manage facilities operations and coordinates space planning, facilities, IT, security, HR, and vendor activities to complete moves safely, on time, and with minimal disruption. The process also ensures accurate updates to space and asset records, access permissions, cost allocations, and emergency rosters.

Objectives:
- Enable business agility by executing moves efficiently and predictably
- Minimize downtime and risk to business operations and employee safety
- Ensure compliance with workplace, health and safety, security, and data governance requirements
- Maintain accurate, auditable space utilization and asset records

Scope:
- Individual and small group moves (MAC: move/add/change)
- Departmental restacks and large-scale moves
- Temporary swing-space moves for renovations
- Onsite-to-onsite, onsite-to-remote/hybrid transitions, and vice versa
- Excludes immigration/legal aspects of international relocation benefits (handled by HR), but includes facility readiness for international arrivals

## Key Activities
- Intake and validation of move requests
- Space planning and allocation (seating assignment, adjacency needs, accessibility)
- Budgeting, approvals, and scheduling
- Site readiness (furniture, power, network, cleanliness, signage)
- IT/telecom provisioning and deprovisioning
- Security access adjustments (badging, restricted areas)
- Move logistics (packing materials, labeling, vendor coordination, chain-of-custody)
- Health, safety, and ergonomic assessments
- Communications and change management
- Day-of move execution, supervision, and incident handling
- Post-move support, issue resolution, and close-out
- Record updates (IWMS/CAFM, HRIS location, asset registry, cost centers, emergency lists)

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Approved move request or trigger (org changes, project plan, lease events, renovation schedule)
- Headcount plan and roster with specific employee names/IDs
- Seating/adjacency requirements; special accommodations (ADA, ergonomic needs)
- IT and equipment requirements (monitors, docks, phones, specialty peripherals, lab gear)
- Floor plans, space inventory, and occupancy/utilization data
- Move windows/blackout dates and business critical calendars
- Vendor contracts and quotes (movers, cleaners, electricians, low-voltage)
- Security requirements (zone restrictions, confidentiality level)
- Budget/cost center and approval thresholds
- Policies and standards (move lead times, labeling, chain-of-custody, EHS)

Prerequisites:
- Current and accurate space and asset records in IWMS/CAFM
- Designated move governance (approval matrix, SLAs, tiered move types)
- Validated facility capacity and compliance (fire codes, egress, density)
- Available swing space if needed
- IT network and power infrastructure in destination location
- Insurance and permits (where applicable)
- Union/labor and landlord coordination rules understood (if applicable)

Dependencies on other processes:
- Workforce planning and organizational changes
- Manage space and occupancy, Manage workplace services, Manage IT provisioning/deprovisioning
- Manage security and access control, Manage EHS
- Manage vendor and contract management, Procure-to-Pay
- Change management and internal communications
- Records management and asset lifecycle management

## Process Steps
1. Intake and triage
   - Receive move request via service portal or project trigger.
   - Classify move type (individual MAC, small team, departmental restack, building-to-building).
   - Validate completeness (roster, dates, requirements) and assign a Move Coordinator.

2. Feasibility and scoping
   - Review floor plans, capacity, and adjacency/functional needs with Space Planner and business lead.
   - Identify constraints (blackout dates, power/network capacity, security zones).
   - Determine required services (IT, telecom, lab, EHS, cleaners, signage).

3. Estimate costs and secure funding
   - Prepare estimate: movers, materials, overtime, IT work, furniture changes, temp storage.
   - Identify cost center(s) and obtain approvals per policy.
   - Create purchase requisitions and engage vendors per contract.

4. Develop the move plan
   - Create detailed seating plan and move list with employee IDs and asset tags.
   - Define schedule and move window (often after-hours/weekend to minimize disruption).
   - Build RACI and contact list; set up a war room/chat channel for stakeholders.
   - Draft communications plan (leader comms, employee instructions, wayfinding).
   - Prepare risk/issue log and contingency plans (e.g., holdover desks, spare equipment).

5. Site readiness
   - Verify destination readiness: furniture configuration, power outlets, network ports, Wi-Fi coverage, cleanliness.
   - Conduct EHS walkthrough for egress, accessibility, and ergonomic considerations.
   - Order and stage packing materials, labels, carts; prepare color-coded floor maps.
   - Arrange signage/wayfinding, nameplates/desk IDs, and updated emergency maps.

6. IT/Telecom preparation
   - Provision or move user equipment (laptops, docks, monitors) and specialty gear.
   - Configure network ports, VLANs, phone extensions/softphone updates.
   - Validate software licensing for location-specific applications (if applicable).
   - Prepare spares and on-site IT support for day-of and Day 1.

7. Security and access
   - Update badge access permissions for destination areas.
   - Arrange for secure transport of sensitive assets and records (sealed bins, chain-of-custody).
   - Notify reception/front-of-house and update visitor systems.

8. Employee communications
   - Send move packets with date/time, packing instructions, label schema, desk assignment, maps, and FAQs.
   - Provide ergonomic and accessibility guidance; offer pre-move Q&A sessions.
   - Share helpdesk contacts and Day 1 support details.

9. Pre-move confirmations
   - Reconfirm rosters, special accommodations, and business blackout constraints.
   - Conduct final readiness checks with Facilities, IT, Security, EHS, and vendor leads.
   - Issue go/no-go decision per governance.

10. Packing and labeling
   - Employees pack personal and work items per instructions; movers pack shared assets.
   - Apply color-coded labels with name, employee ID, origin/destination, and sequence.
   - Document asset tag lists and photos for high-value or sensitive items.

11. Move execution
   - Supervise vendor crew; control access to floors and elevators; manage loading docks.
   - Sequence moves to reduce congestion; protect building surfaces; enforce safety protocols.
   - Transport equipment, files, and personal effects; install at destination per plan.
   - IT completes connections and tests critical services (network, monitors, phones).

12. Quality checks and Day 1 readiness
   - Perform desk-by-desk verification against the move list.
   - Resolve exceptions and issues; escalate per runbook if delays occur.
   - Update wayfinding and remove obsolete signage at origin.

13. Post-move support
   - Staff a walk-up support desk or roving techs for 1–3 days.
   - Address ergonomic adjustments, minor furniture tweaks, and IT tickets.
   - Collect unused packing materials; arrange cleaning of origin/destination spaces.

14. Decommission and space reset
   - Reset origin space (make-good per lease/landlord rules) or prep for next occupants.
   - Securely dispose of or store unclaimed items per records policy.
   - Remove/transfer phone numbers, print queues, and local configurations.

15. Systems and records update
   - Update IWMS/CAFM seating plans, occupancy, and utilization.
   - Update HRIS location field, emergency rosters, mailroom routing, asset registry, cost allocations.
   - Adjust security access profiles and parking allocations as needed.

16. Close-out and continuous improvement
   - Reconcile vendor invoices against POs; capture actual costs vs. estimate.
   - Conduct post-move survey; review KPIs and lessons learned.
   - Update standard work, checklists, and playbooks.

- Completed move with employees operational in new location
- Updated seating plans and occupancy records
- Updated HRIS location, security access, and emergency rosters
- Installed and tested equipment; decommissioned origin setups
- Accurate asset movements recorded; chain-of-custody logs
- Communications delivered; signage and wayfinding updated

- Post-move survey results and lessons learned

Success criteria:
- On-time move completion within approved budget
- Day 1 readiness achieved (workstations fully functional)
- Minimal business disruption (measured downtime within threshold)
- Zero safety incidents; compliance with EHS and security policies
- Accurate systems updated within SLA
- Positive employee satisfaction score above target

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Move Coordinator (Facilities): Owns end-to-end planning, scheduling, execution, and close-out; single point of contact.
- Space Planner: Designs seating/allocation; ensures code compliance and adjacency needs.
- IT Workplace/End-User Services: Provisions/moves equipment, network/telecom setup, Day 1 support.
- Security/Access Control: Adjusts badge permissions; oversees secure transport procedures.
- EHS Specialist: Reviews safety, ergonomics, accessibility, and compliance; approves move method statements.
- Business Unit Move Lead: Consolidates requirements, approves rosters, coordinates team communications.
- Employees: Pack personal items, label correctly, follow instructions, report issues.
- HR Business Partner: Confirms roster, manages sensitive/confidential moves, updates HR data as required.
- Finance/Procurement: Approves budgets, issues POs, reconciles invoices.
- Vendor(s) (Movers, Cleaners, Low-Voltage, Furniture): Execute field tasks per SOW, adhere to site and safety rules.
- Reception/Mailroom: Update directories, mail routing, and wayfinding.
- Records Management/Legal: Govern handling of physical records, retention, and secure disposal when applicable.

## Best Practices
- Establish a tiered move catalog with SLAs (e.g., small MAC ≤10 people: 10 business days; medium: 20; large restack: project-managed).
- Standardize intake via a single portal with templates (roster upload, special needs checklist).
- Use color-coded labels mapped to destination zones and clear floor maps posted on move day.
- Lock in move windows and freeze periods around critical business events; align with change control calendars.
- Maintain a pre-staged inventory of common equipment and spare kits to recover quickly from failures.
- Enforce chain-of-custody for sensitive assets; use sealed bins and sign-off logs.
- Pilot a subset of moves to validate assumptions and uncover issues before scaling.
- Provide clear, multi-channel communications (email, chat, posters, floor walks) and a Day 1 “white-glove” desk.
- Conduct ergonomic quick-fits on Day 1; provide sit-stand and accessibility accommodations promptly.
- Keep accurate IWMS/CAFM data; perform post-move audits to reconcile reality vs. plan.
- Measure and review KPIs; run regular retrospectives to improve checklists and playbooks.
- Coordinate with landlords and base building management early for dock/elevator bookings and permits.
- Plan for sustainability: reuse furniture, minimize packing waste, and recycle materials.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Incomplete or late requirements: Use mandatory intake fields, deadlines, and gating approvals; hold readiness reviews.
- Conflicting priorities/blackout periods: Maintain a shared move calendar; escalate via governance for trade-offs.
- IT delays or incompatibilities: Engage IT early; pre-test ports and Wi-Fi; stage spares; maintain rollback plans.
- Damage/loss of items: Require labeling, packing standards, insurance certificates, and chain-of-custody for sensitive items.
- Employee resistance and change fatigue: Communicate early, explain rationale/benefits, provide floor ambassadors and quick support.
- Capacity constraints (elevators, docks, vendor crews): Stagger schedules, book resources early, split moves across windows.
- Safety incidents: Enforce PPE/use of trained movers only; EHS-approved method statements; secure pathways and protect surfaces.
- Data inaccuracies post-move: Institute same-day updates and audits; assign data ownership; automate feeds between IWMS and HRIS.
- Confidential moves (e.g., reorganizations): Limit visibility of plans, time-box execution, and use need-to-know rosters with NDAs.

## Performance Metrics
- On-time move rate (% moves completed by planned date/time)
- Day 1 readiness rate (% employees fully operational on first business day)
- Average move cycle time (request to completion), by move tier
- First-contact resolution rate for post-move tickets; average time to resolve
- Cost per person moved vs. budget variance
- Employee satisfaction (post-move survey score/CSAT)
- Safety incident rate (TRIR, near-misses) during moves
- Data accuracy rate (discrepancies between plan and actual seat/asset locations)
- Unplanned downtime hours attributable to the move
- Vendor performance (SLA adherence, quality scores)

- IWMS/CAFM and space planning: Archibus, Planon, Trimble Manhattan, FM:Systems; CAD/BIM tools (AutoCAD/Revit) for floor plans.
- Service/request management: ServiceNow, Freshservice, Jira Service Management for intake and workflow.
- ITSM/Endpoint management: Microsoft Intune, SCCM, Jamf; network monitoring; VoIP/UC platforms.
- Asset and inventory management: Barcoding/label printers, scanners, CMDB integrations.
- Security/access systems: Lenel, Genetec, CCure; visitor and parking systems.
- Project and collaboration tools: MS Project, Smartsheet, Asana; Teams/Slack channels for coordination.
- Survey/feedback tools: Qualtrics, Medallia, MS Forms for post-move CSAT.
- EHS tools: Safety management platforms for risk assessments and incident logging.
- Vendor management: CLM/Procurement systems for POs, insurance tracking, and scheduling.
- Wayfinding and digital signage: Kiosk/QR-based maps; intranet pages for move information.

Process Details:
## Overview
Relocate Material and Tools covers the planning and execution of moving raw materials, WIP, finished goods, tools, fixtures, and (where in scope) portable machinery within or between facilities. The purpose is to enable production layout changes, capacity increases, maintenance shutdowns, 5S/lean improvements, and business continuity with minimal disruption, zero safety incidents, and no loss or damage. This process ensures accurate inventory control, asset integrity (including tool calibration status), compliance with EHS and quality requirements, and timely availability at the new location. It sits within Facilities Operations and coordinates with Production, Warehouse/Logistics, Maintenance, EHS, and Quality.

## Key Activities
- Intake and triage of move requests (scope, priority, timing)
- Risk assessment and permitting (EHS/JHA, lift plan, LOTO, hazardous materials)
- Move planning (routing, scheduling, resource and equipment allocation)
- Inventory and asset verification (count, condition, serial numbers, calibration status)
- Packaging, protection, and labeling (ESD, cleanroom, shock/tilt indicators)
- Route preparation (clearances, floor load verification, barricades, signage)
- Execution of move (handling, transport, scanning, chain of custody)
- Placement, installation, and reconnection (leveling, anchoring, utilities)
- Post-move verification (calibration checks, inventory reconciliation, trial runs)
- Systems updates and closeout (WMS/ERP/EAM updates, as-built floor plans, lessons learned)

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs to begin:
- Approved move request with business justification, scope, and required-by date
- Item list: materials (SKU/lot/qty/status), tools (ID/serial/calibration due date), equipment specs (weight, dimensions, center of gravity, lift points)
- Current/new locations (zone, aisle, rack/bin, station, building), floor plans and load ratings
- Handling requirements: ESD, cleanliness, temperature/humidity, hazardous substance info (SDS)
- System contexts: WMS/ERP locations, EAM/CMMS asset records, tool crib database
- Operational constraints: production schedules, blackout windows, customer orders affected

Prerequisites:
- Risk assessment/JHA and required permits (e.g., lift, hot work, work at height)
- Trained personnel available (forklift, rigger, crane operator, LOTO authorized)
- MHE and rigging certified and inspected; packaging materials on hand
- Change control/quality approvals if regulated (e.g., GMP, aerospace), line clearance plans
- Communication plan approved; stakeholders notified; staging areas identified

Dependencies on other processes:
- 10.1.4 Manage facilities operations (overall coordination)
- Production planning and scheduling (downtime windows)
- Warehouse and inventory management (location control, cycle counts)
- Asset management/maintenance (LOTO, disconnection/reconnection, calibration)
- EHS management (permits, JHA, ergonomic/manual handling standards)
- Quality management and document control (change control, records retention)
- Security and access control (escorts, restricted areas)
- IT/OT change management (machine/network configurations)

## Process Steps
1) Intake and triage
- Receive move request via ticketing system with scope, items, timeline, and constraints.
- Classify move: minor in-area relocation; intra-facility move; inter-building/offsite transfer; critical/regulated.
- Assign Move Coordinator; create preliminary schedule and budget.

2) Define scope and assess risk
- Walkdown current and target areas; perform route survey for clearances, turning radii, ramp gradients, floor load ratings, and overhead obstacles.
- Review item characteristics (weight, COG, fragility, hazardous contents, cleanliness).
- Conduct Job Hazard Analysis; identify required permits (lift, LOTO, hot work, confined space) and controls (PPE, barricades, spotters).
- For equipment: review OEM manuals for lift points, draining/blanking, transport restrictions.

3) Approvals and change control
- Obtain required approvals: Production, EHS, Facilities, Quality, Tooling, IT/OT, and Finance (if asset capitalization/transfer).
- For regulated items/areas, open change control; define validation/qualification impact (e.g., IQ/OQ requalification).

4) Plan the move
- Develop Move Plan detailing:
  - Item list and classification (raw/WIP/finished/hazardous; tools calibrated/non-calibrated; portable equipment).
  - Sequence, time windows, and freeze periods for affected work centers.
  - Resource plan: personnel, MHE (forklifts, pallet jacks, cranes), rigging gear, packaging, and transport.
  - Handling/packaging specs (ESD bags, cleanroom wraps, dunnage, crates; shock/tilt indicators).
  - Route control and staging zones; egress/fire code compliance.
  - Communication plan (pre-move briefing, stakeholder notifications).
  - Contingencies (backup equipment, weather plan if exposed path, alternate routes).
- Create lift plans for heavy/complex lifts, including load calculations and rigging diagrams.

5) Pre-move preparation
- Inventory and condition capture:
  - Count and verify materials by SKU/lot/serial; record conditions; photograph high-value/fragile items.
  - For tools: record serial/calibration due; verify status; plan recalibration if required after move.
  - For equipment: backup configurations/recipes/PLC parameters; drain fluids; purge lines; remove loose parts.
- Documentation and labeling:
  - Generate and affix move labels with barcodes/RFID including old/new location, item ID, handling instructions.
  - Prepare packing lists and chain-of-custody forms; segregate hold/quarantine/status-controlled materials.
- Safety preparations:
  - Conduct LOTO for equipment; verify zero energy; issue permits.
  - Stage barricades/signage; floor protection; edge/overhead protection where needed.
  - Toolbox talk with team covering hazards, roles, signals, and emergency procedures.

6) Execute packing and staging
- Pack items per specification: use anti-static materials, cushioning, cleanroom bagging as required.
- Kit small tools/consumables by workcell; seal containers; apply tamper-evident seals where needed.
- Move items to staging areas; scan to “in transit” status in WMS/EAM/tool crib system.

7) Execute move
- Clear route; deploy spotters; enforce pedestrian exclusion zones.
- Perform lifts/transports per plan; adhere to speed limits and load-handling rules; maintain line-of-sight.
- Real-time scanning at key checkpoints; maintain chain-of-custody logs for high-value/regulated items.
- For inter-building/offsite: comply with DOT/ADR as applicable; prepare BOL/manifests; use secured transport.

8) Placement and reconnection
- Place materials into assigned racks/bins; scan to new locations; perform cycle count sampling.
- Position tools and fixtures; organize per 5S; update shadow boards and visual controls.
- For equipment:
  - Set and anchor; level and align; reconnect utilities (power, air, water, network) per LTO/permit.
  - Torque verification; guards reinstalled; verify interlocks; remove LOTO with authorization.
  - Environmental checks (temperature, humidity, cleanliness) if required.

9) Post-move verification and release
- Materials: reconcile counts; resolve variances; quality inspect for damage; release for use.
- Tools: functional check; calibration verification or recalibration; update status labels and system.
- Equipment: dry run/startup; SAT checklist; verify scrap rate and performance to baseline; QA sign-off if regulated.
- Close permits; remove barricades; clean work areas; dispose of waste/packaging properly.

10) Systems update and closeout
- Update WMS/ERP locations; EAM/CMMS asset records; tool crib database; floor plans and emergency maps.
- Update financial asset master (location, custodian, asset tag); depreciation location if applicable.
- Capture deviations, incidents, near-misses; conduct brief lessons-learned review; archive Move Plan and records.

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs:
- Materials, tools, and equipment relocated to the correct locations, available for use as scheduled.
- Accurate, reconciled inventory and asset records reflecting new locations/status.
- Safe completion without injury, spills, or property damage.

Deliverables produced:

- Calibration transfer log and certificates (if recalibrated)
- Commissioning/startup checklist and sign-offs
- Updated WMS/ERP, EAM/CMMS, tool crib records, and floor plans
- Closeout report (performance, issues, lessons learned)

Success criteria:
- On-time completion within budget and scheduled downtime
- Zero recordable safety incidents and environmental events
- Zero loss/misplaced items; damage rate within target (e.g., <100 ppm)
- Inventory accuracy and tool calibration compliance at or above target thresholds
- Equipment achieves performance-to-baseline within agreed time

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Move Coordinator (Facilities/Operations): Owns plan, schedule, coordination, communication, and closeout.
- EHS Specialist: Leads JHA; issues/monitors permits; ensures compliance with safety standards; conducts toolbox talk.
- Warehouse/Logistics Lead: Manages material picking, packing, staging, scanning, transport logistics, and WMS updates.
- Tool Crib/Tooling Manager: Verifies tool inventory and calibration status; manages kitting and post-move calibration.
- Maintenance/Engineering (Mechanical/Electrical/Utilities): LOTO, disconnection/reconnection, leveling, anchoring, commissioning.
- Qualified Riggers/Operators: Execute lifts and moves per lift plans; inspect and use rigging and MHE safely.
- Production Supervisor: Aligns move with production windows; authorizes line clearance and release back to production.
- Quality/Validation: Oversees handling of quality-status materials; approves release; manages change control/qualification.
- IT/OT Technician: Backs up/restores configurations; reconnects networks; validates machine communications.
- Security/Access Control: Manages access to restricted areas; escorts; monitors high-value transfers.
- Finance/Asset Accounting: Updates asset master location and custody; validates capitalization impacts.
- Project Manager (for large-scale moves): Integrates cross-functional tasks, risk, and stakeholder management.

## Best Practices
- Standardize with SOPs, checklists, and templates for move requests, risk assessment, packing, and commissioning.
- Use visual management: color-coded move waves, labeled staging zones, floor tape for new locations.
- Perform a detailed route and floor load assessment; pre-measure clearances; use 3D/BIM or digital twin when available.
- Enforce LOTO and lift plan discipline; require certified operators and inspected equipment.
- Protect items with appropriate packaging: ESD-safe, cleanroom-compatible, moisture barrier, shock/tilt indicators.
- Apply robust labeling and scanning at every handoff; leverage RFID/RTLS for real-time tracking of critical items.
- Schedule moves during planned downtime/after-hours; communicate widely; use single point of contact.
- Pre/post photos and condition reports for high-value items; insure when needed.
- For equipment, back up control programs and parameters; create a requalification plan before moving.
- Implement 5S at destination: set-in-order, labeled storage, updated shadow boards and addresses.
- Pilot critical moves with a non-critical item; confirm playbook before full execution.
- Document lessons learned and continually refine the Move Plan library.

## Common Challenges
- Production disruption and delays: Mitigate with freeze windows, phased moves, and decoupling buffers.
- Item loss/misdirection: Prevent via mandatory scanning at pick, stage, load, unload, and put-away; clear address labels.
- Damage during handling: Use proper rigging, protective packaging, trained operators, and route prep; deploy shock/tilt indicators.
- Inaccurate inventory/asset records: Require real-time system updates; perform post-move cycle counts and reconciliations.
- Calibration drift or loss of qualification: Verify calibration before/after; quarantine tools until confirmed; plan requalification.
- Space and access constraints: Conduct route surveys; remove obstacles; schedule temporary racking moves; use compact MHE/AMRs.
- Safety incidents: Enforce JHA, permits, toolbox talks, and supervision; maintain exclusion zones and spotters.

- Utility reconnection issues: Pre-validate utility availability; have skilled trades on-call; use checklists for power/network/air/water.

- Calibration compliance post-move (% tools released without OOT)
- First-pass startup success for equipment (% without rework)
- Safety performance (TRIR, near-misses, permit compliance %)
- Budget adherence (cost variance)
- Cycle time per move type (minor/intra-facility/inter-building)
- % moves executed with documented JHA and lift plan
- Stakeholder satisfaction score post-move

## Technology and Tools
- WMS/ERP: Location control, move orders, scanning (e.g., SAP EWM, Oracle WMS, Manhattan).
- EAM/CMMS: Asset records, LOTO, work orders, commissioning logs (e.g., IBM Maximo, Infor EAM).

- MHE and rigging: Forklifts, pallet jacks, hoists, cranes, dollies, skates; load cells; certified slings/shackles.
- AGVs/AMRs: Automated internal material transport for repeatable move lanes.
- Packaging/protection: ESD-safe materials, cleanroom wraps, crates, shock/tilt sensors, moisture barrier bags.
- IT/OT tools: PLC/robot backups, network configuration management.
