Process Details:
## Overview
Manage customer meetings/workshops is the structured process of planning, delivering, and following up on customer-facing meetings, seminars, workshops, and training events. The purpose is to educate prospects and customers on offerings, best practices, and relevant innovations; to uncover and shape demand; to accelerate opportunities; and to drive product adoption, retention, and loyalty. This process spans in-person and virtual formats, including executive briefings, discovery workshops, solution deep-dives, user trainings, and customer communities.

Role in the organization:
- Supports sales strategy by advancing qualified opportunities and expanding existing accounts.
- Strengthens customer relationships and trust through value-focused education and co-creation.
- Feeds market and product teams with real customer insights.
- Aligns commercial motions with product/service roadmaps, delivery, and customer success initiatives.

## Key Activities
- Objective and audience definition: Clarify why the session is needed and who should attend.
- Agenda and content design: Tailor format, topics, demos, and materials to stakeholder needs.
- Logistics and scheduling: Book venues/virtual platforms, align calendars, manage registrations.
- Speaker and resource coordination: Assign facilitators, sales engineers, exec sponsors; prepare demo environments.
- Compliance and approvals: Validate messaging, branding, claims, legal and privacy requirements.
- Promotion and invitations: Craft and send invites, reminders, and pre-reads.
- Delivery and facilitation: Run the meeting/workshop, manage time and engagement.
- Documentation: Capture notes, decisions, risks, objections, and action items.
- Follow-up: Send thank-you, materials, and next steps; update CRM and tasks.
- Measurement and improvement: Analyze outcomes, engagement, and pipeline impact; implement improvements.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs to begin:
  - Qualified lead/opportunity or account plan with clear objectives
  - Stakeholder map (personas, roles, decision makers, champions)
  - Proposed topics/use cases and desired outcomes
  - Availability of presenters/facilitators and required SMEs
  - Approved content and demos (current, compliant, brand-aligned)
  - Budget and logistics constraints (venue, tools, travel)
  - CRM data (contact details, account history, prior interactions)
  - Consent/permissions for outreach and recording, if applicable
- Prerequisites:
  - Defined success criteria and KPIs for the session
  - Internal RACI and owner assigned (Sales/CSM/Event lead)
  - Legal/Compliance review completed for sensitive content, data handling, and claims
  - Technical readiness (sandbox/demo org, AV checks, backup plans)
  - Accessibility plans (captions, interpreters, dietary needs)
- Dependencies on other processes:
  - 3.5.1 Manage leads/opportunities (qualification, account planning)
  - 3.5.1.8 Manage customer sales calls (cadence and governance)
  - Marketing content management and product marketing approvals
  - Legal/compliance and brand governance processes
  - Customer success onboarding/adoption programs for training handoffs
  - IT/Facilities/Event management for logistics

## Process Steps
1) Initiate and scope
- Confirm business objective (e.g., accelerate Stage X opportunity, expand footprint, drive adoption).
- Identify target audience and decision process; build attendee list and roles.
- Select format (briefing, workshop, training, webinar) and expected duration.

2) Plan and design
- Draft SMART session objectives and success criteria.
- Build agenda with timed sections, breaks, and interactive elements (polls, Q&A, exercises).
- Tailor content and demos to customer context (industry, use cases, maturity).
- Assign roles: lead facilitator, co-presenters, note-taker, moderator, executive sponsor.

3) Secure approvals and resources
- Route agenda and content for product marketing/brand and legal/compliance review.
- Book venue or virtual platform; perform AV/tech checks; arrange accessibility services.
- Provision demo environments, data, and credentials; prepare leave-behinds.
- Finalize budget; arrange catering and travel if in-person.

4) Invite and prepare attendees
- Send value-centric invitation with agenda, outcomes, speakers, logistics.
- Capture registrations and dietary/accessibility needs; manage reminders (T-7, T-1).
- Provide pre-reads, prerequisites (e.g., account prep, environment access), and NDAs if needed.
- Conduct internal dry run; rehearse handoffs and Q&A; confirm time zones.

5) Execute session
- Open with purpose, outcomes, and agenda; set norms and timing.
- Deliver content and demos; facilitate interaction; probe for needs, risks, and objections.
- Manage time rigorously; adjust depth based on engagement signals.
- Note decisions, questions, follow-ups, and potential opportunities/risks.

6) Close and immediate follow-up
- Summarize key takeaways, decisions, and agreed next steps with owners and dates.
- Confirm next touchpoint (e.g., proposal review, pilot plan, training schedule).
- Thank attendees; send materials, recording (if consented), and action list within 24–48 hours.

7) Record and operationalize
- Log the meeting in CRM with attendees, notes, outcomes, tasks, and next steps.
- Create/assign follow-up tasks with SLAs; link to opportunity/account records.
- Tag insights for product/marketing (feature requests, competitive intel).

8) Measure outcomes and improve
- Collect attendee feedback survey (CSAT/NPS, content relevance, presenter effectiveness).
- Analyze attendance vs. registrations, engagement metrics, and pipeline influence.
- Conduct internal retrospective; capture improvements to agenda, content, and logistics.
- Update playbooks, templates, and content repository.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Outputs:
  - Confirmed attendee list and attendance record
  - Tailored agenda and session materials (slides, demos, workbooks)
  - Meeting notes, decisions, risks, objections, and action items with owners/dates
  - Recording/transcript (with consent) and shared resources
  - CRM updates linking session to accounts/opportunities
  - Survey results and engagement analytics
- Deliverables:
  - Follow-up plan (tasks, proposals, pilots, training schedules)
  - Executive summary for sponsors and account team
  - Updated account plan and opportunity strategy
  - Insights report to product/marketing/CS regarding features, messaging, and adoption blockers
- Success criteria:
  - Session objectives met (e.g., agreed pilot scope, technical validation achieved)
  - Target attendance and engagement thresholds reached
  - Positive satisfaction/likelihood-to-recommend scores
  - Measurable impact on opportunity progression, expansion, or adoption metrics

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Account Executive (AE) / Sales Lead: Owns objectives, audience, and outcomes; drives invitations; leads business segments; ensures CRM hygiene.
- Sales Engineer / Solutions Consultant: Designs and delivers demos; leads technical deep-dives; validates feasibility; captures technical risks.
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): Aligns content to adoption goals; coordinates training/workshops post-sale; ensures continuity.
- Product Marketing: Reviews and approves messaging; provides tailored collateral; ensures positioning and competitive accuracy.
- Event/Field Marketing or Event Coordinator: Manages logistics, registrations, venues/platforms, and communications cadence.
- Presenter/Facilitator: Delivers content; manages engagement and time; sets session norms.
- Executive Sponsor: Provides strategic context and commitment; engages senior customer stakeholders.
- Note-taker/Moderator: Captures notes and actions; moderates Q&A and chat; monitors time.
- Legal/Compliance: Reviews claims, disclaimers, NDAs, privacy/recording consent, and regional requirements.
- IT/AV Support: Ensures technology readiness; manages backups and live troubleshooting.
- Data/Revenue Operations: Builds reports/dashboards; attributes influence; ensures data quality and taxonomy.

RACI guideline:
- Responsible: AE, SE/SC, Event Coordinator, Presenter, CSM
- Accountable: AE (business outcome), Event Coordinator (logistics)
- Consulted: Product Marketing, Legal/Compliance, Executive Sponsor, IT/AV
- Informed: Sales leadership, Product, CS leadership

## Best Practices
- Start with value: Articulate customer outcomes and why the session matters; design agendas to solve their problems, not to showcase features only.
- Tailor by persona: Customize content for executives, business users, and technical stakeholders; avoid one-size-fits-all decks.
- Make it interactive: Use polls, whiteboarding, breakouts, and hands-on exercises; time-box discussions; assign a moderator.
- Prepare thoroughly: Rehearse end-to-end; run environment and AV checks; prepare answers to expected objections; have backups.
- Keep it accessible and inclusive: Provide captions, readable materials, and content in attendees’ languages when needed; accommodate time zones.
- Secure and compliant: Obtain consent for recording; avoid exposing sensitive data in demos; comply with privacy and regional regulations.
- Set clear next steps: Agree on owners and dates in the room; show the path from session to outcome (e.g., pilot, proposal, training plan).
- Close the loop in CRM: Log activities, outcomes, and tasks the same day; tag insights consistently for analytics.
- Measure and iterate: Collect feedback; run retros; update playbooks and content; sunset outdated materials.
- Align with roadmap and delivery: Sync with product and services teams; avoid overpromising; present supported features/commitments only.

## Common Challenges
- Low attendance or no-shows
  - Solutions: Value-driven invitations, multi-touch reminders, executive outreach, calendar holds, offer alternative times/recordings.
- Misaligned content or expectations
  - Solutions: Pre-call discovery; confirm objectives in invites; share and align on agenda in advance; adjust on the fly with parking lot topics.
- Technical issues (AV, platform, demo failures)
  - Solutions: Redundant connectivity; backup devices; offline content; demo recordings; IT/AV standby; run-of-show checklist and tech rehearsal.
- Time overruns and lack of outcomes
  - Solutions: Strong facilitation; timed agenda; visible timer; decision and action capture in real-time; reserve wrap-up time.
- Sensitive topics and compliance risks
  - Solutions: Pre-approved messaging; legal review; NDAs; avoid roadmap commitments beyond policy; sanitized demo data.
- Difficult group dynamics
  - Solutions: Ground rules; use moderator; breakouts; parking lot; escalate offline for contentious items.
- Poor follow-up discipline
  - Solutions: Immediate creation of tasks with owners and SLAs; automated reminders; manager oversight; dashboards showing overdue actions.
- Global and accessibility barriers
  - Solutions: Localize content; provide captions and translations; rotate time slots; share on-demand recordings with accessible formats.

## Performance Metrics
- Activity and reach:
  - Number of meetings/workshops executed by segment/region
  - Registration-to-attendance rate and no-show rate
  - Attendee mix vs. target personas and buying committee coverage
- Engagement and satisfaction:
  - In-session engagement (poll participation, Q&A volume, chat interactions, time on session)
  - Post-session CSAT and session NPS
  - Content relevance and presenter effectiveness scores

- Customer outcomes:

- Operational excellence:

  - Cost per attendee and ROI (attributed revenue vs. cost)
  - On-time start and agenda adherence rate

## Technology and Tools
- CRM and Revenue Platforms: Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, HubSpot CRM for tracking attendees, outcomes, tasks, and attribution.
- Marketing Automation and Event Management: Marketo, HubSpot, Cvent, Eventbrite for invitations, registrations, reminders, and landing pages.
- Meeting/Webinar Platforms: Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Webex, ON24 for delivery; ensure enterprise licenses and security controls.
- Learning and Training: LMS platforms (e.g., Docebo, Cornerstone) for structured training, certifications, and completion tracking.
- Content and Sales Enablement: Seismic, Highspot, Google Drive/SharePoint for approved collateral and version control.
- Presentation and Collaboration: PowerPoint/Google Slides, Miro/Mural, whiteboarding tools for interactive workshops.
- Engagement Tools: Slido, Mentimeter, Kahoot for polls and Q&A.
- Survey and Feedback: SurveyMonkey, Qualtrics, Typeform for post-session feedback.
- Recording/Transcription and Conversation Intelligence: Zoom recordings, Otter.ai, Gong, Chorus for transcripts, highlights, and insights.
- Project/Task Management: Asana, Jira, Monday.com for run-of-show, checklists, and follow-up tasks.

- Analytics/BI: Tableau, Power BI, Looker for KPI dashboards and pipeline influence analysis.
- Demo Environments: Secure sandbox environments, data generators, and reset scripts to ensure reliable demonstrations.

Process Details:
# [3.5.1.8.5] Record outcome of sales process

## Overview
Record outcome of sales process is the formal closure activity for a sales cycle. It captures the final disposition of an opportunity (won, lost, or no-decision) and, for won deals, completes all commercial, legal, and financial documentation required to convert the sale into an order, invoice, and downstream fulfillment. This process ensures accurate, compliant, and timely handoff from Sales to Order Management, Finance, and Delivery while preserving a complete audit trail.

Purpose:
- Accurately document the final outcome of each sales effort.
- Execute and store binding agreements (contracts, SOWs, work orders).
- Exchange necessary legal/financial information with the customer.
- Book the order in enterprise systems and trigger invoicing and fulfillment.
- Provide reliable data for forecasting, revenue recognition, and analytics.

Role in the organization:
- Connects go-to-market execution with operational delivery and revenue realization.
- Reduces risk through standardized documentation, approvals, and compliance checks.
- Improves customer experience with clear, timely, and correct documentation and billing.
- Supports performance management (win/loss analysis, cycle times, pipeline health).

## Key Activities
- Determine final opportunity disposition (Won, Lost, No Decision/On Hold).
- Finalize commercial terms and pricing; confirm alignment with approvals.
- Generate, negotiate, and execute contracts/SOWs using approved templates and clause libraries.
- Collect and validate customer documentation (PO, vendor onboarding forms, tax certs, payment info).
- Complete internal approvals (deal desk, finance, legal, risk/compliance).
- Set up or verify customer account and master data in CRM/ERP.
- Create and book the order; establish billing schedule and payment terms.
- Issue invoice or proforma invoice per agreed billing triggers.
- Archive all documents and data in designated systems with proper metadata.
- Record win/loss reasons and key outcomes in CRM; communicate handoff to delivery/CS.
- For non-wins: release reserved inventory/quotations, notify stakeholders, schedule nurture/follow-up.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Opportunity record with final proposed configuration, pricing, and terms.
- Approved quote/CPQ output and discount approvals.
- Draft or redlined contract/SOW/work order and NDA (if applicable).
- Customer legal and billing information (legal entity name, address, tax IDs, billing contact, AP instructions).
- Customer purchase order (PO) or confirmation (if required).
- Compliance artifacts (KYC/AML where applicable, export control screening, data processing addenda).
- Credit assessment results and payment terms approval.
- Tax determination information (ship-to/service location, exemptions).

Prerequisites:
- Completed negotiations and internal approvals per authority matrix.
- Customer verbal acceptance or written intent.
- Verified product/service availability, lead times, and delivery feasibility.
- Clean data in CRM (close date, stage, products, quantities, pricing, contacts).

Dependencies on other processes:
- Manage customer sales calls [3.5.1.8] (negotiations, proposal).
- Price and quote (CPQ) and deal approval workflow.
- Credit and risk assessment processes.
- Contract lifecycle management (CLM) and legal review.
- Order fulfillment/provisioning, project initiation/onboarding.
- Billing and revenue recognition setup.

## Process Steps
1) Determine outcome and route
- Sales rep/AE confirms with customer and selects outcome:
  - Won: proceed to contracting and order booking.
  - Lost: update CRM as Closed–Lost; capture reason; skip contracting.
  - No Decision/On Hold: update CRM; set next review date; no contracting.
- Notify stakeholders of the outcome.

2) Validate deal readiness (Won path)
- Confirm latest quote version and approvals match intended terms.
- Validate product/service configuration, delivery dates, SLAs, and inclusions.
- Check export controls, sanctions lists, and any industry-specific compliance.
- Confirm credit approval and payment terms (prepay, net terms, milestones).

3) Finalize agreement documents
- Generate contract/SOW/work order using CLM templates.
- Apply pre-approved clauses; escalate deviations to Legal.
- Align contract pricing and terms with CPQ and approvals (no discrepancies).
- Include data protection, security addenda, and any regulatory clauses as required.
- Collect required insurance certificates or certifications, if applicable.

4) Execute agreements
- Route for internal signatures per delegation of authority.
- Send to customer via eSignature; validate signer authority.
- Capture and store executed documents in CLM/DMS; link to CRM/ERP records.
- If customer requires PO-first, capture PO number and attach.

5) Collect and validate customer documentation
- Vendor onboarding forms, W-9/W-8, customer tax exemption certificates, remittance details.
- Confirm legal entity names and addresses exactly match contract and PO.
- Verify billing contact, email, and EDI formats; confirm invoice requirements.

6) Set up master data
- Create or update customer account, billing/shipping addresses, tax profiles, currency, and payment method in ERP/MDM.
- Assign customer hierarchy/parent-child relationships for consolidated billing if needed.

7) Book the order
- Create sales order in ERP based on executed agreement and/or PO.
- Map items, quantities, SKUs, pricing, discounts, and billing schedule (one-time, subscription, milestones).
- Apply tax determination via tax engine; validate jurisdiction and exemptions.
- Obtain order booking approvals if required; lock order version.

8) Establish billing and revenue schedule
- Define invoice triggers (on signature, on delivery, monthly in advance, milestones).
- Configure revenue recognition rules (ASC 606/IFRS 15) with performance obligations and allocations.
- For prepayments, generate proforma invoice and collect payment if applicable.

9) Issue invoice and confirm
- Generate and send invoice per customer requirements (email, EDI, portal).
- Confirm receipt/acceptance of invoice with AP contact if required.
- Record payment terms, early-pay discounts, and dispute process.

10) Handoff to delivery/operations
- Share order package: executed contract/SOW, order record, scope, delivery dates, contacts, special terms.
- Create delivery or project kickoff tasks; schedule provisioning/implementation.
- For subscriptions/recurring services, activate in billing/provisioning systems.

11) Close and archive
- Update CRM: Closed–Won with products, TCV/ACV, start/end dates, close date, and competitor data.
- For Lost/No Decision: record structured reason codes and qualitative notes; mark follow-up plan.
- Archive all documents in DMS/CLM with retention tags; ensure audit trail.
- Release any temporary holds (inventory, quotes) or partner deal registrations.

Decision points and exceptions:
- If contract and PO terms conflict: reconcile via change order or PO revision.
- If credit denied: require prepayment, adjust scope, or escalate.
- Government/public sector deals: apply required clauses and compliance steps.
- Channel deals: confirm partner of record, deal registration, and invoicing entity (partner vs end-customer).

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs:
- Opportunity disposition recorded (Won/Lost/No Decision) with reason codes.
- Executed contract/SOW/work order and any addenda.
- Customer PO (if required) and vendor onboarding documents.
- Booked sales order in ERP with accurate pricing, terms, and schedules.
- Invoice(s) or proforma invoice generated and sent.
- Configured billing and revenue schedules.
- Complete document pack archived and linked across systems.
- Handoff package delivered to delivery/operations/CS.

Success criteria:
- 100% of closed opportunities have disposition and reason codes.
- Zero material discrepancies between contract, order, and invoice.
- Order booked and first invoice issued within SLA (e.g., 2 business days from execution).
- All required approvals present; audit trail complete.
- No rework due to data or document errors.
- Customer acknowledges receipt of contract/invoice where applicable.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Account Executive (AE)/Sales Rep: Decide disposition; drive contracting; collect customer docs; ensure data accuracy; coordinate handoff.
- Sales Operations: Validate data completeness; ensure system updates; enforce process and SLAs; monitor KPIs.
- Deal Desk: Validate pricing/discounts; ensure policy compliance; coordinate approvals; resolve commercial exceptions.
- Legal/Contracts Manager: Draft/review/redline agreements; manage clause deviations; ensure enforceability; oversee execution.
- Finance/AR: Approve credit and payment terms; generate invoices; manage collections setup; ensure tax compliance.
- Order Management/Revenue Operations: Book orders; set billing/revenue schedules; validate revenue recognition treatment.
- Implementation/Delivery/CSM: Accept handoff; plan delivery; confirm scope and timelines.
- Tax/Compliance/Risk: Validate tax setup, exemptions; conduct KYC/AML/export checks; ensure regulatory adherence.
- IT/Systems Admin: Maintain CRM/CPQ/CLM/ERP integrations; enforce access controls and audit logging.
- Customer Counterparts (Procurement, Legal, AP): Execute contract; issue PO; provide tax/billing details; receive invoices.

## Best Practices
- Standardize templates and clause libraries; maintain a clear approval matrix and delegation of authority.
- Use integrated CRM–CPQ–CLM–ERP with automated data flows and validation rules to eliminate rekeying.
- Apply a close-out checklist for each deal type (direct, channel, subscription, project-based).
- Adopt eSignature with enforced signer roles and identity verification.
- Capture structured win/loss reasons at close; make fields mandatory.
- Implement segregation of duties: sales cannot approve their own discounts or book orders.
- Use tax engines and compliance tools to minimize errors and audit findings.
- Validate customer master data against authoritative sources; avoid free-text entries.
- Time-box legal/commercial escalations with SLAs and clear escalation paths.
- Retain documents per policy (e.g., 7–10 years), with immutable storage for executed agreements.
- For subscriptions, align contract terms with billing system capabilities (co-termination, proration, ramps).
- For milestone billing, define objective acceptance criteria in the SOW.

## Common Challenges
- Missing or inconsistent documentation (contract vs PO vs quote)
  - Solution: Automated cross-checks, required field validations, pre-submission QA by Sales Ops.
- Slow contract cycles due to clause negotiation
  - Solution: Pre-approved fallback clauses, playbooks, and escalation paths; early Legal engagement.
- Credit and payment term issues
  - Solution: Early credit checks; conditional approvals; prepayment or escrow options.
- Tax and invoicing errors leading to disputes
  - Solution: Tax engine integration; clear bill-to/ship-to; customer-specific invoice templates; AP requirements checklist.
- Data quality gaps in CRM/ERP
  - Solution: Mandatory fields, dropdown reason codes, sync rules, periodic data audits.
- System integration failures
  - Solution: iPaaS monitoring, retry logic, and manual fallback procedures with reconciliation.
- Channel complexity (partner vs end-customer invoicing)
  - Solution: Clear deal registration and invoicing rules; partner agreements; accurate sell-to/bill-to mapping.
- Regulatory/export restrictions
  - Solution: Automated screening prior to booking; restricted party checks embedded in workflow.

## Performance Metrics
- Time to close and book: Verbal acceptance to order booking (hours/days).
- Contract cycle time: First draft to full execution.
- First-pass yield: Percentage of deals booked without rework.
- Booking accuracy: Percentage of orders without pricing/term discrepancies.
- Invoice accuracy rate and time to first invoice.
- Documentation completeness: Deals with full document pack attached.
- Win/loss capture rate: Percentage of closed opportunities with reason codes.
- Approval cycle time: Average time per approval stage (deal desk, legal, finance).
- Exception rate: Deals requiring policy exceptions or executive approvals.
- Compliance/audit findings: Number and severity related to order-to-cash close.
- eSignature adoption rate.

Target examples (adjust to context):
- 95% documentation completeness
- <2 business days from execution to booking
- >98% booking accuracy
- >98% invoice accuracy
- <5% exception rate

## Technology and Tools
- CRM: Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, HubSpot (opportunity disposition, data capture).
- CPQ: Salesforce CPQ, Conga CPQ, Oracle CPQ (approved quotes, pricing, configurations).
- CLM: DocuSign CLM, Ironclad, Icertis, Conga CLM (contract templates, workflows, repository).
- eSignature: DocuSign, Adobe Acrobat Sign (execution and audit trail).
- ERP/Order Management: SAP S/4HANA, Oracle Cloud ERP, NetSuite, Microsoft D365 (order booking, invoicing, master data).
- Billing/Revenue: Zuora, Chargebee, SAP BRIM, Oracle RevPro/ARM (billing schedules, revenue recognition).

- Compliance/KYC and Export Screening: Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, LexisNexis, Descartes MK Denial.
- Document Management: SharePoint, Box, OpenText (archival, retention).
- Integration/iPaaS: MuleSoft, Boomi, Workato (data synchronization, workflow orchestration).
- Analytics/BI: Tableau, Power BI, CRM dashboards (KPIs and monitoring).
- Ticketing/PM: Jira, Asana, ServiceNow (handoff to delivery, project initiation).

Process Details:
## Overview
De-duplicate customer data is the process of identifying and resolving multiple records that represent the same customer entity across and within systems. Its purpose is to maintain an accurate, unified “golden record” for each customer so sales, marketing, service, finance, and analytics operate on trustworthy, non-redundant information.

This process sits within Manage Customer Master Data and underpins the organization’s ability to:
- Improve customer experience (fewer misdirected communications, faster service).
- Increase sales and marketing effectiveness (correct segmentation, attribution, and reach).
- Reduce operational waste (duplicate outreach, returned mail, misaligned accounts).
- Ensure regulatory compliance and data subject rights management.
- Enable robust reporting and identity resolution across channels and lifecycle stages.

It can run in batch (periodic sweeps of the master) and/or real time (at point-of-capture in CRM/e-commerce and during integrations). It spans individuals, households, and organizations, and may include cross-domain links (account-contact relationships).

## Key Activities
- Data profiling and discovery: assess duplicate patterns, fields, and sources.
- Standardization and normalization: canonicalize names, addresses, phones, emails.
- Blocking and indexing: create comparison-friendly keys to reduce match space.
- Matching and clustering: apply deterministic and probabilistic/ML rules to identify potential duplicates.
- Scoring and classification: assign confidence scores and route as auto-merge, review, or no-match.
- Survivorship and consolidation: determine attribute-level winners and create/update golden records.
- Exception handling and stewardship: human review, approval, merge/unmerge decisions, and audit.
- Publishing and synchronization: propagate deduped master to downstream systems.
- Monitoring and tuning: track KPIs, adjust rules/thresholds, and continuously improve.
- Governance and controls: enforce privacy, security, and change management.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Source customer records (CRM, ERP, e-commerce, service desk, marketing automation, POS, data lake).
- Data model and metadata (entity definitions, attributes, data types).
- Reference data (postal address standards, phone country codes, email domains).
- Existing master data and crosswalks (source IDs to master IDs).
- Match rules, thresholds, and survivorship policies.
- Consent, privacy, and suppression flags.

Prerequisites:
- Defined customer entity scope (person, organization, household) and match domains (e.g., consumer vs B2B).
- Data quality baselines and canonical formats (e.g., E.164 for phone, lowercase emails).
- Governance model and RACI for data stewardship and approvals.
- Security and privacy controls for PII (role-based access, masking, audit).
- Environments and test datasets for safe rule tuning and UAT.
- Rollback/unmerge procedures and backup strategy.

Dependencies on other processes:
- Ingest and standardize customer data.
- Manage customer consent and privacy.
- Maintain account hierarchies and relationships.
- Integrate and distribute master data to consuming systems.
- Data quality monitoring and issue management.

## Process Steps
1. Trigger and scope
   - Triggered by schedule (e.g., nightly), event (bulk import), or real-time record creation/update.
   - Define scope (systems, geographies, customer segments) and sampling strategy for profiling.

2. Data profiling
   - Measure duplicate rates, field completeness, and value distributions.
   - Identify high-signal fields by domain (e.g., email for B2C; tax ID/DUNS for B2B).

3. Standardization and normalization
   - Clean and parse names (prefix/suffix, transliteration), addresses (CASS/DPV where applicable), emails (lowercase, trim aliases), phones (E.164), organization names (remove legal suffixes).
   - Apply tokenization and phonetic keys (Soundex, Metaphone) as needed.

4. Blocking and indexing
   - Generate blocking keys to cluster likely matches (e.g., normalized email; soundex(last)+zip; org_key+city).
   - Build search indexes to enable fuzzy lookups (e.g., Elasticsearch with analyzers).

5. Matching
   - Deterministic rules: exact/key matches on high-trust identifiers (email, tax ID, CRM external ID).
   - Probabilistic/fuzzy: weighted comparisons (Jaro-Winkler, Levenshtein, token-based) across name, address, phone, org.
   - Optional ML/entity resolution model trained on steward-labeled pairs to improve recall/precision.
   - External referential matching (postal/phone/email verification, business registries) to boost confidence.

6. Clustering and classification
   - Group candidate records into clusters representing a single entity.
   - Score each pair and cluster; classify into:
     - Auto-merge: score above upper threshold and no conflicts.
     - Steward review: between thresholds or conflicting attributes.
     - No-match: below lower threshold.

7. Survivorship determination
   - Apply attribute-level survivorship logic:
     - Source trust hierarchy (e.g., verified service > CRM > web form).
     - Recency/latency (most recent verified update).
     - Completeness and validation status.
   - Preserve all source values in history for audit and potential unmerge.

8. Merge and golden record creation/update
   - Create or update master ID (persistent key).
   - Consolidate attributes per survivorship rules; link all source record IDs in crosswalk.
   - Maintain slowly changing dimensions/versioning for the golden record.

9. Exception handling and stewardship
   - Route “review” items to data stewards with evidence (side-by-side compare, score breakdown, change impact).
   - Stewards approve merge, reject, or request more info; enforce SLAs.
   - Support manual split/unmerge with full audit.

10. Referential integrity and downstream alignment
    - Reassign related transactions, opportunities, cases, subscriptions to the surviving master ID.
    - Update account-contact relationships, hierarchies, and ownership rules.
    - Close/mark duplicates in source CRMs and create redirects where applicable.

11. Publishing and synchronization
    - Publish changes to MDM hub and downstream via APIs, CDC, or ETL.
    - Notify system owners of updates/merges; coordinate with integration runtime windows.

12. Controls and compliance
    - Log all match/merge decisions and actors for audit.
    - Honor consent and suppression rules across merged entities.
    - Apply data minimization and masking in logs and review UIs.

13. Monitoring and reporting
    - Update dashboards for duplicate rates, false merges, backlog, SLA adherence.
    - Alert on spikes or rule drift; capture user feedback from front-line systems.

14. Continuous improvement
    - Periodically recalibrate thresholds; retrain ML models with new labels.
    - A/B test rules on holdout datasets; review business impacts (deliverability, CSAT).

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Deduplicated customer master (golden records with persistent IDs).
- Crosswalk/linkage tables mapping source record IDs to master IDs.
- Match/merge logs, audit trails, and stewardship decisions.
- Exception queues with disposition and SLA metrics.
- Data quality and operational dashboards.
- Updated downstream systems aligned to master IDs.
- Documentation: match rules, survivorship policies, unmerge/rollback procedures.

Success criteria:
- Duplicate rate reduced below target thresholds for each domain.
- False merge rate below acceptable risk threshold.
- Stewardship backlog within SLA; high auto-merge precision.
- Downstream systems synchronized without integrity issues.
- Compliance with privacy/security policies and positive business impact (e.g., improved deliverability).

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Data Owner/Business Owner: Defines entity scope, business rules, and acceptance criteria.
- MDM/Data Architect: Designs data model, match strategy, survivorship, and integration patterns.
- Data Engineer/Integration Engineer: Implements pipelines, indexes, APIs, and publishing mechanisms.
- Data Steward: Reviews exceptions, executes merges/unmerges, ensures data quality, maintains documentation.
- Data Quality Analyst: Profiles data, monitors KPIs, tunes rules, conducts root-cause analysis.
- CRM/MarTech Admins: Configure duplicate prevention at point-of-entry; manage downstream alignment.
- Privacy/Compliance Officer: Ensures adherence to GDPR/CCPA and audit requirements.
- Security/IT Ops: Manages access controls, encryption, monitoring, and backups/restore.
- Product Owner/Process Manager: Prioritizes improvements, manages releases, and stakeholder communication.

## Best Practices
- Prevent at the source: enable real-time duplicate checks and search-as-you-type in CRMs and web forms.
- Canonical formats: enforce standard formats for names, addresses, phones, and emails before matching.
- Layered matching: use deterministic rules for high-confidence identifiers and probabilistic/ML for the rest.
- Conservative auto-merge: set high thresholds; route ambiguous cases to stewards; never auto-merge across domains without strong signals.
- Attribute-level survivorship: apply trust hierarchies, recency, and validation status per field.
- Preserve history: keep full lineage, crosswalks, and the ability to unmerge with rollback.
- Tune by segment: different rules for B2C vs B2B, region/language, and channel.
- Use reference and verification services: postal, phone, email, and business registries to validate inputs.
- Secure PII: mask sensitive fields in logs and steward tools; apply least-privilege access.
- Operational safety: run large merges off-peak; lock/queue related updates; test in lower environments with realistic data.
- Continuous learning: gather steward feedback to improve rules and retrain models; regularly review KPIs.
- Govern changes: version control for rules; peer review and change approval for match logic.

## Common Challenges
- Poor or missing identifiers: Solve with stronger standardization, data enrichment, and source data contracts.
- International/multilingual data: Use locale-aware parsing, transliteration, and reference datasets.
- High false merges: Tighten thresholds, add negative signals (e.g., different birthdates), require multi-attribute agreement.
- High manual review volume: Improve blocking keys, add features to models, and focus on better source validation.
- Reappearing duplicates: Implement point-of-entry checks and CDC-based continuous dedupe.
- Downstream key conflicts: Use persistent master IDs and robust crosswalks; coordinate cutovers carefully.
- Performance at scale: Optimize blocking strategies, indexing, and horizontal scaling; batch large clusters.
- Compliance risk: Minimize PII exposure in tooling; maintain auditable logs; automate subject rights propagation after merges.

## Performance Metrics
- Duplicate rate per 1,000 records (by domain/system).
- Auto-merge precision and recall; false merge rate; false non-match rate.
- Percentage auto-resolved vs manual; manual review acceptance rate.
- Time to resolve duplicate (average, 95th percentile); stewardship backlog size and SLA attainment.
- Downstream sync latency after merge and number of sync failures.
- Data quality improvements: deliverability, bounce rate, returned mail, suppression accuracy.
- Business impact: reduction in duplicate outreach, improvement in conversion/upsell, CSAT/NPS change.
- System performance: match throughput (records/hour), index latency, job duration and resource usage.

## Technology and Tools
- MDM platforms: Informatica MDM/IDMC, Reltio, IBM InfoSphere MDM, SAP MDG, Oracle Customer Data Management.
- Data quality and matching: Informatica DQ, Talend Data Quality, Ataccama, Experian, Senzing, Data Ladder, OpenRefine, Dedupe.io, Splink, RapidFuzz.
- Address/identity verification: Loqate/GBG, Melissa, Smarty, USPS CASS/DPV, Twilio Lookup; email verification providers.
- Search and indexing: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, Apache Lucene/Solr for fuzzy matching and blocking.
- Integration and pipelines: Informatica IICS, Talend, Azure Data Factory, AWS Glue, dbt, Kafka, Debezium for CDC.
- Data stores: Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, PostgreSQL for staging and mastering.
- Governance and catalog: Collibra, Alation, Microsoft Purview; policy management and lineage.
- Workflow and ticketing: ServiceNow, Jira for stewardship queues and approvals.
- Analytics/dashboards: Power BI, Tableau, Looker for KPI monitoring.
- CRM/MarTech configuration: Salesforce Duplicate Management/Matching Rules, Dynamics 365 duplicate detection, marketing automation dedupe tools.

Process Details:
# [3.5.4.2.2] Retrieve full customer details

## Overview
Retrieve full customer details is the process of obtaining a complete, accurate, and authorized view of a customer’s information to support sales order capture, order amendments, invoicing, fulfillment, credit decisions, tax determination, and customer service. It ensures that the right data is available at the right time, from a trusted source, and shared in a compliant way with downstream processes and systems.

Positioned under “Collect and maintain account information,” this process:
- Serves as the operational gateway to the customer “golden record” during order execution.
- Reduces rework and order errors by validating identity, hierarchy, addresses, payment terms, tax status, and entitlements before order submission.
- Enforces data governance, privacy, and security controls when accessing personally identifiable information (PII) or sensitive business data.

## Key Activities
- Identify and authenticate the requester and purpose of access.
- Search and match customer records across CRM/MDM and related systems.
- Retrieve core account and contact data, including bill-to, ship-to, and sold-to relationships.
- Enrich with financial, tax, compliance, and contractual details (credit status, tax exemption, sanctions flags, contracts/entitlements).
- Validate and standardize critical fields (addresses, emails, phone numbers; de-duplication).
- Apply privacy and access controls (data minimization, masking, consent).
- Compile a unified, consumable payload for the requesting process/system.
- Log access and outcomes; route exceptions for resolution.

## Inputs and Prerequisites
- Required inputs to begin:
  - Customer identifiers: account ID, CRM ID, email, phone, billing account, tax ID/VAT, PO number reference, DUNS (B2B), or government ID where allowed.
  - Purpose of retrieval: order creation/amendment, credit check, tax determination, KYC refresh, service provisioning, or customer service request.
  - Requester credentials and role: sales rep, order management specialist, API client, partner portal user.
  - Channel/context: assisted sales (CRM), e-commerce checkout, call center, API integration.

- Prerequisites:
  - Defined data model and “golden record” standards for customers, contacts, and hierarchies.
  - System access configured (RBAC/ABAC), SSO/MFA, and data privacy policies (lawful basis, consent management).
  - Connectivity to source-of-truth systems (CRM/MDM, ERP/Finance, tax, credit, contracts/entitlements, service/support).
  - Data quality rules and validation services (address/email/phone verification).
  - Audit logging enabled.

- Dependencies on other processes:
  - 3.5.4.2.1 Create or update customer record (to ensure data availability).
  - 3.5.4 Manage sales orders (order capture depends on retrieved details).
  - Credit approval and risk management processes (use retrieved credit and compliance info).
  - Tax determination/exemption management.
  - Data governance and master data management (MDM) processes.
  - Consent and privacy management (e.g., opt-in/opt-out handling).

## Process Steps
1. Intake and purpose validation
   - Capture the request with identifiers and intended use.
   - Verify lawful basis and consent where required (GDPR/CCPA/other applicable regulations).
   - Authenticate the requester (SSO/MFA) and authorize based on role and purpose.
   - If unauthorized or unlawful purpose, deny and log with reason.

2. Initial record search
   - Query CRM/MDM using strong identifiers (account ID, email, DUNS).
   - If none provided or no exact match, perform fuzzy search on name, address, phone; apply configurable match score thresholds.
   - If multiple candidates:
     - Present ranked candidates with key disambiguators (legal name, country, parent, recent order).
     - If ambiguity persists, initiate a clarification workflow or request more identifiers.

3. Identity resolution and golden record selection
   - Resolve duplicates using MDM matching rules; select the golden record (or best candidate).
   - Retrieve linked entities:
     - Account hierarchy (parent/child/ultimate parent).
     - Ship-to/bill-to/sold-to locations and default preferences.
     - Contacts and roles (buyer, AP, technical, legal).
   - If no record found:
     - Trigger “provisional account” creation workflow (if allowed), or redirect to customer creation process.
     - Flag downstream processes that data is provisional and may require re-validation.

4. Data retrieval from federated sources
   - CRM/MDM: core profile, hierarchy, contacts, preferences.
   - ERP/Finance: payment terms, credit status/limit/hold flags, account balance, invoicing profile.
   - Tax engine: tax ID validation status, exemption certificates, nexus applicability.
   - Contracts/subscriptions: active MSAs, SLAs, entitlements, renewal dates, pricing terms.
   - Support/CS: open cases, service levels, installed base/assets, RMA flags.
   - Marketing/consent: communication preferences, opt-in/out status, do-not-contact flags.
   - Compliance: sanctions/denied-party screening status, export controls, restricted jurisdictions.
   - External enrichment (if permitted): firmographics (e.g., D&B), VAT validation (e.g., VIES), business registration registries.
   - Apply caching where allowed; respect TTL to ensure freshness.

5. Data validation and standardization
   - Validate addresses against postal standards and geocoding; standardize formats.
   - Validate email syntax and bounce risk; phone number format and region.
   - Check field completeness per data quality rules (e.g., must-have fields by country/segment).
   - Ensure consistency across systems (e.g., payment terms alignment).
   - Reconcile conflicts using predefined survivorship rules (source priority, recency, data quality score).

6. Privacy and access controls
   - Apply data minimization: include only fields necessary for the stated purpose.
   - Redact or mask sensitive attributes based on role (e.g., partial tax ID masking for sales reps).
   - Enforce regional data residency and cross-border transfer rules.
   - If customer has specific restrictions (e.g., do-not-contact), tag in the payload and constrain use.

7. Exception handling and approvals
   - If customer is on credit hold or exceeds limit, route to Credit for review.
   - If sanctions/denied-party hits occur, route to Compliance; halt fulfillment steps.
   - If tax documents are missing or expired, trigger tax certificate collection workflow.
   - If data quality falls below threshold (e.g., missing bill-to), create data stewardship ticket.

8. Compile unified payload
   - Map retrieved and validated data into the standard customer schema, including:
     - Identification: legal name, aliases, IDs, DUNS.
     - Hierarchy: parent/child links, sold-to/bill-to/ship-to.
     - Contacts: names, roles, emails/phones, preferences, consent flags.
     - Locations: standardized addresses, geocodes, delivery instructions.
     - Financial: currency, payment terms, credit status/limits, incoterms (if applicable).
     - Tax: tax IDs, validation status, exemptions, certificate references.
     - Contracts/entitlements: active agreements, SLA levels, subscription status.
     - Compliance: screening status, risk flags, embargo restrictions.
     - Operational: delivery windows, special handling, required documents.
     - Metadata: source systems, timestamps, data quality scores, lineage.
   - Mark any provisional fields and confidence levels.

9. Delivery to requesting process/system
   - Provide the payload via the appropriate channel:
     - API response (JSON), CRM screen population, order entry UI, or secured report.
   - Annotate with SLA status and any flags requiring action (e.g., “Credit review required”).
   - Ensure idempotency and versioning for repeat requests.

10. Logging and closeout
   - Write detailed audit logs: who accessed what, when, why, from where, and what was delivered.
   - Update “last accessed” and freshness indicators.
   - If feedback from the requester indicates discrepancies, capture and route to data stewardship.
   - Close the request within SLA; monitor for downstream failures and remediate as needed.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Outputs:
  - Unified customer details payload aligned to the enterprise schema, suitable for order processing.
  - Data quality metrics (completeness, confidence scores).
  - Flags and tasks for exceptions (credit review, tax docs, compliance).

- Deliverables:
  - Populated order entry/customer view in operational systems.
  - Audit log entries and access records.
  - Data stewardship tickets or change requests (if issues found).

- Success criteria:
  - Correct customer identified and full details delivered within SLA.
  - Data meets quality thresholds (e.g., >98% completeness on mandatory fields).
  - Access is authorized and compliant; no privacy violations.
  - Downstream order processing proceeds without rework due to customer data issues.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Sales/Order Management Specialist: Initiate retrieval; verify customer selection; act on flags; proceed with order entry.
- Sales Operations: Define standards; monitor adherence; resolve process questions.
- Data Steward/MDM Analyst: Maintain matching rules; resolve duplicates; curate golden records; handle DQ tickets.
- CRM/MDM Administrator: Configure integrations, schemas, RBAC; maintain validation services.
- Credit Analyst: Review holds/limits; set or update credit terms.
- Tax/Finance Analyst: Validate tax IDs, exemptions; ensure invoice requirements are met.
- Compliance/Legal: Oversee sanctions screening/export controls; approve or block restricted customers.
- Customer Service: Provide context on entitlements, installed base; update contact preferences as needed.
- Privacy/InfoSec Officer: Define and audit access policies; ensure lawful basis and data protection controls.
- Integration/Platform Engineer: Maintain APIs, orchestration, monitoring, and error handling.
- Channel/Partner Manager (if applicable): Validate partner/reseller account structures and permissions.

## Best Practices
- Establish a single source of truth (MDM) with clear survivorship rules and lineage.
- Use unique identifiers consistently (account IDs, DUNS, tax IDs) and maintain crosswalks.
- Implement robust identity resolution with deterministic and probabilistic matching.
- Standardize addresses and contact details; validate at point of use and regularly thereafter.
- Enforce least-privilege access and data minimization aligned to purpose and role.
- Maintain up-to-date consent and communication preferences; respect do-not-contact flags.
- Automate sanctions and tax validations; re-check periodically and upon major changes.
- Cache non-sensitive data with short TTL to improve performance; ensure freshness for critical fields (credit status).
- Monitor data quality via dashboards; close the loop with stewardship workflows.
- Design APIs with idempotency, pagination, partial responses, and explicit versioning.
- Define clear SLAs and error handling (timeouts, retries, fallbacks, circuit breakers).
- Log comprehensively and review audit trails; periodically test access controls.
- Segment process variants (B2B vs B2C, direct vs partner) with tailored rules.

## Common Challenges and Solutions
- Fragmented data across silos
  - Solution: Implement MDM, integration middleware, and a canonical customer schema.
- Duplicate or ambiguous records
  - Solution: Advanced matching, survivorship rules, stewardship queue, and periodic dedupe campaigns.
- Outdated or low-quality contact and address data
  - Solution: Automated validation services; scheduled refresh; bounce/return-to-sender feedback loops.
- Privacy and consent complexities
  - Solution: Centralized consent management; purpose-based access controls; data minimization and masking.
- Compliance holds (sanctions/export controls)
  - Solution: Real-time screening with escalation; block downstream steps until cleared.
- Credit risk and payment term disputes
  - Solution: Integrate real-time credit checks; alert and approval workflows; clear owner routing.
- Integration failures and latency
  - Solution: Resilient patterns (retry/backoff), health checks, graceful degradation, and caching.
- International variations (formats, local regulations)
  - Solution: Country-specific validation rules, localized address standards, regional data residency handling.

## Performance Metrics
- Retrieval SLA attainment (e.g., 95% within 2 seconds for API, 5 seconds for UI).
- First-attempt match rate (exact and resolved).
- Data completeness score for mandatory fields by segment/country.
- Accuracy/validation pass rate (address/email/phone).
- Exception rate and mean time to resolve (credit, compliance, tax).
- Duplicate rate trend and time-to-merge.
- API availability and latency percentiles.
- Percentage of retrievals blocked due to authorization/privacy.
- Downstream rework due to customer data errors (defect leakage).
- User satisfaction (CSAT) for assisted channels.

## Technology and Tools
- CRM/Operational systems: Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP CX.
- MDM/Identity resolution: Informatica MDM, Reltio, SAP MDG, Semarchy xDM.
- Data quality/standardization: Informatica DQ, Talend, Melissa, Loqate/GBG, Smarty.
- Address/email/phone validation: Loqate, Smarty, Google Maps APIs; Kickbox, ZeroBounce; Twilio Lookup.
- Tax determination and validation: Avalara, Vertex; EU VIES for VAT checks.
- Credit and firmographic enrichment: Dun & Bradstreet, Experian, Equifax, Creditsafe.
- Compliance screening: Refinitiv World-Check, Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, Descartes Visual Compliance.
- Integration and API management: MuleSoft, Boomi, Azure Integration Services, Kafka, Apigee, Kong.
- Consent/privacy management: OneTrust, TrustArc; IAM/SSO: Okta, Azure AD.
- Logging/monitoring: Splunk, ELK, Datadog; ticketing/workflows: ServiceNow, Jira; BPM: Camunda.
- Analytics and catalog: Power BI/Tableau, Collibra, Alation.
- Security: Data masking/tokenization (Protegrity, Skyflow); encryption key management (HSM/KMS).

Process Details:
## Overview
Process Name: [3.5.4.2.6] Record key customer communication profile details

Purpose:
- Capture, validate, and maintain business rules that govern how, when, and for what purposes the organization communicates with a customer (account and its contacts).
- Ensure all communications (sales, order/fulfillment, service, billing, legal) adhere to customer preferences and regulatory requirements (e.g., GDPR, CAN-SPAM, CASL, TCPA).

Role in the organization:
- Supports Manage sales orders by ensuring order acknowledgments, delivery updates, changes, and invoices are sent via approved channels, at approved times, to the correct recipients.
- Feeds upstream and downstream systems (CRM, marketing automation, telephony, ERP, service desk) with enforceable contact policies and consent signals.
- Reduces regulatory risk and customer complaints; improves deliverability, customer experience, and operational efficiency.

Scope:
- Applies to all customers and prospects where communications are initiated or received.
- Covers company-to-individual (B2C) and company-to-company (B2B) scenarios, including partners/resellers.
- Includes transactional, operational, service, marketing, billing/collections, and legal/regulatory communications.

## Key Activities
- Intake and identification of the account and contact(s)
- Identity verification of preference/consent submitter
- Capture and classification of communication preferences by purpose/category and channel
- Consent management and lawful-basis recording (including evidence)
- Time zone, language, and quiet-hours configuration
- Special handling rules (accessibility needs, security/sensitivity, blackout periods)
- Escalation and notification matrix setup (who gets what, when)
- Policy validation against corporate/regional templates and regulations
- Approval workflow (as needed) and assignment of ownership/effective dates
- Synchronization to operational systems and enforcement mechanisms
- Confirmation to customer and provision of self-service preference center access
- Ongoing monitoring, review, and change control with full audit trail

## Inputs and Prerequisites
Required inputs:
- Account and contact identifiers (CRM IDs, legal entity, region/country)
- Contact details (email, phone, address), time zone, language
- Communication categories needed (e.g., order status, delivery updates, billing notices, service outages, marketing newsletters)
- Channel preferences and constraints: email/SMS/phone/push/portal/in-app/social
- Consent records: purpose-specific, channel-specific, source, timestamp, lawful basis, expiry
- Special requirements: accessibility (e.g., large print), security (e.g., no PII via email), blackout periods, frequency caps
- Notification and escalation contacts with roles (e.g., Purchasing, AP, Logistics, IT Ops)
- Applicable regulatory regime(s) per location (GDPR, CASL, CAN-SPAM, TCPA, CTIA, HIPAA/PCI/FINRA constraints)

Prerequisites:
- Customer and contact exist in CRM/MDM with minimum viable data quality
- Preference/consent capture mechanisms are available (forms, portal, verbal scripts)
- Consent Management Platform and preference center configured with corporate policy taxonomy
- Data protection and access controls in place for PII
- Defined communication policy templates by region/industry

Dependencies on other processes:
- [3.5.4.2] Collect and maintain account information (source and master data stewardship)
- Consent and preference management governance (Legal/Compliance)
- Onboard new customers (to trigger initial profile capture)
- Change management for customer master data and contracts
- System integration and data synchronization (CRM, CDP, MAP, telephony, ERP, service)

## Process Steps
1) Trigger and scope determination
- Triggers: new account/prospect, contract signing, order creation, customer kickoff, regulatory change, M&A/organization change, customer-requested update, campaign launch.
- Determine entities affected: account, specific contacts, business units, regions.

2) Intake and identity verification
- Accept preferences via authenticated channels: portal login (SSO), verified email link, recorded call (with script), signed document, or verified AM/CSM request.
- Verify identity and authority to set preferences (e.g., role/title, purchasing authority). For B2B, confirm whether preferences apply at account, buying center, or individual.

3) Map to data model
- Link to Account, Contact, and (if used) Communication Profile object(s).
- Assign country/region, time zone, and preferred language. Infer time zone from address/phone if not explicitly provided; confirm with customer.

4) Capture communication categories and channels
- For each category (examples below), capture allowed channels, recipients, frequency caps, and SLAs:
  - Sales and opportunity updates
  - Order acknowledgments, changes, shipping/delivery notifications
  - Service cases, maintenance/outage notices, incident alerts
  - Billing, dunning, tax/regulatory notices
  - Product updates, release notes
  - Marketing and events
- Record quiet hours (e.g., no calls 8pm–8am local time), permitted days, and blackout dates.

5) Consent and lawful basis recording
- Capture consent per purpose and channel with: consent status, lawful basis (e.g., consent, contract), source, timestamp, expiration, and evidence (document, recording, web event).
- Apply double opt-in for marketing where required; record confirmation hash/time.
- Record DNC/opt-out flags and link to national registries where applicable.

6) Special handling and constraints
- Accessibility: alternative formats, assistive technology preferences.
- Security sensitivity: do not include PII/financial data in emails; require portal for statements; encryption required for attachments.
- Industry constraints: healthcare/financial services (e.g., HIPAA/FINRA retention).

7) Escalation and notification matrix
- Define primary and backup recipients per category (e.g., AP for invoices, Logistics for delivery).
- Define escalation timeframes and channels (e.g., 24-hour non-response escalates to Purchasing Manager).

8) Validation and policy checks
- Validate against corporate templates by country/industry.
- Check conflicts (e.g., marketing opt-in but DNC for phone; TCPA restrictions).
- Flag risks requiring Legal/Compliance review.

9) Approvals and effective dating
- Route for approval when exceptions to standard policy exist.
- Set effective start and end dates; schedule reviews (e.g., annual).

10) Persist and synchronize
- Update CRM Communication Profile and CMP records with versioning and audit trail.
- Push suppression/allow lists to marketing automation; update dialer DNC; configure service notification groups; set ERP billing contacts; configure journey orchestration rules.
- Ensure idempotent integrations via middleware; handle failures with retry/alerts.

11) Customer confirmation and self-service
- Send confirmation summary with effective rules and self-service link.
- Provide instructions to modify preferences and point of contact.

12) Testing and enforcement verification
- Execute a controlled test (non-marketing) to verify correct routing and suppression.
- Validate deliverability and time-window enforcement; log results.

13) Monitoring and change control
- Monitor violations (e.g., calls outside quiet hours) and remediate.
- Reconcile suppression lists across systems weekly.
- Process updates upon customer request; re-run approval if exceptions persist.

14) Audit, retention, and review
- Retain consent evidence per policy and regulation.
- Record of processing activities updated if scope changes.
- Conduct periodic reviews; deprecate stale profiles; archive with version history.

## Outputs and Deliverables
Expected outputs:
- Complete, versioned Customer Communication Profile linked to account and contacts
- Consent records by purpose and channel with immutable evidence
- Active suppression/allow lists propagated to all relevant systems
- Configured notification and escalation matrices in service and ERP systems
- Confirmation notification to customer

Deliverables:
- Profile summary report (PDF/HTML) and machine-readable profile (JSON) for integrations
- Audit logs: who changed what, when, why (including approvals)

Success criteria:
- 100% of active accounts with a current, approved communication profile
- Zero regulatory violations or out-of-hours contact incidents
- Accurate enforcement across channels (no unintended sends/calls)
- Increased deliverability and reduced complaints/unsubscribes

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Account Manager/CSM: Initiates capture, validates business needs with customer, confirms recipients and escalation paths.
- Sales Operations: Owns process execution, data entry quality, and coordination across systems.
- Marketing Operations: Ensures marketing consent and suppression are correctly configured; runs double opt-in; manages preference center.
- Service Operations: Configures service notification groups and outage/incident communications.
- Billing/AR Operations: Defines and maintains billing/collections contacts and channel constraints.
- Legal/Compliance/Privacy: Defines policy templates, reviews exceptions, interprets regulations, audits adherence.
- Data Steward/MDM: Maintains master data quality, resolves duplicates, governs taxonomy and data standards.
- IT/Integration: Builds and maintains synchronization, idempotency, and monitoring; manages failures and SLAs.
- Security: Ensures encryption, access controls, DLP, and secure handling of sensitive communications.
- Telephony/Contact Center Admin: Manages dialer DNC, quiet-hour enforcement, and call recording consent scripts.
- Regional Leads: Localize policies for country/region requirements and holidays.

## Best Practices
- Use a unified communication profile model: account-level defaults plus contact-level overrides; clearly define inheritance and conflict resolution.
- Segment by communication purpose; collect consent granularly per purpose and channel.
- Default marketing to opt-in (with double opt-in) and transactional to lawful basis of contract as appropriate.
- Capture time zone explicitly and enforce quiet hours; infer cautiously and confirm during onboarding.
- Maintain a single source of truth for consent (CMP) and expose via APIs to all channels.
- Provide customer self-service preference management; honor changes within strict SLAs.
- Record immutable evidence for consent; store provenance and version history.
- Enforce policies at the edge (MAP, dialer, service desk, ERP) and centrally (policy engine) to prevent bypass.
- Localize language and holiday blackouts; maintain a rules library by country/industry.
- Test enforcement regularly (A/B suppression tests, synthetic transactions).
- Implement strong access controls and segregation of duties; restrict who can override policies.
- Automate DNC and regulatory list scrubbing; schedule regular reconciliations across systems.
- Establish a governance forum with Sales Ops, MOPS, Compliance, and IT for continuous improvement.

## Common Challenges
- Fragmented systems cause inconsistent enforcement; solution: centralize profile and consent via APIs and enforce in all channels.
- Missing or incorrect time zones leading to out-of-hours contact; solution: capture at onboarding, verify periodically, system-level timezone detection.
- Ambiguous authority in B2B accounts; solution: define roles and authorization matrix; require documented authority to set account-wide rules.
- Global subsidiaries and complex legal entities; solution: map communication policies per entity and region with inheritance rules.
- Legacy data without consent evidence; solution: run re-permissioning campaigns; quarantine until compliant.
- Manual updates and delays in propagation; solution: event-driven integrations with monitoring and SLAs.
- Conflicts between contact and account preferences; solution: apply most restrictive rule by default; allow documented exceptions with approval.
- Regulatory changes; solution: maintain rules library and trigger mass policy updates with Legal oversight.
- Channel partners contacting end customers outside policy; solution: include communication clauses in partner agreements; provide shared suppression services.

## Performance Metrics
- Coverage: percent of active accounts/contacts with complete profiles
- Consent completeness: percent of required purposes with valid consent/lawful basis
- Time to propagate: average time to update preferences across all systems
- Violation rate: number of out-of-policy contacts per 1,000 communications
- Complaint rate: spam complaints, DNC complaints, regulatory inquiries
- Deliverability: email bounce rate, SMS delivery rate, call connect compliance
- Preference change SLA adherence: percent of requests completed within SLA
- Data quality: percent with accurate time zone/language; duplicate rate
- Audit readiness: number of audit findings; evidence retrieval time
- Suppression accuracy: false positive/negative suppression incidents

- CRM: Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics (Account/Contact/Communication Profile objects)

- CDP/MDM: Segment, Tealium, Adobe RT-CDP, Informatica MDM

- Email/SMS/Push providers: SendGrid, SparkPost, Twilio, Sinch, Firebase
- Service Management: ServiceNow, Zendesk (notification groups)
- ERP/Billing: SAP, Oracle, NetSuite (billing contact policies)
- Integration/Middleware: MuleSoft, Boomi, Azure Integration Services, Kafka for event propagation
- Data Quality and Enrichment: address and phone validation; time zone inference services
- Security: IAM/SSO, encryption key management, DLP, audit logging
- Compliance utilities: DNC scrubbing services, regulatory list management, consent evidence storage

4. Curriculum and Assessment Design
   - Write learning objectives aligned to competencies (Bloom’s taxonomy).
   - Design modular pathways: microlearning + workshops + practice labs + coaching.
   - Draft exam blueprint and item bank plan; create capstone scenarios mapped to marketing campaigns.
   - Ensure accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) and localization strategy.

5. Content Development
   - Produce e-learning (Storyline/Rise), VILT decks, facilitator guides, participant workbooks.
   - Build simulations (role-plays, call recordings), interactive calculators, battlecards, talk tracks, outreach cadences aligned to campaigns.
   - Develop labs (e.g., using demo environments or virtual labs).
   - Create assessments: quizzes, scenario items, performance rubrics.
   - Run legal/brand review and SME QA; package for LMS/PRM.

6. Pilot and Iterate
   - Deliver beta to a representative partner cohort across regions.
   - Collect L1/L2 feedback, analyze exam item performance (psychometrics), and measure task performance.
   - Iterate content, adjust cut scores, retire or revise weak items.

7. Operate Certification
   - Publish schedule and catalog; open enrollment; handle SSO via PRM.
   - Manage exam registration, proctoring, ID verification, accommodations.
   - Issue digital badges/certificates with metadata (skills, validity, version).
   - Sync completions and credentials to PRM/CRM for tiering and incentives.

8. Deliver at Scale
   - Run VILT/ILT calendars, on-demand releases, office hours, community forums.
   - Execute train-the-trainer and certify partner trainers.
   - Roll out localization; maintain version parity across languages.

9. Communication and Adoption
   - Launch plan: partner newsletters, portal updates, sales kits for CAMs.
   - Tie MDF eligibility, deal registration prioritization, or spiffs to certification.
   - Provide managers with dashboards and coaching guides.

10. Measure and Improve
   - Track adoption, completion, pass rates, time-to-certify, L1–L4.
   - Correlate certification with pipeline, win rate, deal size, velocity.
   - Monitor exam security (item exposure, abnormal patterns).
   - Maintain backlog for enhancements; plan quarterly content refresh and annual blueprint review.

11. Recertification and Lifecycle Management
   - Define CE requirements (e.g., quarterly update modules, product release briefings).
   - Notify partners of renewal windows; automate reminders.
   - Deprecate outdated credentials and manage transitions.

12. Compliance and Risk Management
   - Enforce anti-cheating policies, data privacy (GDPR/CCPA), export controls.
   - Maintain accessibility and brand compliance audits.

## Outputs and Deliverables
- Training program assets: curricula, learning paths, instructor and learner materials, labs.
- Certification artifacts: exam blueprints, item banks, scoring rubrics, cut score documentation, proctoring procedures.
- Operational collateral: schedule, FAQs, policies, badging metadata, TTT kits.
- Systems data: enrollment/completion records, credential registry, PRM/CRM syncs, dashboards.
- Reports: adoption and impact reports, item analysis, localization coverage, accessibility compliance.
- Success criteria:
  - Target percentage of active partners with role-appropriate certifications.
  - Measurable uplift in partner-led pipeline, win rates, and deal velocity for certified reps.
  - Time-to-ramp reduction for new partner sellers.
  - Certification integrity (acceptable item exposure and pass rate bands).
  - Positive partner satisfaction (CSAT/NPS) and manager endorsement.

## Roles and Responsibilities
- Partner Enablement Manager: Owns program strategy, roadmap, governance, budget, and outcomes.
- Certification Program Manager: Manages certification framework, exams, security, recertification.
- Instructional Designer/Curriculum Architect: Designs learning paths and content.
- Subject Matter Experts (Product Marketing, Sales Enablement, Demand Gen, Sales Ops): Provide expertise, review content, ensure alignment to campaigns and GTM.
- Trainers/Facilitators: Deliver ILT/VILT, evaluate performance, certify trainers.

- Exam Delivery/Proctoring Lead: Operates test centers/online proctoring and incident handling.
- Marketing Communications: Launches programs, maintains partner portal content.
- Legal/Compliance: Reviews claims, data privacy, accessibility, and trademark usage.
- Channel/Partner Account Managers (CAMs): Drive adoption with partners, tie to incentives/tiering.
- Data/BI Analyst: Builds dashboards, conducts impact analysis and ROI modeling.
- IT/Security: SSO, platform security, data retention, and access control.

## Best Practices
- Anchor design in JTA and measurable competencies; use Bloom’s taxonomy.
- Align every module and assessment to real campaigns and sales plays.
- Use blended learning: microlearning for knowledge, VILT/role-plays for skills, labs for application.
- Implement rigorous exam development: blueprinting, item writing standards, psychometrics, and secure delivery.
- Offer role-based and level-based pathways; certify partner trainers to scale.
- Tie certification to partner incentives, tier requirements, and MDF eligibility.
- Localize strategically for top markets; maintain release parity across languages.
- Ensure accessibility from the outset; test with assistive technologies.
- Maintain a quarterly content refresh aligned to product and campaign releases.
- Provide practice assessments and readiness checks; publish transparent exam outlines.
- Use digital badging with verifiable metadata; enable social and PRM display.
- Monitor outcomes at Kirkpatrick Levels 1–4; continuously close the loop with improvements.

## Common Challenges
- Low partner engagement or time constraints:

- Content obsolescence due to frequent releases:
  - Solutions: Modular content architecture, quarterly refresh cadence, release notes micro-updates, content owner SLAs.
- Exam security and cheating:

- Compliance and accessibility gaps:

## Performance Metrics
